name: The Ward File — a Seattle chronicle (fan, unofficial)
caption: Seattle, November 2026. The whole chronicle, ready to run.
description:
Imports into the world 22 scenes, 51 actors (PCs, NPCs and the Puget Cell), 101 journals (the adventure, the city, the characters and the documents to hand out), 11 items of FIRSTLIGHT gear, 6 macros and 1 playlist of music (each scene plays its ambience when activated), with their folders.

Importing again updates the existing documents without duplicating them.

Demeanor

Looks about twenty-eight, though he moves like an older man. Shaved head, a knife scar through his left eyebrow, a broken nose that healed badly; dark work clothes under Vance's coat. He's left-handed.

August Krell · Combat Version

Full profile in Chapter 4.

Health 7 · Willpower 6 · Usual Hunger 2 · Blood Potency 3

Unarmed attack 10 (Strength + Brawl + Prowess). +2 superficial damage, or lethal against mortals (Lethal Body). With iron bar 8 (Strength + Melee), +2 damage.

Defense 8 (Dexterity + Athletics; 9 with Dexterity + Brawl). Editor's Note: doc 14 said 7. Initiative 7. Stealth 8. Escape 8, plus Blink.

Key combat powers: Prowess (+4 damage for one scene, costs Hunger), Blink (moves up to 50 meters in one turn), Soaring Leap (reaches rooftops), Daunt (mortals back away).

The inverted guard: against David or anyone with @UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.oGnroV6R68YdMQyD]{LOR-01 · The Doctrine of Controlled Fury} at level 4 or higher, −2 dice to melee defense.

Tactics: he strikes first, always in the same sequence (ribs, sternum, throat). If the fight lasts more than three turns, he leaves. He doesn't fight David head-on if he can avoid it. He doesn't kill mortals unless he has to. If he drops to half his Health, he flees toward the water.

Demeanor

Slim, medium height, black hair parted on the side, and tired brown eyes; a classic dark suit, white shirt, and thin tie.

Charles Halloway · Combat Version

Full profile in Chapter 4.

Health 6 · Willpower 8 · Usual Hunger 1 · Blood Potency 3

Halloway doesn't fight. His defense pool is 6 (Dexterity + Wits) and he never attacks in person.

Dread Gaze (Presence 3): Charisma + Intimidation (6 dice) vs. Composure + Resolve. Whoever fails flees or freezes for one scene.

Dominate: Manipulation + Dominate (9 dice). He uses Compel (“Stop,” “Drop that”) and Forgetful Mind on mortal witnesses.

Fortitude 2: reduces superficial damage taken by 2.

Tactics: surround himself with ghouls (Dawson and @UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{Halloway's Security Ghouls}), use Dread Gaze on the most dangerous opponent, and flee. On the ferry, toward the bridge. In the tower, toward the private elevator. If he's cornered with no way out, he negotiates: he offers everything.

@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr.JournalEntryPage.nyaVnQSG4rVgzoFI]{Last Bastion of the Masquerade}

Source: doc 17. Last Bastion of the Masquerade (Fortitude ••••). Homebrew – optional amalgam with Presence or Auspex, if you want to fine-tune it further.

“I don't go down until the job is done.”

Theme / fiction. When David marks someone as an enemy of the Masquerade, his body and his will refuse to fall. Broken bones, bullets, fire… all of it held together by sheer refusal. It isn't blind Brujah fury: it's the brutal calm of the executioner who won't let himself die until he's finished off the condemned.

Mechanical Version (V5-Friendly)

Requirements

  • Fortitude 4
  • Humanity 6+ (or at least 1 Conviction tied to “protecting the Masquerade / the balance”)
  • Optional as an amalgam: Presence 2 or Auspex 2 (Presence if you want it more “imposing,” Auspex if you see it as an almost mystical focus on his mission).

Cost

  • 1 Rouse Check on activation.
  • Can only be used once per scene, and once per night for its big effect.

Activation. You must declare a target a “Veil-breaker”:

  • It must be someone who, in David's judgment (and the Storyteller's), is actively endangering the Masquerade:
    • a Kindred using Disciplines in front of mortals,
    • a Sabbat carrying out massacres,
    • a Cainite about to reveal the existence of vampires, etc.
  • Quick action: David locks his gaze / pronounces the “sentence” (a whisper, a stony line, whatever you like) and activates the power.

As long as this sentenced target remains present in the scene (or David is pursuing them directly), the power is active.

Effects

1. I Won't Fall Yet. As long as the sentenced target remains in the scene or in direct pursuit:

  • If David would be Incapacitated by damage (superficial or aggravated) on a damage roll:
    • Instead of falling, he's left at 1 superficial Health level.
    • He automatically gains the Dazed / Staggered condition (the Storyteller can impose -2 on complex physical actions, no multiple actions, etc.).
    • This effect can only happen once per scene and per night.

In short: 👉 The first time someone “would drop him” while he's executing an enemy of the Masquerade… he doesn't fall. He stays on his feet at 1 Health.

2. Executioner's Flesh. As long as the sentenced target remains present:

  • David gains +Fortitude (4) dice on tests to:
    • Resist frenzy from damage or provocation by the target.
    • Resist Dominate / Presence / Auspex from the target (or from their direct allies in the scene, at the Storyteller's discretion).
  • He also ignores wound penalties (as if Deny Pain were “boosted”) against that specific target.
  • Outside that hunt, Deny Pain works normally.

Narrative effect: 👉 While he's hunting a real danger to the Masquerade, he doesn't break, doesn't flee, and doesn't bend mentally at that enemy's hands.

3. Moral Limit. Because otherwise it gets out of hand:

  • If the Storyteller decides David has activated it against someone who isn't really a threat to the Masquerade, or out of pure personal grudge:
    • The power works the same, but at the end of the night David breaks (see “When He Breaks”): he twisted his Conviction and used “the Masquerade” as an excuse to kill.
    • If a PC saw it, they decide whether to tell him.

This nails it to the concept of an enforcer with a code, not a thug justifying himself.

Is It Broken or Reasonable?

If you compare it with the official Fortitude 4 powers:

  • Draught of Endurance: gives Fortitude and powers to another Kindred for one night.
  • Gorgon Scales: gives brutal defenses, but very situational and tied to Resonance.

Last Bastion of the Masquerade:

  • It's very strong, but:
    • It only works in scenes where there's a real threat to the Masquerade.
    • The “I don't go down” is once per night, and it leaves you wrecked.
    • It doesn't increase damage or give super attacks; it only keeps David on his feet to finish the job.
    • It has a moral cost if abused.

At the table it's a power that:

  • Reinforces his role as “the Black Dog of the Masquerade.”
  • Delivers a very cinematic moment: the blow that should put him on the ground… and he gets up at 1 Health with his jaw broken and his gaze fixed.
  • Doesn't unbalance things as much as a constant brute-force damage-reduction buff against anything and everyone.

Simpler / Quicker Version

If you'd rather have something even easier to use, the same concept can be boiled down to:

Lite Version:

  • Cost: 1 Rouse Check.
  • Effect: Once per night, when you take damage that would leave you Incapacitated while fighting someone who is endangering the Masquerade, you stay at 1 Health instead of falling.
  • Extra: +2 dice to resist frenzy and mental Disciplines from that enemy until the end of the scene.

Hears breathing, footsteps, pulses of vitae.

Auspex 1. Power from the V5 core rulebook.

Brief visions of immediate danger; ideal for anticipating attacks or ambushes.

Auspex 2. Power from the V5 core rulebook.

Hunters@UUID[JournalEntry.bJA2iRyDgbm2TcuK]{Dana Okafor}, @UUID[JournalEntry.D611Mcr17F6HHEUw]{Sasha Hale}, @UUID[Actor.5ywnpdrw93wmy235]{Cole Ransom}, @UUID[Actor.cacjzuu13Bv7mJH5]{Teresa “Tess” Navarro}, @UUID[Actor.yyJApTmnANPPdw3O]{Owen Pak}, @UUID[Actor.2hdWrhkD65ZNl4Xs]{Lena Sorensen}

A small cell, with a tight budget and a clear order: confirm whether Seattle has “an organized structure” and, if it does, don't touch it until it can be torn out by the roots. Special Agent Dana Okafor runs it from an eleventh-floor office in South Lake Union. It has one analyst who doesn't sleep, two more analysts, six operators contracted as a counterterrorism unit, and a liaison with the FBI's Seattle field office.
system.privatenotes:
Starting Desperation 1: a single cell, a budget that doesn't stretch far enough, and a source nobody trusts. Starting Danger 0: the quarry doesn't know the Cell exists. See @UUID[JournalEntry.dnsWkdXVJ19riBLa.JournalEntryPage.O8yPSIYLlTrKHm8G]{The Puget Cell} for how they rise and fall during the adventure.

Proposed (not in the docs)

  • Starting Desperation 1 and starting Danger 0 (maximum 5), and the rules for moving them during the adventure (page CEL-01).
  • The motto sums up the order doc 14 gives Okafor.

text.content:
Sheet: @UUID[Actor.NDI68PA4J59Be6ts]{Abel Thornquist}

“Everything's for sale down below. The only thing that changes is who pays.”

Clan: Nosferatu · Position: Primogen · Sect: Camarilla

pages.name: Mortal Days: The Carpenter of the New City

text.content: Abel Thornquist arrived from Sweden in 1887 with a toolbox and nothing else. Two years later the city burned, and the rebuilding meant work for everyone. He built the timber structures that held the new streets up over the old ones. He was among the first to go down into the basements left underneath. In the winter of 1890 a section collapsed in Pioneer Square, and he was trapped for three days in the dark, with a broken leg and the water rising.

He was found by a Nosferatu who had lived down there since before the fire, an old woman the Underground still calls “the Mother.” She gave him a choice: drown or stay. He chose to stay, and he stayed for more than a century. When the Mother fell into torpor in the '40s, Thornquist inherited the Sealed Underground and everything that moved through it: secrets, favors, contraband, people.

He isn't cruel, but he isn't kind either. He's a merchant. He has sold information to every Prince the city has had and to their enemies. He protects the thin-bloods on the docks because they bring him news from the surface, and he charges for that protection in favors. He Embraced Ezra Lund (@UUID[JournalEntry.PBJeE9T9n0BjB6ag]{Ezra “Static” Lund}) in 2019 because he understood before anyone else that the underground of the twenty-first century is made of cables, not stone.

The auction of the File. Thornquist already has two partial copies of the File, bought from Jun Takeda without her knowing what she was carrying. He is quietly organizing an auction in the Undermarket. He doesn't know that Krell is destroying the buyers.

The most expensive vote. He knows Halloway is going to bring a motion against the Prince. He's waiting for offers from both sides.

The firmware. He suspects Ezra wrote the Gale Sentinel code. He hasn't told him. He's waiting until it's worth more.

The Sealed Underground, beneath Pioneer Square (@UUID[JournalEntry.jg1zpvYlDFMJRY8Q]{The Sealed Underground (Seattle Underground)}; Haven 4). He feeds on homeless people who sleep in the lowest entrances to the Underground. In exchange he offers them a dry place, blankets, and the assurance that nobody else will bother them. Most of them don't remember the feeding part. The ones who do keep coming back.

The Undermarket (Influence 3 in the Underground): a network of vendors, runners, and watchers.

The thin-bloods (Allies 2): a dozen young people who gather information on the surface.

Contacts 4: cops, doormen, night janitorial staff, and maintenance techs all over the city.

Ezra Lund: his childe and his best investment.

@UUID[JournalEntry.PBJeE9T9n0BjB6ag]{Ezra Lund} (pride). The only Kindred he doesn't charge. Ezra doesn't know that yet.

@UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Charles Halloway} (calculation). Good client, bad partner. He has sold him information for forty years.

@UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Ethan Montgomery} (respect). The only one who never tried to haggle with him.

@UUID[JournalEntry.BRQMU0Tf8VSNaZ5o]{Jun Takeda} (guilt). He hired her for deliveries without telling her what she was carrying. If Krell kills her, it'll be partly his fault.

@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith} (caution). He sells him information on Kindred who are out of control. He knows that if the Hound ever decides the problem is him, there won't be enough tunnel in the world.

• “The Mother Below is still alive in some corner of the Sealed Underground, and Thornquist feeds her.” (True: she's in torpor, and he brings her blood once a year.)
  • “Thornquist has a copy of the File.” (True: two partial copies.)
  • “Thornquist can see through any camera in the city.” (False: the one who could is Ezra.)
  • “Thornquist sold out O'Connor in '78.” (False, though he did sell Halloway the photographer's name.)

He has no mortal Mask (Mask 0). He's huge and stooped. His skin looks like wet wood, gray and cracked; his jaw is twisted from the 1890 fall, and his fingers are long as roots. He wears a three-piece suit from the '20s, patched a thousand times, and a pocket watch that doesn't work. He speaks with a Swedish accent, quietly, as if every word cost money. He always carries a carbide lamp, though he doesn't need one.

• Sire: “the Mother Below”
  • Embraced: 1890 (born 1863)
  • Ambition: that no one can rule Seattle without going through the Underground.
  • Convictions: “A deal is a deal” · “What's buried isn't lost.”
  • Touchstone: Dee Watkins, a worker at a Pioneer Square shelter, who leaves the back door open for “the ones from below” and never asks questions.
  • Humanity: 6
  • Generation: 9th
  • Blood Potency: 4

Secondary Attributes: Health 7 · Willpower 7

Skills: Craft 3 (Carpentry), Streetwise 4 (Black Market), Awareness 3, Finance 3 (Favors), Intimidation 3, Investigation 3, Brawl 3, Insight 4 (Lies), Persuasion 3 (Haggling), Stealth 4 (Tunnels), Subterfuge 3

  • Animalism 2: Sense the Beast (Sense the Beast), Feral Whispers (Feral Whispers; rats)

Background figure (no actor sheet) · Boston Ventrue · Prince of Seattle from 1897 to 1962 · sire of @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Charles Halloway}.

This page gathers what docs 00–16 say about Grange. The source doc for each fact is in parentheses.

• “Prince Adelaide Grange, a Boston Ventrue, ruled from 1897 with an accountant's hand” over the city's first Camarilla, small and harbor-bound (doc 05, history; timeline: “1897 · Adelaide Grange (Ventrue), Prince”).
  • In 1931 she named @UUID[JournalEntry.oQ2AhEeDkwdPRv71]{Liam O'Connor} Sheriff, “because nobody knew the port better than he did” (doc 05), “and because that kept him on her side” (doc 07, O'Connor's profile). O'Connor survived her fall and served Whitmore for sixteen more years (doc 07).
  • In 1958 she Embraced Charles Halloway for his press contacts (doc 06, Halloway's profile: “Sire: Adelaide Grange (PNJ-22) · Embraced: 1958”).
  • In the spring of 1962, the year of the World's Fair, she “left the city ‘for health reasons’ and was never seen again” (doc 05). @UUID[JournalEntry.sCVTjJFrnyyVnQDt]{Marcus Whitmore} took the throne. “Whitmore understood something Grange never saw: in a city that looks forward, power isn't imposed, it's displayed” (doc 05).
  • ID registry: “PNJ-22 · Adelaide Grange, former Ventrue Prince, vanished in 1962 (background)” (doc 05); “PNJ-22 · Adelaide Grange, Halloway's sire, driven out by Whitmore in 1962” (doc 06).

• Whitmore gathered evidence of a Masquerade breach by Grange, “some real and some exaggerated,” and showed it to her in private. She left the city without a fight. It was a clean coup, without bloodshed (doc 06, Whitmore's profile). His strategy with Halloway is the same one he used with Grange: wait for him to overreach (doc 06).
  • Halloway saw it up close: his sire “had been defeated without a drop of blood,” and the method worked. In 1978 he used it against O'Connor (doc 06, Halloway's profile).

• Whitmore (unease): “He never knew whether she left or whether others made her disappear. He prefers not to know” (doc 06).
  • Halloway: “Halloway knows where Grange is.” (False. He'd give anything to know) (doc 06).

• “Whitmore ran Grange out with blackmail.” (True) (doc 06).
  • “Halloway is the childe of former Prince Grange.” (True. Few people remember) (doc 06).

• In @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}, if the coterie defends the Prince well, Whitmore tells Halloway: “Charles. Sixty-four years ago I watched your sire make the same mistake. She believed a good story was the same thing as the truth” (doc 13). Halloway's sire is Grange (doc 06).
  • In @UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO.JournalEntryPage.RqeQkW5KfFjPYFhg]{FIN-B · The Hound Changes Masters}, Whitmore abdicates “‘for health reasons,’ like Grange in 1962, and vanishes from the city” (doc 13).

Background figure (no actor sheet) · Camarilla Archon in the service of Justicar @UUID[JournalEntry.gSMgBLLYggWyAN2W]{Helena Panhard} · Role in @UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File}: waits on Bainbridge for the briefcase holding the File if @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway} wins the Council (@UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.tG1m5PTkmBA1pvmc]{A4-E03 · The Last Ferry}); lead figure of @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.MbCyCqKpBUEan9GR]{GAN-07 · The Archon Calls}.

This page gathers what docs 00–16 say about Duval. The source doc for each fact is given in parentheses. The docs give him no first name, clan, or stats.

• He appears as a background figure, like Justicar Panhard and @UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Vance} (doc 01, NPC index; ID registry v2: “PNJ-07 · Archon Duval (background)”).
  • He knew Vance (doc 09, @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.MbCyCqKpBUEan9GR]{GAN-07 · The Archon Calls}).
  • He serves as Justicar Panhard's envoy (doc 13, @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.tG1m5PTkmBA1pvmc]{A4-E03 · The Last Ferry} and ID registry: “Archon Duval appears on Bainbridge as the Justicar's envoy”).

• Night 8. If Halloway wins the Council (@UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}), at 12:30 a.m. Mr. Pell (@UUID[Actor.eRE6FTNdGO76lzPK]{Mr. Pell}) leaves Halloway Tower with the briefcase to hand over the original File “to an envoy of the Justicar on Bainbridge”: it is the proof Panhard asked of him before she will recognize the regency (doc 13, Storyteller Notes for A4-E01). Pell travels with Dawson and two ghouls (@UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{Halloway's Security Ghouls}) and means “to deliver it to Archon Duval, who waits on Bainbridge as the Justicar's envoy, as proof of the ‘crisis’ that justifies the regency” (doc 13, A4-E03).
  • The endings. If the File reaches Duval and Halloway lost or was exposed: @UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO.JournalEntryPage.UnOqmjERvnxNb7gL]{FIN-A · The Truth Before the Throne} (“Duval returns it”). If Halloway won: @UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO.JournalEntryPage.RqeQkW5KfFjPYFhg]{FIN-B · The Hound Changes Masters}. If Halloway won but the coterie kept the File: partial FIN-B, because Halloway has no proof to show the Justicar (doc 13, endings table). The briefcase ending up “in Duval's hands” is one of the four possible endings (doc 13, Notes for A4-E03).

pages.name: Chronicle Hook: GAN-07 · The Archon Calls

text.content:
• Doc 01: “Duval asks a favor that forces David to leave the city.”
  • Doc 09: Mr. Pell typed three copies of Vance's journals. Halloway sent copy 3 to Justicar Panhard in 2025 as a goodwill gift. Duval, who knew Vance, has read it and wants to talk to @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David}. He asks him to travel to Marseille. It isn't an order. Not yet.
    • Before answering, David tells the coterie. What they say carries weight, and if they go with him, the trip becomes a coterie story.
    • David goes: Duval shows him copy 3, which has folios that aren't in the other two, including the ones about Krell. David earns an Archon's favor (temporary Mawla 2), but he is away from Seattle for one story. If he goes alone, the coterie plays that story without him and without his +1 die. Proposed: the PC who went with him to Marseille shares Duval's favor (temporary Mawla 2).
    • David refuses: Duval doesn't press, but he takes note. Next time it will be an order.
    • Panhard takes an interest in Seattle: if the ending was FIN-B, the Justicar sends Duval to the city to investigate. He arrives with one question: who is Prince now?

pages.name: Mortal Days: The Legionnaire of the Docks

text.content: August Krell was born in Hamburg in 1944, between bombing raids, and grew up in the port of Marseille, where his mother took him fleeing from everything. At seventeen he enlisted in the Foreign Legion under a false name and reached Algeria for the last year of the war. He came back with a medal he never wore and a strange calm about violence: he didn't enjoy hurting people, but it didn't cost him anything either. After that he worked as a longshoreman, as muscle for smugglers, and as whatever the docks needed.

In 1972, Marcus Vance (@UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Marcus “Ironjaw” Vance}) watched him fight three men armed with iron bars in a dockside warehouse, and win. He Embraced him that same night. Krell is Vance's childe, like David. Nobody in Seattle knows, not even David.

Vance trained him for four years with the same doctrine, the same discipline, and the cold water. But in 1976 he decided Krell wasn't fit: the Beast asked him for permission too often, and he gave it too gladly. Vance taught him the inverted guard, the one given to those who don't finish (@UUID[JournalEntry.kzeWNRBY6tgLP37S]{Journal of M. Vance, Marseille, 1963, Folio 14 (Typewritten Copy)}), and left without saying goodbye.

Krell spent fifty years as a mercenary. He worked for Archons, for the Sabbat, for whoever paid. He killed a lot, and he killed well. He never stopped wondering what he'd done wrong. In early 2026, Mr. Pell, Halloway's archivist, found him in Lisbon: Vance's journals mention “the German” three times. Halloway offered him Vance's coat, which came in the same auction lot, a domain in Seattle, and, above all, the journal folios where Vance writes about him. Krell said yes before he finished the sentence.

Clean up the copies. He destroys the Kindred who buy or transport copies of the File, using Controlled Fury so it looks like Vance's work (@UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.DtetdHiBnOLQaM6Y]{A1-E02 · Ash on Pier 46}, @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.j4TnqYOwVuSCeQ0z]{A2-E02 · “Locate. Evaluate. Execute.”}). Jun Takeda is his next target (Night 4).

Make his brother see him. He doesn't want to beat David; he wants David to acknowledge him. In @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.7brn5AgmWggUl420]{A3-E01 · The Other Son} he goes after one of the coterie's Touchstones to force David to look him in the face. In @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell} he offers to talk. He demands David; the coterie decides whether to bring him and how. Krell only looks at David: the PCs talk and David confirms.

The folios. Halloway promised him the journal pages that talk about him and still hasn't handed them over. Krell is starting to suspect they don't exist, or that they say something Halloway doesn't want him to read. If the coterie shows him those folios, he switches sides (@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.jXff6tMXQQbmJg0m]{Krell's Testimony}). If he also learns the other guard, he can become Allies 2 for the coterie.

The promised domain. Halloway promised him Harbor Island, David's domain. Krell hasn't yet asked himself how Halloway plans to keep that promise.

A rusted barge in dry dock in Georgetown, south of the port, which Halloway rents him through a shell company (Haven 1). He sleeps in the hold, in a toolbox the size of a coffin. He feeds on night-shift longshoremen and truckers. He finds them alone, hits them once, hard, and drinks fast. He doesn't kill anyone unless he has to. He finds it unprofessional.

Vance's coat: a long gray wool coat, tailored for a man broader in the shoulders. It's too big for him. It's “the coat that isn't his” from @UUID[JournalEntry.BxMkvzNl7Yt8OyTI]{r/SeattleAfterDark: “Anyone Else See This on Harbor Island?”} and @UUID[JournalEntry.FVBnf3yE87K4BOhh]{Wendell Fry: “Song for the Son of the Fist”}.

Copy 2 of 3 of Vance's journals (@UUID[JournalEntry.kzeWNRBY6tgLP37S]{Journal of M. Vance, Marseille, 1963, Folio 14 (Typewritten Copy)}), with his pencil notes.

Halloway's support: an electric car with no registered plates, and two security ghouls (@UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{Halloway's Security Ghouls}) if he asks for them.

Resources 1: what Halloway pays him.

Marcus Vance (wounded love). He hates him and needs him. He believes Vance is dead and isn't sure that changes anything.

David Smith (envy). The one who finished. The one who got the other guard. The good son.

Charles Halloway (distrust). He knows he's being used. He doesn't care, as long as Halloway gives him the folios.

Hal Brekke (respect). He watches Hal track from a distance, and Hal reminds him of the good legionnaires.

Rosa Iturbe (indifference). He knows Halloway is using her as a scapegoat. It's none of his business.

• “Vance came back and he's cleaning up the city.” (False. It's Krell.)
  • “The dock killer fights with his left side forward.” (True: it's the inverted guard, @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.HYE4rNbNf1sEbYGe]{The Inverted Guard}.)
  • “The killer works for the Everett Anarchs.” (False. Halloway is running him.)
  • “There's an old Brujah sleeping on a barge in Georgetown.” (True. The Nosferatu know, and they sell it dear.)

He has no Mask (Mask 0); he uses forged papers from a Portuguese passport. He looks about twenty-eight, but he moves like someone older. His head is shaved, an old knife scar cuts across his left eyebrow, his broken nose healed badly, and his hands are full of broken knuckles. He wears dark work clothes under Vance's coat. He's left-handed. He says little, with a French accent, and when he's serious he drops his voice so low you have to lean in. He smells of wet wool.

Editor's Note

Doc 07 said “looks about thirty-five”; it was decided that he looks the age he was at his Embrace (1972, born in 1944): about twenty-eight.

• Sire: Marcus “Ironjaw” Vance (@UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Marcus “Ironjaw” Vance})
  • Embraced: 1972 (born in 1944)
  • Ambition: for someone to acknowledge that he was Vance's son too.
  • Convictions: “A job gets finished” · “Never hit someone who can't hit back.”
  • Touchstone: none living. The last was his mother, who died in 1981. Krell has lost a great deal of Humanity since then.
  • Humanity: 4
  • Generation: 9th
  • Blood Potency: 3

Attributes: Strength 5, Dexterity 4, Stamina 4 · Charisma 2, Manipulation 2, Composure 3 · Intelligence 2, Wits 4, Resolve 3

Secondary Attributes: Health 7 · Willpower 6

Skills: Firearms 3, Athletics 4, Streetwise 2 (Docks), Awareness 3, Intimidation 4 (Silence), Brawl 5 (Incomplete Controlled Fury), Melee 3 (Bars and knives), Stealth 4, Survival 2

Disciplines:

  • Potence 4: Lethal Body (Lethal Body), Soaring Leap (Soaring Leap), Prowess (Prowess), Draught of Might (Draught of Might)
  • Celerity 3: Cat's Grace (Cat's Grace), Fleetness (Fleetness), Blink (Blink)
  • Presence 2: Daunt (Daunt), Lingering Kiss (Lingering Kiss)

The inverted guard (special rule): against an opponent who knows the complete doctrine of Controlled Fury (any PC with @UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.oGnroV6R68YdMQyD]{LOR-01 · The Doctrine of Controlled Fury} at level 4 or higher), Krell loses 2 dice from all his close-combat defense pools. David knows it too, but he doesn't roll: the Storyteller narrates what he does, and Krell loses those 2 dice against the PC who attacks alongside David. Krell knows this, and that's why he avoids fighting David head-on if he can.

Editor's Note · LOR-01 Level and Disciplines

The chapter 4 sheet (doc 07) called for LOR-01 at level 3 or higher. Chapter 7 (doc 10) and the combat version in chapter 8 (doc 14) call for level 4 or higher, which is the level of “The Complete Guard” on the Loresheet (doc 08). The newest doc wins: level 4.

Doc 07 gave him five powers at Potence 4 and four at Celerity 3; in V5 there's one per dot. Spark of Rage (Spark of Rage) was removed, since it's an amalgam that requires Presence 3 and Krell has Presence 2, and so was Rapid Reflexes (Rapid Reflexes). In Celerity, Blink is the only one named by the scenes and the combat version; of the other three, Cat's Grace and Fleetness fit his rooftop escapes, and Rapid Reflexes is the one he uses least.

Quick pools: Unarmed attack 10 (Strength + Brawl, plus Prowess) · Initiative and defense 7 · Stealth 8

pages.name: 0 · Opening Fiction—“What the Water Won't Take”

text.content: A 2,000–2,500-word story. It is the night of the theft seen through the eyes of Helen Ward (@UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen Ward}): the podcast, the rain in Ballard, the flip phone with a single number, and someone who is already inside the apartment. It ends when Helen dials SAFE. David appears only as a voice on the phone.

Sheet: @UUID[Actor.zFbC97X8iaeScDzY]{Celeste Arden}

Concept: investment analyst and childe of Charles Halloway, the Ventrue Primogen.

Celeste grew up in Bellevue, in a lake-view house that her father, a real estate developer, lost in 2008 along with everything else. She was nineteen, and she watched the money disappear first and the friends after. She swore she would never again be on the wrong side of a spreadsheet. She studied quantitative finance, landed at a small fund, and by twenty-six she was spotting companies about to collapse before anyone else. That caught Halloway's attention.

Halloway Embraced her in 2011 and offered her what she wanted most: never to lose again. Today she runs Halloway Meridian Capital's network of shell companies. She knows her sire is ambitious. She feeds only on people who have just been ruined: the Blood of someone who has lost everything is the only kind that works for her, and it always reminds her of her father.
Her folder in the File is a photo of her at the scene of a suicide in a Bellevue parking garage. She was there to feed, not to kill, but the photo doesn't prove it.

Ambition: to make her name worth more than her sire's. Desire: for Halloway to recognize her as his equal. Suggested Conviction: “Never let anyone fall alone.” Touchstone: her mother, who lives in a memory care facility with dementia and still calls her by her name.
Resources 3, Contacts (finance) 2, Influence (Eastside) 1, Mawla (Halloway) 2. Flaw: a level 2 Blood Bond to Halloway.

@UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.uL8F2YNogcToiFc6]{A2-E01 · Elysium Night}, @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center}, @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell} (@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.jqTQDyJH3ogdAuWO]{The Folios on the German} comes out of her sire's house), and @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}.

She doesn't know that among Halloway's companies is the one that controls Gale Sentinel. Halloway chose her as his scapegoat. The fragments leaked to FIRSTLIGHT go out through accounts in her companies' names. At the Council (@UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}), he will offer her up as the traitor. Celeste will have to choose between her sire, the coterie, and the truth.

pages.name: What the Water Doesn't Wash Away

text.content:
At 2:40 a.m., Helen Ward had been listening to the same sentence for three hours.

A sixty-one-year-old woman said it in a kitchen in Lake City, with the TV on in the background and a dog that barked every time a car went by on the street. “My son didn't do drugs. My son was afraid of needles.” On the recording she said it twice, and both times her voice cracked on the same syllable, the “-fraid” in afraid. Helen had cut the first one and kept the second. Then she'd put the first one back and taken out the second, because the second sounded rehearsed and the first didn't, and on a podcast like hers people could smell rehearsed before the sentence was over.

Outside it was raining the way it rains in Ballard in November, halfhearted and without letup. It was a fine rain that didn't soak you all at once but didn't go away either, and it left the whole neighborhood with the tired shine of a badly dried plate. The apartment was on the third floor, above a hardware store on Market Street that closed at six. It had two rooms and a window onto the fire escape, where Helen smoked even though the lease prohibited it. The walls of the room she called the studio were covered in printed maps of the city. There were red pins for the deaths, blue for the disappearances, and a few yellow ones she didn't know how to classify.

Nadia had sent her the mix for episode 113 at midnight, with an eleven-second voice memo: “It's good. Cut the dog. And get some sleep, Helen, seriously.” Helen hadn't cut the dog. She liked the dog. The dog was proof that the kitchen existed, that the woman wasn't an actress, and that the son had lived in a house with noise, with an animal that waited for him, with someone who knew he was afraid of needles.

He was the third in eighteen months. Three young men from Ballard and Crown Hill, dead of overdoses according to the county report, no history, no old track marks, and all three with less blood than they should have had. That last part wasn't in any report. Helen knew because an assistant at the medical examiner's office, who had owed her a favor for years, had told her in a parking lot, looking the other way: “It's not that they were dry. It's that some was missing. Like somebody had helped themselves to a share.”

On the desk, plugged into the laptop by a cable already fraying at the end, was the drive. It was a black box, matte, the size of a paperback, with a strip of painter's tape on top where she'd written DO NOT TOUCH in marker. A second copy waited in a shoebox at the back of the closet, and a third lived in the cloud, in a folder with a deliberately boring name. Ten years of notes, audio, photos, clippings, screenshots of deleted threads, maps with dates. In her head she called it the basement, because that was where she went down when she didn't want to think about what was upstairs.

Inside the basement there was a folder with no name. Helen opened it rarely and always alone, with the door closed even though she lived alone. It held fourteen photos. The first was from 2014, from the Larchmont Building fire in Tacoma: a man with his back to the flames, in a dark jacket, looking toward a neighbor's camera as if he knew exactly where it was. The last was from 2025, from the docks on Harbor Island: the same man under a streetlight. He had the same jacket, or one just like it, and the same scar running down from his right cheekbone to the edge of his lip. It was the same face. Eleven years had passed and he hadn't gained a single line.

She was thirty-four and already finding gray hairs in the bathroom mirror.

The right-hand desk drawer held a flip phone, the kind nobody makes anymore, with a single number in the contacts. SAFE. No last name, no photo, no recognizable area code. That man had left it with her on a street by the port, the night she got to a scene too early and he was there, cleaning up, calm as someone sweeping his own kitchen. He'd said her name without her giving it. He'd quoted an article of hers that the paper pulled from its website six hours after publishing it. And he'd told her something Helen remembered word for word, because she repeated it to herself when she couldn't sleep: “Keep looking. But when something's too big for you, you call this number first. Not the police. Not your podcast. Me.”

She'd never used it. She charged it every Sunday anyway, the way you'd change the water in an empty vase.

At 2:50 she ran out of cigarettes.

She sat looking at the empty pack for a while, as if it might refill itself. The gas station on 15th Avenue was four blocks away and open all night. She put on her hoodie, stuck her keys and a few bills in the pocket, and left the laptop open with the Lake City woman's sentence paused halfway through the word afraid.

Stepping into the hallway, she noticed the doorbell. In the spring the landlord had installed doorbell cameras on every door in the building, all the same brand, Gale Sentinel, free with a subscription the tenants paid for without realizing it as part of the rent. Each one had a little blue light that stayed on all night, and Helen had gotten so used to it she didn't see it anymore. That night she saw it because it wasn't there: the one on her door was off, and so was the one on 3B, across the hall. She filed it in the same place in her head where she filed the things that mean nothing until they mean something. Lights off, 2:52. And she went down.

The street was empty and shining. A 44 bus went by with its interior lights on and nobody in the seats. From the corner she could see, in the distance, the outline of the cranes along the canal, their little red lights blinking for planes that never came. At the gas station, a kid with earbuds rang her up without looking up. Helen paid cash, as always. Her father, who'd been a patrol cop in Tacoma for twenty-two years, used to say that everything you pay for with a card, somebody writes down, and the people who write things down aren't always who you think.

She got back at 3:04.

She knew something was wrong before she understood what. She climbed the stairs with the new pack in her hand, and the door to her apartment was closed, the way she'd left it, but the handle sat a little higher than it should. Helen always locked it with two turns, and with two turns the handle stayed drooping. That night it was level. Someone had opened it and locked it again with only one.

And there was a smell in the hallway. Wet wool, first, like a coat that never dried right. Underneath, something metallic and sweetish, like the smell left on your hand after you've squeezed a fistful of coins for a long time.

Helen froze on the top step. From inside came a sound she knew better than her own voice: the squeal of the studio closet door, which stuck halfway and had to be lifted a little to open the rest of the way. Someone was lifting it. Nobody was talking. There were no hurried footsteps, no drawers dumped on the floor. It was the sound of someone working.

Her body decided before she did. She backed up the stairs, toward the landing by the roof door, slowly, pressed to the wall, and crouched in the dark behind the railing, where the hallway light didn't reach. Her cell phone was in her pocket. She took it out and looked at it and put it back. She could call 911, and they'd ask her what she was seeing, and she'd have to say she wasn't seeing anything, that there was a smell of coins and a door that squeaked. And tomorrow there'd be a report with her name on it, and a month from now the report would be gone, the way every report that touched what she touched disappeared.

She counted. She was at a hundred and eighty when the door opened.

There were two of them. They wore dark clothes with no logos, gloves, caps, and one carried a gray bag, the kind delivery drivers use. They moved like people who'd done this many times, without a word, without looking at each other. The one with the bag closed the door carefully, almost tenderly. The other one stayed in the hallway for a second, and Helen stopped breathing, because the man lifted his head toward the stairs, toward the landing where she was, and drew a breath through his nose. It wasn't the gesture of someone smelling something odd. It was long and attentive, like a dog working a scent.

The one with the bag touched his shoulder. One touch, two fingers. Time. The two of them went down.

From the street there was no sound of an engine starting. There was a low electric hum that moved off to the west and was lost in the rain.

Helen waited nine more minutes, counting, before she went down.

The apartment was almost untouched. That was the worst part. The TV was still in its place, and so were the bills in the kitchen jar, and in the studio the laptop was still open with the Lake City woman's sentence on pause. The maps on the walls were intact, not a pin out of place. The frayed cable hung from the desk, plugged into nothing. The shoebox was gone from the closet. Helen sat down at the laptop, opened the cloud folder with the boring name, and the screen answered her in polite gray letters: This folder is empty. It was last modified at 3:01.

They hadn't taken anything worth money. They'd taken the memory.

She sat on the floor for a while, her back against the wall of maps. She thought about Danny Ruiz, who used to lend her his Media Law notes in college and laughed at her because she highlighted in three colors. Danny had lived on the fourth floor of the Larchmont Building, in Tacoma, until the night in 2014 when the building burned and seven tenants were “unaccounted for.” There were no bodies. There was an article, hers, that the paper paid to kill. And there was a photo of a man with his back to the fire, looking at the camera.

She opened the right-hand drawer.

The flip phone had a charge. Of course it did. She flipped it open, found the only entry in the contacts, and pressed the green button, and she only realized her hand was shaking when the phone knocked against her ear.

It rang once. Then, silence. Not the silence of a dead line: the silence of someone listening. In the background there was something that could have been rain on sheet metal, or the sea.

“Helen.”

It wasn't a question. The voice was deep and low, unhurried, as if he'd been expecting her.

“They took the basement,” she said, and as soon as she said it she knew he couldn't know what the basement was, and she knew too that he wasn't going to ask.

“Are you hurt?”

“No.”

“Are they still there?”

“No. There were two. They left ten minutes ago, in an electric car. They took the drive and the copy in the closet. And they wiped the cloud, at three-oh-one. They had my password or they didn't need it. One of them...” She stopped. “One of them was smelling the stairwell. Like a dog.”

There was a pause. It was short, but Helen had spent ten years listening to pauses for a living, and she recognized this one. It was the pause of someone who has just heard something he didn't want to hear.

“Don't touch anything,” he said. “Don't call anyone. Don't use the other phone.”

“How do you know I have another...?”

“Fifteen minutes.”

“Wait.” She pressed the phone against her face. “At least tell me who you are. Eleven years. I've got your face from 2014 and I've got your face from last year and it's the same. Tell me what you are.”

This time the silence was long. Helen heard the rain on her end and the rain, or the sea, on the other.

“Someone who usually gets there too late,” the voice said. “Not this time.”

And he hung up.

Helen snapped the flip phone shut and sat there holding it. Then she got up, went to the door, and looked through the peephole. The hallway was empty and yellow. Across from her door, on the doorbell of 3B, the camera's little blue light had come back on. It shone steady, calm, looking toward her.

She pulled up her hood, sat down on the floor facing the door, and started counting.

Her father used to say that in this city the rain washes everything away. Helen had spent ten years proving it wasn't true, and someone had just sent her the bill.

The story takes place right before @UUID[JournalEntry.w9xeQJg6psfiMjFU.JournalEntryPage.yyXMKcpDOIhGuZIB]{A0-E01 · The Call from SAFE}. The call to SAFE is what kicks off the adventure. After hanging up, David summons the coterie.

The thieves are the @UUID[Actor.9rv5Jdb3y6bZZ1fj]{Lonnie Barras} team, hired by Preston Gale (@UUID[JournalEntry.y8Ao3xEHH3W11EJe]{Preston Gale}). The one who sniffs the stairwell is one of Gale's ghouls (@UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{Halloway's Security Ghouls}). His Vitae is the P-02 trail.

The dark lights on the Gale Sentinel cameras are P-01 and lead to @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.wIpc0OR2nQf7WDFO]{A1-E05 · The City's Eyes}. The one that comes back on at 3B is still streaming: someone saw Helen come back.

David's fourteen photos are part of the File. Each PC has their own folder (@UUID[JournalEntry.vtenvgNlXVPd99Rc]{“Your Folder in the File”}).

Danny Ruiz and the Larchmont (@UUID[JournalEntry.Oiln4o98kvxKbOvS]{The Larchmont Building}, @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.9fTKL8Oeq36BCfU9]{A2-E05 · The Ashes of the Larchmont}): David didn't make it in time. Helen doesn't know that yet.

Nadia appears by name. If nobody plays @UUID[JournalEntry.rg50DlMYSzgbZeBv]{Nadia Ferro}, she's an NPC with the same background.

You can read this story aloud at session zero or hand it out as advance reading.

Seattle is a city that watches itself all the time. It has cameras in its doorbells, phones in every pocket, apps that know what time each neighbor leaves the house, companies that turn that information into money, and agencies that turn it into files. For decades, the Seattle Camarilla survived thanks to three things: the rain, which makes people indifferent; a Toreador Prince who prefers appearances to war; and a Gangrel Sheriff who erases whatever is left over without asking too many questions.

This book describes that city at the moment it stops working. It presents the Kindred who rule it and those who want to rule it, the places where they hunt and deal, the rumors that make the rounds in Elysium, and a complete adventure, The Ward File (@UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File}), in which the characters discover that their existence is recorded on a mortal journalist's hard drive, and that someone stole it to use it.

The book is designed for a coterie of 4 or 5 new characters. Two NPCs go with them: David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}), the Sheriff's Brujah enforcer, and his ghoul, Tom “Bear” Whitman (@UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Tom “Bear” Whitman}). The story revolves around David, but the characters are the ones who live it: they uncover his past, decide what they tell him, and carry whatever that costs.

The Masquerade as Debt

Every secret the Kindred keep is paid for by a mortal: the mother who will never know what her son died of, the journalist whose article got killed, the medical examiner who signs false reports. In this chronicle, protecting the Masquerade has a price, and someone collects it. When the characters make a decision “for the Masquerade,” ask yourself who pays for it, and show it.

Parents and Children in the Blood

Vance and David. David and Bear. Halloway and his childe, Montgomery and his, the Prince and his. And Emily, David's daughter, dead in the '90s. The adventure revolves around what gets inherited: techniques, loyalties, guilt.

August Krell (@UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{August Krell}) exists so David can see what he might have become if Vance hadn't chosen him. And so the coterie has to decide what to do with both of them.

The City That Records Everything

In this Seattle, the predator is also prey. Not prey to hunters with stakes, at least not at first, but to data: a light that goes out on a doorbell, a bill paid by card, an eleven-second video. The Second Inquisition (FIRSTLIGHT) is present throughout the adventure, but almost never in plain sight. It's measured with the Thermometer (@UUID[JournalEntry.b13NIR35K7HpthZv]{FIRSTLIGHT's Thermometer}), which rises with every mistake. Use it to make the players feel the air closing in without anyone firing a shot.

Order Versus Conscience

The characters work, one way or another, for Camarilla law. The adventure asks them what they do when the law is used for something their code won't accept. There's no right answer, and the four possible endings reflect that.

Seattle in Three Senses

To describe the city without repeating yourself, keep these images at hand:

  • Sight: gleaming asphalt, cranes with red lights over the port, office windows lit at three in the morning, the little blue light of a doorbell camera.
  • Sound: rain on sheet metal, the hum of an electric car, the foghorns out on the Sound, the silence of an empty bus.
  • Smell: salt and diesel on the docks, wet wool, burnt coffee, the coppery smell of Vitae.

Term What It Is
Ballard Northwest neighborhood, once a Scandinavian fishing village. Bars, boatyards, new apartments over old shops. Helen lives there.
Harbor Island Artificial industrial island in Elliott Bay. Containers, cranes, and David's hangar.
Pioneer Square The oldest neighborhood. Beneath it lie the buried streets of the 19th century: the Seattle Underground.
Capitol Hill Nightlife, music, clubs. The Toreador Rack.
South Lake Union Glass towers of the tech companies. At night, empty offices with the lights on.
The Eastside Bellevue and Redmond, across Lake Washington. New money and data centers.
The Sound Puget Sound, the arm of the sea that surrounds the city. Ferries, fog, and cold water.
Everett / Tacoma The cities to the north and south. One for the Anarchs, the other for the exiles and what's left of the Sabbat.
FIRSTLIGHT The American branch of the Second Inquisition. In Elysium they say it has an office in Seattle; nobody knows where.
The File Helen Ward's archive. Ten years of deaths that don't add up.
SAFE The only number in Helen's flip phone.

The city doesn't stop when The Ward File ends. These twelve hooks let you continue the chronicle after the adventure, fill the nights between parts, or give each character a story of their own. They're grouped by theme.

Every hook uses the same format: Cast (who appears), What happened (the starting situation), What could happen (two or three outcomes with mechanical consequences), and Emphasis (which kind of Attributes it tests).

Theme: Humanity

Cast: Marcos Delgado (mortal, 45), Hal Brekke (@UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{Halvard “Hal” Brekke}), David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}), analyst S. Hale (@UUID[JournalEntry.D611Mcr17F6HHEUw]{Sasha Hale}).

What happened: in 1996, Marcos was fifteen and in the Rainier Valley apartment the night Ray Dorsey killed Emily Smith. He was the only kid who survived. Before he passed out, he saw a man with a scar on his face shoot Dorsey and kneel beside the social worker. Today Marcos is a youth counselor in the same neighborhood. He's spent thirty years looking for that man to thank him.

Now someone else is looking for him. Analyst Hale, cross-referencing fragments of the File, found the 1996 folder: a juvenile witness who talked about “a man who didn't bleed.” Hale is going to visit Marcos next week.

What could happen:

  • The coterie gets there first and lets David be seen. Marcos recognizes him thirty years later, unchanged. He can become a new Touchstone for David, and the loss of Emily hurts a little less: play him more whole, less alone. But Marcos knows something now, and FIRSTLIGHT is going to ask him about it.
  • Hal wipes the memory. Hal already cleaned up that scene once. He can do it again, this time with Dominate or Presence. The Masquerade is safe, but taking away the one memory that made Marcos who he is costs 1 Stain.
  • Hale gets there first. Marcos tells her everything. FIRSTLIGHT's Thermometer rises by 2, and the Inquisition has a composite sketch of David.

Emphasis: Social.

pages.name: GAN-02 · The Night She Beholds the Beast

text.content:
Theme: Humanity

Cast: Helen Ward (@UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen Ward}), David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}), Nadia Ferro (@UUID[JournalEntry.rg50DlMYSzgbZeBv]{Nadia Ferro}).

What happened: sooner or later, Helen sees David do something no man can do. It can happen during @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.7brn5AgmWggUl420]{A3-E01 · The Other Son}, if Krell goes after her, or on any night afterward: a steel door torn off its hinges, a three-story fall he gets up from, eyes that shine in the dark. She doesn't see everything, but she sees enough.

What could happen:

  • She pulls away. Helen stops answering, moves, turns off the flip phone. She's still alive, but David loses his Touchstone. He's shaken: quieter, harder, closer to the Beast. The coterie notices.
  • She doubles down. She's finally found something real. Helen demands answers and threatens to publish if she doesn't get them. Someone has to negotiate with her: Manipulation + Persuasion (Difficulty 4) to keep her quiet without using Disciplines. If anyone uses Dominate, 1 Stain.
  • She starts investigating who she's been helping. Helen begins cross-referencing the dates of SAFE's messages against her cases and finds the Larchmont. If Nadia feeds her information, the discovery comes sooner. If she gets to the bottom of it, the relationship changes forever (see @UUID[JournalEntry.Oiln4o98kvxKbOvS]{The Larchmont Building}).

Theme: Humanity

Cast: Hal Brekke (@UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{Halvard “Hal” Brekke}) or whichever PC is closest to David, David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}), and someone of the Storyteller's choosing.

What happened: for the past few months, someone has been leaving fresh flowers every Sunday on Emily Smith's grave (@UUID[JournalEntry.uhtM1iF2WrHHlcd8]{Emily Smith's Grave}), wrapped in newspaper. David never leaves flowers. Nobody else should know that grave matters.

Who leaves the flowers? The Storyteller picks one option, depending on where they want to take the chronicle:

  • Marcos Delgado (@UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.pCLncsxglYsxJtbu]{GAN-01 · The Boy Who Survived}). The most human outcome: a link to the past that threatens no one.
  • Rosa Iturbe (@UUID[JournalEntry.WHkwE8CYfaKW5WyO]{Rosa “Salt” Iturbe}). It's her way of paying a debt she's never confessed. She's been doing it since 1996, but only recently started going in person.
  • Someone who signs “M. V.” The flowers come with a card bearing those initials. See @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.Y1E4i0kdsA7wcPIj]{GAN-10 · Letters from Cluj}.

What could happen:

  • The coterie watches the grave and finds whoever leaves the flowers. The players decide whether to tell David or take it to the grave. If David is part of that conversation, he comes out of it changed: more at peace or more broken. Decide based on what gets said.
  • Nobody asks. The coterie lets it go on. David knows and says nothing; as long as the flowers keep coming, he's a little more at peace.
  • Someone uses it against him. If FIRSTLIGHT discovers the grave, it has a place to wait for the Hound.

Emphasis: Social.

Theme: Hunger

Cast: Dana Okafor (@UUID[JournalEntry.bJA2iRyDgbm2TcuK]{Dana Okafor}), Ezra Lund (@UUID[JournalEntry.PBJeE9T9n0BjB6ag]{Ezra “Static” Lund}), Ruth Abernathy (@UUID[JournalEntry.gRfqeOIXEHOcLemr]{Dr. Ruth Abernathy}), the thin-bloods of the docks.

What happened: FIRSTLIGHT has put a batch of blood bags into circulation on the port's black market. The blood carries a chemical marker that makes the Vitae of whoever drinks it glow under ultraviolet light for 48 hours. The Puget Cell installs discreet UV lamps at three known hunting grounds and waits.

What could happen:

  • Someone drinks. If a PC drank from a bag in the batch, any UV lamp gives them away for two nights. Thermometer +1 for each scene in which they're seen.
  • The thin-bloods fall. Three thin-bloods are captured in a single night. Thornquist demands vengeance or compensation, and Rosa offers shelter in Everett.

Emphasis: Mental.

Theme: Hunger

Theme: Beast

Cast: Tom “Bear” Whitman (@UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Tom “Bear” Whitman}), Cole Ransom (mortal, former SEAL), David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}), Dana Okafor (@UUID[JournalEntry.bJA2iRyDgbm2TcuK]{Dana Okafor}).

He runs into Bear at a bar by the port. He recognizes him. And he notices something strange: Bear moves like he did at twenty-five, and he isn't limping on the wrecked knee.

What could happen:

If they kill him, 2 Stains for whoever does it, and Bear never looks at them the same way again. If they make him a ghoul, Bear knows exactly what's in store for his friend.

Emphasis: Social and Physical.

Theme: Frenzy

Cast: Ethan Montgomery (@UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Ethan Montgomery}), Hal Brekke (@UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{Halvard “Hal” Brekke}), David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}), Dr. Lucy Harlan (Montgomery's Touchstone).

The Sheriff smells the blood.

  • Hal faces his sire. Hal is the only one Montgomery's Beast might recognize. A Charisma + Animal Ken (Difficulty 5) test can calm him. If it works, Hal earns the recognition he was looking for. If it fails, Hal ends up badly hurt.

Cast: Archon Duval (@UUID[JournalEntry.CRdeqlwyfpxGPyzT]{Archon Duval}), Justicar Panhard (@UUID[JournalEntry.gSMgBLLYggWyAN2W]{Justicar Helena Panhard}), David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}), Celeste Arden (@UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{Celeste Arden}).

Cast: the coterie, David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}), August Krell (@UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{August Krell}), and whoever signs the letters.

What happened: weeks after the end of the adventure, an envelope with no return address arrives at the hangar, postmarked Cluj-Napoca, Romania. Inside is a single sheet of paper with one line, handwritten in Marcus Vance's hand: “There are two. You know that already. Finish the lesson.” Signed: “M. V.” A PC finds it, not David. What they do with it is the first decision.

Who wrote it? The Storyteller decides, depending on what they want to do with the chronicle:

  • Vance is alive. He survived in 1985, changed somehow, and he knows what happened in Seattle. This opens an international arc. If David knows, the coterie has to decide whether to help him look for his sire or convince him to leave it buried.
  • It's Krell. If Krell survived the adventure, this is his last play: he wants David to believe their father is still alive so they'll look for him together.

What could happen:

  • They answer. The coterie, or David if they give it to him, sends a reply to the address on the postmark. What comes back depends on who wrote it.
  • They look for Krell. If Krell is alive, the coterie finds him and shows him the letter, with or without David present. The conversation between Vance's two sons can make Krell an ally or an enemy for good.

An adventure for a coterie of 4 or 5 characters, with @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith} and @UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Bear} as NPC allies. Estimated length: 6–8 sessions. ID: AVE-01.

A Seattle journalist spent ten years documenting deaths that didn't add up. Without knowing it, she built the most complete map in existence of the city's Kindred: where they hunt, where they slip up, who doesn't age. In the early hours of Thursday, November 12, 2026, someone stole it from her.

From that night on, the characters have to recover the File before it falls into the hands of the Second Inquisition or of someone at court who wants to use it as a weapon. Along the way they'll discover that someone on the docks is destroying Kindred with the technique of David's sire, that the Ventrue Primogen has spent sixty years preparing a coup, and that the whole city is watching them through 412,000 doorbells.

Installment 2 Adjustment · Ten or Twelve Years

Helen started documenting in 2014. The archive covers twelve years, though she still says “ten” because it's what she's been repeating for a long time. See @UUID[JournalEntry.nuyiQmnE32yq4wOG]{Revision to Part 1 · The Chain of Copies}.

The Truth, in One Paragraph

@UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Charles Halloway} wants the crown. His ghoul @UUID[JournalEntry.y8Ao3xEHH3W11EJe]{Preston Gale} located @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen Ward}'s archive using data from his company's cameras, and a team of mortals (@UUID[Actor.9rv5Jdb3y6bZZ1fj]{MEN-01}) stole it. @UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{August Krell}, the discarded childe of @UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Marcus Vance}, destroys whoever buys copies using Vance's doctrine, so that David chases a ghost and @UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Montgomery} stops trusting him. Meanwhile, Halloway feeds fragments of the archive to FIRSTLIGHT as the source ARCHER. When the Inquisition strikes the Prince's and the Sheriff's assets, Halloway will petition the Primogen for the regency.

The adventure is written for “The Archived” (@UUID[JournalEntry.azX1hjbc0PUp2AA2.JournalEntryPage.kiaygGF4KgylB6fb]{COT-00}): 4 or 5 characters who appear in the File. The concepts @UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{PJ-02} through @UUID[JournalEntry.gRfqeOIXEHOcLemr]{PJ-06} fit directly; with 4 players, one goes unused. David isn't part of the coterie: he's their ally, the Sheriff's Hound, who stays with them for the whole story and lends them the hangar as a haven. The Storyteller runs him, just like Bear. If the players create their own characters, keep the following in mind:

  • Clans that work best: Ventrue (access to @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway}'s circle), Nosferatu (information and surveillance), Toreador (the court and @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen}'s world), Gangrel (the Sheriff's pack), Tremere (forensics and Blood Sorcery). Malkavian and Banu Haqim also fit. Avoid more Brujah: the city already has four.
  • Useful Backgrounds: Contacts (police, press, port, tech), Influence, Herd, Camarilla Status, and any Mawla at court. A solid Mask (2 or more) helps: in this adventure, surveillance is the main danger.
  • Key Skills: Investigation, Technology, Insight, Stealth, Persuasion, Politics, and Brawl. At least one character with Technology 2 or more makes things much easier.
  • Motivations: every character has something in the File. Before you start, have each player decide what their folder contains (@UUID[JournalEntry.vtenvgNlXVPd99Rc]{AYU-09}) and one Touchstone who could be in danger in Part 3.
  • How to run @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David}: he's the emotional center of the plot, but the PCs are the ones who live it. He knows two things the coterie doesn't: why he sent the November 9 message (@UUID[JournalEntry.EQ3lkuiGnEvoSW7x]{DOC-05}) and what really happened at the Larchmont (@UUID[JournalEntry.Oiln4o98kvxKbOvS]{LUG-11}). He doesn't volunteer them: the PCs uncover them and decide what to do with them. When he helps, he adds +1 die to whoever is rolling or does something you narrate without a roll. He never single-handedly solves what the players have to solve, and the big decisions (forgive, hand over, kill, lie) are theirs. David weighs in, pushes, or reacts.
  • How they know David: at session zero, have each player say how their PC knows the Hound, even if only from a distance. Hal has known him for thirty years (@UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{PJ-05}); the others, whatever the table agrees on. This lets David summon them in @UUID[JournalEntry.w9xeQJg6psfiMjFU.JournalEntryPage.yyXMKcpDOIhGuZIB]{A0-E01 · The Call from SAFE}.

Sheet: @UUID[Actor.ys08GDwMs80NuOlf]{Charles Halloway}

“This city doesn't need a Prince who watches. It needs one who sees.”

Clan: Ventrue · Position: Ventrue Primogen · Sect: Camarilla · Role in @UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File}: main antagonist

Charles Halloway was born in 1921 into a Seattle family that had made its fortune in timber and multiplied it in the press. By thirty he was running three newspapers and a radio station. He was cold, methodical, and very patient. His father had taught him that a story doesn't run when it happens, but when it's convenient. He also learned that a story that never runs can be worth even more.

pages.name: Kindred Nights: The One Who Learned by Watching

text.content:
Prince Adelaide Grange Embraced him in 1958 for his press contacts. Four years later, Whitmore drove her out of the city by blackmailing her with photographs and documents, and Halloway understood two things. First, that his sire had been defeated without a drop of blood spilled. Second, that the method worked.

In 1978 he used it against O'Connor. In 1986 he bought Vance's journals, thinking they might someday serve him against the Sheriff's Hound. He has been waiting ever since. He has accumulated money (Halloway Meridian Capital), information (Thornquist), and patience. A year ago he began writing to Justicar Panhard. In 2026, with the city full of cameras and the Second Inquisition at the door, he decided he had waited long enough.

The File. His ghoul Preston Gale found Helen's archive using data from his company's doorbell cameras. The @UUID[Actor.9rv5Jdb3y6bZZ1fj]{Lonnie Barras} crew stole it on Night 1. Halloway keeps it in his vault (@UUID[JournalEntry.L6Fl1S0tjkWno2we]{Halloway Tower}) from Night 6 on.

The ghost. He hired August Krell (@UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{August Krell}) with the promise to “give him what Vance denied him”: a name, a place, recognition. Krell destroys the buyers of copies by imitating Controlled Fury.

ARCHER. Through Gale, he feeds FIRSTLIGHT fragments of the File that point only to the Prince's and the Sheriff's assets (@UUID[JournalEntry.WW7eg88I0uDGj8ks]{FIRSTLIGHT, Internal Memo SEA-0411}). When the raid comes, he'll ask for a regency “to protect the Masquerade.”

The expendable childe. If things go wrong, the accounts behind the leak lead to Celeste Arden (@UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{Celeste Arden}) or to her NPC substitute (@UUID[Actor.GidWqhJ9e6JUxiTS]{Julian Ashby}). He'll offer her up as a traitor at the Council (@UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}) without blinking.

Halloway Tower downtown, with a penthouse and a vault (@UUID[JournalEntry.L6Fl1S0tjkWno2we]{Halloway Tower}; Haven 4). He also controls the Eastside. He feeds only on mortals who have signed a contract with him (Ventrue feeding restriction): employees, partners, debtors. He believes a signature is a form of consent and has never wondered whether people knew what they were signing.

Preston Gale (@UUID[JournalEntry.y8Ao3xEHH3W11EJe]{Preston Gale}; Allies 3): ghoul, CEO of Gale Sentinel.

@UUID[Actor.eRE6FTNdGO76lzPK]{Mr. Pell}: his ghoul archivist since 1958. A 96-year-old man who looks 60, who typed all three copies of Vance's journals and knows where everything is.

Editor's Note

Doc 06 said Pell had been his ghoul “since 1950,” before Halloway's Embrace (1958); we settled on “since 1958.” The 96 years and the 60-year-old appearance stay: he was made a ghoul at 28 and aged during the stretches when Halloway kept him without Vitae.

Halloway Meridian Capital (Resources 5, Influence 4 in finance and media).

Security (@UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{Halloway's Security Ghouls}): armed ghouls in the tower and at Gale Sentinel.

Contacts 3: the press, City Hall, and a state senator's office.

@UUID[JournalEntry.sCVTjJFrnyyVnQDt]{Marcus Whitmore} (contempt). He took Halloway's sire from him with a trick. Halloway has spent sixty years preparing the same trick.

@UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Ethan Montgomery} (fear). The only one who could destroy him without a trial. That's why he has to be made to doubt his Hound.

@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith} (calculation). A piece to be taken off the board, not destroyed. Destroying him would raise suspicions.

@UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{August Krell} (disdain). A wounded dog he promised a bone.

@UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{Celeste Arden} (possession). He made her. She's his. He can spend her.

Justicar Panhard (hope). If she recognizes his regency, no one in Seattle will be able to oppose him.

• “Halloway brought down O'Connor.” (True.)
  • “Halloway is the childe of the former Prince Grange.” (True. Few people remember.)
  • “Halloway has the Justicar in his pocket.” (False. She hasn't answered him.)
  • “Halloway knows where Grange is.” (False. He'd give anything to know.)

To the mortal world he is Charles Halloway Jr., grandson of the founder and reclusive chairman of an investment fund, who never appears in public due to a chronic illness and takes meetings only by video call, with his camera off (Mask 3). He looks about forty. He is slim and of medium height, with black hair parted on the side and brown eyes that seem tired. He wears dark, classically cut suits, a white shirt, and a narrow tie. His hands don't move when he talks. He never interrupts. He smiles when he loses.

• Sire: Adelaide Grange (@UUID[JournalEntry.FOgT9FF3NF7ZHdCa]{Adelaide Grange})
  • Embraced: 1958 (born 1921)
  • Ambition: the crown of Seattle.
  • Convictions: “Order is a service, not a privilege” · “Never let them see you get your hands dirty.”
  • Touchstone: Margaret Halloway, his 22-year-old grandniece, a journalism student who believes her great-uncle is an anonymous benefactor of her scholarship.
  • Humanity: 5
  • Generation: 9th
  • Blood Potency: 3

Attributes: Strength 2, Dexterity 2, Stamina 3 · Charisma 3, Manipulation 5, Composure 4 · Intelligence 4, Wits 4, Resolve 4

Secondary Attributes: Health 6 · Willpower 8

Skills: Academics 2, Awareness 3, Etiquette 4 (Camarilla), Finance 5 (Shell Companies), Intimidation 3 (Silences), Investigation 3, Leadership 3, Insight 4, Persuasion 4 (Negotiation), Politics 5 (Power Grabs), Subterfuge 5 (Lying Without Lying), Technology 1

Disciplines:

  • Dominate 4: Compel (Compel), Mesmerize (Mesmerize), Forgetful Mind (Forgetful Mind), Rationalize (Rationalize)
  • Fortitude 2: Unswayable Mind (Unswayable Mind), Toughness (Toughness)
  • Presence 3: Awe (Awe), Daunt (Daunt), Dread Gaze (Dread Gaze)

In combat: Halloway doesn't fight. If cornered, he uses Dread Gaze and escapes in his private elevator. His defense pool is Dexterity + Wits (6).

Editor's Note

Doc 06 gave him five Dominate powers at 4 dots and three Fortitude powers at 2; in V5 there is one per dot. We dropped Cloud Memory (Cloud Memory), which Forgetful Mind already covers, and Resilience (Resilience), which his Health 6 doesn't include.
Capitol Hill · The Toreador rack · Map: no

A black door with no sign on a street full of bars. Inside, an exposed-brick basement with a small stage and a crowd that dances with their eyes closed. The music is slow and low, with a bass line that gets inside your chest. Under the red lights, everyone looks a little paler than they should. Someone at the bar is writing on a napkin.

The Prince's foundation owns it. Nadia (@UUID[JournalEntry.rg50DlMYSzgbZeBv]{Nadia Ferro}) feeds here. @UUID[JournalEntry.AeAhHuCNHL9KWVnT]{Wendell Fry} comes in almost every night and writes on napkins (@UUID[JournalEntry.FVBnf3yE87K4BOhh]{Wendell Fry: “Song for the Son of the Fist”}).

Hunting here is easy (Difficulty 2), but the Club belongs to the Prince: you ask permission or you pay.

It's a good place for an improvised social scene or for finding Fry outside Elysium.
