In Seattle, nobody survives alone for long. Not even the Hound. This chapter presents the five coteries that move the city during The Ward File: the players' coterie and four NPC coteries. At the end there are three new Loresheets (@UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5]{Loresheets}).

Each coterie follows the same format: name and nickname, members and agendas, customs, type, domain (Chasse, Lien, and Portillon), and shared Backgrounds. Coterie types that have no official Spanish name carry the original in italics.

“The ones who were on the drive.” · A coterie born of a shared threat: they all appear in the Ward File, and either they get it back together or they go down together.

The Concept

From doc 02. Every character appears in the Ward File. Helen never knew what they were, but each of them has a folder: a blurry photo, a date that doesn't add up, a pattern. When the drive is stolen, they're all exposed at once, and Sheriff Montgomery wastes no time telling them so, bluntly: “You're all on the same drive. You get it back together, or you go down together.”

Alternatives, if you'd rather use a different link: B) they're an existing coterie that Montgomery uses as a strike force; C) they're strangers who cross paths at Helen's apartment (@UUID[JournalEntry.YD0Td8Y9aJyIpGSl]{Helen Ward's Apartment}) the night of the theft.

Members and Agendas

Depending on which characters are in play. Each agenda includes the secret only the Storyteller knows.

Celeste Arden (@UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{Celeste Arden}, Ventrue). Agenda: prove she's worth more than her sire.

What she doesn't know: that her sire has already picked her as the scapegoat.

Ezra “Static” Lund (@UUID[JournalEntry.PBJeE9T9n0BjB6ag]{Ezra “Static” Lund}, Nosferatu). Agenda: expose whoever controls the cameras.

What he doesn't know: that the backdoor is his own code.

Nadia Ferro (@UUID[JournalEntry.rg50DlMYSzgbZeBv]{Nadia Ferro}, Toreador). Agenda: protect Helen's work.

What she doesn't know: that her cloud calendar led the thieves to the door.

Hal Brekke (@UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{Halvard “Hal” Brekke}, Gangrel). Agenda: earn his sire's respect.

What he's hiding: he's been reporting on David for years.

Dr. Ruth Abernathy (@UUID[JournalEntry.gRfqeOIXEHOcLemr]{Dr. Ruth Abernathy}, Tremere, alternate). Agenda: keep the city's dead invisible.

What she doesn't know: that FIRSTLIGHT has her at number one on its list.

Allies, Not Members

David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}, Brujah), NPC. The Sheriff's Hound. He's on the same drive they are, he calls them together the night of the theft, and he lends them the hangar as a haven. He stays with the coterie and helps them throughout the story, but he isn't a member. Agenda: get the File back without Helen paying the price.

What he doesn't know: that he has a blood brother in the city. What the coterie tells him about Krell and Vance when he finds out is up to the players.

Tom “Bear” Whitman (@UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Tom “Bear” Whitman}), NPC. David's ghoul. He comes with the hangar.

Suggested Customs

The players can change them in session zero. They're a starting point.

  • Your own folder. Everyone has read what Helen knew about them (@UUID[JournalEntry.vtenvgNlXVPd99Rc]{“Your Folder in the File”}). Nobody reads someone else's folder without permission.
  • The hangar is neutral. Inside @UUID[JournalEntry.104UV0anmZHNCTrD]{The Harbor Island Hangar}, nobody argues about clans or sires.
  • Nobody goes alone. Since the drive was stolen, no member goes out to hunt without telling at least one other.
  • The flip phone. To stay in touch, they use phones with no data connection that Bear gets for them.

Type

Commando (Commando): a unit assembled for a mission. If it survives @UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File}, it can become another type depending on the ending: Cerberus (Cerberus) if it stays on to guard the port, Regency (Regency) if one of its members takes an office.

Doc 02: Commando. It's a unit assembled for a mission that became permanent.

Domain

The Harbor Island docks.

Trait Value What it means
Chasse 2 Night-shift workers. Hunting is possible, but you have to be careful.
Lien 1 The coterie has hardly any sway over the port's mortals. Bear knows a few.
Portillon 2 Lots of access points, containers, and water. Easy to get in and out. For enemies too.

Doc 02 (suggested domain): the Harbor Island docks, around David's hangar (Chasse 2, Lien 1, Portillon 1).

Suggested Shared Backgrounds

  • Haven 3 (the hangar David lends them): with Water Access and Armory.
  • Contacts 1 (port): through Bear.
  • Ally: David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}), from the start. He helps because if they fall, he falls.
  • Ally: Tom “Bear” Whitman (@UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Tom “Bear” Whitman}), David's ghoul, shared with him.

Depending on how the adventure ends, Rosa Iturbe (@UUID[JournalEntry.WHkwE8CYfaKW5WyO]{Rosa “Salt” Iturbe}) and August Krell (@UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{August Krell}) can join as Allies 2.

Each player can contribute 1 point of their Backgrounds to the common pool.

Doc 02 (suggested shared backgrounds): Haven (the hangar, contributed by David), Contacts (port) 1.

Handout

@UUID[JournalEntry.vtenvgNlXVPd99Rc]{“Your Folder in the File”}, “Your Folder in the File.” Each player gets a page with what Helen knew about their character, written in her voice.

“The Sheriff's pack.” · The ones who clean up the city while the Prince raises a glass in the Gallery.

Members and Agendas

  • Ethan Montgomery (@UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Ethan Montgomery}, Gangrel), the alpha. Agenda: get the File back and find out whether Vance is in the city.
  • Hal Brekke (@UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{Halvard “Hal” Brekke} or an NPC with the same background), the tracker. Agenda: hear his sire tell him, just once, that he did well.
  • The bounty hunters (@UUID[Actor.L1oU4dlqHg8Yszon]{Montgomery's Bounty Hunters}): six mortals, ex-military and ex-cops. Agenda: get paid and ask no questions. One of them, Dutch Lindqvist, is starting to ask them.
  • The dogs: twelve canine ghouls. They sense Montgomery's will and react to the Beast of any Kindred.
  • David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}), outside ally. He isn't a member, but the Wolves treat him as one of their own.

Customs

  • The monthly report. Every member gives Montgomery a report on the first Sunday of each month, in person and out loud. Nobody puts it in writing.
  • No hunting where you patrol. No Wolf feeds inside Seattle city limits.
  • The porch. Montgomery receives visitors on the porch. If he invites you inside, it's serious.
  • The list. Everyone knows it exists. Nobody knows the eleven names except the alpha.

Type

Sbirri: enforcers in the service of a Camarilla office.

Domain

The farm and the Snohomish Valley (@UUID[JournalEntry.NNzMhIvsavpG0iTQ]{The Sheriff's Farm and Boat Landing}).

Trait Value
Chasse 3 (truckers, hunters, rest areas)
Lien 2 (the town sees them as an odd family of dog breeders)
Portillon 4 (open fields, dogs, a single gravel road, and the tunnel to the river)

Backgrounds

Haven 3 · Herd 2 · Contacts 3 (state patrol, port, private security) · Status 4 (Montgomery's) · Allies 3 (David)

In AVE-01

The Wolves are the coterie's natural backup until @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.aGN9NHO00wmdUzVn]{A3-E04 · The Pack Wavers}. From there on, if Montgomery doubts David, the bounty hunters can turn into pursuers. Dutch Lindqvist is a possible crack: if the coterie wins him over, he warns them about the order before it comes down.

“The ones who look down from above.” · A Primogen, his childe, two ghouls, and an investment fund. None of them uses the word “conspiracy.”

Members and Agendas

  • Charles Halloway (@UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Charles Halloway}, Ventrue). Agenda: the crown of Seattle.
  • Celeste Arden (@UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{Celeste Arden}) or her NPC replacement (@UUID[Actor.GidWqhJ9e6JUxiTS]{Julian Ashby}). Agenda: make her name worth more than her sire's. She believes the Council is a business meeting. She doesn't know she's the patsy.
  • Preston Gale (@UUID[JournalEntry.y8Ao3xEHH3W11EJe]{Preston Gale}, ghoul). Agenda: a billion-dollar valuation for Gale Sentinel, and the next dose of Vitae.
  • Mr. Pell (@UUID[Actor.eRE6FTNdGO76lzPK]{Mr. Pell}, ghoul). Agenda: to serve. He's 96 and afraid of what will happen if his master stops feeding him.
  • Three mortal investors (no ID): they believe they're part of an exclusive fund with an ailing genius for a chairman.

Customs

  • Cameras off. The meetings are video calls. Halloway never turns his on.
  • Everything under contract. Nobody works for the Council without signing a nondisclosure agreement. Halloway only feeds on people who've signed.
  • Nothing in writing with his name on it. Orders come through Pell or Celeste.
  • Smile when you lose. Halloway always does. The others have learned to fear that smile.

Type

Regency (Regency): a coterie preparing to rule.

Domain

Halloway Tower (@UUID[JournalEntry.L6Fl1S0tjkWno2we]{Halloway Tower}) and the Eastside.

Trait Value
Chasse 2 (only employees and partners under contract)
Lien 4 (half of Bellevue works for someone who works for Halloway)
Portillon 5 (private elevators, ghoul security, ANOMALY cameras)

Backgrounds

Resources 5 · Influence 4 (finance, media) · Contacts 3 · Allies 3 (Gale Sentinel) · Haven 4 · Herd 1

In AVE-01

The Council is the hidden antagonist. The coterie shouldn't know it exists until @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center}, when they find Gale's signature (). If Celeste is in play, the Council is inside the coterie from the first scene.

“The ones who don't kneel.” · The Anarchs of the Everett shipyard: they vote, they weld, and they owe no Prince a thing.

Members and Agendas

  • Rosa “Salt” Iturbe (@UUID[JournalEntry.WHkwE8CYfaKW5WyO]{Rosa “Salt” Iturbe}, Brujah), Baroness. Agenda: clear Everett's name and settle the debt of 1996.
  • Bas Okonjo (@UUID[Actor.k2TLqQkkzzjSLzkp]{Salt's Anarchs}, Gangrel). He left the Camarilla in 2019 and had been one of Montgomery's Wolves. Agenda: make sure Montgomery never makes him pay for deserting.
  • Tavi Mercer (@UUID[Actor.k2TLqQkkzzjSLzkp]{Salt's Anarchs}, Brujah). Young and impatient, she wants to hit Elysium “before they hit us.” Agenda: war. Halloway is feeding her rumors through Thornquist.
  • A dozen more Anarchs (@UUID[Actor.k2TLqQkkzzjSLzkp]{Salt's Anarchs}): longshoremen, mechanics, a nurse, two thin-bloods.

Customs

  • Decisions get voted on. Assembly every Friday in the back room of the bar. Rosa has one vote, like everybody else.
  • Nobody uses a minor as herd. The only rule Rosa has never put to a vote.
  • Dues. Every member puts something into the common fund: money, bagged blood, or labor.
  • The open door. Any Kindred can ask for shelter for one night. By the second night, they have to present themselves before the assembly.

Type

Cerberus (Cerberus): a coterie that guards a territory.

Domain

The old shipyard and the Port of Everett (@UUID[JournalEntry.JMwTSsJAcyYdCs3m]{Salt's Bar and the Old Shipyard}).

Trait Value
Chasse 3 (welders and longshoremen, some of them willing)
Lien 3 (the union is theirs)
Portillon 2 (one road in, but the water has no doors)

Backgrounds

Haven 2 · Herd 2 · Allies 3 (the union) · Influence 2 (Port of Everett) · Contacts 1 (naval base)

In AVE-01

Salt's can be an ally or an enemy (@UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.aJxUAHXcYpRWrhmG]{A2-E03 · Salt's}). If the coterie wins Rosa over, the Anarchs can show up at the climax (@UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.tG1m5PTkmBA1pvmc]{A4-E03 · The Last Ferry}) as backup. If not, Tavi Mercer may attack Elysium on her own during Part 4, which hands Halloway the perfect excuse for his motion.

“Everything's for sale down below.” · The brokers of the Seattle Underground: the stone of 1889 and the cables of 2026.

Members and Agendas

  • Abel Thornquist (@UUID[JournalEntry.dj4gIszHHTN1QRKk]{Abel Thornquist}, Nosferatu), the owner. Agenda: sell the File to the highest bidder and cash in his vote on the Council.
  • Ezra Lund (@UUID[JournalEntry.PBJeE9T9n0BjB6ag]{Ezra “Static” Lund} or an NPC with the same background), the tech. Agenda: expose whoever controls the cameras.
  • The dockside thin-bloods (no ID; Jun Takeda, @UUID[JournalEntry.BRQMU0Tf8VSNaZ5o]{Jun Takeda}, is one of them): runners and couriers. Agenda: survive.
  • The Mother Below: Thornquist's sire, in torpor in a corner of the Sealed Underground. She has no agenda. Yet.

Customs

  • Everything has a price. Nobody gives anything away in the Undermarket, not even advice.
  • Nobody asks about anybody's face. In the Sealed Underground, you don't comment on another Kindred's looks.
  • No fighting in the Market. Whoever breaks this rule never comes down again.
  • Packages stay closed. Runners carry without looking. Jun follows this one to the letter.

Type

Brokers: a type unique to this book. It uses the Mercenary Company rules for closing deals and the Questari rules for getting information.

Domain

The Sealed Underground (@UUID[JournalEntry.jg1zpvYlDFMJRY8Q]{The Sealed Underground (Seattle Underground)}).

Trait Value
Chasse 2 (unhoused people, in exchange for shelter)
Lien 3 (doormen, janitors, and technicians all over the city)
Portillon 5 (nobody gets into the Sealed Underground without Thornquist knowing)

Backgrounds

Haven 4 · Contacts 4 · Influence 3 (the underground) · Allies 2 (the thin-bloods) · Resources 2

In AVE-01

The Moles sell information to everyone. In @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.lM1EiE1FoXMkf3Uo]{A1-E04 · Everything Sells Below}, Thornquist confirms there are copies on the market. If the coterie pays him well, he also sells them the location of Krell's barge, though that costs a bigger favor.

Sheet: @UUID[Actor.15UcuyhvNvNqkCOf]{Dana Okafor}

“Every source wants something. Until you know what it wants, it's bait.”

Mortal · FIRSTLIGHT, head of the Puget Cell · Role in @UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File}: latent antagonist

pages.name: Before: The Woman Who Counted Bodies

text.content: Dana Okafor was born in 1981 in Houston, the daughter of a Nigerian engineer and a schoolteacher from Louisiana. She joined the FBI at twenty-six and spent eleven years in the Chicago violent crimes unit, where she made her name closing cases others had written off. In 2017 she investigated a string of disappearances on the South Side that fit no known pattern. She found the pattern. She also found the basement where it ended. Inside was something that tore two fingers off her left hand before she emptied her magazine into its head and it kept moving.

Six months later, a man from the Department of Homeland Security visited her in the hospital and told her she wasn't crazy. In 2018 she joined FIRSTLIGHT. In 2024 they sent her to Seattle to open a small cell, with a tight budget and a clear order: confirm whether the city had “an organized structure” and, if it did, leave it alone until it could be torn out by the roots.

Okafor doesn't hate the Kindred: she fears them methodically, the way you fear a fire. She's patient, meticulous, and distrustful, above all of anything that comes to her easily. ARCHER came too easily. She uses ARCHER anyway, because it's all she has, but she doesn't buy it.

The full index. ARCHER promised her the entire File. If she gets it, she requests reinforcements from national headquarters.

Helen Ward. At Thermometer 5 she contacts her. She offers her protection and a salary. She genuinely believes Helen is in danger, and she's right.

The “R. A.” anomaly. She's spent months preparing a visit to the medical examiner behind the fifteen impossible reports. If the Thermometer reaches 7, she makes it.

Who is ARCHER? She suspects it's an insider who wants to use FIRSTLIGHT to settle a score. If someone confirms it for her with evidence, she stops trusting the deliveries and starts investigating the source.

The Puget Cell: analyst S. Hale (@UUID[JournalEntry.D611Mcr17F6HHEUw]{Sasha Hale}), two more analysts, the tactical team (@UUID[Actor.abaWg7NwNQvM0sDc]{FIRSTLIGHT Tactical Team}), and a liaison with the FBI's Seattle field office.

Northline Cyber Advisory (@UUID[JournalEntry.KioeAEZP78U0Coz5]{Northline Cyber Advisory}), the front.

Access to ANOMALY through the pilot program with Gale Sentinel.

Equipment: see “The FIRSTLIGHT Arsenal” below.

S. Hale (trust). The only person in Seattle she listens to without reservation.

ARCHER (suspicion). A gift she still hasn't fully unwrapped.

Helen Ward (respect). Did alone in twelve years what took FIRSTLIGHT two with a federal budget.

Cole Ransom (usefulness). Good operator. Asks questions that aren't his to ask.

• “The Second Inquisition has an office in South Lake Union.” (True.)
  • “The hunters' boss lost two fingers to one of us.” (True. Thornquist knows it, through a Chicago contact.)
  • “FIRSTLIGHT already knows where the Prince sleeps.” (True since Night 2, thanks to ARCHER.)

Forty-five years old. Tall, close-cropped graying hair, unbranded office clothes: gray blazer, slacks, flat shoes. Her left hand is missing the ring finger and the pinky, and she keeps it in her pocket most of the time. She speaks quietly, unhurried, and has a habit of repeating the other person's last sentence before answering. She drinks black coffee all day. She never sits with her back to a door.

Attributes: Strength 2, Dexterity 3, Stamina 3 · Charisma 3, Manipulation 3, Composure 4 · Intelligence 4, Wits 4, Resolve 5

Secondary Attributes: Health 6 · Willpower 9

Skills: Firearms 4 (Pistol), Athletics 2, Drive 2, Awareness 4 (Ambushes), Intimidation 3 (Interrogation), Investigation 5 (Patterns), Leadership 3, Occult 2 (Kindred), Insight 4 (Lies), Persuasion 2, Brawl 2, Politics 2 (Agencies), Technology 2

Advantages: Unshakable Faith (Dominate and Presence take −2 dice against her; if they fail, she notices). Contacts 3 (FBI, Homeland Security, Seattle police). Resources 3 (federal budget).

Personal equipment: Glock 19 pistol with incendiary ammunition (aggravated damage against Kindred), pocket UV flashlight, light body armor vest (armor 2), encrypted phone.

In combat: Okafor doesn't enter combat if she can avoid it. She directs by radio from outside. If she's cornered, she shoots for the head and falls back toward a light source.

Quick pools: Shoot 7 · Interrogate 7 · Detect a lie 8 · Resist mental Disciplines 9 (Composure + Resolve; her Faith also takes 2 dice off the attacker's Dominate and Presence)

Reference (deceased mortal, no actor) · @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen Ward}'s college friend · one of the seven “unaccounted for” tenants of the @UUID[JournalEntry.Oiln4o98kvxKbOvS]{Larchmont} in 2014.

This page collects what docs 00–16 say about Danny. The source doc for each fact is in parentheses.

• In college, Danny lent Helen his Media Law notes and laughed at her because she highlighted in three colors (doc 03, Opening Fiction @UUID[JournalEntry.CeLqLZCfHQEtHYlk]{Chapter 0 · What the Water Doesn't Wash Away}).
  • He lived on the fourth floor of the Larchmont Building, in Tacoma, until the night in 2014 when the building burned and seven tenants were “unaccounted for.” There were no bodies. There was an article, Helen's, that the paper paid her not to publish. And there was a photo of a man with his back to the fire, looking at the camera (doc 03).
  • In the list Helen writes from memory (@UUID[JournalEntry.ifdmxLzsoLizs9uN]{Index of the Ward File}): “2014 · LARCHMONT. Seven ‘unaccounted for.’ Danny. Forty-one photos of the fire, the fire department report that doesn't add up, the doorman's statement he later retracted. THE PHOTO.” (doc 15).

• The Larchmont burned in the small hours of a March night in 2014. The official version blamed a short circuit (doc 05, history; locked in: “Larchmont fire in March 2014”).
  • A pack of three Sabbat Kindred who didn't leave for Gehenna was using the basement as a farm: they kept seven tenants locked in the old cistern and fed on them for weeks. David arrived after the pack had already set the building on fire; the seven tenants were already dead (doc 05, LUG-11).
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Montgomery} ordered the cistern sealed without removing the bodies: seven bloodless corpses were a Masquerade breach. “Danny Ruiz (REF-02) is still down there” (doc 05, LUG-11; doc 11, @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.9fTKL8Oeq36BCfU9]{A2-E05 · The Ashes of the Larchmont}).
  • ID registry: “REF-02 · Danny Ruiz, in the Larchmont cistern” (doc 05).
  • Helen still doesn't know; David didn't get there in time (doc 03, CAP-00's Storyteller Notes).

• @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.9fTKL8Oeq36BCfU9]{A2-E05 · The Ashes of the Larchmont} · The Ashes of the Larchmont (doc 11): with Auspex 4 on the slab, seven presences can be felt; one keeps repeating a thought: “Helen's going to come.” If the coterie opens the cistern (Thermometer +2) and takes Danny out to hand him over to the Hecata family of Tacoma, the family owes them a major boon.
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO.JournalEntryPage.xgVY2zlstK7IN1Rp]{FIN-C · Cleansing Fire} · Purifying Fire (doc 13): if the File is destroyed, gone are “twelve years of Helen's work… the Lake City mothers, Danny Ruiz, all the cases nobody else looked at.”

• @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.18vJtyOOVZe1Uk41]{GAN-09 · The Larchmont Survivor} · The Larchmont Survivor (doc 09): the Tacoma Hecata ask for someone to open the cistern and hand over the seven bodies so they can be properly buried. “That means telling Helen about Danny Ruiz, or at least risking that she finds out.”

Sheet: @UUID[Actor.g4XbpMuCHwxVhzeC]{David Smith}

“Some must burn so the rest can see the light.”

Clan: Brujah · Sect: independent, operational ally of the Camarilla · Role in @UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File}: ally of the coterie; the emotional center of the story
ex-Navy commando Embraced in Haiti in 1960 by Marcus Vance, turned outside enforcer for the Sheriff of Seattle.

he's the emotional center of @UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File} and an allied NPC, like @UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Bear}: he calls the coterie together in @UUID[JournalEntry.w9xeQJg6psfiMjFU.JournalEntryPage.yyXMKcpDOIhGuZIB]{A0-E01 · The Call from SAFE}, Montgomery assigns him to go with them in @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.xWx5IoPih8fX83b1]{A1-E03 · The Sheriff Asks}, and he stays with them all the way to the last ferry. Krell is his blood brother and he doesn't know it; Helen is his Touchstone; the Larchmont and Emily's night are the two times he arrived too late.

The PCs live that plot. They find out about Krell, about Rosa, about the Larchmont, and about Hal's reports. They decide what to tell David, when, and how. And they carry whatever happens next.

He helps; he doesn't star. If David assists on a roll, the PC rolling adds +1 die. If he does something on his own (covering an exit, opening an armored door, recognizing a guard stance), narrate it without rolling. He never solves on his own what the coterie should be solving.

He weighs in; he doesn't decide. Forgive, hand over, kill, lie: the players decide that. David pushes, argues, or keeps quiet. If the coterie picks something he wouldn't, he says so once, briefly, and then goes along or leaves the scene. He doesn't undercut them in front of others.

What he doesn't know. That Krell is Vance's childe. That Rosa gave Ray Dorsey shelter in 1996. What folios 41 and 42 say. What Hal tells Montgomery every month. Each of those things reaches David from a PC's mouth, or it doesn't reach him.

The voice. Short sentences, long silences, operational language: “target,” “exit,” “time.” He treats the coterie as colleagues, not subordinates. The rest is in @UUID[JournalEntry.zmabWuRnBZLfmd9l]{General Tone: The Supernatural Professional}.

Everyone else looks at him. Montgomery calls him “Hound.” Halloway, “Mr. Smith.” Krell talks only to him. Use it: let it bother the PCs that the city looks at David and not at them, and that they have to speak through him or make themselves heard.

pages.name: What He Does for the Coterie

text.content:
• Haven and domain. He lends them the Harbor Island hangar (@UUID[JournalEntry.104UV0anmZHNCTrD]{The Harbor Island Hangar}) as a haven. The coterie's domain is the surrounding docks.
  • The arsenal and Bear. Weapons, vehicles, and a ghoul who drives, repairs, and covers the door (@UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Tom “Bear” Whitman}).
  • Contacts. Police and ex-military ghouls. A word from him gets them in to see Montgomery.
  • Reading violence. He looks at a combat scene and knows who did it and how. With @UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.oGnroV6R68YdMQyD]{LOR-01 · The Doctrine of Controlled Fury} at level 4 he recognizes the inverted guard the moment he sees it.
  • The name. “The Black Dog of the Masquerade” opens doors in the Camarilla and closes them among the Anarchs.

Scene What David does What's left for the coterie
@UUID[JournalEntry.w9xeQJg6psfiMjFU.JournalEntryPage.yyXMKcpDOIhGuZIB]{A0-E01 · The Call from SAFE} Calls the coterie together and arrives with Bear. Helen trusts him more than anyone. Convincing Helen, reading the apartment.
@UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.DtetdHiBnOLQaM6Y]{A1-E02 · Ash on Pier 46} Reads the blows on the shipping container: +1 die. Knowing what they mean.

David Smith is the kind of vampire they call when other vampires become a problem. His training as a Navy commando was only the beginning.

🩸 Potence 4 — Supernatural Strength

  • Lethal Body (Potence 1 homebrew; Lethal Body): Your blows hit like a jackhammer. Superficial damage converted to lethal.
  • Prowess (Potence 2; Prowess): Lets you perform impossible feats of strength or lift up to a ton. Perfect for breaching, rescuing, or opening armored entrances.
  • Shattering Blow (Potence 3 homebrew): A single concentrated impact that can bring down walls or incapacitate with one hit. Ideal as a finishing execution.
  • Kinetic Bullet (Potence ••••, Celerity 2 amalgam – Homebrew):
    • Cost: 1 Rouse Check to activate. Lasts one scene. Allows up to Potence (4) shots at no extra cost; more shots require new Rouse Checks (1 per additional shot).
    • Effect: David can throw any small/medium object (marble, rock, nut, small stake, etc.) as if it were a heavy pistol shot.
    • Range: up to Potence × 10 m (40 m); no penalty within half that distance.
    • Attack: Dexterity + Athletics + Potence (or Strength + Athletics, table's choice); the target uses normal defense.
    • Damage: as a .45 → base damage 3 + net successes; lethal against mortals/ghouls, and against Kindred without Fortitude.
    • 1/scene you can make an “Execution Shot”: +1 Diff.; with 3+ net successes, a mortal/ghoul is dead or unconscious; a Kindred suffers a heavy penalty (-2) on the body part hit.
    • With stakes / bolts and +2 Diff., with 4+ net successes you can stake or pin the Kindred's chest (Storyteller ruling).
    • It also works for breaking cameras, lights, weapons in mortals' hands, etc., with no visible firearms and no shell casings.

💬 Note: “Lethal Body + Shattering Blow” is a valid and brutal combination, but Potence 4 is usually used with Prowess or Superhuman Assault. In his case, Shattering Blow is better for a hunter of the Masquerade.

Source: doc 17. Last Bastion of the Masquerade (Fortitude ••••). Homebrew – optional amalgam with Presence or Auspex, if you want to fine-tune it further.

“I don't go down until the job is done.”

Theme / fiction. When David marks someone as an enemy of the Masquerade, his body and his will refuse to fall. Broken bones, bullets, fire… all of it held together by sheer refusal. It isn't blind Brujah fury: it's the brutal calm of the executioner who won't let himself die until he's finished off the condemned.

Mechanical Version (V5-Friendly)

Requirements

  • Fortitude 4
  • Humanity 6+ (or at least 1 Conviction tied to “protecting the Masquerade / the balance”)
  • Optional as an amalgam: Presence 2 or Auspex 2 (Presence if you want it more “imposing,” Auspex if you see it as an almost mystical focus on his mission).

Cost

  • 1 Rouse Check on activation.
  • Can only be used once per scene, and once per night for its big effect.

Activation. You must declare a target a “Veil-breaker”:

  • It must be someone who, in David's judgment (and the Storyteller's), is actively endangering the Masquerade:
    • a Kindred using Disciplines in front of mortals,
    • a Sabbat carrying out massacres,
    • a Cainite about to reveal the existence of vampires, etc.
  • Quick action: David locks his gaze / pronounces the “sentence” (a whisper, a stony line, whatever you like) and activates the power.

As long as this sentenced target remains present in the scene (or David is pursuing them directly), the power is active.

Effects

1. I Won't Fall Yet. As long as the sentenced target remains in the scene or in direct pursuit:

  • If David would be Incapacitated by damage (superficial or aggravated) on a damage roll:
    • Instead of falling, he's left at 1 superficial Health level.
    • He automatically gains the Dazed / Staggered condition (the Storyteller can impose -2 on complex physical actions, no multiple actions, etc.).
    • This effect can only happen once per scene and per night.

In short: 👉 The first time someone “would drop him” while he's executing an enemy of the Masquerade… he doesn't fall. He stays on his feet at 1 Health.

2. Executioner's Flesh. As long as the sentenced target remains present:

  • David gains +Fortitude (4) dice on tests to:
    • Resist frenzy from damage or provocation by the target.
    • Resist Dominate / Presence / Auspex from the target (or from their direct allies in the scene, at the Storyteller's discretion).
  • He also ignores wound penalties (as if Deny Pain were “boosted”) against that specific target.
  • Outside that hunt, Deny Pain works normally.

Narrative effect: 👉 While he's hunting a real danger to the Masquerade, he doesn't break, doesn't flee, and doesn't bend mentally at that enemy's hands.

3. Moral Limit. Because otherwise it gets out of hand:

  • If the Storyteller decides David has activated it against someone who isn't really a threat to the Masquerade, or out of pure personal grudge:
    • The power works the same, but at the end of the night David breaks (see “When He Breaks”): he twisted his Conviction and used “the Masquerade” as an excuse to kill.
    • If a PC saw it, they decide whether to tell him.

This nails it to the concept of an enforcer with a code, not a thug justifying himself.

Is It Broken or Reasonable?

If you compare it with the official Fortitude 4 powers:

  • Draught of Endurance: gives Fortitude and powers to another Kindred for one night.
  • Gorgon Scales: gives brutal defenses, but very situational and tied to Resonance.

Last Bastion of the Masquerade:

  • It's very strong, but:
    • It only works in scenes where there's a real threat to the Masquerade.
    • The “I don't go down” is once per night, and it leaves you wrecked.
    • It doesn't increase damage or give super attacks; it only keeps David on his feet to finish the job.
    • It has a moral cost if abused.

At the table it's a power that:

  • Reinforces his role as “the Black Dog of the Masquerade.”
  • Delivers a very cinematic moment: the blow that should put him on the ground… and he gets up at 1 Health with his jaw broken and his gaze fixed.
  • Doesn't unbalance things as much as a constant brute-force damage-reduction buff against anything and everyone.

Simpler / Quicker Version

If you'd rather have something even easier to use, the same concept can be boiled down to:

Lite Version:

  • Cost: 1 Rouse Check.
  • Effect: Once per night, when you take damage that would leave you Incapacitated while fighting someone who is endangering the Masquerade, you stay at 1 Health instead of falling.
  • Extra: +2 dice to resist frenzy and mental Disciplines from that enemy until the end of the scene.

Narrative description of David Smith

Standing under dim light, David Smith looks like a statue carved from steel and shadow. His face, angular and firm, is that of a man who has seen too many battles and forgets none of them. The square jaw, clenched, seems made for biting rather than talking. His weathered skin has the pallor of someone who hasn't felt the sun in years; a jagged scar runs across his right cheek, from the cheekbone to the edge of his lip, a dry line that never quite finished healing.

His hair, short and dark, shows the first gray at the temples, witnesses to an age when reflexes still outrun thought. His eyes—dark gray, almost black—don't look: they assess, calculate, weigh every movement. There's something unsettling about them, a dull gleam, like that of a hunter who has learned to recognize prey even in total darkness.

He wears a black tactical jacket, heavy, reinforced at the shoulders and chest, with multiple pockets and Velcro closures and no insignia. It's a uniform without a flag, the uniform of someone who serves only his own cause. Every fold seems designed for combat, every buckle cinched with the precision of a soldier who leaves nothing to chance. Beneath it, the silhouette reveals a strong, contained body, muscles tense more from habit than from effort.

The air seems to smell of gunpowder, rust, and dried blood. It's the scent that has followed him for decades, the same one that soaks his clothes and his soul. David Smith needs neither words nor weapons to command respect. His presence alone, still but charged with pent-up tension, makes you think he's one heartbeat away from unleashing a storm.

Doc 17 also includes three images of the haven (“Safe Heaven,” “Interior,” and “Weapons Room”) and the arsenal inventory: they're in @UUID[JournalEntry.104UV0anmZHNCTrD]{The Harbor Island Hangar}.

pages.name: Tactical Synergies Between Disciplines and Skills

text.content:
Source: doc 20. Storyteller guide for when David fights alongside the coterie. Let him shine, but let a PC land the decisive blow.

1. Celerity (Quick Reflexes, Blink, Lightning Movement)

  • Best use: pursuit, ambushes, evasion, and surprise attacks.
  • Synergy:
    • Athletics + Celerity: moves from cover to cover before enemies react.
    • Brawl or Melee + Blurred Rush: closes the distance and strikes in the same action, before the opponent finishes reacting.
    • Stealth + Celerity: moves through shadows or closes distance without being seen.
  • How he uses it: Blink on the turn before attacking and Blurred Rush when striking: an appear-and-attack sequence that's nearly impossible to stop.

Editor's Note

Doc 20 used Lightning Strike (Lightning Strike), which was removed from the sheet (see Disciplines). Where the doc combined it with Lightning Movement, Blink and Blurred Rush now go instead.

2. Potence (Lethal Body, Shattering Blow)

  • Best use: melee combat, physical intimidation, breaking structures or equipment.
  • Synergy:
    • Brawl + Lethal Body: lethal damage even unarmed.
    • Melee + Shattering Blow: multiplies the weapon's damage; breaks bones or armor effortlessly.
    • Intimidation + Potence: backs up a threat with supernatural strength (breaking a table or a door as a gesture).
  • Tactical combination: Lethal Body and Shattering Blow together against tough enemies, then Fortitude (Deny Pain) to weather the counterattacks.

3. Fortitude (Toughness, Deny Pain)

  • Best use: resisting physical, fire, and lethal damage, and staying on his feet when others would fall.
  • Synergy:
    • Stamina + Fortitude: each level adds an automatic success to his soak or endurance rolls.
    • Prolonged combat + Deny Pain: keeps fighting with severe penalties.
    • Prowess + Fortitude: keeps control even in the middle of frenzy.
  • Narrative use: David can take bullets, keep advancing, grab the enemy by the throat, and deliver a precise blow with Potence.

4. Presence (Instinctive Authority, Majesty of War)

  • Best use: intimidating, subduing, or controlling the social environment in seconds.
  • Synergy:
    • Intimidation + Instinctive Authority: subdues enemies or ghouls without raising his voice.
    • Persuasion + Majesty of War (Kindle Emotions): imposes his will in social scenes or interrogations.
    • Intimidating stares + Presence: forces a “halt” before the fight.
  • Key combination: before combat, Instinctive Authority to intimidate or scatter weak enemies. If it fails, he switches to Celerity or Potence without losing rhythm.

5. Auspex (Heightened Senses, Premonition)

  • Best use: tracking, detecting traps, anticipating attacks.
  • Synergy:
    • Awareness + Heightened Senses: detects snipers, heartbeats, or slight movements.
    • Tailing + Premonition: anticipates ambushes or the target's movements.
    • Investigation + Premonition: tracks Masquerade violators or prepares a night hunt.
  • Strategy: Premonition before the hunt or a confrontation. If he gets a vision, he tells the coterie in two words: it's a clue, not a solution.

💀 Standout Tactical Combos for David Smith

Situation Disciplines + Skills Result
Silent ambush Celerity + Stealth + Auspex (Premonition) Gets ahead of the victim, predicts their movement, and attacks before they react.
Close combat (1v1) Potence + Fortitude + Brawl (Tactical combat) More damage, ignores wounds, and lands devastating blows.
Surprise attack from above Celerity (Lightning Movement) + Athletics (Jumping) Drops from a rooftop and strikes before he's seen.
Hunting a Masquerade violator Auspex (Premonition) + Stealth + Presence (Instinctive Authority) Follows the trail, locates them, and neutralizes them without open combat.
Against multiple enemies Fortitude (Flesh of Marble) + Celerity (Quick Reflexes) + Potence (Shattering Blow) Takes minimal damage, acts before them, and takes them down one by one.
Intimidating a whole room Presence (Majesty of War) + Intimidation + Iron Will Silences everyone and commands respect or terror even among older vampires.

🧠 How He Fights Alongside the Coterie

  1. Before the confrontation: Auspex. He scans the surroundings and says where the exits are.
  2. Start of the conflict: Presence (Instinctive Authority) to cut off the social flow or disorient the enemy.
  3. Physical combat: Celerity + Potence + Fortitude in tandem. He takes the toughest enemy or covers the most exposed PC.
  4. Finish: when the opponent falls or surrenders, he stops before frenzy. If a PC keeps hitting, he holds them back.
  5. After: Auspex or Premonition to see whether the Masquerade held.

The earlier sources (docs 17–20) predate docs 00–16. Where they clash, docs 00–16 win:

  • Arrival in Seattle. Doc 17 places David in Seattle from 2010 on (and before that, from 1970 to 2010, between Europe, the Maghreb, and Sabbat hunts). In the adventure he's already in Seattle in 1996 (@UUID[JournalEntry.VYpDoFtqKkL7FlqL]{Emily Smith}), and doc 16 marks as provisional that he arrived in the '80s. Emily's sheet (doc 24) also says he watched her from the car when she got out of school.
  • The Sheriff. The file cites a “relationship of respect with Sheriff O'Connor”; in docs 00–16 O'Connor stopped being Sheriff in 1978 and the Sheriff is Montgomery (@UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Ethan Montgomery}).
  • Haven. The sheet gives Safe Haven 4; @UUID[JournalEntry.104UV0anmZHNCTrD]{The Harbor Island Hangar} (doc 05) gives Haven 3 with Water Access and Armory.
  • Age at death. Born 03/15/1935 and dead 07/08/1960, he'd be 25; the file says 27 and the sheet, 28/30.
  • Predator Type. The sheet says Silent Hunter; the file, Hunter of Hunters.
  • Touchstones. The sheet lists Helen and Bear; docs 00–16 give Helen and Emily, with Bear as an anchor.
  • Celerity. The sheet and doc 20 use Lightning Strike (in V5 it's Lightning Strike, level 5) and Lightning Movement; doc 17 swaps it for Temporal Burst. The sheet adds Blurred Rush, with no description. Doc 20 also names Toughness and Flesh of Marble (Fortitude) and Quick Reflexes, which aren't on the sheet. By editorial decision, the sheet swaps Lightning Strike for Blink and sets Blurred Rush at level 3 (see Disciplines).
  • LOR-01. No earlier source mentions the Loresheet; doc 17 calls channeling the Brujah Compulsion “Controlled Fury,” while in docs 00–16 it's Vance's doctrine (@UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.oGnroV6R68YdMQyD]{LOR-01 · The Doctrine of Controlled Fury}).

Sheet: @UUID[Actor.75UbIo5Kl9zVsd0V]{Dr. Anneliese Voight}

“The epidemic never begins with the first death. It begins with the first data point nobody wanted to look at.”

Clan: Tremere · Positions: Regent of the Observatory Chantry and Primogen · Sect: Camarilla

pages.name: Mortal Days: The Statistician of Vienna

text.content: Anneliese Voight earned her doctorate in medical statistics at the University of Vienna in 1919, when women were barely allowed into the lecture halls. She spent the influenza pandemic counting the dead on maps of the city and was one of the first to see that the infections followed the streetcar lines. Nobody listened to her in time. Ever since, she can't stand it when someone ignores a pattern.

pages.name: Kindred Nights: The Regent of the Dome

text.content:
A Regent of the Vienna Chantry Embraced her in 1924 so she would apply her methods to something more important than the flu. In 1964 she was sent to Seattle to run a small Chantry the Pyramid considered irrelevant. When the Pyramid fell, Voight kept the Chantry, its books, and her independence, and she joined none of the houses that emerged.

Since 2019 she has turned the old Queen Anne observatory (@UUID[JournalEntry.OSMVQHNXfk9zRyLM]{The Observatory Chantry}) into a network surveillance center. She was the first to detect FIRSTLIGHT in the city and the one who imposed the 2024 law on devices in Elysium. She wrote the Prince a detailed report that took him two nights to open. She's beginning to think the Seattle Camarilla won't survive its Prince.

Watch Northline. She intercepts part of the Puget Cell's traffic. She knows there's an inside source, but she doesn't know who ARCHER is. She'd give a lot to find out.

Protect Ruth. She knows FIRSTLIGHT has marked her childe (@UUID[JournalEntry.gRfqeOIXEHOcLemr]{Dr. Ruth Abernathy}) or the NPC medical examiner who takes her place. She's preparing an evacuation plan.

A Prince who listens. She doesn't want Halloway to win, but she doesn't want Whitmore to stay either. If the coterie proves it knows how to read patterns, it could become her candidate in the shadows.

The Observatory Chantry in Queen Anne (@UUID[JournalEntry.OSMVQHNXfk9zRyLM]{The Observatory Chantry}; Haven 3, with Blood Sorcery wards). She feeds on blood-bank blood the Chantry buys through a research lab, and occasionally on researchers working late on the university campus.

The Chantry: three Tremere apprentices and Ruth Abernathy, if she's in play.

The dome's servers (Resources 3, Contacts 2 in technology).

Research lab (Influence 2 at the university).

Rituals: ward against ghouls, blood communion, tracking by Vitae.

@UUID[JournalEntry.sCVTjJFrnyyVnQDt]{Marcus Whitmore} (frustration). She gave him the data. He chose not to look at it.

@UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Charles Halloway} (suspicion). He seems too calm to her for someone with so much to lose.

@UUID[JournalEntry.gRfqeOIXEHOcLemr]{Ruth Abernathy} (responsibility). She turned her into a weapon and feels obligated to protect her.

@UUID[JournalEntry.PBJeE9T9n0BjB6ag]{Ezra Lund} (interest). She'd like to work with him. Thornquist won't let her get close.

@UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Ethan Montgomery} (mutual respect). Two professionals in a court of amateurs.

• “Voight can read anyone's email in the city.” (False: only Northline's, and not all of it.)
  • “The Observatory Chantry no longer answers to anyone outside Seattle.” (True.)
  • “Voight wants to be Prince.” (False. She wants a Prince who listens to her.)

To mortals she's Dr. A. Voight, director of a private computational epidemiology lab affiliated with the university (Mask 2). She looks about thirty-three. She's petite, with very short hair in her natural color, and she wears rimless glasses, black turtlenecks, and a lab coat she forgets to take off. She speaks perfect English with a Viennese accent. She has a habit of answering questions with a percentage.

Editor's Note

Doc 06 said “looks about fifty” and “white hair”; it was decided that she looks the age she was at her Embrace (1924, born in 1891): about thirty-three, with her hair in its natural color.

• Sire: Regent Friedrich Ahlers of Vienna (destroyed in 1945)
  • Embraced: 1924 (born in 1891)
  • Ambition: for the Seattle Camarilla to survive the age of data.
  • Convictions: “Never ignore a pattern” · “Knowledge without action is complicity.”
  • Touchstone: Mateo Ruiz-Okoye, an epidemiology PhD student whose dissertation she supervises by email without his knowing who she is.
  • Humanity: 6
  • Generation: 9th
  • Blood Potency: 4

Attributes: Strength 1, Dexterity 2, Stamina 2 · Charisma 2, Manipulation 3, Composure 4 · Intelligence 5, Wits 4, Resolve 4

Secondary Attributes: Health 5 · Willpower 8

Skills: Academics 4 (Epidemiology), Science 4 (Statistics), Awareness 3, Etiquette 2, Investigation 4 (Patterns), Medicine 3, Occult 4 (Thaumaturgy), Politics 2, Technology 4 (Networks)

Disciplines:

  • Auspex 3: Heightened Senses (Heightened Senses), Premonition (Premonition), Share the Senses (Share the Senses)
  • Dominate 2: Compel (Compel), Mesmerize (Mesmerize)
  • Blood Sorcery 4: Corrosive Vitae (Corrosive Vitae), Extinguish Vitae (Extinguish Vitae), Blood of Potency (Blood of Potency), Theft of Vitae (Theft of Vitae)

Rituals: Ward against Ghouls (Ward against Ghouls), Communicate with Kindred Sire (Communicate with Kindred Sire), Blood Walk (Blood Walk)

Sheet: @UUID[Actor.9Sei2feAoKaQPPto]{Dr. Ruth Abernathy}

Concept: night-shift pathologist at the county medical examiner's office and a member of Voight's chantry.

Ruth performed autopsies for twelve years. She was meticulous, dry, and had no patience for the living. In 2004 she signed the report on a body with no blood and no visible wounds. The next day the body had vanished from the morgue cooler, and her boss asked her to “revise” the report.

Dr. Anneliese Voight (@UUID[JournalEntry.yaAsxCkCLf8CANL5]{Dr. Anneliese Voight}) Embraced her in 2005: a medical examiner who asks questions is a danger, but a medical examiner who answers to the chantry is a weapon. Since then, Ruth is the reason Kindred deaths in Seattle end up as “overdose,” “accidental fire,” or “animal attack.” This week she's on leave: a substitute is signing the night-shift reports. She feeds in hospitals, on sedated patients.
The File holds a table of Helen's listing fifteen “impossible” autopsy reports. Every one of them bears Ruth's signature.

Ambition: find the body that disappeared in 2004. Desire: one night without corpses. Suggested Conviction: “The dead deserve the truth, even if the living don't.” Touchstone: her ex-husband, a retired homicide detective who still calls her when he can't sleep.
Influence (medical examiner's office) 2, Contacts (police) 2, Resources 2, Mawla (Voight) 1.

@UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.DtetdHiBnOLQaM6Y]{A1-E02 · Ash on Pier 46}, @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.j4TnqYOwVuSCeQ0z]{A2-E02 · “Locate. Evaluate. Execute.”} (forensic analysis of Controlled Fury), and @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.ogKpm1VYgcVGCw1T]{A4-E02 · The Raid}.
Agent Dana Okafor (@UUID[JournalEntry.bJA2iRyDgbm2TcuK]{Dana Okafor}) already has a file on her. FIRSTLIGHT considers her “statistical anomaly number one.” She's the first person they'll come for.

Background figure (no actor sheet) · nomadic Gangrel · sire of @UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Ethan Montgomery}.

This page collects what docs 00–16 say about Kane. The source doc for each fact is in parentheses. The docs give him no sheet, no Generation, and no current whereabouts.

• Number PNJ-09 was reserved for “Elijah Kane, Montgomery's sire” (doc 01, note to the ID registry v2) and set as “PNJ-09 · Elijah Kane, Montgomery's sire (background)” (doc 06, ID registry).
  • He was a nomadic Gangrel. In 1885, Montgomery, a frontier tracker, spent three weeks hunting a killer of travelers near Eureka and discovered that his quarry wasn't a man. Kane “spared his life because he found him interesting and Embraced him because he found him useful” (doc 06, Montgomery's sheet).
  • Montgomery spent eighteen years roaming the coast with him. In 1903, after the San Francisco earthquake, Montgomery entered the service of the Camarilla and never left it (doc 06). The city timeline dates that move to 1903, in San Francisco (doc 05).
  • Montgomery's sheet: “Sire: Elijah Kane · Embraced: 1885 (born 1845)” (doc 06).
No doc has him appear in @UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File} or in the hooks. He explains where Montgomery got his tracking and his habit of following a trail to the end.

“She stayed with the ones nobody wanted.” (her headstone, @UUID[JournalEntry.uhtM1iF2WrHHlcd8]{Emily Smith's Grave})

Daughter of @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}. Background character, no actor. Main source: doc 24, “Emily Smith” (Touchstones, earlier source), filled out with docs 00–16.

His daughter is the reason David takes the Masquerade so seriously. And also the reason that, some nights, he would rather not wake up.

• Birth: February 14, 1958 (@UUID[JournalEntry.woF61Oy8f19xxrkA]{Emily Smith's Obituary}). February 14 is the date on SAFE's messages to Helen (@UUID[JournalEntry.EQ3lkuiGnEvoSW7x]{SAFE: Saved Messages}); Helen doesn't know that.
  • Death: fall of 1996, in Rainier Valley. She was 38. The exact date, October 21, 1996, is provisional (doc 16).
  • Obituary (@UUID[JournalEntry.woF61Oy8f19xxrkA]{Emily Smith's Obituary}, The Puget Courier, 10/24/1996): social worker with the King County Department of Youth Services; bachelor's degree in Social Work from the University of Washington in 1981; fifteen years with at-risk youth in the south end of the city; “the one who never hung up the phone” and “the one who took the cases nobody wanted.” Born in San Diego and raised in Seattle by her mother, Anne Smith, who died in 1989 (San Diego and Anne Smith: provisional, doc 16). Her father, “Navy Sergeant David Smith,” died in the line of duty in 1960, when she was two. Next to “She leaves no immediate family,” David wrote by hand: Yes.
  • The killer: Ray Dorsey (@UUID[JournalEntry.LqMKPCSaUzAWcGYi]{Ray Dorsey}), an Anarch who used Rainier Valley teenagers as his herd. A week earlier, @UUID[JournalEntry.WHkwE8CYfaKW5WyO]{Rosa Iturbe} had given him shelter at the Everett shipyard without knowing what he was going to do. She never forgave herself.
  • The night: David arrived minutes too late and destroyed the Anarch with a single shot. The backup who cleaned up the scene while David was still on his knees was @UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{Hal Brekke}, two years into unlife. To the city, it was a gang settling scores. To Montgomery (@UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Ethan Montgomery}), it was the reason he started keeping an eye on his Hound.
  • The survivor: Marcos Delgado (@UUID[Actor.rOqsigq4dAfIYQMh]{Marcos Delgado}), fifteen at the time, the only kid who survived. Before he passed out, he saw a man with a scar on his face shoot Dorsey and kneel beside the social worker. Today he's a youth counselor in the same neighborhood (@UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.pCLncsxglYsxJtbu]{GAN-01 · The Boy Who Survived}).
  • The grave: @UUID[JournalEntry.uhtM1iF2WrHHlcd8]{Emily Smith's Grave}, in a cemetery north of the city. Someone leaves fresh flowers every Sunday (@UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.cGEW4b4hCJlaDeSK]{GAN-12 · The Visited Grave}).
  • In the adventure: Emily's night is one of David's two late arrivals (the other is the Larchmont). It's told only in memories, never in detail (Safety Tools). Vance mentions her in his journal: “He has a daughter across the sea and doesn't speak of her” (@UUID[JournalEntry.kzeWNRBY6tgLP37S]{Journal of M. Vance, Marseille, 1963, Folio 14 (Typewritten Copy)}). With Krell, a PC telling him about Emily, with David present, counts as one step (@UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell}). The letters from @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.Y1E4i0kdsA7wcPIj]{GAN-10 · Letters from Cluj} arrive every February 14.

• Name: Emily Smith
  • Year of birth: 1958
  • Tie to David: Biological daughter, his only child.
  • Profession: Social worker in Seattle, specializing in at-risk youth, addiction, and domestic violence.

David knew her alive for only a few years.

When the girl was 2, he was Embraced in Haiti (1960). He came back to the U.S. as a dead man with a new face, and the official version was simple:

“Your father died in a classified operation. A hero. There's no body.”

Emily grew up with the image of the absent hero, the black-and-white photo in the living room, the folded flag. Meanwhile, David watched her from a distance when he could:

  • Watching her leave school from his car.
  • Following her school records through contacts.
  • Making sure money never ran out entirely, through “anonymous payments” or help that always showed up at just the right moment.

When she grew up:

  • She became a social worker because she hated seeing kids broken by poverty and violence.
  • She set her jaw the same way he did when something struck her as unfair.

To David, Emily was:

  • His primary Touchstone: living proof that something worth protecting still existed.
  • The reminder that he was once truly human.

He never revealed himself. He always watched her from afar. He never wanted to contaminate her life with what he was.

The tragedy began the way so many things do in the World of Darkness: with something small nobody took seriously.

  • Emily worked with teenagers from rough neighborhoods.
  • One of them, a kid named Marcos, started talking about a guy who:
    • gave them drugs for free,
    • asked them for “weird favors” now and then,
    • made them drink from a shared bottle, and then the nights went blurry.

Emily, being Emily, didn't let it go.

What she didn't know was that this “guy” was an out-of-control Anarch Kindred who used the kids as his personal herd, and sometimes as messengers in business that brushed up against the Masquerade.

She did what she knew how to do:

  • She took notes,
  • talked to other kids,
  • cross-checked names,
  • started building a file to report him—her way, legal, human.

One of those reports, far too detailed, ended up on the wrong desk. Or rather: on the wrong screen, with cameras and microphones the Camarilla was also watching.

David's Failure

David got an indirect warning:

  • “Human social worker asking too many questions about a problem asset. Anarch. Possible exposure. Watch or clean up.”

His initial plan:

  • Move fast,
  • take the Anarch off the board,
  • steer Emily away without having to touch her.

But he underestimated two things:

  1. The Anarch's own paranoia: he realized someone was tying him to his crimes.
  2. How fast human affairs can go bad without any need for fangs.

The key night:

  • Emily went to see Marcos at an apartment in a half-abandoned building.
  • The Anarch decided to tie up loose ends and turn the scene into a “gang shootout.”
  • The police would log it as a fight between gangs.
  • The Anarch didn't know David was already in the area, on the Sheriff's orders.

David arrived minutes too late.

  • When he burst into the apartment:
    • the smell of gunpowder and blood was already in the air,
    • the hallway lights were flickering,
    • the bodies of two kids lay on the floor,
    • Emily was against the wall, trying to put pressure on someone else's wound, her hands covered in blood that wasn't hers.

The Anarch took her hostage, laughing out loud, fangs half out, the Beast halfway there.

David had to choose:

  • A clean shot to the Anarch's head,
  • or try to close in and negotiate.

He chose the shot.

The Anarch went down.

But first, he pulled the trigger with the hand that held the gun against Emily's neck.

It wasn't a dramatic death. It was fast, dirty, no speech. That's what hurts David most.

By the time he reached her, she was already on the floor.

Emily, dying, looked at him. And in that second, her ears filling with noise and the world narrowing, she recognized him:

Not as a “vampire,” not as a “monster.”

She recognized him as her father.

What came out, in a broken voice, wasn't epic. It was simple:

“You did… come… after all…”

And she faded out.

In theory, David had another option: he could have Embraced her.

He didn't.

He knew that wouldn't be saving her, but damning her to the same hell as him.

And that's what truly haunts him: he decided it was better to let her die than to drag her into his world.

pages.name: Why She Is a Lost Anchor

text.content:
Since then:

  • Emily is no longer alive.
  • He can't call her, can't visit her, can't spy on her life and console himself thinking “at least she's still out there.”
  • All that's left is:
    • the grave,
    • the case file,
    • the memories of watching her as a little girl, playing with toys he paid for anonymously.

As a Lost Anchor / dead Touchstone:

  • Every time the chronicle touches on:

    • daughters,
    • broken families,
    • people who die for getting too close to the truth,

    David goes quiet, walks off, or turns hard, and that night he doesn't help the coterie (see “When He Breaks” in @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}).

  • If a situation reminds him too much of Emily, he responds with disproportionate harshness or, the other way around, with a compassion that breaks his code.

The nightmares aren't subtle. They're variations on the same hell:

  1. The hallway nightmare
    • He's in the same apartment building.
    • He hears gunshots, footsteps, young voices.
    • He's always a few seconds late.
    • Sometimes he sees Emily standing, sometimes already on the floor, but the worst is when she turns her back on him and walks out through a door David never reaches.
  2. The nightmare of the Embrace that never was
    • Emily is dying and he feeds her his blood.
    • She opens her eyes, gets up…
    • but she isn't his daughter: she's an unhinged Brujah who hates him for turning her.
    • She accuses him: “You didn't save me. You stole my death.”
    • He wakes with high Hunger, his hands dug into the mattress.
  3. The replacement nightmare
    • He sees Helen, or any other young human, in Emily's place.
    • The apartment scene plays out again.
    • Sometimes he misses the shot, sometimes he kills the innocent, sometimes everyone dies.
    • The feeling when he wakes is always the same: “I'm going to do it again. I'm going to repeat the pattern.”

The nightmares aren't rolled: they're seen. David shows up late to the meeting, knuckles split from the hangar wall, and explains nothing. Bear knows why, if anyone asks.

If the Storyteller has to roll a Compulsion or frenzy for him that night, the first Resolve or Composure roll takes a one-time penalty.

pages.name: How She Affects David at the Table

text.content:
• He feels a mix of hatred and need toward his role as enforcer:
    • he knows that life indirectly killed his daughter,
    • but he also believes that if he'd been faster, more brutal, more unbending… maybe he would have saved her.
  • With young women who remind him of Emily:
    • he tends to be overprotective,
    • or brutally cold, so as not to repeat the attachment.
  • When someone suggests “using” mortals as bait, as hostages, as tools:
    • the Storyteller can call for a roll to resist frenzy,
    • or have his Brujah anger flare against whoever treats mortals as disposable, even a PC.

Emily, as a Lost Anchor, is no longer available to “raise his Humanity.” What she does is the opposite:

  • Remind him that he can lose everything even when he does “the right thing.”
  • Sharpen the question: “Is the Masquerade really worth it, if the cost is lives like hers?”

• Seattle and her childhood. Doc 24 says David watched her leave school from his car and kept a close watch on her as she grew up (the '60s and '70s). The timeline in doc 17 places him outside the U.S. from 1970 to 2010, folio 14 of @UUID[JournalEntry.kzeWNRBY6tgLP37S]{Journal of M. Vance, Marseille, 1963, Folio 14 (Typewritten Copy)} puts him in Marseille in 1963 with “a daughter across the sea,” and doc 16 gives as provisional that he arrived in Seattle in the '80s.
  • The mother. Doc 24 doesn't name the mother or say where Emily was born; Anne Smith and San Diego come from @UUID[JournalEntry.woF61Oy8f19xxrkA]{Emily Smith's Obituary} and are provisional (doc 16).
  • The father in the obituary. @UUID[JournalEntry.woF61Oy8f19xxrkA]{Emily Smith's Obituary} calls him “Navy Sergeant”; the earlier sources, a SEAL commando.
  • The Anarch. Doc 24 doesn't give him a name; docs 00–16 call him Ray Dorsey (@UUID[JournalEntry.LqMKPCSaUzAWcGYi]{Ray Dorsey}) and add Rosa and Hal.
  • The kid. Doc 24 mentions “two kids” dead on the floor and Marcos; in docs 00–16 Marcos Delgado is the only kid who survived (consistent).
Cemetery north of the city · Map: no

A plain gray granite headstone on a hillside of cedars. EMILY ROSE SMITH · 1958–1996 · “She took in the ones nobody wanted.” The grass is trimmed. At the foot of the stone lies a bouquet of fresh flowers, wrapped in newspaper, still beaded with rain.

The fresh flowers are the heart of @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.cGEW4b4hCJlaDeSK]{GAN-12 · The Visited Grave}. Who leaves them is left open for the chronicle (Marcos from @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.pCLncsxglYsxJtbu]{GAN-01 · The Boy Who Survived}, someone from Salt's, or someone who signs “M.V.”).

It appears in the Epilogue of @UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File} as one of the three possible codas.

Use as a lost Touchstone: if the coterie brings David, the visit leaves him a little more at peace, but it also makes him ask himself a question he doesn't want to ask. He may ask it out loud, to whoever brought him.

The ending depends on two things: how the Council ended (@UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}) and what happened to the File (@UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.tG1m5PTkmBA1pvmc]{A4-E03 · The Last Ferry}). The Storyteller cross-references the two on this table.
