pages.name: FIN-A · The Truth Before the Throne

text.content:
@UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway} falls. Prince @UUID[JournalEntry.sCVTjJFrnyyVnQDt]{Whitmore} declares him a traitor before the Primogen and gives him a choice between exile and a Blood Hunt. If the coterie captured him, the Sheriff destroys him that same night at the farm (@UUID[JournalEntry.NNzMhIvsavpG0iTQ]{The Sheriff's Farm and Boat Landing}), with no witnesses. If he fled, he becomes an enemy outside the city with resources, patience, and a grudge.

Consequences:

  • Each member of the coterie gains Status (Camarilla) +1; +2 for whoever presented the case. @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David} is cleared before the court, and the court now knows who he works with.
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Montgomery} owes the coterie a major favor. He crosses the first name off his list.
  • (FIRSTLIGHT loses its source).
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.yaAsxCkCLf8CANL5]{Voight} offers the coterie a standing alliance against the Inquisition: Contacts 1 or Mawla (Voight) 1 for whoever accepts.
  • Halloway Meridian Capital is left headless. @UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{Celeste}, if she survived and sided with the coterie, can take a piece of it: Resources +2. Her Blood Bond to Halloway breaks.
  • Whitmore stays on the throne, but everyone knows someone else saved him. His Status drops and the city starts talking about succession.
  • If the File was also destroyed (FIN-A + FIN-C): the consequences of @UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO.JournalEntryPage.xgVY2zlstK7IN1Rp]{FIN-C · Cleansing Fire} for Helen apply as well.

@UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway} becomes Regent of Seattle, with the recognition of Justicar @UUID[JournalEntry.gSMgBLLYggWyAN2W]{Panhard} if the File reached @UUID[JournalEntry.CRdeqlwyfpxGPyzT]{Duval}. @UUID[JournalEntry.sCVTjJFrnyyVnQDt]{Whitmore} abdicates “for health reasons,” like @UUID[JournalEntry.FOgT9FF3NF7ZHdCa]{Grange} in 1962, and vanishes from the city. If the coterie made a deal with Halloway, @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David} is named Sheriff and the coterie receives the domain of Harbor Island.

Consequences:

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Montgomery} becomes a declared enemy. That same night he starts working through his list. The chronicle becomes a cold war between the new court and the old Sheriff and his Wolves (@UUID[JournalEntry.azX1hjbc0PUp2AA2.JournalEntryPage.bxduXJhh2oXcM6Uy]{COT-01 · Whitmore's Wolves}).
  • If the coterie made the deal: each PC who accepted gains Status +2, but takes 2 Stains for selling out the ones who protected them, and makes the Remorse test at the end of the session. David accepts the post and stops being the same man: play him as someone who changed masters because his own people asked him to. @UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Bear} asks him for a talk that night, at the hangar (see Coda 3 of the Epilogue).
  • FIRSTLIGHT still has ARCHER inside the court, now as Prince. The Inquisition and the Seattle Camarilla are, without knowing it, on the same side. The Thermometer doesn't change, but it doesn't rise again while Halloway reigns.
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{Celeste}, if she was handed over as a traitor and survived, is placed in the custody of the new Sheriff... who is David, and with him the coterie.
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen} stays alive, but the new Prince knows who she is. The chronicle has a permanent problem.

The File disappears: dumped in the Sound, burned, or wiped. The coterie also takes care of the thumb drives, @UUID[JournalEntry.dj4gIszHHTN1QRKk]{Thornquist}'s duplicates, and the cold subject database. No one can use it anymore: not @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway}, not the Inquisition, not the Justicar.

Consequences:

  • . The Seattle Masquerade is safer than ever.
  • Twelve years of @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen}'s work are gone. The Lake City mothers, Danny Ruiz, all the cases nobody else looked at. If they tell her, Helen has to decide what to do with what's left: her memory. Remorse test for @UUID[JournalEntry.rg50DlMYSzgbZeBv]{Nadia}, if she's in play. Helen is @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David}'s Touchstone, and the coterie destroyed what she made: David is shaken, and his relationship with Helen is damaged. Whether it can be repaired depends on what the coterie does next.
  • If Halloway won the Council, his regency lacks the proof the Justicar asked for: @UUID[JournalEntry.gSMgBLLYggWyAN2W]{Panhard} doesn't recognize it. Seattle is left in political limbo, with two Kindred who both claim to be the authority. Chronicle hook.
  • The coterie gains +1 Humanity if one of them offers to tell Helen in person, without Disciplines.

The File, or enough of it, ends up in the hands of @UUID[JournalEntry.bJA2iRyDgbm2TcuK]{Dana Okafor}. FIRSTLIGHT now has twelve years of evidence, hunting maps, photos, and names. The Puget Cell asks national headquarters for reinforcements. Within two weeks there are three cells in the city.

Consequences:

  • Thermometer 10. Purge. In the first week at least one Camarilla haven falls (the Storyteller chooses; if the coterie doesn't move, theirs).
  • Every PC who appears in the File loses Mask −1 and Haven −1 until they relocate.
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.sCVTjJFrnyyVnQDt]{Whitmore}, if he's still Prince, closes Elysium. The court scatters. @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway}, if he survived, has nothing left to gain: he vanishes from the city.
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen} gets a visit from Okafor. They offer her a job. What she decides is the first hook of the new chronicle.

Crossover with Hunter

The chronicle changes tone: survival. If you want to cross it over with Hunter: The Reckoning (H5), this is the moment: the coterie becomes the quarry, and the hunters from your supplement become the pursuers.

journal.name: Epilogue · What the Water Doesn't Take

pages.name: Epilogue · What the Water Doesn't Take

text.content: One week later. Choose one of these three codas based on the ending (@UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO]{Endings of the Climax}), or read all three if the session allows. Each one plays as a short scene, five or ten minutes, with no tests.

For @UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO.JournalEntryPage.UnOqmjERvnxNb7gL]{FIN-A · The Truth Before the Throne} or @UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO.JournalEntryPage.xgVY2zlstK7IN1Rp]{FIN-C · Cleansing Fire}, or if @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David}'s story with @UUID[JournalEntry.VYpDoFtqKkL7FlqL]{Emily} was the heart of the adventure. Location: Emily Smith's grave (@UUID[JournalEntry.uhtM1iF2WrHHlcd8]{Emily Smith's Grave}). Play it with the PCs who go with David.

The cedar hillside is wet and silent. The grass around the gray granite headstone has just been cut. EMILY ROSE SMITH · 1958–1996 · “She stayed with the ones nobody wanted.” At its foot, a bouquet of fresh flowers wrapped in newspaper. There are still raindrops on them. Someone was here less than an hour ago.

Notes: the coterie decides whether to wait with David to see who brings the flowers next time (@UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.cGEW4b4hCJlaDeSK]{GAN-12 · The Visited Grave}) or to let it be. David doesn't ask. If @UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{Krell} survived and is an ally, he may be some distance off, among the trees, not coming closer. If @UUID[JournalEntry.WHkwE8CYfaKW5WyO]{Rosa} confessed in @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.aJxUAHXcYpRWrhmG]{A2-E03 · Salt's}, the flowers are hers. Ask the players what they do. This is the last image of David's story in this adventure.

For any ending in which @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen} is still alive.

[THEME MUSIC. 12 seconds. Fades under the voice.]

“This episode isn't the one I promised you. The one I promised you was about three kids from Crown Hill and a mother who says her son was afraid of needles. That episode exists. I'm going to put it out. But not this week.

This week I want to tell you about something I learned. I learned there are files you can't keep on a drive. That there are people who watch and people who look after, and sometimes they're the same people, and sometimes they're not. That the city has blue eyes that don't blink.

[pause]

And I learned that someone who always shows up late does, sometimes, show up.

This is ‘What the City Forgets.’ I'm Helen Ward. I'm still watching.”

[THEME MUSIC. End.]

Notes: the episode's content changes with the ending. In @UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO.JournalEntryPage.xgVY2zlstK7IN1Rp]{FIN-C · Cleansing Fire}, Helen talks about what she lost. In @UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO.JournalEntryPage.on9MlxGjJpFF8yf2]{FIN-D · Red Tide}, the episode never airs: the recording cuts off when someone knocks at the door. In @UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO.JournalEntryPage.RqeQkW5KfFjPYFhg]{FIN-B · The Hound Changes Masters}, Helen says nothing at all: she airs the Crown Hill episode. @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David}, listening with the coterie, turns off the radio: he knows someone asked her not to talk. If @UUID[JournalEntry.rg50DlMYSzgbZeBv]{Nadia} is a PC, she's at the mixing board.

For any ending. Essential if @UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Bear} was taken hostage, if there was a raid, or if the coterie made a deal with Halloway. Location: the Harbor Island hangar (@UUID[JournalEntry.104UV0anmZHNCTrD]{The Harbor Island Hangar}).

The hangar smells of gun oil, salt, and reheated coffee. Bear is at his workbench, cleaning a pistol that's already clean. He doesn't look up. On the bench, next to the parts, is a notebook page folded in quarters, worn thin along the creases. Bear looks at it, then at David, then goes back to the pistol. “There's coffee,” he says. “If you want some.”

Notes: the page is @UUID[JournalEntry.5mQIPoGa4I0tQtbR]{Note Kept in Bear's Safe}. Bear took it out of the safe. What happens depends on the adventure: if the coterie, with David at its side, crossed a line (@UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO.JournalEntryPage.RqeQkW5KfFjPYFhg]{FIN-B · The Hound Changes Masters}, a massacre, Dominate used on Helen), Bear gives it to David to read, in front of them. If not, he puts it away again without a word and pours him a coffee. Both options are the right ending.

To close the final session, after whichever coda you choose.

Three weeks later, an envelope with no return address arrives at the hangar, postmarked Cluj-Napoca, Romania. Heavy paper, yellowed. Inside, a single handwritten line, in a hand David knows better than his own: “There are two. You already know. Finish the lesson.” And beneath it, two initials: M. V.

End of The Ward File. The chronicle continues in @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.Y1E4i0kdsA7wcPIj]{GAN-10 · Letters from Cluj}.

Sheet: @UUID[Actor.dd9CRIHVGO38YUhN]{Ethan Montgomery}

“I am the guardian between the Beast and the city. If one wakes, the other falls.”

Clan: Gangrel · Position: Sheriff of Seattle · Sect: Camarilla (out of personal loyalty to the Prince)

pages.name: Mortal Days: The Man Who Could Smell Footsteps

text.content: He was born in 1845 to a family of settlers on the Rogue River, in Oregon Territory. He learned to track before he learned to read. By twenty he was already working for the army and the railroad companies, running down outlaws, deserters, and horse thieves, and on the frontier they said that if Montgomery was on your trail, it didn't matter how fast you ran. In 1885 he spent three weeks hunting a killer of travelers near Eureka. When he finally caught up with him, he discovered that his quarry wasn't a man.

The nomad Gangrel Elijah Kane (@UUID[JournalEntry.dHE63u1Rtqst0CLb]{Elijah Kane}) spared his life because he found him interesting and Embraced him because he found him useful. Montgomery spent eighteen years roaming the coast with him. In 1903, after the San Francisco earthquake, he entered the service of the Camarilla and never left it. In 1978, Whitmore named him Sheriff of Seattle to replace O'Connor.

Since then he has kept the city clean without asking for anything in return. When his clan broke with the Camarilla, he stayed. He didn't do it for the Prince, whom he considers weak, but for the city, which he considers his. Now he is tired and afraid, though he would never say so. The theft of the File and the ashes on the docks smell to him like something he can't name.

The list. Montgomery has written down the names of eleven Kindred he will destroy the night Whitmore falls, before anyone can stop him. The first is Halloway.

Watching the Hound. Since 1996 he has received a monthly report on David, first from several bounty hunters and, for years now, from his childe Hal (@UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{Halvard “Hal” Brekke}). He trusts David more than anyone, and that is exactly why he never stops watching him.

Vance? He knows Vance only by reputation and genuinely fears him. If David's sire is alive and in the city, Montgomery believes David's loyalty will split in two. Halloway exploits exactly that fear.

The Larchmont. He was the one who ordered the cistern sealed with seven bodies inside (@UUID[JournalEntry.Oiln4o98kvxKbOvS]{The Larchmont Building}). If that comes out, he falls, and probably the Prince with him.

A farm in the Snohomish Valley with a tunnel down to a boat landing on the river (@UUID[JournalEntry.NNzMhIvsavpG0iTQ]{The Sheriff's Farm and Boat Landing}; Haven 3). He feeds on the line between rural and urban: truckers at rest areas, hunters in the woods, the occasional deer when the Hunger bites and there are no humans around. He never feeds inside the city, because he says the Sheriff doesn't hunt where he patrols.

The bounty hunters (@UUID[Actor.L1oU4dlqHg8Yszon]{Montgomery's Bounty Hunters}; Herd 2): six mortals, ex-military and ex-cops, who know him as “the Boss.”

The dogs: twelve ghouled working dogs that sense and obey his will (Animalism).

Contacts 3: state police, the port, and security firms. They cover up deaths and steer investigations elsewhere.

Allies 3: David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}).

@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith} (respect). He calls him “Hound,” and he doesn't mean it as an insult. He sees in him what he himself would be if he lost his soul.

@UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{Hal Brekke} (pride). He has never told him so. He makes Hal hand over the reports on David and knows Hal hates him for it.

@UUID[JournalEntry.sCVTjJFrnyyVnQDt]{Marcus Whitmore} (loyalty). He doesn't respect him. He serves him because the alternative is worse.

@UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Charles Halloway} (contempt). He thinks he's a snake in a suit. What he lacks is the proof to act.

@UUID[JournalEntry.oQ2AhEeDkwdPRv71]{Liam O'Connor} (guilt). He took his post without asking questions. He knows he should have asked them.

• “Montgomery turns into a wolf on moonlit nights and hunts in the Snohomish woods.” (Half true: he doesn't turn into a wolf, but he does hunt in the woods.)
  • “The Sheriff has a list of eleven names.” (True.)
  • “Montgomery and the Hound have been lovers since the '70s.” (False: David came to Seattle in the '80s. What binds them is respect and debt.)
  • “The Sheriff knows what happened at the Larchmont and covered it up.” (True.)

To the mortal world he is Ethan Montgomery, a retired private security consultant and breeder of working dogs (Mask 2). He looks about forty. He's heavyset, with weathered skin, a short graying beard, and enormous hands. He wears flannel shirts, a waxed jacket, and work boots. He speaks little and slowly, and holds your gaze one second longer than is comfortable. Under stress, his eyes turn amber (metamorphosis scars).

• Sire: @UUID[JournalEntry.dHE63u1Rtqst0CLb]{Elijah Kane}
  • Embraced: 1885 (born 1845)
  • Ambition: for Seattle to outlive its Prince.
  • Convictions: “The Beast doesn't rule: it is mastered” · “No lawless monster deserves the gift of the night”.
  • Touchstones: Dr. Lucy Harlan, a Snohomish veterinarian who treats his dogs and makes him coffee he never drinks.
  • Humanity: 5
  • Generation: 8th
  • Blood Potency: 5

Attributes: Strength 4, Dexterity 4, Stamina 5 · Charisma 2, Manipulation 3, Composure 5 · Intelligence 3, Wits 4, Resolve 3

Secondary Attributes: Health 8 · Willpower 8

Skills: Firearms 4 (Sniper), Athletics 3, Awareness 4 (Supernatural tracking), Streetwise 2, Intimidation 3, Leadership 3 (Authority through respect), Occult 2 (Limits of the Beast), Brawl 4 (Savage combat), Stealth 3, Survival 5 (Tracking), Animal Ken 4 (Dogs)

Disciplines:

  • Animalism 3: Bond Famulus (Bond Famulus), Feral Whispers (Feral Whispers), Quell the Beast (Quell the Beast)
  • Fortitude 4: Resilience (Resilience), Unswayable Mind (Unswayable Mind), Toughness (Toughness), Defy Bane (Defy Bane)
  • Protean 3: Eyes of the Beast (Eyes of the Beast), Feral Weapons (Feral Weapons), Earth Meld (Earth Meld)

Flaws: metamorphosis scars (amber eyes under stress); Predatory instinct (frenzy test when he smells fresh human blood, Difficulty 2); Distrust of neonates (−1 die on Social tests with Kindred under 50 years old).

Source: doc 22, “⚖️ Sheriff Ethan Montgomery” (earlier source, predating docs 00–16). Where it conflicts with doc 06, doc 06 wins; see the last page.

Alias: “The Sentinel of Puget Sound”

Clan: Gangrel

Generation: 8th

Sect: Camarilla

Position: Sheriff of Seattle

Apparent age: 40

Actual age: ~180

Date of birth: 1845

Date of Embrace: 1885

Place of Embrace: Northern California coast, Oregon border

🩸 Background and History

Ethan Montgomery was a tracker before he was a hunter. He was born into a family of pioneers of the American West who settled near the Rogue River.

He grew up close to nature and to the violence that survival demanded in territories contested by humans, beasts, and, unbeknownst to him, the children of Caine.

During the railroad expansion, Montgomery worked as a tracker and outlaw hunter for the army and private companies.

His talent for following human quarry made him a local legend:

“If Montgomery's on your trail, it doesn't matter how fast you run, he can already smell you.”

In 1885, he hunted a killer who was slaughtering travelers near Eureka.

When he finally caught up with him, he discovered that his quarry wasn't human. The vampire he was hunting beat him easily, but before killing him, found him... fascinating.

He offered him “a new way to hunt.”

That was his Embrace, under the tutelage of a nomad Gangrel named Elijah Kane, who trained him in Cainite survival.

For decades, Ethan roamed the West Coast eliminating Sabbat, out-of-control childer, and monsters that threatened the Masquerade.

His disciplined nature caught the attention of the Prince of Seattle, Marcus Whitmore, who named him Sheriff in 1978.

🧠 Personality

Montgomery is a man of few words, with an almost animal presence.

His calm is as unsettling as his restrained violence.

He treats the city's vampires as predators allowed to live under his watch, not as citizens.

He has a professional respect for @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}, whom he considers “the younger version of what I'd be if I lost my soul.”

To neonates, Sheriff Montgomery is a figure of fear and respect.

To the Elders, he is a living weapon of the Camarilla that keeps both the Sabbat and the rebel Brujah in check.

  • Conviction: “The Beast must not rule; not mine, not yours.”

🕯️ Backgrounds

Trait Value Description
Status (Camarilla) •••• Respected Sheriff, Prince Whitmore's enforcer.
Herd •• A network of bounty hunters and human watchers under his command.
Haven ••• Fortified farm on the outskirts of Seattle, with tunnels connected to a private boat landing.
Allies (David Smith) ••• A relationship of tactical trust and mutual respect.
Contacts (State police, private agencies) ••• Uses his human networks to cover up deaths and conceal operations.

⚠️ Flaws

  • Metamorphosis scars: his eyes change color under the moon or under stress (2 pts).

  • Predatory instinct: must make frenzy tests when he smells fresh human blood (2 pts).

  • Distrust of neonates: –1 penalty to Social tests with vampires under 50 years old (1 pt).

Total: 5 points of Flaws—a balance against his power.

🩸 Relationship with David Smith

  • Considers Smith his “unofficial right hand.”

  • Calls him “Hound” (out of respect).

  • Montgomery avoids manipulating him: he trusts his morals and his coldness.

  • In combat, they're the perfect duo: the beast and the reason.

“Smith hunts to keep the balance.

I hunt so the balance doesn't destroy him.”

— Ethan Montgomery, private conversation with Archon Duval (@UUID[JournalEntry.CRdeqlwyfpxGPyzT]{Archon Duval}) (2017).

(Doc 22 includes a portrait of Montgomery here, not exported.)

🩸 KINDRED IDENTIFICATION

Name: Ethan Montgomery

Known aliases: The Sentinel of Puget Sound, Whitmore's Wolf

Clan: Gangrel

Generation: 8th

Sect: Camarilla

Position: Sheriff of Seattle

Known residences: Fortified haven on the outskirts of the city, underground connection to a private boat landing.

Current status: Active, in permanent service since 1978.

⚰️ CHRONOLOGICAL DATA

Event Date Detail
Mortal birth 1845 Oregon Territory, USA — son of settlers.
Mortal occupation 1865–1885 Professional tracker and hunter; known as “the man who sniffs out the footsteps of the dead.”
Embrace 1885 By Elijah Kane (nomad Gangrel), after surviving an attack by a predatory Kindred on the frontier.
Age at death (apparent) 40 Sturdy build, weather-beaten features.
True age approx. 180
Joined the Camarilla 1903 Joint operations in San Francisco after the earthquake.
Appointed Sheriff 1978 By direct decree of Prince Whitmore.
Last confirmed activity 2025 Confirmed in an operation against an Anarch cell in Everett.

⚔️ BLOOD PROFILE

  • Blood Potency: 5

  • Humanity: 5

  • Willpower: 8

  • Convictions:

    1. “The Beast doesn't rule: it is mastered.”

    2. “Only balance keeps the hunt alive.”

    3. “No lawless monster deserves the gift of the night.”

  • Gangrel Compulsion: Feral Impulses—his Beast manifests physically during moments of frenzy or rage.

🦴 PSYCHOLOGICAL AND BEHAVIORAL PROFILE

Montgomery displays an unusual balance between discipline and wild nature.

He speaks little and observes much.

His temperament is not explosive like a Brujah's, but glacial and methodical, with an instinctive command of his surroundings.

He treats the Kindred of the domain as predators under control, not as subjects.

He maintains a silent chain of command:

  • Ghouls and human bounty hunters know him only as “the Boss.”

  • Vampires see him as the invisible authority behind the executions that cleanse the city.

His sense of justice is pragmatic, not moral: he doesn't judge, he neutralizes.

The Primogen recognize his effectiveness but fear his independence.

🐺 DOMINANT DISCIPLINES

Fortitude (4): Supernatural resilience and physical dominance.

Animalism (3): Communication with beasts and instinctive control of groups.

Protean (3): Physical mutability, animal senses, and blending into the terrain.

💬 “Montgomery doesn't need weapons.

His body is the weapon, and the Beast his shield.”

— Report by the Ventrue Primogen, Charles Halloway.

🩸 KEY SKILLS

  • Survival 5—Supernatural tracking and total adaptation to the environment.

  • Brawl 4—Brutal close-quarters combat, geared toward incapacitating quickly.

  • Alertness 4—Advanced, instinctive night perception.

  • Firearms 4—Effective sniper, though he prefers live quarry.

  • Intimidation 3—Predatory presence with no need for words.

  • Leadership 3—Respect earned through effectiveness, not rank.

🕯️ BACKGROUNDS

Trait Value Description
Status (Camarilla) •••• Respected Sheriff of the domain.
Allies (David Smith) ••• A relationship of mutual trust; uses him as an outside enforcer.
Herd •• A network of bounty hunters and human watchers.
Contacts (State police / ports / contractors) ••• Covering up vampire incidents.
Haven ••• Fortified property on the outskirts of the city, with underground access.

⚠️ RECORDED FLAWS

Flaw Level Description
Metamorphosis scars 2 Animal features (amber eyes, hardened nails) visible under stress.
Predatory instinct 2 Prone to frenzy when he smells fresh blood.
Distrust of neonates 1 Social penalty in dealings with young vampires.
Total 5 points Offsets his high Potency status and abilities.

💀 JUSTICAR'S ASSESSMENT

“Montgomery represents what the Camarilla needs and fears in equal measure:

a predator who remembers why we're still alive.

If he ever turns against us, the city will not see the dawn.”

— Justicar Helena Panhard (@UUID[JournalEntry.gSMgBLLYggWyAN2W]{Justicar Helena Panhard}), confidential assessment, 2019.

📎 INTERNAL COMMENTS

  • Relationship with David Smith: close, based on tactical respect.

    • Montgomery trusts him with cleanup operations.

    • Both share a philosophy: violence as balance, not chaos.

  • Attitude toward the Prince: loyal, but critical.

    • Considers Whitmore a weak politician, but necessary to maintain the facade.

  • Current situation: keeps Anarch cells in Everett and rumors of a residual Sabbat in Tacoma under surveillance.

🩸 FILE EPITAPH

“I am the guardian between the Beast and the city.

If one wakes, the other falls.”

— Ethan Montgomery, record of his oath before Prince Whitmore (1978).

The doc 06 wins. What the earlier source (doc 22) says differently:

  • Mental Attributes. Doc 22 gives “Perception 4, Intelligence 3, Wits 3” (Perception doesn't exist in V5); doc 06, Intelligence 3, Wits 4, Resolve 3.
  • Disciplines. Doc 22 gives Fortitude 4 (Resilience, Deny Pain, Marble Skin, Unbreakable Armor) and Animalism 3 (Feral Whispers, Call of the Alpha, Pack Bond); doc 06, Fortitude (Resilience, Unswayable Mind, Toughness, Defy Bane) and Animalism (Bond Famulus, Feral Whispers, Quell the Beast). Protean matches.
  • Skills. Doc 22 has no Athletics, Streetwise, Stealth, or Animal Ken; it gives Survival 5 with the specialty “Urban and wilderness environments” (doc 06: “Tracking”).
  • Convictions. Doc 22 gives three; doc 06 keeps two and leaves out “Only balance keeps the hunt alive.” Doc 22 also has another: “The Beast must not rule; not mine, not yours.”
  • Backgrounds. Doc 22 adds Status (Camarilla) 4, which doc 06 doesn't give. The rest matches (Herd 2, Haven 3, Allies 3 David Smith, Contacts 3).
  • Flaws. They match; doc 22 assigns them values (2, 2, and 1 points).
  • Place of Embrace. Doc 22 says “Northern California coast, Oregon border” and, in the file, “Oregon Territory” as his place of birth; doc 06 places it near Eureka (the pursuit) and gives the Rogue River as his origin. Compatible.
  • Current situation. Doc 22 mentions Anarch cells in Everett and rumors of a residual Sabbat in Tacoma (verified in 2025). Docs 00–16 don't mention that Sabbat in Tacoma.

Sheet: @UUID[Actor.zGqiDTb68QRTrlLv]{Ezra Lund}

Concept: network security engineer, Embraced by the Underground's information broker.

Ezra worked six years for a big cloud company in South Lake Union. In 2018 he discovered that thousands of Seattle doorbell cameras were sending video to a server that didn't appear in any contract. He reported it internally. Two weeks later they fired him for a made-up “policy violation,” and no company in the city ever answered him again.

Abel Thornquist (@UUID[JournalEntry.dj4gIszHHTN1QRKk]{Abel Thornquist}) Embraced him in 2019. He wanted someone who could see the city's digital nervous system the way he sees the tunnels. Ezra lives in the Sealed Underground (@UUID[JournalEntry.jg1zpvYlDFMJRY8Q]{The Sealed Underground (Seattle Underground)}), among recycled servers and cables that run down through 19th-century holes. He sells information with no face and no name. His Mask is an anonymous account on a dozen forums. He feeds on blood bags he gets by hacking a blood bank's inventory (Bagger).
The File has a thermal camera capture showing a figure with no body heat going into a manhole in Pioneer Square. It's him.

Ambition: expose whoever controls the city's cameras. Desire: for someone to see his face and not look away. Suggested Conviction: “Information belongs to whoever needs it, not whoever pays for it.” Touchstone: his sister Maja, a night-shift nurse, who leaves food at his door even though she knows he doesn't eat it.
Contacts (hackers) 2, Herd 1, Haven 2 (in the Underground), Mawla (Thornquist) 1. Advantage: feed from bags without penalty.

@UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.lM1EiE1FoXMkf3Uo]{A1-E04 · Everything Sells Below}, @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.wIpc0OR2nQf7WDFO]{A1-E05 · The City's Eyes}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center}. He's the natural specialist for @UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.qA75WygzgVjOeJvT]{LOR-03 · The City's Eyes} The City's Eyes.
In 2017, as a contractor, Ezra wrote the firmware for Gale Sentinel's cameras. The back door Preston Gale uses is his code. Ezra suspects it, but he's never confirmed it.

journal.name: From the Other Side · FIRSTLIGHT Interludes

pages.name: From the Other Side · FIRSTLIGHT Interludes

text.content:
Three playable interludes with the hunters of the Puget Cell (@UUID[JournalEntry.dnsWkdXVJ19riBLa.JournalEntryPage.O8yPSIYLlTrKHm8G]{The Puget Cell}). For how and when to use them, see @UUID[JournalEntry.dnsWkdXVJ19riBLa]{Playable FIRSTLIGHT}. For what they leave behind for the raid, see @UUID[JournalEntry.dnsWkdXVJ19riBLa.JournalEntryPage.8DXPPUEUUp5bHka5]{INT-00 · Advantages and Cracks for the Raid}. For the character sheets, see @UUID[JournalEntry.LfywH6qtS3GxDxJx]{The Puget Cell · Pregenerated Characters}.

This entire journal is new content. The schedules, the van, and what appears on the recordings are Proposed except where a doc is cited.

Storyteller Context

Play this when the Thermometer reaches 3 (👁 Someone Is Watching the Journalist). FIRSTLIGHT puts @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen} under passive surveillance: a van outside her building on Market Street (@UUID[JournalEntry.YD0Td8Y9aJyIpGSl]{Helen Ward's Apartment}), occasional drones, and an analyst who listens closely to her podcast. That much is in the docs. What follows is that night, from inside the van.

Proposed: the van is white, no rear windows, with the logo of a fiber-optic company that doesn't exist. It arrives at dusk the night after the threshold is crossed and parks half a block down, across from the closed hardware store. It stays until seven.

The interlude has two parts. The footage: Hale pulls from Northline what the Gale Sentinel doorbell cameras recorded on Market Street in the early hours of the theft, and the players watch, from the outside, the scene their vampires played in @UUID[JournalEntry.w9xeQJg6psfiMjFU.JournalEntryPage.yyXMKcpDOIhGuZIB]{A0-E01 · The Call from SAFE}. The street: the stakeout itself, with whatever Helen does and whatever the coterie does.

Who's there: @UUID[Actor.yyJApTmnANPPdw3O]{Pak} on the drone and the screens, @UUID[JournalEntry.D611Mcr17F6HHEUw]{Hale} on the headphones, @UUID[Actor.cacjzuu13Bv7mJH5]{Navarro} on the window camera, @UUID[Actor.5ywnpdrw93wmy235]{Ransom} behind the wheel. @UUID[Actor.2hdWrhkD65ZNl4Xs]{Sorensen}, if someone's playing her, rides shotgun because she knows the street: she grew up four blocks away. @UUID[JournalEntry.bJA2iRyDgbm2TcuK]{Okafor} is at Northline, on the radio.

The rain sounds like gravel on the roof of the van. Inside, it smells of cold coffee and hot plastic. Three screens: the street in green, the street in gray, the street as a heat map where everything alive is orange. Across the way, above a closed hardware store, there's a third-floor window. Hale has one earphone in and the other dangling. In the one she's wearing, a woman is talking about a man who doesn't age.

What the Hunters Want

  • Hale: cross-reference the voice from episode 112 with what she sees on the screens. If there's a pattern, she wants to be the first to see it.
  • Pak: prove the drone sees more than the van. Always.
  • Navarro: see one. Prove Tucson wasn't made up.
  • Ransom: work the shift, ask no questions, go back to the warehouse. And yet he asks.
  • Sorensen: get paid for the night. And not be recognized by anyone from the street.
  • Okafor (by radio): a clean report. “Facts. Theories tomorrow.”

The Footage

Hale requests from Northline the ANOMALY logs for Market Street between 2:30 and 4:30 a.m. on Night 1. What they see depends on what the coterie did in @UUID[JournalEntry.w9xeQJg6psfiMjFU.JournalEntryPage.yyXMKcpDOIhGuZIB]{A0-E01 · The Call from SAFE}:

In A0-E01 the coterie… What's on the footage
Left down the hallway without touching the 3B camera Three COLD_SUBJECT alerts in the third-floor hallway, one after another. Gray silhouettes in an orange hallway. Among them, a warm figure: Helen. The faces are only half visible
Smashed the camera The last image: a hand moving faster than it should. Before that, nothing useful
Disconnected the camera carefully, or left by the fire escape No alerts. Northline only receives alerts, not video. The only odd thing is the disconnection log for the whole block, from 2:52 to 3:03 (): eleven clean minutes. Hale circles it
Used Obfuscate in front of the camera The camera records the others, not whoever used it. A door in the hallway that opens by itself. Hale watches it four times

In every case, a doorbell camera on the opposite sidewalk records two things without triggering an alert, because they're warm: a pickup truck parked half a block down, with a big man at the wheel who never gets out (@UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Bear}), and a gray electric car with someone inside, which leaves at 4:10 (the watcher from @UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{Halloway's Security Ghouls}). The hunters don't know who either of them is.

The Street

After the footage, the night. What happens depends on where Helen is:

  • Helen is at home. At 1:20 a.m. she goes down to buy cigarettes at the gas station on the corner. If any of the coterie's vampires is with her that night, ask the player what they do: the hunters see it from the van. On the thermal screen, whoever walks beside Helen isn't orange.
  • Helen is with the coterie. The third-floor window is dark. Ask the table whether any of their vampires went back that night for clothes, papers, or the cat. If someone did, the hunters see them go in. If no one did, it's a stakeout: rain, coffee, the podcast, and at 4:10 a.m., the same time as the night of the theft, the gray electric car rolls slowly past the front door and leaves.

If nothing happens on the street, the interlude is the footage and a conversation. Don't drag it out: stakeouts are boring inside the fiction, not at the table.

Tests

  • Pull something from the footage: Hale: Intelligence + Technology (Difficulty 3) (Desperation: Inquisitive). With the Perk Close Listening, +2 dice if she cross-references the footage with episode 112. On a success, the full timeline. With 3 or more successes, and only if there were alerts, a usable frame of one of the faces.
  • Watch the street: Navarro or Ransom: Wits + Awareness (Difficulty 3). With the drone up, +2 dice (@UUID[Item.bpgcVRH8MZeyFVG3]{Thermal camera drone}).
  • Fly the drone without being heard: Pak: Dexterity + Technology (Difficulty 3) (Desperation: Underground). In heavy rain, Difficulty 4.
  • Keep the van from drawing attention: if a vampire passes nearby, Ransom: Dexterity + Stealth (Difficulty 3) (Desperation: Underground, if Pak is driving) against the PC's Wits + Awareness the Storyteller calls for. At Danger 3 or higher, Difficulty 4.
  • Recognize the man in the truck: only Ransom, and only if Bear shows up on the footage. Ransom: Wits + Insight (Difficulty 2). On a success, it's Tom Whitman. They served together. He hasn't heard from him in years.

Decisions

If… Then
They put the frame in the report Okafor receives it at four and says nothing for a minute. . Advantage V1 (that PC). Desperation −1
They have it and don't upload it No one else knows. The Thermometer doesn't rise. The Cell comes back empty-handed: Desperation +1
The drone spots a vampire on the street that night It logs it as ANOMALY: , unless they've already uploaded the frame (the interlude raises it by no more than 1)
Ransom recognizes Bear and tells Okafor That's @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.NONJmwNuBweLPdPQ]{GAN-04 · The Old Comrade}, “Ransom Reports”: . Advantage V2 (the truck). Bear is marked
Ransom recognizes Bear and keeps quiet Crack F1. If you like, @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.NONJmwNuBweLPdPQ]{GAN-04 · The Old Comrade} starts here: Ransom goes looking for him at the bar by the port that same week
The coterie spots the van (the Stealth test failed with a PC nearby) Danger +1. Crack F2

How It Affects A4-E02

It can leave V1, V2, F1, and F2 (@UUID[JournalEntry.dnsWkdXVJ19riBLa.JournalEntryPage.8DXPPUEUUp5bHka5]{INT-00 · Advantages and Cracks for the Raid}). Nothing else: what's seen on Market Street doesn't reveal where the coterie is hiding.

Closing

At 6:40 a.m. the sky turns a dirty gray. Pak brings the drone down with the battery at four percent. Hale keeps one earphone in and writes in her notebook: “Why him?” Ransom starts the engine. Return to the coterie's scene where you left it.

Storyteller Notes

  • Don't show faces the coterie didn't let the camera record. If they dealt with the camera in @UUID[JournalEntry.w9xeQJg6psfiMjFU.JournalEntryPage.yyXMKcpDOIhGuZIB]{A0-E01 · The Call from SAFE}, the footage has nothing. Let that be the reward for doing it right.
  • Bear always shows up on the footage, because he stayed in the truck watching the street. Whether Ransom recognizes him depends on someone playing Ransom; if no one is, no one recognizes him.
  • The gray car is a loose end for the hunters, not for the coterie: don't resolve it. Hale can note the time. Nothing more.

Storyteller Context

Night 5, Monday, November 16, from 8:00 p.m. on. Northline (@UUID[JournalEntry.KioeAEZP78U0Coz5]{Northline Cyber Advisory}), 11th floor: three lights on and the conference room with the blinds down. ARCHER makes the second delivery through the agreed channel. It's the memo Hale signs that night: @UUID[JournalEntry.WW7eg88I0uDGj8ks]{FIRSTLIGHT, Internal Memo SEA-0411}.

Proposed: the channel is an encrypted drop box. At 8:12 p.m. a package with no sender comes in, reference SEA-0411. Inside, what DOC-07 says: three locations of interest (a rural property in the Snohomish Valley with a boat landing, a hangar on Harbor Island, a penthouse in Capitol Hill held by a cultural foundation), the claim that the source has access “to the local structure,” and the promise of the “complete index.”

At the start, apply the delivery if you haven't already: .

What's already written and doesn't change: Hale recommends treating the deliveries as possible bait (DOC-07, point 6). Okafor uses the delivery anyway, because it's all she has. What's in play is how.

The night's schedule (from the docs; it doesn't move):

  • At 11:00 p.m., nrthln_research meets a seller at a Denny's on Aurora Avenue (@UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.5Vgl8slqjXlVRbie]{A2-E06 · The One Who Kept One}). Okafor goes in person, with two operators in a van. She has to leave Northline at 10:15 p.m.
  • If @UUID[JournalEntry.dj4gIszHHTN1QRKk]{Thornquist}'s auction is still on (@UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.lM1EiE1FoXMkf3Uo]{A1-E04 · Everything Sells Below}), Hale goes to buy a copy later that night.
  • If the Thermometer is at 5 or higher, Okafor calls Helen tonight (☎ Someone Calls the Journalist).

There's time for two things before Okafor heads down to the garage.

Who's there: Okafor and Hale, who are the interlude. Ransom comes up to pick Okafor up for the Denny's and can stay on as escort. Navarro and Pak, if anyone is playing them, are at the port warehouse, a phone call away.

The corkboard covers the whole wall. Photos of Seattle at night, clippings, the transcript of episode 112 with lines underlined in three colors. Hale is standing in front of her laptop, which beeps once. A package. No sender. Reference: SEA-0411. Okafor sets her coffee on the table without looking at it and repeats, slowly: “No sender.”

What the NPCs Want

  • Okafor: something solid. She distrusts what comes easy, and this came on its own. If the source gives her the complete index, she requests reinforcements from national headquarters.
  • Hale: to know why. “Every source wants something.”
  • ARCHER (run by the Storyteller, never appearing): for the Cell to act on the list and not ask questions.
  • Ransom (if present): for someone to tell him why those three addresses and not others.

Tests

  • Read the sample: Hale or Okafor: Intelligence + Investigation (Difficulty 3) (Desperation: Inquisitive). On a success, the three locations match areas from episode 112 (DOC-07, point 3). With Close Listening, automatic.
  • Read the source: Okafor: Wits + Insight (Difficulty 4) (Desperation: Inquisitive). On a success, Okafor notices what isn't there: a source that gives up three addresses and none of its own. “Whoever wrote this hates somebody.”
  • Trace the channel: Hale: Intelligence + Technology (Difficulty 5) (Desperation: Inquisitive). On a success, the package bounced through a data center on the Eastside. No name: just an area on the map. This is one of the night's two things.
  • Verify a target tonight: Pak puts the drone up over one of the three, Pak: Dexterity + Technology (Difficulty 3) (Desperation: Underground), or Navarro drives by, Navarro: Wits + Awareness (Difficulty 3). If no one is playing them, Hale rolls from Northline using the city cameras, at Difficulty 4. This is the other of the two things.
  • Talk to Helen (Thermometer 5 or higher): no roll. Okafor offers her protection and a salary, and means it. Helen decides like Helen: the Storyteller handles that in the coterie's scenes.

Decisions

If the Cell… Then
Plays along (logs the delivery as reliable and asks for the complete index) The three addresses go onto the target list as they arrived. Nothing else moves tonight. It's what Okafor does if no one stops her
Verifies a target On a success at the hangar or the farm: there's activity at night. . Advantage V3 for that target. Desperation −1. With a 1 on the Desperation dice and Overreach, Danger +1: Bear hears the drone, or the farm dogs bark at something they can't see
Traces the channel On a success, Okafor writes in her notebook: “ARCHER: inside? Eastside.” Crack F3. Desperation +1: their only gift may be poisoned
Files the delivery as bait (they don't use it) Nothing gets verified and the list goes in a drawer. The Cell is left with nothing: Desperation +1. If there's a raid, it arrives without V3

The delivery happened regardless: the +1 from the start isn't undone. No outcome of this interlude lowers the Thermometer.

How It Affects A4-E02

It can leave V3 (one target) and F3 (@UUID[JournalEntry.dnsWkdXVJ19riBLa.JournalEntryPage.8DXPPUEUUp5bHka5]{INT-00 · Advantages and Cracks for the Raid}). And a question in Okafor's notebook that comes back in @UUID[JournalEntry.jiea701LDJdMoHoY]{Red Tide · Continuation After FIN-D}.

Closing

At 10:15 p.m. Okafor grabs her coat and looks at Hale's unfinished memo on the screen. “Point six,” she says. “Leave it as it is.” In the elevator her phone buzzes: nrthln_research: confirmed, 11:00 PM. If the Thermometer is at 5 or higher, before the doors close she dials a Ballard number. “Helen Ward? My name is Dana Okafor. Don't hang up.”

Cut. The next scene, if the coterie goes after Lonnie, is @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.5Vgl8slqjXlVRbie]{A2-E06 · The One Who Kept One}, and Okafor is already sitting by the window.

Editor's Note · The Date of SEA-0411

@UUID[JournalEntry.WW7eg88I0uDGj8ks]{FIRSTLIGHT, Internal Memo SEA-0411} is dated 11/10/2026 and titled “second delivery,” but Halloway's Clock places the deliveries on Nights 2 and 5 (November 13 and 16). This interlude follows the Clock: Hale writes the memo on Night 5. If the players find DOC-07 in @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center}, the Storyteller can read the date as 11/16 or leave it as is. The document has not been corrected.

Storyteller Notes

  • The players see the list. They know whose each address is; Okafor and Hale don't. Play with that: make Okafor's player decide what to do with the penthouse “of a cultural foundation” knowing whose it is.
  • The Truth of DOC-07 doesn't come out at the table. Hale can suspect someone on the inside. She can't get to Halloway: there's nothing to get it from tonight.
  • If FIRSTLIGHT ends up with Lonnie later (@UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.5Vgl8slqjXlVRbie]{A2-E06 · The One Who Kept One}) and the Cell traced the channel, Okafor has two things pointing east of the lake. It isn't evidence. It's a better question.

Storyteller Context

Night 8, Thursday, November 19. The Thermometer hit 9 at the end of @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.aGN9NHO00wmdUzVn]{A3-E04 · The Pack Wavers}: 🚨 Knocking at the Door. The raid (@UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.ogKpm1VYgcVGCw1T]{A4-E02 · The Raid}) is at 9:40 p.m. This interlude is what comes before: the 8:30 p.m. briefing in the port warehouse where the tactical team sleeps, the drive, and the entry, up to the exact moment the scene switches to being played with the coterie.

The Storyteller chooses the target before starting, using the table in A4-E02 (the hangar, the farm, or the penthouse). In the briefing it's on the whiteboard, circled in red.

What's non-negotiable (doc 13): FIRSTLIGHT arrives at 9:40 p.m. with all six operators, light body armor, incendiary ammunition, UV flashlights, the thermal drone, and the generator van. Okafor directs from a car parked a block away. The objective is to capture a Kindred alive or, failing that, destroy it and take all the material. Okafor doesn't abort: the order comes from above, and the Cell's existence is on the line.

Who's there: everyone. Okafor and Hale in the car, with the body cameras on a tablet. Ransom, Navarro, Sorensen, and two operators from @UUID[Actor.abaWg7NwNQvM0sDc]{FIRSTLIGHT Tactical Team} on the entry team, always in pairs. Pak in the van, with the drone.

Before starting, check the Cell's Desperation (@UUID[JournalEntry.dnsWkdXVJ19riBLa.JournalEntryPage.O8yPSIYLlTrKHm8G]{The Puget Cell}): at 3 or higher, the generator arrives already running; at 4 or higher, there's no bullhorn; at 5, Okafor goes in.

The port warehouse has broken heating and a whiteboard on wheels. Six cots, six lockers, a coffee maker nobody cleans. The rain pounds the sheet-metal roof like it wants in. There are three photos on the whiteboard. One is circled in red. Okafor waits for the last one to sit down, puts her left hand in her pocket, and says: “Tonight isn't surveillance.”

What the Hunters Want

  • Okafor: a Kindred alive, or the evidence that justifies the three cells. No dead operators. If she loses two, she orders a withdrawal and waits for dawn (@UUID[Actor.abaWg7NwNQvM0sDc]{FIRSTLIGHT Tactical Team} tactics).
  • Hale: the material. Phones, papers, drives. “What they leave behind is worth more than what they take.”
  • Ransom: bring everyone home. If there's a photo of Tom Whitman on the whiteboard, that changes the night.
  • Navarro: to be up front when one shows. Take point, with the medal and the flashlight.
  • Pak: a perfect flight, the kind people tell stories about.
  • Sorensen: for the door to go down on the first try and the generator to start. She's paid for both.

The Briefing

Okafor presents the target. The players propose the plan: where they go in, where the van goes, who covers what, when the drone goes up. Then, the plan test:

  • The plan: Okafor: Intelligence + Leadership (Difficulty 3). On a success, choose one plan advantage: V4 Generator in Position, V5 Radio Silence, or V6 Cordon (@UUID[JournalEntry.dnsWkdXVJ19riBLa.JournalEntryPage.8DXPPUEUUp5bHka5]{INT-00 · Advantages and Cracks for the Raid}). With a margin of 2 or more, two. On a failure, the plan is the usual one and leaves nothing.
  • V4 needs Sorensen: Sorensen: Intelligence + Craft (Difficulty 3) (Desperation: Entrepreneurial) to have the generator warmed up without the light showing. On a failure, V4 is lost.

Ransom and the photo. If the target is the hangar, or if @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.NONJmwNuBweLPdPQ]{GAN-04 · The Old Comrade} has already happened, there's a photo of @UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Bear} on the whiteboard with a label: Night watchman. Thomas Whitman. Ransom's player decides right then:

Ransom… Then
Says he knows him Okafor looks at him for a long while. She pulls him off the door and puts him on the perimeter. If F1 was in play, it's lost: during the raid, Ransom isn't where Bear can see him
Keeps quiet Crack F1, if it wasn't already in play. He goes in third with the pair at the big door
Asks to go first F1, and something more: when Bear comes out with his hands up, Ransom is the one who cuffs him. Whatever they say to each other, they say quietly

The Approach

  • Arrive quietly: Entry team: Dexterity + Stealth (Difficulty 3), one per pair (Ransom, Navarro, and Sorensen roll for theirs). At Danger 3 or higher, Difficulty 4. If any fails, Crack F4.
  • Drone up: Pak: Dexterity + Technology (Difficulty 3) (Desperation: Underground). In heavy rain, Difficulty 4. On a failure, Crack F5. With Low Flight and 3 successes, the drone looks inside before anyone goes in: the players know how many are inside. Their vampires don't.
  • The body camera: any operator can tape over theirs before going in. No roll needed. Crack F6, and Okafor sees it on the tablet: she goes quiet and makes a note. After the raid, that operator is out of the Cell (@UUID[JournalEntry.jiea701LDJdMoHoY]{Red Tide · Continuation After FIN-D}).
  • The door: if the plan is a forced entry, Sorensen: Dexterity + Craft (Difficulty 3) (Desperation: Entrepreneurial) for the breaching charge. On a success, it goes down in one turn. On a failure, it goes down in two and someone hears: Crack F4.

The Cut

When the first operator touches the door, or when the generator light starts creeping in under it, cut. Ask the players to turn their hunter sheets face down and pick up their vampires' sheets. Read the “Read Aloud” from @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.ogKpm1VYgcVGCw1T]{A4-E02 · The Raid} that matches the target. From then on, the Storyteller runs the hunters, with their actors and whatever was decided in this interlude.

If the coterie isn't at the target (the Prince's penthouse, for example), the interlude doesn't cut at the door: the hunters go in. What they find is what A4-E02 says: @UUID[JournalEntry.sCVTjJFrnyyVnQDt]{Whitmore} escapes alone, using Presence (Majesty), and reaches the Council late and humiliated. Okafor's Faith takes 2 dice off that Majesty if she went in (Desperation 5); the outcome is the same, but Okafor notices, and notices it up close. What the hunters can gain is material: papers, phones. It's a hook for @UUID[JournalEntry.jiea701LDJdMoHoY]{Red Tide · Continuation After FIN-D}, not evidence for the Council.

Consequences

This interlude doesn't move the Thermometer: it's already at 9, and what happens at the door is decided by A4-E02. What's in play is what each side brings to it:

  • The plan advantages V4, V5, V6.
  • The approach cracks F1, F4, F5, F6.
  • The Cell's Desperation as it stood at the start.

If the Cell comes out of the raid with two operators down or with nothing, Desperation +1 for whatever comes next.

Storyteller Notes

  • The irony is the point. The players are going to play the raid against the plan they just made. Don't ask them to forget it: ask them to play their vampires, who don't know it. The A4-E02 test to detect the raid is rolled as normal.
  • Don't let the plan eat the session. Ten minutes of briefing, one roll, and out the door. If the players want to plan more, have them do it out loud while they drive.
  • Okafor on the radio is the voice of the raid. If her player wants to say the lines from the A4-E02 dialogue guide, let that player say them: it's their scene until the cut.

journal.name: Gale Sentinel Campus and Data Center

pages.name: Gale Sentinel Campus and Data Center

text.content: Bellevue, Eastside · Map: yes

The campus is an office park with artificial turf and benches nobody uses. In the lobby, a giant screen shows a mosaic of thousands of live doorbell feeds: porches, hallways, rain. Below it, the company motto: “We see what the city doesn't.” The building out back has no windows. It hums.

Structure: an office building (@UUID[JournalEntry.y8Ao3xEHH3W11EJe]{Preston Gale}'s office is on the third floor), a windowless data center with three levels of security, and a testing room where the ANOMALY model is trained.

Security: mortal guards; at night, four of Gale's ghouls (@UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{Halloway's Security Ghouls}). There are ANOMALY cameras at the entrances, so any Kindred who comes in through the front door gets logged as a “cold subject” (Thermometer +1: ), unless @UUID[JournalEntry.PBJeE9T9n0BjB6ag]{Ezra} or someone with Technology 3 disables the module first.

Scenes: @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.wIpc0OR2nQf7WDFO]{A1-E05 · The City's Eyes} and @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center}.

Clues: , , , @UUID[JournalEntry.YhmNvLugMfCZezEH]{Gale Sentinel: 2027 Product Roadmap, Confidential}.

A guide for the Storyteller to play @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}, the coterie's NPC ally, in social scenes. Source: doc 19 (earlier source). It complements the tactical synergies on his character sheet.

With the coterie, David helps, but he doesn't lead. He gives his opinion, pushes, and reacts; the decisions belong to the players. His help is +1 die to the PC who rolls, or an action you narrate without a roll. He never resolves on his own what is the coterie's to resolve.

David Smith doesn't argue—he defines. When he socializes, he isn't after sympathy or political power; he's after efficiency and truth. His presence should convey this:

“I'm not your enemy, but I'm not your friend either. I'm here to finish the job.”

pages.name: 🧠 1. CONTROL THE SPACE (Physical and Psychological Dominance)

text.content:
The body before the words.

Narrative tools:

  • He enters slowly. He observes first, speaks later. (Describe how his eyes sweep the room as if he were measuring lines of fire or exits).

  • Speak for him in a low but clear voice. Make the other person have to listen closely.

  • He doesn't gesture. Every movement he makes should seem measured.

  • He doesn't sit first. If he does, it's after assessing the surroundings.

  • If the other person moves too much, he follows them with his eyes, not his body: as if he were marking them in combat.

💬 Example:

“David rests both hands on the table, without pressing down. His knuckles look like marble. He doesn't interrupt, but every time the other person pauses, the silence turns uncomfortable.”

pages.name: 🔥 2. ECONOMY OF WORDS (The Weight of Silence)

text.content:
The less he says, the more you feel the danger.

Narrative tools:

  • He answers with short or ambiguous lines: “We'll see,” “Depends on what you bring to the table,” “I don't like the sound of that”.

  • Use long pauses, but natural ones.

  • He doesn't explain himself: he lets the others wear themselves out justifying themselves. The PCs too.

  • If someone asks him something he doesn't want to answer, he deflects:

    • “That's not relevant to the mission.”
    • “What matters is that we meet the objective.”
    • “Why exactly are you interested in that?”

💬 Example:

“The Brujah listens to him talk for minutes. Then he nods, once. ‘You done?’ His tone isn't aggressive, but something in the way he says it sounds like a verdict.”

He cooperates, but on his own terms.

Narrative tools:

  • His language is operational, not emotional: ‘Objective,’ ‘phase,’ ‘contact,’ ‘deadline’.

  • He doesn't promise; he proposes temporary arrangements:

    • “For now, we work together.”
    • “Later we'll see if we're still on the same side.”

  • He treats the PCs as colleagues, not as superiors or subordinates, unless it's unavoidable.

  • He respects only efficiency or loyalty. Not lineage, not power.

💬 Example:

“Smith doesn't argue with the Ventrue's order. He simply says: ‘Understood. But if the Masquerade breaks, the report carries your signature, not mine.’”

David doesn't look: he examines.

Narrative tools:

  • Describe how he observes microdetails: ‘He sees how the other man touches his ring when he lies,’ ‘The smell of old blood on his coat tells him he fed recently’.

  • Before speaking, he drops small statements that reveal what he's observed:

    • “You changed your perfume. You're expecting to see someone else.”
    • “You don't carry that gun out of habit.”
    • “You're hungry. And hungry people make mistakes.”

💬 This isn't meant to intimidate directly, but to show that nothing gets past him. If a PC rolls to read someone with David at their side, what he notices is worth +1 die.

He doesn't seek domination; he seeks respect earned through results.

Narrative tools:

  • He speaks from experience, not from ideology.

    • “I've seen what happens when Cainites think they're gods. Blood in the sewers, dust at dawn.”

  • He rejects gratuitous violence matter-of-factly, the coterie's included:

    • “If you want to prove how strong you are, there are cemeteries full of idiots who tried.”

  • He acknowledges other people's skill without giving ground:

    • “I don't like you. But you know how to do your job. That's enough.”

He doesn't need to show his fangs. You can tell.

Narrative tools:

  • When he gets angry, he doesn't shout: his voice gets lower and slower.

  • Physical gestures (cracking his knuckles, moving a chair with one hand) say more than words.

  • Let the silence after one of his lines last a little longer than normal.

  • In a verbal fight, he doesn't challenge: he warns.

    • “Don't bring that up again.”
    • “If you lie to me again, I'll know.”
    • “Don't make me remind you why I'm still alive after all these years.”

pages.name: 🧩 7. COOPERATION WITHOUT ATTACHMENT (The Art of Functional Distance)

text.content:
“I work with you, not for you.”

Narrative tools:

  • When he receives an instruction, he rephrases it in tactical terms:

    • “Fine. You open, I clean up. Then we go our separate ways.”

  • If the other person tries to get close emotionally, he redirects:

    • “Let's not mix the past with work.”

  • If he notices manipulation, he doesn't confront it directly: he files it away for later. (David doesn't react: he plans.)

His narrative signature: leaving the other person wondering whether he was an ally or a threat.

Narrative tools:

  • He ends conversations before anyone else does.

  • He closes with lines that imply an ending, not a goodbye:

    • “The job's done.”
    • “If you need me, you know how not to find me.”
    • “See you next night, if the city's still standing.”

💬 That's how he keeps the mystique of the lone hound without fully cutting his operational ties.

pages.name: 🎭 In Summary—The Perfect Balance for Cooperation

text.content:
Aspect Narrative tool Discipline it enhances
Control of the environment Silence, fixed stare, measured movements Presence (Instinctive Authority)
Reading others Microexpressions, active observation Auspex (Heightened Senses)
Tactical cooperation Professional language, temporary arrangements Resolve + Leadership
Handling tension Veiled threats, long pauses Fortitude + Composure
Graceful exit Short lines, clean-cut endings Potence + Intimidation
Downtown · Charles Halloway's Haven · Map: yes (penthouse and vault)

Forty-two stories of dark glass in the financial district. The private elevator rises without a sound and opens onto a penthouse with soaring ceilings and furniture that looks like it has never been used. The entire west wall is a window over Elliott Bay: the port cranes, the ferries, the island where the Hound lives. From up here, the city looks like a game board.

Layout: floors 1 through 38 are Halloway Meridian Capital offices (Influence and Resources); floor 40 has ghoul security (@UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{Halloway's Security Ghouls}); the penthouse holds the Council chamber and the study; an underground vault on level −3, reachable only by the private elevator.

The vault holds the original of Vance's journals, copy 1 of 3, and, from Night 6 on (Night 6), the File's original drive.

Backgrounds: Haven 4, Resources 5, Influence 4.

Scenes: @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}. A possible infiltration before the climax, if the coterie plans one.

Sheet: @UUID[Actor.doLuya2qqzFb2wqn]{Halvard Brekke}

Concept: former crab fisherman, childe of Sheriff Montgomery, and member of his pack.

Hal is the grandson of Norwegian fishermen from Ballard. He spent his summers on the Bering Sea, on boats where someone died every season. He was the one who never got seasick, the one who went out on deck in thirty-foot waves. In 1994, a storm sank his boat. He was the only one who made it to shore alive, half frozen, on a beach where Montgomery was hunting.

Montgomery (@UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Ethan Montgomery}) Embraced him that night because he saw someone who didn't know how to give up. Since then Hal has been one of Whitmore's Wolves (@UUID[JournalEntry.azX1hjbc0PUp2AA2.JournalEntryPage.bxduXJhh2oXcM6Uy]{COT-01 · Whitmore's Wolves}): he tracks, covers up, and keeps watch. He has known David for thirty years. He was the backup who reached the apartment the night Emily died, and he was the one who cleaned the scene while David was still on his knees. They've never talked about it. He feeds on fishermen and longshoremen in the waterfront bars (Alleycat).
The File has a 2023 cell phone video of a man running after a car, faster than the car. It's him.

Ambition: earn a domain of his own. Desire: for Montgomery to tell him, just once, that he did well. Suggested Conviction: “Never leave anyone in the water.” Touchstone: his niece Ingrid, who now captains the family boat and saves him a seat at the Christmas table even though he never comes.
Allies (longshoremen) 2, Contacts (port police) 1, Mawla (Montgomery) 2, Haven 1 (a boat moored in Salmon Bay).

@UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.DtetdHiBnOLQaM6Y]{A1-E02 · Ash on Pier 46} (tracking), @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.wQ2BqzruUybEIhSO]{A2-E04 · The Sheriff That Was} (works David's corner against O'Connor), @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.7brn5AgmWggUl420]{A3-E01 · The Other Son}, @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell} (he was in Emily's apartment in 1996), @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.aGN9NHO00wmdUzVn]{A3-E04 · The Pack Wavers}, @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.ogKpm1VYgcVGCw1T]{A4-E02 · The Raid}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.cGEW4b4hCJlaDeSK]{GAN-12 · The Visited Grave}.

Years ago, Montgomery ordered him to watch David and report back. Hal has done it every month. Now that David runs with the coterie, every report covers them too. In @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.aGN9NHO00wmdUzVn]{A3-E04 · The Pack Wavers}, when the Sheriff hesitates, he's going to ask for Hal's reports. Hal has to decide what to tell him.

Sheet: @UUID[Actor.cHnmNaT8zN7q4yvy]{Helen Ward}

“You can't just make people disappear.”

Mortal · Investigative journalist and host of “What the City Forgets”

These three characters already have their full documentation in the project folder. Here's a summary to keep on hand during play.
34, daughter of a cop and a nurse from Tacoma, she has spent ten years documenting what the city would rather not see.
her archive is the File. She doesn't know what David is, but she has fourteen photos of him. FIRSTLIGHT is watching her. She is David's and Fry's Touchstone.
“Helen Ward” (Touchstones).

Stats: Strength 2, Dexterity 2, Stamina 2 · Charisma 3, Manipulation 3, Composure 3 · Intelligence 4, Wits 4, Resolve 3 · Health 5 · Willpower 6

Skills: Academics 2, Streetwise 3, Drive 2, Awareness 3, Investigation 4 (Cold Cases), Insight 4 (Contradictions), Persuasion 3 (Interviews), Subterfuge 2, Technology 2

Earlier source: doc 26, “Helen Ward” (Touchstones). Where it clashes with docs 00–16, those win; see the last page.

Helen Ward wasn't born looking for monsters. She found them because nobody else wanted to look.

  • Name: Helen Ward

  • Age: 34

  • Profession: Freelance investigative journalist / regular contributor to digital outlets and investigative podcasts.

  • City: Seattle

  • Specialty: Cold cases, disappearances, “inexplicable” incidents, police and corporate corruption.

  • Status: Human, without knowing exactly what David is (she knows he isn't normal, but she isn't putting the label “vampire” on him yet).

Helen grew up in a gray Tacoma neighborhood, the daughter of a patrol cop and an ER nurse. The house always smelled of cold coffee, Betadine, and exhaustion.

  • From her father she learned to smell a lie in a statement.

  • From her mother, that most victims never make the news.

As a teenager she became obsessed with the crime pages:

unsolved murders, disappearances of girls the police wrote off as “she probably ran off with the boyfriend,” fires with “unknown” causes.

She studied journalism with the naïve idea of “bringing the truth to light.” What she found was:

  • Editors who told her:

    “This is too dark, it doesn't sell. Give me some light corruption or a sex scandal instead.”

  • Law enforcement that closed doors… or flat-out asked her to “drop it.”

She didn't drop it.

Helen specialized in:

  • Strange disappearances in specific neighborhoods

  • Deaths classified as overdoses with no prior history

  • “Accidental” fires in buildings with shady records

  • Cases of extreme violence with details that didn't fit (blood in strange patterns, bodies nearly drained of blood, witnesses talking about “glowing eyes” or “impossible shadows”).

She started publishing in:

  • Independent investigative blogs.

  • Small digital outlets with some prestige.

  • Later, a cult true crime podcast, focused on “what the city would rather forget.”

Her reputation became two-sided:

  • To some, a paranoid who sees conspiracies everywhere.

  • To others, the only one who dares to ask “what if it wasn't just somebody settling a score?”.

The first time she crossed into David's orbit was over a case that shouldn't have existed:

  • A series of “animal” attacks near the port, with bodies nearly drained of blood but no clear sign of a real predator.

  • The police quickly closed the cases as “stray dog attacks” and “bad trips.”

  • Helen started pulling the thread:

    • camera footage where the figures looked blurry or too fast,

    • witnesses who said “the streetlights went out all at once” right before the attack.

At one of the scenes, she got there too early.

David was there.

Not in the middle of the crime, but “cleaning up”:

a tall man, too calm for the hour, in a jacket with no insignia but with a soldier's bearing.

She aimed her phone at him, recording.

He looked at her, and for a second Helen felt like she'd pointed it at a black hole.

Instead of killing her, David did something different:

  • He walked over, unhurried, without raising his voice.

  • He said her name (he already knew it), mentioned a couple of her articles, one of them pulled from the web.

  • He described details of the scene that nobody outside the police and the medical examiners could know.

And then he offered her a very simple deal:

“You want the truth.

I want the city not to burn.

You keep looking, but when something's too big for you, you call this number first.

Not the police. Not your podcast. Me.”

He left her an old flip phone with a single number saved:

SAFE – no ID. (The saved messages are @UUID[JournalEntry.EQ3lkuiGnEvoSW7x]{SAFE: Saved Messages}.)

That was the beginning.

Helen is:

  • A source of information:

    • she combs forums, listens to police scanners, reads reports, snoops around hospitals.

    • When something “smells like a monster,” she sends an encrypted message:

      “Another rabid dog in Ballard. Two drained. Info attached.”

  • An early warning for a broken Masquerade:

    • if she sees strange viral videos, paranoid threads, or testimony that “gets too close,” she warns David.

  • An inconvenient conscience:

    • sometimes she asks too much,

    • sometimes she wants to save someone David would consider “collateral damage.”

She doesn't know exactly what David is.

But she knows that:

  • He doesn't age.

  • He shows up at scenes where he shouldn't be.

  • He moves too fast, sees too much, and sometimes his gaze is too old for someone “thirty-something.”

In her head, she shuffles explanations:

  • Government black ops.

  • Military experiments.

  • Something… not human, but she doesn't dare put the word “vampire” to it and believe it.

Helen is driven by a mix of:

  • Moral rage:

    • she hates that victims are invisible,

    • she can't stand whitewashed headlines.

  • Self-destructive curiosity:

    • deep down, she knows she's messing with things that could kill her.

    • But she can't let go of the bone.

Central wound:

  • Years ago she investigated a multiple disappearance in a building that ended up burning. (It's the Larchmont, 2014: @UUID[JournalEntry.Oiln4o98kvxKbOvS]{The Larchmont Building}; the friend is Danny Ruiz, @UUID[JournalEntry.5xUDUgkyHXGD8IPY]{Danny Ruiz}.)

    • They killed her article,

    • the paper paid for silence,

    • one of the missing was her college friend.

  • She's convinced the official version is a lie.

    • What she doesn't know is that the case was a Masquerade hunt, probably one where David didn't get there in time.

When David uses her as a Touchstone, part of his guilt is that:

he sees in Helen what his daughter (@UUID[JournalEntry.VYpDoFtqKkL7FlqL]{Emily Smith}) could have been: human, brilliant, stubborn, looking right where she shouldn't.

pages.name: 🎭 How Helen Behaves at the Table

text.content:
• Style: ironic, sarcastic, smokes too much, sleeps too little. Wears glasses when she's exhausted, but won't admit it.

  • Talks fast, but listens better: she's trained to catch contradictions.

  • She's no combat badass: if fists fly, she protects herself however she can. Her real weapon is:

    • a recorder,

    • a notepad,

    • three contacts in the police,

    • and a memory for things others have tried to bury.

With David:

  • Sometimes they argue.

    • Her: “You can't just make people disappear.”

    • Him: “Neither can you, and yet sometimes your work kills them all the same.”

  • She senses that he drags his own dead behind him too.

    • That's why she doesn't fully demonize him, even though she's afraid of him.

1. The Case That Brought Them Together Returns (in the adventure, @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.9fTKL8Oeq36BCfU9]{A2-E05 · The Ashes of the Larchmont} and @UUID[JournalEntry.Oiln4o98kvxKbOvS]{The Larchmont Building})

    • Someone is reopening the file on the fire/massacre that shaped Helen's career.

    • The new clues point to a group of vampires David knows very well.

    • Helen gets in up to her neck; if nobody steers her, neither David nor the coterie, she could get far too close to the truth.

  2. The Helen File (it's the Ward File: the premise of @UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File})

    • She has a hard drive with years of notes, names, blurry photos, geographic patterns…

    • To a vampire, that material is a near-perfect map of the city's hunting grounds and Masquerade breaches.

    • If someone from the Camarilla or the Sabbat gets their hands on it, or takes her out, it becomes a ticking time bomb.

  3. The Night She Beholds the Beast (developed as @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.j1wUSqY1dsP0iFfp]{GAN-02 · The Night She Beholds the Beast})

    • A scene where Helen sees David in “Executioner's Verdict” or “Last Bastion” mode.

    • Not all of it, no clear details, but enough:

      • bones that don't break the way they should,

      • inhuman speed,

      • eyes with that light that isn't human.

    • From there:

      • does she pull away from him out of fear?

      • does she double down, because she's finally found something “real”?

      • does she start investigating who she's been feeding for years?

To David, Helen is:

  • A reminder of why he does what he does:

    • every time she sends him a case, it's a chance to prevent impossible headlines.

  • A bridge to humanity:

    • she's willing to take risks for truths that don't benefit her.

    • she reminds him that he, too, chose a code when he could have been just another killer.

  • A permanent risk:

    • if she dies, it'll probably be from being too close to him or his people.

    • her death would leave David without his only living Touchstone, and David would break (see “When He Breaks” in @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}).

• The podcast. Doc 26 speaks of “a cult true crime podcast, focused on ‘what the city would rather forget’”; in docs 00–16 it's called “What the City Forgets” and Helen hosts it.
  • What she knows about David. They agree: she doesn't know what he is. Docs 00–16 add that she has fourteen photos of him, the first from 2014 (the Larchmont).
  • The SAFE phone. Doc 26 doesn't date the first encounter; the first message in @UUID[JournalEntry.EQ3lkuiGnEvoSW7x]{SAFE: Saved Messages} is from February 14, 2023.
  • Hook 3. It mentions the powers “Executioner's Verdict” and “Last Bastion”; the first doesn't appear on David's sheet (doc 18), the second is his Fortitude 4 power (see @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}).
  • Touchstone. Docs 00–16 also make her Fry's Touchstone (@UUID[JournalEntry.AeAhHuCNHL9KWVnT]{Wendell Fry}); doc 26 only talks about David.
Ballard, Market Street · Map: yes

Third floor, above a closed-down hardware store. A one-bedroom apartment someone has turned into an investigation room: walls covered in maps stuck with red, blue, and yellow pins, mugs of cold coffee, an ashtray on the sill of the fire-escape window. On the desk, a stripped cable hangs plugged into nothing. The woman sitting on the floor, hood up, looks toward the door and doesn't seem surprised.

Layout: third-floor hallway (Gale Sentinel doorbells on every door), living room and kitchen, study with the maps and the creaking closet, bathroom, and a fire escape that lets out into the alley.

Clues: (the camera lights), (ghoul Vitae on the doorknob; spotted with Wits + Awareness (Difficulty 3), or with Auspex). In the hallway, the camera at 3B is still streaming.

Scenes: @UUID[JournalEntry.w9xeQJg6psfiMjFU.JournalEntryPage.yyXMKcpDOIhGuZIB]{A0-E01 · The Call from SAFE} and @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.T8gJWjZpOnL4OisP]{A1-E01 · What They Took}.

Careful: any visible use of Disciplines in front of @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen} sets @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.j1wUSqY1dsP0iFfp]{GAN-02 · The Night She Beholds the Beast} in motion.

Core adventure: The Ward File (@UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File})

System: Vampire: The Masquerade 5th Edition. The Second Inquisition (FIRSTLIGHT) is a latent presence in the plot.

City: Seattle and Puget Sound, November 2026. Main areas: Elliott Bay and Harbor Island, Pioneer Square and the Seattle Underground, Capitol Hill, Ballard, the Eastside, Tacoma, and Everett.

Play format: a coterie of 4–5 players with the five PCs (@UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{Celeste Arden} to @UUID[JournalEntry.gRfqeOIXEHOcLemr]{Dr. Ruth Abernathy}). David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}) and Tom “Bear” Whitman (@UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Tom “Bear” Whitman}) are allied NPCs who travel with the coterie.

Seattle is the city that knows the most about its residents: every phone, every doorbell camera, and every delivery algorithm leaves a trail. Prince Marcus Whitmore's Camarilla survives thanks to the rain, to indifference, and to Sheriff Montgomery and his Hound, David Smith, erasing everything that shouldn't be there. One night, Helen Ward's hard drive is stolen from an apartment in Ballard: ten years of notes, blurry photos, and geographic patterns. Without anyone meaning for it to be, it is the most complete map in existence of the city's hunting grounds and Masquerade breaches. At the same time, Kindred start turning up destroyed on the docks, killed with the technique of Controlled Fury, the doctrine David learned from a sire presumed dead since 1985. If the Ward File reaches the Second Inquisition, the city burns. If it reaches the Primogen, someone gains a weapon to bring down the Prince. And if the coterie recovers it, they'll have to read what the file says. And decide what to tell David.

• The Masquerade as debt: every secret that gets protected is paid for by a mortal.
  • Fathers and sons in the Blood: Vance and David, David and Tom, David and Emily.
  • Surveillance: in the tech city, the predator is also prey to the data.
  • Order versus conscience: does the enforcer serve the law or his own code?
Rainy, tactical noir, with personal horror. Few words, long silences, and brief violence that has consequences. The threat is cold and procedural: drones, reports, and databases.
Core adventure: 6–8 sessions. Chronicle hooks: 12 more, to extend the campaign to 15–25 sessions.

# Question Decision
1 Who's pulling the strings? Charles Halloway, Ventrue Primogen (@UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Charles Halloway}). The signs of Vance are fake; August Krell (@UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{August Krell}) leaves them. Vance is not in the city.
2 Sheriff O'Connor He was the previous Sheriff, until 1978. He's a background piece (@UUID[JournalEntry.oQ2AhEeDkwdPRv71]{Liam O'Connor}).

5 The Larchmont fire David didn't get there in time.
6 Prince Whitmore's clan Toreador.
