Sheet: @UUID[Actor.l3z7Cp6AX0CmtLI6]{Jun Takeda}

“I just deliver. I don't open the packages. That's rule number one.”

Clan: thin-blood · Sect: none (Thornquist's protégée) · Role in @UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File}: courier, possible victim, and clue (@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.wZxrfXenQd62yVtT]{Jun, the Thin-Blood Courier})

pages.name: Mortal Days: The Beacon Hill Courier

text.content: Jun Takeda is 22. She grew up on Beacon Hill, between her grandmother's flower shop in the International District and the hills she biked up to get to class. She dropped out of college to pay her mother's rent and started delivering for several apps at once: food by day, packages by night. She knew the city better than any map. In the spring of 2025, at four in the morning, she dropped off an order at a building in Georgetown, and the customer opened the door with a stained mouth.

pages.name: Kindred Nights: The Courier from Below

text.content:
She doesn't know who Embraced her. She woke up in the doorway the next night, hungry and without a pulse, though sometimes, when she eats something, a little of it comes back. She drifted for two weeks until a thin-blood from the docks brought her down to the Underground. Thornquist offered her what she does best: delivering. Ever since, she has carried packages between Kindred without asking what's inside.

On Night 1, Thornquist had her take two USB drives to two different buyers. One was for the Nosferatu destroyed at Pier 46. The other was for a buyer who never showed up to the meet. Jun still has that second drive in her jacket pocket. Krell knows it.

Survive. Since she heard about Pier 46, she sleeps somewhere different every day. She hasn't gone back to the Underground.

Hand it over or throw it away. She doesn't know what to do with the USB drive. If she gives it to Thornquist, she figures he'll sell it anyway. If she throws it away, she'll have nothing to bargain with. If the coterie finds her before Krell does, she may give it to them in exchange for protection.

Learn. If she survives, she wants to learn to hunt for real (@UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.cjmyT3bfPbka0X6O]{GAN-11 · Jun's Fast}).

Nothing fixed. She sleeps in rented storage units, in the back room of her grandmother's flower shop, or at a friend's bike shop (Haven 0). As a thin-blood, she can eat some food and stand sunlight for a while, but she needs blood. She buys expired bags from a hospital orderly and, when she's out of money, carefully bites other couriers asleep at the bus stop.

The bike: electric, modified, the fastest in the Underground.

Contacts 2: couriers across half the city.

The USB drive: a partial copy of the File, with the folders from 2019 through 2022.

Abel Thornquist (dependence). She owes him everything and doesn't trust him.

Rosa Iturbe (admiration). She once saw her argue with the Sheriff and not look away.

Ezra Lund (complicity). The only Nosferatu who talks to her like a person.

August Krell (terror). She saw him once, from a distance, in the coat. She doesn't know his name.

• “There's a thin-blood selling secrets in the Underground.” (Half-true: she delivers them; she doesn't sell them.)
  • “Jun can walk in daylight.” (True, for a while and in a lot of pain.)
  • “Jun knows who Embraced her.” (False.)

To mortals she is Jun Takeda, delivery courier (Mask 3: she has a legal life, accounts, and family). She looks her age. She is small and wiry, with hair dyed a faded blue, ear piercings, a yellow waterproof delivery jacket, an insulated backpack, and a helmet covered in stickers. She talks fast, cracks jokes when she's scared, and never stays still.

• Sire: unknown
  • Embraced: 2025 (born 2004)
  • Ambition: not to die in a doorway.
  • Conviction: “Don't open the packages.”
  • Touchstone: her grandmother Haruko, who runs a flower shop in the International District and reads her fortune in tea leaves.
  • Humanity: 8
  • Generation: 15th
  • Blood Potency: 0

Attributes: Strength 2, Dexterity 4, Stamina 2 · Charisma 3, Manipulation 2, Composure 2 · Intelligence 2, Wits 3, Resolve 2

Secondary Attributes: Health 5 · Willpower 4

Skills: Athletics 4 (Bicycle), Streetwise 3 (Shortcuts), Drive 2, Awareness 2, Persuasion 1, Stealth 3, Subterfuge 2, Technology 1

Background figure (no actor sheet) · Camarilla Justicar · Role in @UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File}: the authority to whom @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway} wants to send the regency minutes; with her recognition, “the regency becomes a crown.”

This page gathers what docs 00–16 say about Panhard. In parentheses, the source doc for each fact. The docs give her no explicit clan, age, or stats; the Council's order of business speaks of “the Justicar of Clan Ventrue” (doc 15, @UUID[JournalEntry.8EZofopivOgpo5tE]{Primogen Council Agenda}).

• Background figure alongside Archon @UUID[JournalEntry.CRdeqlwyfpxGPyzT]{Duval} and @UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Vance} (doc 01, NPC index; ID registry v2: “PNJ-08 · Justicar Helena Panhard (background)”).
  • Duval acts as her envoy (doc 13).
  • She holds copy 3 of Vance's journals, the one Mr. Pell typed: Halloway sent it to her in 2025 “as a goodwill gift” (doc 09, @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.MbCyCqKpBUEan9GR]{GAN-07 · The Archon Calls}; ID registry: “Copy 3 of 3 of Vance's journals, held by Justicar Panhard”).

• The city's Rumor 4, “Halloway has Justicar Panhard's support”: half true. “He's been writing to her for a year. She doesn't answer him, but she doesn't tell him no either” (doc 05).
  • Halloway started writing to her a year ago; to him she is his “hope”: “If she recognizes his regency, no one in Seattle will be able to oppose him” (doc 06, Halloway's sheet).
  • Whisper: “Halloway has the Justicar in his pocket.” (False. She hasn't answered him) (doc 06).
  • Halloway told her about @UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{Celeste}: if David turns Duval down in GAN-07, Celeste receives a parallel invitation from the Justicar (doc 09).
  • At the Council (@UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}), if a majority of the Primogen votes for the “emergency regency,” Halloway “can send the minutes to Justicar Panhard, with whom he's been corresponding for a year. With a Justicar's blessing, the regency becomes a crown” (doc 13). The motion asks that the minutes be forwarded “to the Justicar of Clan Ventrue for her information and confirmation” (doc 15, AYU-08).
  • The original of the File “is the evidence Panhard asked him for in order to recognize the regency” (doc 13, A4-E01 Notes).

Two Versions of the Correspondence

Docs 05 and 06 say Panhard doesn't answer Halloway. Doc 13 says she asked him for the File as evidence and, in an ambiguous phrase, that “he's been corresponding with her for a year.” If it matters at your table, decide whether the Justicar has already answered or whether Halloway only believes she will.

• @UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO.JournalEntryPage.RqeQkW5KfFjPYFhg]{FIN-B · The Hound Changes Masters}: Halloway is Regent “with Justicar Panhard's recognition if the File reached Duval” (doc 13).
  • Partial FIN-B: if Halloway wins the Council but the coterie keeps the File, “Halloway doesn't have his evidence before the Justicar: his regency is weak” (doc 13, endings table).
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO.JournalEntryPage.xgVY2zlstK7IN1Rp]{FIN-C · Cleansing Fire}: if Halloway won the Council and the File is destroyed, “his regency lacks the evidence the Justicar asked for: Panhard doesn't recognize it.” Seattle is left in political limbo (doc 13).

• @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.MbCyCqKpBUEan9GR]{GAN-07 · The Archon Calls} · The Archon Calls: if the ending was FIN-B, Panhard sends Duval to Seattle to investigate (doc 09).

Clan: Brujah · Sect: independent · Role in @UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File}: witness and informant (@UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.wQ2BqzruUybEIhSO]{A2-E04 · The Sheriff That Was})

pages.name: Mortal Days: The Longshoreman from Cork

text.content: Liam O'Connor was born in Cork in 1868 and crossed the ocean at nineteen with his brother, who died of typhus on the ship. He reached Seattle just after the Great Fire and worked the docks hauling lumber, coal, and salmon. He was big, he had the loudest voice on the waterfront, and he was afraid of nothing. In 1897 he organized the city's first longshoremen's strike. They beat him half to death in an alley and left him for dead.

pages.name: Kindred Nights: The Badge and the South

text.content:
A union Brujah who had been following the strike found him in the alley and Embraced him in 1899. O'Connor went on defending the longshoremen for thirty years, only now by night. In 1931 Prince Grange named him Sheriff because nobody knew the port better, and because it kept him on her side. He was a hard Sheriff, but a fair one. He survived Grange's fall and served Whitmore for sixteen more years.

In 1978 he fell over some photos nobody saw being taken (@UUID[JournalEntry.4858IAb89fTokFfV]{Letter from Sheriff O'Connor to Prince Whitmore, 1978}). He left for Tacoma. He opened a boxing gym on that city's waterfront, where he trains neighborhood kids and drinks blood with whiskey. When the Brujah broke with the Camarilla, he didn't join the Anarchs: he said he'd already lost one badge and had no intention of pinning on another. Today he lives like an old lion in a small zoo, waiting for someone to ask him what he knows.

The Truth About '78. He wants it known that Halloway brought him down. He doesn't want to be Sheriff again. He wants it on the record.

The Journals. He has known since 1986 that Halloway bought Vance's journals; an old contact from the port who saw the shipment come in from Lyon told him (@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.TOvLdg2zhgDzjOAG]{The Journals Bought in 1986}). Nobody ever asked him. If the coterie asks, he tells them, in exchange for someone taking @UUID[JournalEntry.4858IAb89fTokFfV]{Letter from Sheriff O'Connor to Prince Whitmore, 1978} before the Primogen.

The Survivor. He knows an old, patient Sabbat Kindred lives in Tacoma (@UUID[Actor.wop4zqE8KwywxhTL]{The Larchmont Survivor}). He watches him from a distance. He hasn't told the Sheriff anything, because the Sheriff doesn't ask him anything.

The Shamrock Gym, on the Tacoma waterfront: two brick stories, a ring, heavy bags, and a windowless room in the basement (Haven 2). He feeds at the underground fights he runs on Saturdays: he drinks from the losers while he stitches up their eyebrows. He pays them double.

The gym kids (Herd 1, Allies 1): young boxers who take him for an old trainer with insomnia.

Contacts 2: the Port of Tacoma and retired old longshoremen.

@UUID[JournalEntry.4858IAb89fTokFfV]{Letter from Sheriff O'Connor to Prince Whitmore, 1978}: the original letter, kept in a plastic sleeve under the ring.

Charles Halloway (patient hatred). He's been waiting forty-eight years.

Marcus Whitmore (bitterness). He read the letter and filed it away.

Ethan Montgomery (resentment without hatred). He took his post. He's done it well. That hurts more.

Rosa Iturbe (fondness). A union woman. She reminds him of himself.

David Smith (curiosity). He's heard about the Hound. He wants to see whether he's a dog or a man.

• “O'Connor lost the badge protecting a childe of his clan.” (Half true: he protected him, but he fell because of Halloway's photos.)
  • “O'Connor is working with the Everett Anarchs.” (False.)
  • “O'Connor knows things about Halloway nobody else knows.” (True.)

To mortals he's Liam O'Connor, the owner of the gym, “an Irishman who doesn't sleep” (Mask 2); among Kindred, “the Irish ancilla.” He looks about thirty-one. He's huge and round-shouldered, with red hair and a short beard, a nose broken several times over, and cauliflower ears. He wears an undershirt, suspenders, and a wool cap. He smells of liniment and whiskey. He talks loud, laughs louder, and has a voice that's plainly used to silencing arenas.

Editor's Note

Doc 07 said “looks about fifty” and “graying red hair”; it was decided that he looks the age he was at his Embrace (1899, born in 1868): about thirty-one, with red hair and no gray. For the same reason, “an old Irishman” became “an Irishman” for mortals and “the Irish ancilla” among Kindred (also in Rosa's line in A2-E04).

• Sire: a union Brujah, destroyed in 1934
  • Embraced: 1899 (born in 1868)
  • Ambition: to get the truth about 1978 on the record.
  • Convictions: “Nobody gets left alone in the alley” · “A badge is a promise, not a license.”
  • Touchstone: Dani Okeke, his best boxer, 19, whom he's preparing for her first professional fight.
  • Humanity: 6

These three Loresheets are tied to Seattle and to the adventure. They are bought with experience points like any Background. A character can only have one Loresheet at level 4 or 5, unless the Storyteller says otherwise.

pages.name: LOR-01 · The Doctrine of Controlled Fury

text.content:
“Locate. Assess. Execute. Everything that comes after the first blow is the Beast asking permission.”

In the '50s, the Brujah Marcus “Ironjaw” Vance (@UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Marcus “Ironjaw” Vance}) developed a method of combat and discipline for hunting Kindred without losing control of one's own Beast. He taught it to very few, in brutal sessions with cold water and broken bones. Today the doctrine survives in a handful of Camarilla enforcers on three continents. In Seattle, two know it: the one who finished the lesson and the one who didn't.

Prerequisite: trained by Vance or by someone who has this Loresheet at level 4 or higher.

Level Name Effect
• Locate When you pursue a specific target (a Kindred you were sent to find), gain +1 die on Awareness and Investigation tests to find them.
•• Assess Once per scene, after observing a Kindred for one turn, make a Wits + Insight test against their Composure + Subterfuge. On a win, the Storyteller tells you their Hunger level and whether they'll try to flee, fight, or negotiate.
••• Execute Against a target you have assessed (level 2) this scene, your first attack gains +2 dice. If that first attack misses, you can't use this effect again this scene.
•••• The Full Guard You recognize the doctrine the moment you see it (, ). A rival using the inverted guard loses 2 dice from their melee defense pools against you. In addition, gain +1 die to resist fury frenzy during combat.
••••• Heir of the Fist You can teach the doctrine up to level 3. Once per story, spend 1 point of Willpower to automatically succeed on a test to resist frenzy in combat. The Camarilla's Archons know your name, for better and for worse.

Tests: Assess: Wits + Insight (vs. Composure + Subterfuge) · the target resists with Composure + Subterfuge.

Note: David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}), an NPC, has this Loresheet at level 4. Krell (@UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{August Krell}) has level 2 and the inverted guard, without level 4. A PC can buy it with David as mentor, since he meets the prerequisite: normally up to level 3. But David chooses whom he teaches. If Krell learns the other guard (@UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell}), David goes up to level 5.

“The city above is the one you see. The one below is the one that remembers.”

Since 1889, there have been buried streets, storefronts, and sidewalks beneath Pioneer Square. Tourists see three blocks. The Nosferatu see the rest: tunnels connecting basements, sewers, old steam conduits, and bricked-up passages that run all the way to the port. Whoever knows the underground knows a city that appears on no map.

Prerequisite: none, though levels 4 and 5 require permission from Thornquist (@UUID[JournalEntry.dj4gIszHHTN1QRKk]{Abel Thornquist}) or his successor.

Level Name Effect
• Shortcuts Downtown and in Pioneer Square, gain +2 dice on tests to escape a pursuit or reach a place first by going beneath the streets.
•• The Undermarket You have access to the Undermarket. Once per story, you can buy a specific piece of information in exchange for a minor favor to the Moles (@UUID[JournalEntry.azX1hjbc0PUp2AA2.JournalEntryPage.Dy9L39SvdB7rns0t]{COT-04 · The Moles}).
••• Sealed Haven You know a bricked-up passage that only you know how to open. It works as an additional Haven 1, with the Hidden advantage, and it's less than ten minutes from any point downtown.
•••• The Mother You know where the Mother Below sleeps. Once per chronicle, you can wake her for a moment to ask her a question. She knows things from before 1889. She sets the price.
••••• Architect Below You can open and close sections of the Sealed Underground. Once per story, you can create a new Portillon for your coterie (+1 Portillon in a downtown domain). The Nosferatu of Seattle treat you as if you were clan.

Location: the Sealed Underground (@UUID[JournalEntry.jg1zpvYlDFMJRY8Q]{The Sealed Underground (Seattle Underground)}).

“We see what the city doesn't.” (Gale Sentinel slogan)

Seattle has more cameras than streetlights: doorbells, traffic, public transit, stores, delivery drones. Almost all of them are connected. Kindred who understand this network can use it to their advantage. Those who don't end up in a file.

Prerequisite: Technology 2 or higher, or a contact who has it.

Level Name Effect
• Blind Spots You know which parts of the city have fewer cameras and at what hours they fail. Gain +1 die on Stealth against electronic surveillance.
•• Access Once per session, make an Intelligence + Technology test (Difficulty 3) to view doorbell and traffic camera footage of a specific location from the last 72 hours.
••• Erase You know how to make yourself disappear from footage. Once per story, when FIRSTLIGHT's Thermometer would rise because of a camera, it doesn't.
•••• Cold Subject You know Gale Sentinel's ANOMALY model and how to fool it with thermal clothing, heat, or interference. ANOMALY cameras don't register the members of your coterie if you prepare beforehand (one Intelligence + Technology test, Difficulty 4, per scene).
••••• The Eye Inside You have a trusted contact inside Gale Sentinel or Northline. Once per story, you can learn the current value of the Thermometer and FIRSTLIGHT's next target.

Tests: Access: Intelligence + Technology (Difficulty 3) · Cold Subject: Intelligence + Technology (Difficulty 4).

Note: Ezra Lund (@UUID[JournalEntry.PBJeE9T9n0BjB6ag]{Ezra “Static” Lund}) is the natural candidate for this Loresheet. If he discovers that Gale's firmware is his (@UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.wIpc0OR2nQf7WDFO]{A1-E05 · The City's Eyes} or @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center}), he can buy level 4 without needing training.

“Violence is not chaos. It is judgment.”

Clan: Brujah · Generation: 8th · Sect: Camarilla · Sire of: @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith} (Haiti, 1960) and @UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{August Krell} (Marseille, 1972)

Background character: he doesn't appear in the adventure and has no character sheet. Main source: doc 23, “🩸 Sire of David Smith: Marcus ‘Ironjaw’ Vance” (earlier source), supplemented by docs 00–16.

Vance is not in Seattle. Every sign of him is false. What is real is Krell, the other son, the one who wasn't chosen (doc 01).

  • The journals. In 1986, a year after his disappearance in the Carpathians, a middleman from Lyon sold the Brujah's journals at a private auction. Vance had asked for his havens to be burned. Someone didn't do it. The buyer was @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway}, who had three typewritten copies made (by Mr. Pell, @UUID[Actor.eRE6FTNdGO76lzPK]{Mr. Pell}) and kept the original in his vault (@UUID[JournalEntry.L6Fl1S0tjkWno2we]{Halloway Tower}). Vance, Marseille, 1963, Folio 14 (Typewritten Copy)} (folio 14, Marseille 1963), @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.xQqepYpthm1bxP8u]{Halloway Knows About the Cold Water} (Halloway quotes a line of Vance's that appears only in the journals), @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.HYE4rNbNf1sEbYGe]{The Inverted Guard} (the inverted guard), @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.TOvLdg2zhgDzjOAG]{The Journals Bought in 1986} (the journals bought in 1986), @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.jqTQDyJH3ogdAuWO]{The Folios on the German} (folios 41 and 42 on “the German”), @UUID[JournalEntry.9zcPuCCutNfUtYJ0]{Vance's Lineage Tree} (lineage tree).

The handwriting is a near-perfect match for Vance's, but it's in English: Vance wrote his journals in French (@UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.aGN9NHO00wmdUzVn]{A3-E04 · The Pack Wavers}).

Marcus Vance was a World War II veteran, an artillery commander and military strategist who, after his Embrace in the '40s by an exiled European Brujah, became a figure of order and discipline within the clan—a rarity among his kind.

Unlike chaotic or idealistic Brujah, Marcus believed that revolution needed structure, and violence, purpose. In his view, the Masquerade was the wall that held the balance between Cainite anarchy and total extinction.

During the Cold War, he operated as a roving enforcer for the Camarilla, hunting Kindred who threatened political stability. His nickname, Ironjaw, came as much from his iron jaw as from his unbreakable resolve: he never backed down, not from humans and not from Elders.

Nicknames: Ironjaw, The Red Commander, The Hammer of Order · Years active: 1940–1985 · Place of origin: New York, USA · Last known location: Port-au-Prince, Haiti—1960 · Fate: Presumed destroyed by the Sabbat in the '80s, though unconfirmed. · Sect: Camarilla (missing, possibly hunted by the Inquisition).

Date: July 8, 1960 · Place: Haiti, during a covert SEAL mission.

David, then an American commando, was leading an infiltration operation on the Haitian coast, investigating a string of disappearances tied to blood cults. His squad was ambushed—not by rebels, but by a Sabbat pack that had turned the place into an experimentation camp.

Marcus Vance was in the area, hunting the same group on Camarilla orders. He arrived too late to save Smith's platoon… but in time to watch the young soldier, gravely wounded, refuse to die, dragging himself forward with a knife in hand to take out the last enemy even as he bled out.

“I saw something in him I hadn't seen in decades—not fear, not fury. I saw will. And I thought: men like that must not die. They must be used.” — Excerpt from the memoirs of Marcus Vance, recovered from his haven in Marseille.

Marcus Embraced him not out of compassion but out of strategic principle: David was the ideal soldier, a being with discipline, conscience, and an unbreakable moral code. He shaped him for a decade, teaching him the balance between the violence of the Beast and the structure of duty. Thus was born “the Hound of the Masquerade,” an enforcer deadlier and more precise than any Archon.

In 1985, Marcus Vance disappeared in Eastern Europe while investigating a Sabbat outbreak in Romania. Rumor among the Kindred says he was destroyed in direct combat with a Tzimisce Elder, though some reports link him to the Black Hand.

David never confirmed his death. But he still keeps the military knife he carried on the day of his Embrace, a relic of the moment he died as a human and was born as a hunter.

• Emotional bond: absolute respect, without sentimentality.
  • Blood Bond: dissolved decades ago, but the philosophical loyalty persists.
  • Influence: Marcus's voice still echoes in David's mind when he faces hard moral decisions.
  • Legacy: “Violence is not chaos. It is judgment.”

Doc 23 includes a portrait of Vance (image not exported).

📜 CONFIDENTIAL FILE—CAMARILLA / CLAN BRUJAH

Classification: SECRET—For active Justicars and Archons only

⚰️ Chronological Data

💀 Career and Historical Significance

Marcus “Ironjaw” Vance stood out among the Brujah for his unusual loyalty to the Camarilla and his devotion to the Masquerade as a principle of survival. While others of his clan championed revolution, Marcus championed order. He was an old-school soldier: he believed in hierarchy, discipline, and force as the language of justice.

“Where others see rebellion, I see indiscipline. The Beast does not need to be free. It needs to be tamed.” — Marcus Vance, Marseille, 1973.

During the Cold War, he acted as a roving agent of the Camarilla, eliminating Sabbat cells, Anarch heresies, and uncontrolled vampires in conflict zones. His modus operandi was direct and surgical: “Locate. Assess. Execute.”

Vance was a mentor and, to some, an executioner. His reputation was that of an incorruptible enforcer, feared even by the Ventrue he served.

🩸 The Embrace of David Smith

In 1960, during a joint operation with agents of the Sheriff of New Orleans, Vance intercepted a Sabbat pack in Haiti. There he found a dying young commando: David Smith, sole survivor of a platoon devoured by the enemy Cainites.

According to reports recovered from his hermetic journal (Marseille, 1963):

“Not all men deserve to die. Some only need a different war. Smith did not ask to be saved. But he did not surrender either. That is enough.”

He Embraced Smith to forge a living weapon against vampiric indiscipline. For nearly a decade he trained him under a martial code: obedience, precision, and restraint of the Beast. The Archons of Paris describe their relationship as “father and son in death.”

⚠️ Internal Assessment

Trait Assessment
Loyalty to the Camarilla Absolute (never questioned)
Threat level Lethal only if set against a Justicar's direct authority
Autonomy High; avoided fixed havens and clan structures
Psychology Cold, analytical; obsessive profile centered on discipline and emotional control
Known weakness Inability to delegate. Extreme belief in “duty before emotion”

🕯️ Fate and Legacy

Vance's last recorded communication dates to 1985, an encrypted message addressed to Archon Duval (@UUID[JournalEntry.CRdeqlwyfpxGPyzT]{Archon Duval}):

“If I do not return, burn my havens. Whatever is left of me will no longer serve order.”

No physical remains were found. He is presumed destroyed in a confrontation with a Tzimisce Elder near Cluj-Napoca, Romania. Black Hand files confirmed activity in the area 48 hours later.

🔖 Documented Legacy

  • Founder of the “Controlled Fury” doctrine used by Camarilla Brujah hunters.
  • Mentor of David Smith, current enforcer for the Sheriff of Seattle.
  • Forerunner of the tactical training model for operational Kindred (1958–1978).

“He wasn't looking for soldiers. He was looking for monsters with a conscience.” — David Smith, private remark, 2004.

📎 Annex—Note from Archon Duval (2021)

“If Vance lives, he does so in absolute silence. If he died, his echo still resounds in every hunter who does not kill for pleasure. Either way, the Camarilla owes him the night.”

• Fate. The header of doc 23 says “presumed destroyed by the Sabbat in the '80s”; the dossier and docs 00–16 set it in 1985, near Cluj-Napoca. They agree on the essentials.
  • Journals. Doc 23 cites “memoirs recovered from his haven in Marseille” and a “hermetic journal (Marseille, 1963)” as if they were in Camarilla archives. In docs 00–16 the journals weren't burned; they were sold in 1986 and Halloway has them; the Camarilla has had only copy 3, since 2025 (@UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.MbCyCqKpBUEan9GR]{GAN-07 · The Archon Calls}). Sheet: @UUID[Actor.mS4hVbBIId47tDop]{Marcus Whitmore}

“A Prince doesn't rule. He chooses who rules in his name, and applauds.”

Clan: Toreador · Position: Prince of Seattle · Sect: Camarilla

Marcus Whitmore was born in Baltimore in 1838 and came to San Francisco with the Gold Rush, though not to look for gold. He opened a theater. Then another. By 1870 he owned the most elegant variety hall on the West Coast, where rich miners spent in one night what they had dug up in a year. He was charming, generous, and up to his neck in debt. His talent was making people feel part of something beautiful.

pages.name: Kindred Nights: The One Who Never Got His Hands Dirty

text.content:
A Toreador soprano at the San Francisco opera Embraced him in 1871, enchanted with the man who had filled her theater. Whitmore spent eighty years at that city's court learning what he does best: being in the picture. In 1952 he moved to Seattle, and in 1962, with the World's Fair, he took the throne.

This is how he did it, though no one tells the story: Whitmore gathered evidence of a Masquerade breach by Prince Grange, some of it real and some of it exaggerated, and showed it to her in private. She left the city without a fight. It was a clean coup, bloodless, and Whitmore has ruled the same way ever since: letting others get dirty. Montgomery gets dirty for him. Halloway, who was Grange's childe, learned the technique by watching him.

Voight's envelope. He opened it two nights after Elysium. It says FIRSTLIGHT has a cell in the city and that someone at court might be feeding it. He did nothing. He expects Montgomery to handle it.

Let him overreach. He suspects Halloway is behind something. His strategy is to wait for him to go too far and punish him once it's obvious to everyone. It's the same strategy he used on Grange. This time he may be too late.

The collection. He Embraces artists the way others buy paintings. Nadia Ferro (@UUID[JournalEntry.rg50DlMYSzgbZeBv]{Nadia Ferro}) is his latest piece. If she fails him in public, he'll make her pay for it.

A penthouse in Capitol Hill in the name of his cultural foundation (Haven 4), the same one that appears in @UUID[JournalEntry.WW7eg88I0uDGj8ks]{FIRSTLIGHT, Internal Memo SEA-0411}. Club Cinder (@UUID[JournalEntry.ciIKIq7hoVokkr0J]{Club Cinder}) and the Glass Gallery (@UUID[JournalEntry.iyojT7kJHH23BWLd]{The Glass Gallery (Elysium)}) are his as well. He feeds only on people who have just wept in front of a work of art. At Club Cinder there is always someone whose job is to spot them.

The cultural foundation (Resources 4, Influence 3 in art and culture).

The Sheriff and, through him, the pack.

Status 5 (Camarilla).

Herd 2: Club Cinder's loyal crowd.

@UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Ethan Montgomery} (dependence). He knows he wouldn't last a year without him. He has never told him so.

@UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Charles Halloway} (distrust). He sees him as an uncomfortable mirror.

@UUID[JournalEntry.rg50DlMYSzgbZeBv]{Nadia Ferro} (pride). He shows her off at court like a jewel.

@UUID[JournalEntry.bB0eDKVFcxQW4C2d]{Solène Marchetti} (affection). The only one who knew him before he was Prince.

@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith} (utility). Someone else's weapon, worth keeping close.

@UUID[JournalEntry.FOgT9FF3NF7ZHdCa]{Adelaide Grange} (unease). He never learned whether she left or whether others made her disappear. He'd rather not know.

• “Whitmore ran Grange out with blackmail.” (True.)
  • “The Prince never opened Voight's envelope.” (False: he opened it and did nothing.)
  • “Whitmore has a secret deal with the Justicar to retire to Europe.” (False.)
  • “Whitmore knows Halloway is plotting and lets him get on with it.” (Half true: he suspects it and lets him get on with it.)

To mortals he is Marcus Whitmore III, the discreet philanthropist who chairs an arts foundation (Mask 3, with a fictitious family line that renews itself every forty years). He looks about thirty-three. He is tall, with slicked-back hair, no gray, and very pale gray eyes. He wears impeccably cut suits without a tie and a single ring set with a black stone. His voice is warm and his laugh contagious. He makes anyone feel like the most important guest in the room. He hates being rushed.

Editor's Note

Sheet: @UUID[Actor.0IIsgytowpgAWwK6]{Nadia Ferro}

Concept: sound producer for Helen's podcast and childe of Prince Whitmore.

Nadia played bass in Capitol Hill bands for fifteen years. She was never famous, but she was the one who made everyone else sound good. In 2015, an infection damaged her left ear and took her off the stage. She moved to the mixing board, where she found what truly obsessed her: the human voice at three in the morning, when people tell the truth.

Prince Marcus Whitmore (@UUID[JournalEntry.sCVTjJFrnyyVnQDt]{Marcus Whitmore}) heard her mixing live at a club and Embraced her in 2016. To him she was one more piece in his collection. She lives at court, but she doesn't belong to him. In 2021 she started producing “What the City Forgets,” Helen's podcast. Helen's voice hooked her. Ever since, she has been passing Helen anonymous tips to make the episodes better. She feeds at late-night shows, on audiences lost in a trance.
The File has a note from Helen about her own producer: “N. never shows up in group photos. Coincidence?”

Ambition: record something that outlives the Masquerade. Desire: for Helen to finish her big story. Suggested Conviction: “Never silence someone who tells the truth.” Touchstone: Theo, her old bandmate, who still plays Thursdays at a dive bar on Capitol Hill.
Fame 1 (music scene), Contacts (media) 2, Status (Camarilla) 1, Mawla (Whitmore) 2, Herd 1.
They both orbit Helen. David keeps her away from the truth; Nadia pushes her toward it. David is an ally of the coterie and is with them every night: that tension is going to be at the table.

@UUID[JournalEntry.w9xeQJg6psfiMjFU.JournalEntryPage.yyXMKcpDOIhGuZIB]{A0-E01 · The Call from SAFE} (she knows the apartment), @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.uL8F2YNogcToiFc6]{A2-E01 · Elysium Night}, and @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}.

Episode 112 (@UUID[JournalEntry.kY9btWylMLztTB1j]{“What the City Forgets,” Episode 112: “The Ones Who Don't Age”}), the one that woke up FIRSTLIGHT, was built on material Nadia leaked to Helen. And the thieves pulled Helen's schedule from the production calendar Nadia syncs to the cloud.
South Lake Union, office tower, 11th floor · FIRSTLIGHT front · Map: yes

An office like any other in South Lake Union: gray carpet, plastic plants, standing desks, a welcome sign with the logo of a cybersecurity consultancy. At three in the morning, three lights are on on the 11th floor. One of them belongs to a conference room with the blinds drawn.

Layout: reception, open-plan desks (the analysts), a conference room with a corkboard covered in photos (Helen's podcast included), a locked armory, and a white room with high-intensity UV lamps, an “interview room.”

Occupants: Dana Okafor (@UUID[JournalEntry.bJA2iRyDgbm2TcuK]{Dana Okafor}), S. Hale (@UUID[JournalEntry.D611Mcr17F6HHEUw]{Sasha Hale}), and the tactical team @UUID[Actor.abaWg7NwNQvM0sDc]{FIRSTLIGHT Tactical Team}, which spends its nights in a warehouse at the port, not here.

Danger: breaking in here is the fastest way to raise the Thermometer (+3 if the intrusion is discovered: ). Watching the place is more useful than going in.

It doesn't appear in any set scene. Save it for the chronicle or for a very bold coterie.

Nights 1 and 2. The coterie works out what was lost, discovers that someone is destroying Kindred on the docks, and receives a deadline and an uncomfortable question from the Sheriff.

Installment 2 Adjustment

Installment 2 corrects the origin of the copies of the File (Lonnie Barras, Sal Medeiros, and Thornquist's duplicates) and the Clock for Nights 2 to 6. Wherever it contradicts this Part, @UUID[JournalEntry.nuyiQmnE32yq4wOG]{Revision to Part 1 · The Chain of Copies} wins. The specific changes are marked in each scene.

Storyteller Context

Night 1 continues. The coterie has @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen} and a few hours before dawn. This is the moment to understand what was in the File, who could have known about it, and what trail the thieves left. Helen can make a list from memory of what the file contained (@UUID[JournalEntry.ifdmxLzsoLizs9uN]{AYU-02}), and she shows them her voice memos (@UUID[JournalEntry.zNhdOMSnEHdvMIGE]{DOC-01}) and the flip phone (@UUID[JournalEntry.EQ3lkuiGnEvoSW7x]{DOC-05}).

If the scene takes place in the @UUID[JournalEntry.104UV0anmZHNCTrD]{hangar}, Helen sees @UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Bear}'s arsenal and @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David}'s cot for the first time. Keep this in mind for @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.j1wUSqY1dsP0iFfp]{GAN-02}.

If the coterie already searched the apartment thoroughly in @UUID[JournalEntry.w9xeQJg6psfiMjFU.JournalEntryPage.yyXMKcpDOIhGuZIB]{A0-E01 · The Call from SAFE}, skip the “Search the apartment” section and go straight to the conversation with Helen.

Helen lights a cigarette with hands that are still shaking a little and looks at the wall of maps. Red pins, blue, yellow. “They left this,” she says. “They left the maps. They took what was underneath. What you can't see.” She sits on the floor with a notebook and starts writing without looking up. “I'll make you the list. What was there. Everything I remember.”

Tests

  • Search the apartment: Intelligence + Investigation (Difficulty 3). The lock wasn't forced: it was opened with a professional electronic pick. They only opened the closet in the study and the desk: they knew exactly where to look (, reinforced).
  • With 3 or more successes: on the doorframe there's a tiny black adhesive patch, a signal repeater, that let them take the hallway cameras offline without touching the building's network. It's commercial-grade technology, not police-grade.
  • Wits + Insight (Difficulty 3), talking with Helen: Helen doesn't suspect @UUID[JournalEntry.rg50DlMYSzgbZeBv]{Nadia}. But when she says her producer has “access to the recording calendar,” she hesitates for half a second. Something just crossed her mind.
  • Intelligence + Technology (Difficulty 4), on Helen's laptop: the cloud was wiped with the correct credentials, from an IP address at an Eastside data center. It isn't a conclusive clue, but it points east of the lake (, partial).

Coterie Options

Escape If the coterie decides to move Helen, there are three options: the @UUID[JournalEntry.104UV0anmZHNCTrD]{hangar}, which is safe but exposes her to seeing too much; the home of some mortal contact; or one of the passages of the Underground, if Ezra suggests it and @UUID[JournalEntry.dj4gIszHHTN1QRKk]{Thornquist} charges for it. Any option works, but Helen doesn't want to be alone.
Manipulate To keep Helen from publishing anything about the theft: Manipulation + Persuasion (Difficulty 3). To keep her from telling Nadia anything (if Nadia isn't a PC): Manipulation + Persuasion (Difficulty 4), because Nadia is her friend. To get her to agree to stop investigating “for now”: Manipulation + Persuasion (Difficulty 5). Helen isn't easy to convince.
Combat Not applicable in this scene.
Disciplines Dominate to make Helen forget what she saw that night: possible, but it also erases the file's contents from her memory, and the coterie loses its best source on what was in it. Costs 1 Stain. Auspex (Scry the Soul): Helen has the aura of someone frightened, furious, and, beneath it all, determined. And a color that flares every time she looks at David.

Dialogue Guide: Helen Ward

  • “What exactly was in the file?” — “Ten years. Two hundred fourteen cases. Deaths, disappearances, fires, photos, audio. And maps: where and when. If you look at it from a distance, you see the pattern. You see where someone hunts.” (Hand out @UUID[JournalEntry.ifdmxLzsoLizs9uN]{AYU-02}.)
  • “Was there anything about us?” — She looks at them one by one. “There were folders. No names, because I don't have names. I have photos. Dates. Patterns.” She pauses. “Yes. I think so.”
  • “Who would want this?” — “Not a newspaper. Not the police either: if they wanted my files, they'd come with a warrant. Whoever wants this is someone who's in them. Or someone who wants to find the people who are.”
  • “Did you tell anyone what you had?” — “Never the whole thing. On the podcast I talked about patterns. In episode 112 I talked about a man who doesn't age.” She looks at David. “I didn't show your photo. But I talked about it.” (Hand out @UUID[JournalEntry.kY9btWylMLztTB1j]{DOC-02} if they don't have it.)
  • “Why didn't you leave when you got the message?” (@UUID[JournalEntry.EQ3lkuiGnEvoSW7x]{DOC-05}; she answers looking at David, no matter who asks) — “Because it was the first time in four years you'd said anything besides ‘still watching.’ And you didn't say why.”

Dialogue Guide: Ethan Montgomery

He says little, and slowly. He leaves long pauses. He never raises his voice. He calls David “Hound.”

  • (He opens) “Why are we here?” — “Because you're all on the same drive.” He taps the list. “A mortal journalist has your photos, your dates, your patterns. Not anymore. Someone else has them. Either you get it back together or you go down together. There's no third option.”
  • “Why us?” — “Because you're the ones with the most to lose if it gets out. People with something to lose work harder.”
  • “What do you know about Pier 46?” — Silence. He looks at David. “I know what I saw in the police photos. Short blows. Always in the same places. I know that way of working, because I've got it sitting on my porch.”
  • (David asks, or a PC defending him) “What are you implying?” — “Nothing. I'm asking.” A long pause. “Is your sire still alive, Hound?”
  • David: “I don't know.” — He nods slowly. “Good. That's the answer I'd give. I don't like it, but it's the right one.” (David is telling the truth. If a PC tells what they saw on the pier here, David doesn't deny it: he leaves it to them.)
  • “How much time do we have?” — “Three nights. After that, if I don't have the drive and I don't have a name, I go looking myself. My way.”
  • “What happens if we find the one killing on the docks?” — “You bring him to me. In one piece, if you can. If you can't, whatever's left.”

Brick sidewalks, boarded-up storefronts with hand-painted signs, violet skylights overhead that let in the dirty light from the street. Dialogue Guide: Abel Thornquist

He speaks low, unhurried, with a Swedish accent. Every word seems to cost money. He never gives anything away.

  • “Do you have the File?” — “I have pieces. Two. Pieces sell for more than the whole, because every buyer thinks his is the important one.”
  • “Where did you get them?” — “They were brought to me. How much is it worth to know who?”
  • “Who's Pike?” — Silence. “Was. A runner. I gave him a package to deliver. He didn't deliver it.” A pause. “He didn't deserve it, either.”
  • “Who killed him?” — “That I don't sell, because I don't know. And what I don't know bothers me more than what I do.”
  • “Who wants to buy?” — “Everyone. A Ventrue who pays without haggling. A Regent who asks too many questions. And someone who never gives a name and always pays cash.” (They're @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway}, @UUID[JournalEntry.yaAsxCkCLf8CANL5]{Voight}, and, the last one, FIRSTLIGHT's @UUID[JournalEntry.D611Mcr17F6HHEUw]{Hale} through an intermediary. Thornquist doesn't know that last part.)
  • (To Ezra, if he's there) “Why didn't you tell me?” — “Because it wasn't worth enough yet.”

Installment 2 Adjustment · “Where Did You Get Them?”

This answer replaces the one above: “From a fence in SoDo who buys what nobody else wants to touch. He got it from a mortal who kept something that wasn't his. The fence's name is worth a minor favor. The mortal's name, I don't know, and that bothers me.” (, partial.)

Dialogue Guide: Jun Takeda

  • “Do you have something of Thornquist's?” — “I don't open the packages. Rule number one.” She touches her jacket pocket without realizing it. “But I have one I didn't deliver. The buyer didn't show.”
  • “Have you seen anyone following you?” — “A big guy, in a coat that's way too big for him. I saw him twice. Once on the pier, once yesterday, on a corner. He wasn't looking at me. He was looking at my backpack.”

Halloway has three goals tonight: sow doubt about the Sheriff, rekindle the rumor that @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David} destroyed his sire, and take the measure of the coterie. He makes one mistake: he mentions a detail about @UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Vance} that only appears in the journals (P-07).

The scene works as a round of conversations. The Storyteller decides the order based on who approaches whom. At the end, the Prince takes the floor.

At the entrance, a woman in gray holds out a velvet tray: “Your phones, please.” Inside, hundreds of pieces of blown glass hang from the ceiling like frozen jellyfish, red, amber, and black, and the light passing through them shifts across the floor whenever someone walks by. A string quartet plays, and no one can see it. Everyone has a glass in hand, and no one drinks from it. At the far end, by the terrace, a silver-haired man laughs at something, and the whole room seems to turn slightly toward him.

Tests

  • Read the room: Wits + Etiquette (Difficulty 3). Who's talking to whom. Halloway moves through the room like a host, even though the host is the Prince. Voight stands alone by the terrace, checking her watch. Thornquist is in a corner, and no one approaches him.
  • Spot Halloway's mistake: Intelligence + Academics (Difficulty 3). See the dialogue guide. Halloway quotes a phrase of Vance's that doesn't appear in any Camarilla archive, only in the private journals (). David knows the moment he hears it, but doesn't say so in front of Halloway. Noticing that something changed in his face is Wits + Insight (Difficulty 2). If a PC asks him later, he explains: “Nobody knew that but him and me.” If David didn't hear the phrase and a PC repeats it to him, he recognizes it all the same.
  • Listen without being seen: Wits + Awareness (Difficulty 4). On the terrace, Halloway tells a lesser Kindred: “The Sheriff is old. And the Hound has loyalties that aren't ours.” Useful for @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.aGN9NHO00wmdUzVn]{A3-E04 · The Pack Wavers}.
  • Ask to see Marchetti's register (Status 2 or higher): Charisma + Etiquette (Difficulty 3). Hands over @UUID[JournalEntry.lcO0CdwUlZHg2wAX]{DOC-03}.

Coterie Options

Escape Leaving before the Prince speaks is a discourtesy: −1 Status for whoever does it, unless Marchetti excuses them.
Manipulate With Halloway: goading him into saying too much is Manipulation + Subterfuge vs. Halloway's Composure + Insight (8 dice). It's very hard. But if the coterie shows him something he didn't expect, like the Pike USB drive or Krell's name, a smile slips out (Halloway smiles when he loses). With Whitmore: asking him to open an investigation is Charisma + Politics (Difficulty 5). He says yes and does nothing. With Voight: see the dialogue guide.
Combat Forbidden by the first law of Elysium: expulsion, −1 Status, and a trial. If someone loses their cool with Halloway, Halloway wins the night.
Disciplines Hostile ones are forbidden. Passive Auspex is tolerated. With Scry the Soul on Halloway: a dark green aura, very stable, with a streak of anticipation, like someone waiting on the outcome of a bet. On Whitmore: gold, weariness, and fear. Marchetti notes the use of Auspex in her register if she detects it (her Wits + Awareness: 6 dice).

Dialogue Guide: Charles Halloway

Courteous, calm, never interrupts. His hands don't move. He calls David “Mr. Smith,” never “Hound.” He speaks to David, but he's measuring the coterie: he wants to see who jumps.

  • (He approaches David and the coterie) “What do you want?”—“To offer my condolences, Mr. Smith. I'm told things have turned up on the docks that remind you of someone. It must be difficult.”
  • “What do you mean?”—“Your sire. A remarkable man. ‘Locate, evaluate, execute.’ And the cold water in the mornings, yes? A severe method.” (The cold water only appears in the journals: .)
  • “How do you know about the cold water?”—The briefest pause. “We Ventrue read a great deal, Mr. Smith. The Archons' reports from the seventies were very detailed.” (A lie. Wits + Insight (Difficulty 4) to notice it.)
  • “What do you think of the Sheriff?”—“That he's done excellent work for fifty years. And that fifty years is a long time for anyone.”
  • (To @UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{Celeste}, if present) “What do you need from me?”—Quietly, in front of the others: “Go over the Cascade accounts this week. There's a payment I don't remember authorizing.” (It's a trap: he wants Celeste to touch the payment to the thieves and leave her signature a second time.)
  • “Do you have the File?”—He smiles for the first time. “I have many things. But I don't collect podcasts.”

Dialogue Guide: Dr. Anneliese Voight

Precise, dry, speaks in percentages. She prefers the terrace because from there she can see who comes in.

  • “Are you worried?”—“I have been for fourteen months. Now I'm worried with data.”
  • “What data?”—She glances around. “There's a Second Inquisition cell in South Lake Union. I've known since 2024. What I didn't know until Monday is that they have a source inside this court.”
  • “Who?”—“If I knew, I wouldn't be on the terrace. I'd be talking to the Sheriff.”
  • “Why are you telling us?”—“Because the Prince opened my envelope two nights late and did nothing. And because you appear in the same file that cell is looking for. The probability that you have an incentive to help me is high.”
  • (To @UUID[JournalEntry.gRfqeOIXEHOcLemr]{Ruth}, if present) “What do I do?”—“Nothing with your name signed to it. For two weeks, nothing.”

Dialogue Guide: Wendell Fry

  • (He approaches, headphones around his neck) “Who are you?”—“The one who listens. You're the son of the fist.” To David: “The other one's listening too, you know. But he only hears half.”
  • “What other one?”—“The one who signs with his left hand.” (He gives them the napkin: @UUID[JournalEntry.FVBnf3yE87K4BOhh]{DOC-10}.)
  • “What does this mean?”—“I don't know. The radio said it.” Pause. “Are you going to interrupt me? If you interrupt me, I start over.”

Dialogue Guide: Marcus Whitmore

  • (Closing speech, to the whole room)—“Friends. I'm told the rain brings rumors this week. Rumors are like the rain in this city: they soak everyone and drown no one. The Sheriff has my confidence. The Sheriff has his dogs.” He smiles toward David. “Let us go on enjoying the evening.”
  • (In private, if someone secures an audience) “Halloway is conspiring against you.”—“Charles has been conspiring since 1962. It's how he breathes. When he makes a mistake everyone can see, I'll deal with it. Until then, I'd rather he believe I don't see it.”
  • (To @UUID[JournalEntry.rg50DlMYSzgbZeBv]{Nadia}, if present) “What do you want from me?”—“Tell me what your journalist is saying. You know which one.” He touches her shoulder. “No one in this room knows you work for her. Keep it that way.”

Storyteller Context

Night 4, Sunday, November 15, around 2:00 a.m. @UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{Krell} raids @UUID[Actor.mto8LnnsUQgFr1DI]{Sal Medeiros}'s warehouse in SoDo, a scrap-and-antiques building beside the railroad tracks. He destroys @UUID[Actor.Q2t6M2IxrRHCJCnC]{Corwin}, the Caitiff who protected Sal, kills the fence, and searches the place for the USB drives that are no longer there. On the wall he writes @UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Vance}'s motto in Sal's blood. If @UUID[JournalEntry.BRQMU0Tf8VSNaZ5o]{Jun} isn't under the coterie's protection, she had come to collect her cut and dies here too.

The coterie can arrive before, during, or after:

  • Before (if they followed P-13 from @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.lM1EiE1FoXMkf3Uo]{A1-E04 · Everything Sells Below} or are watching the warehouse): they can set an ambush. See Combat.
  • During (if they arrive between 1:50 and 2:10 a.m.): they find Krell in the middle of the job. Krell flees as soon as he sees @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David}. He doesn't want to fight him yet.
  • After (most likely): a neighbor heard noise and called 911. The police arrive at 3:15 a.m. The coterie has a short window.

The building smells of rust, old furniture wax, and something much fresher. Among shelves of antique radios, headless mannequins, and crates of vinyl, an older man lies facedown beside an overturned desk. Farther on, near the back door, a pile of gray ash, still warm. On the brick wall above the desk, someone has written in a steady hand, in ink that drips: LOCATE. EVALUATE. EXECUTE.

Tests

  • Read the fight: Intelligence + Brawl (Difficulty 4). The sequence of blows on Corwin's ashes is the Doctrine of Controlled Fury, but with the inverted guard: weak hand forward. Whoever attacked is left-handed or fights like it. Vance didn't fight like that ().
  • If David is there: he sees it before anyone else (@UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.oGnroV6R68YdMQyD]{LOR-01} at level 4) and understands what it means: the killer learned from Vance, but never finished. He doesn't say so on his own. If a PC asks him to look at the ashes, the clue comes out without a roll: “Somebody left him half-finished.” Noticing that he saw it, if nobody asks him, is Wits + Insight (Difficulty 3).
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.gRfqeOIXEHOcLemr]{Ruth}, or anyone with Medicine 3: Intelligence + Medicine (Difficulty 3) on Sal. A single blow to the back of the neck. He died instantly. The killer didn't want him to suffer. “Professional,” says the body.
  • Search the desk: Wits + Investigation (Difficulty 3). Sal's ledger is lying under the desk. Krell didn't see it, or didn't care: he doesn't read handwritten English well. Entry for November 13: “L.B.—3 sticks, 2 sold (T.), 1 pending. Motel?” ().
  • Follow Krell's trail: Wits + Survival (Difficulty 4; Hal +2 dice), or @UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{Hal} with +2 dice. The smell of wet wool toward the back door, then toward the tracks, then south. Georgetown. With 4 or more successes, Hal finds the barge (but see Notes).

Coterie Options

Escape If the police arrive with the coterie inside: slipping out the back door toward the tracks is Dexterity + Stealth (Difficulty 3). A freight train passes at 3:22 a.m.: jumping aboard is Dexterity + Athletics (Difficulty 3) and guarantees the escape.
Manipulate The scene is a Masquerade problem: a human body, apparent human ash, and a phrase written in blood. There are three ways to fix it. Stage it as a robbery: Intelligence + Subterfuge (Difficulty 3), scrub the wall, and take the ash. Call Montgomery: his contacts cover it up, but the Sheriff learns the coterie was there, and about the phrase on the wall. Ruth signs the autopsy: it works, but FIRSTLIGHT's “R. A.” anomaly gains another report ().
If they do nothing, the police find the phrase. , and the local press talks about “a ritual killing in SoDo.”
Combat If the coterie arrives early and sets an ambush, Krell comes in through the back door at 1:55 a.m. He fights the coterie if David isn't there; if David is, he watches, barely smiles, and flees. Fleeing is his Dexterity + Athletics pool (8) against the coterie's pursuit, at 3 successes. He uses Celerity (Blink) to cover ground. If cornered, he fights for real (see @UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{PNJ-12}). Krell shouldn't die here. If the coterie truly corners him, he jumps into the river from the warehouse dock.
Disciplines Auspex 4 (Spirit's Touch) on the written wall: old rage, envy, and a repeated question: why him and not me? Blood Sorcery (Ruth or @UUID[JournalEntry.yaAsxCkCLf8CANL5]{Voight}): with a Vitae-tracking ritual on a drop of Krell's blood on the floor, they learn his blood is Brujah of the Ninth Generation, the same as David's. (This is the first clue that they're blood brothers. Give it privately to whoever performed the ritual. If Voight did it, she tells whoever asked her, not David. Whether they tell David, and when, is up to the players. See @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell}.)

Storyteller Context

Optional scene, any night of Part 2. Elysium rumors blame the @UUID[JournalEntry.azX1hjbc0PUp2AA2.JournalEntryPage.SSDCSJFv8Esl6Ki5]{Everett Anarchs} for the deaths on the docks. The coterie can go to Everett to ask questions, on their own initiative or because @UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Montgomery} asks them to “take a look at the Salt's crowd.” @UUID[JournalEntry.WHkwE8CYfaKW5WyO]{Rosa Iturbe} receives them in her bar (@UUID[JournalEntry.JMwTSsJAcyYdCs3m]{LUG-10}) with hostility: she knows the Sheriff is watching her, and she thinks the coterie has come looking for a convenient culprit.

The scene has two layers. On the surface, a negotiation: Rosa doesn't know who's killing on the docks, but she knows it isn't one of hers, and she's willing to prove it. Underneath, a confession: Rosa gave shelter to the Anarch who killed @UUID[JournalEntry.VYpDoFtqKkL7FlqL]{Emily Smith} in 1996. She can't bring herself to tell @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David}. If the coterie wins over the assembly, she tells a PC and leaves the decision to them. If David came and is the last to leave, she tells him.

Skip this scene if the coterie has no interest in the Anarchs. Its consequences show up in Part 4 anyway (Tavi Mercer).

The road dies at a shuttered shipyard, rusted cranes cut out against a slate-colored sky. Beside the fence stands a bar with a neon sign missing a letter: SA T'S. Inside: tables of scarred wood, a bar built from the split hull of a boat, and black-and-white photos of strikes. When you walk in, the conversations stop. A short woman with cropped hair and blue coveralls sets a welding torch on the bar and leans on her elbows. “The Sheriff's dogs,” she says. “What an honor. You here to find someone or to make someone up?”

Tests

  • Win over the assembly: Charisma + Leadership (Difficulty 4), or Manipulation + Persuasion (Difficulty 5). Rosa doesn't decide alone: the decision to help is put to a vote. If the coterie brings evidence (P-08, the inverted guard, or P-07, the Halloway business), the Difficulty drops by 1 for each clue.
  • Notice the tension: Wits + Insight (Difficulty 3). A young Brujah, Tavi Mercer (@UUID[Actor.k2TLqQkkzzjSLzkp]{MEN-05}), won't take his eyes off them and has his fists clenched. An older Gangrel, Bas Okonjo, hides in the back so @UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{Hal} won't see him.
  • Rosa and David: Wits + Insight (Difficulty 4). Rosa looks at David differently: not with contempt, but with something like guilt.

Coterie Options

Escape Leaving without talking is easy: nobody stops them. But the chance at an alliance is lost, and Tavi takes it as weakness: in Part 4, he acts on his own.
Manipulate With Rosa: see Tests. With Tavi: calming him down is Charisma + Intimidation (Difficulty 3) or Persuasion ( Charisma + Persuasion (Difficulty 4)). If it works, Tavi doesn't attack Elysium in Part 4. With Bas: Hal can talk to him alone. Bas is afraid Montgomery will make him pay for his 2019 desertion. If Hal promises to intercede, Bas becomes the coterie's ally inside Salt's.
Combat Fighting in the bar pits the coterie against a dozen Anarchs. Rosa stops it in the second round: “Not here.” But the alliance is broken and @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.0e8h94hwnGDTnixI]{GAN-06} is triggered.
Disciplines Dominate at an Anarch assembly is a mortal insult: if anyone notices (Rosa's Wits + Awareness: 5 dice), they're thrown out and never welcomed back. Presence (Awe) is subtler and tolerated, but Rosa notices and says out loud: “Nice trick. We still vote here.”

Dialogue Guide: Rosa Iturbe

Direct, fast, Biscayan accent. She swears in Basque when she's angry. She never looks away.

  • “We're not here to accuse anyone.”—“Everybody says that. Then a Blood Hunt shows up with our name on it.”
  • “The killer fights like David's sire.”—She looks at David. “And that surprises you? You dogs all look alike.”
  • “Someone at court is blaming you.”—“I know that. What I don't know is who.” Pause. “Tavi says we go ask Elysium with welding torches. I say we wait. Bring me a name and maybe I win.”
  • “Will you help us?”—“The assembly votes on it. If they vote yes, you've got fifteen Anarchs at the Port of Everett and a boat whenever you need one.”
  • (To a PC, alone, if the coterie won the vote)—She looks at the floor, something she never does. “There's something the Hound needs to know, and I can't tell him. Thirty years ago. A guy named Ray Dorsey asked me for shelter for a week. Said the Sheriff was after him. I gave him a bed at the shipyard.” She looks up. “A week later he killed a social worker in Rainier Valley. His daughter. You tell him. Or don't. Your call.”
  • (To David, alone, if the PCs let him be the last to leave)—She looks at the floor. “There's something I have to tell you. Thirty years ago. A guy named Ray Dorsey asked me for shelter for a week. Said the Sheriff was after him. I gave him a bed at the shipyard.” She looks up. “A week later he killed a social worker in Rainier Valley. You know which one.”
  • “Did you know?”—“No. I swear it on my father. But I gave him the bed.” Pause. “Since then, nobody in Everett uses a kid as herd. It's the only thing I could do.”

Consequences of the Confession

  • If the PC keeps quiet: no immediate cost. Rosa never brings it up again. The flowers on Emily's grave (@UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.cGEW4b4hCJlaDeSK]{GAN-12}) may be hers. If David later learns the coterie knew, he stops helping them (+1 die) until someone explains it to his face.
  • If David finds out inside the bar (from Rosa or from a PC): he's on the edge of a fury frenzy. A PC has to stop him before he moves: Charisma + Persuasion (Difficulty 3), or get in his way with Strength + Brawl (Difficulty 4). If both attempts fail, David goes for Rosa: see Combat and “If David attacks her.”
  • If he finds out outside the bar, there's no frenzy, but he wants to go back to Everett that night. Whether to let him go alone or go with him is up to the players.
  • If the coterie gets David to hear her out without violence: Rosa becomes the coterie's Allies 2 permanently, and Salt's shows up at the climax. David doesn't say he forgives her. He says “That's done” and never speaks of it again. The PC who stood beside him can take the Conviction “Debts are paid with deeds, not with blood.”
  • If David attacks her, Salt's becomes an enemy. GAN-06 is triggered, and Halloway gets the excuse he was looking for. David is shaken: he blames himself, not the coterie.

None about Halloway. This scene is about allies and David's wound.
