Storyteller Context

Any night of Part 2. The coterie travels to Tacoma, about forty minutes south, to talk to @UUID[JournalEntry.oQ2AhEeDkwdPRv71]{Liam O'Connor} at his gym, the Shamrock. O'Connor knows two things no one has asked him about: that @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway} brought the Sheriff down in 1978 with fabricated photos, and that in 1986 Halloway bought @UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Vance}'s journals.

O'Connor gives nothing away, but he doesn't want payment either. He wants to see whether the Hound “is a dog or a man.” He offers @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David} three rounds in the ring. He doesn't care who wins. He cares how he fights. Who steps in, and who works the corner, is up to the coterie.

The Shamrock gym takes up the ground floor of a brick building at the Port of Tacoma. Inside, it smells of liniment, old sweat, and whiskey. A couple of kids work the heavy bags under yellow lights. In the ring, a huge man with red hair and cauliflower ears holds mitts for a girl who hits with fury. Without breaking rhythm, the man looks toward the door. “Tell the kids to go home, Dani,” he says. “The city folks are here.”

Tests

  • The fight in the ring: three rounds, no Disciplines and no fangs. Winning isn't what matters.
  • If David steps in: the Storyteller narrates the rounds without rolling. What's at stake is the corner. Between rounds, O'Connor needles him to see if he cracks. A PC in the corner keeps him in Controlled Fury with Charisma + Leadership (Difficulty 3). On a success, David fights with short, measured punches, without trying to humiliate, and O'Connor respects him even if O'Connor wins. On a failure, David loses his composure in the third round.
  • If a PC steps in (because David didn't come or because the coterie prefers it), O'Connor accepts: “Let's see what kind of people run with the Hound.” Each round is a contested test of Strength + Brawl (contested; O'Connor: 10 dice). Same rule: fighting clean, without humiliating, earns his respect.
  • If whoever fights uses Potence or loses their composure, O'Connor stops the fight: “A dog.” It takes a Manipulation + Persuasion (Difficulty 4) roll to get him to talk anyway.
  • If nobody steps in, O'Connor understands, but raises the Difficulty of everything else by 1.
  • Win O'Connor's trust: Charisma + Streetwise (Difficulty 3) if the coterie treats the gym kids and Dani with respect. With 3 or more successes, he pulls @UUID[JournalEntry.4858IAb89fTokFfV]{DOC-08} out from under the ring without anyone asking.

Coterie Options

Escape Doesn't apply: O'Connor isn't a threat to anyone who doesn't threaten him.
Manipulate What O'Connor wants in exchange for DOC-08 is a promise: that someone takes it before the Primogen. Promising is easy; keeping it happens in @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}. If the coterie promises and doesn't deliver, O'Connor will know.
Combat See the ring. Attacking O'Connor outside the ring is stupid: he has Potence 3, Presence 3, and fifteen kids who love him.
Disciplines Dominate on O'Connor works (he has no Fortitude), but if he notices, he stops talking for good. Auspex: a red and gray aura. Old rage, gone cold. And an unexpected glow when he looks at Dani: pride.

Dialogue Guide: Liam O'Connor

Talks loud, laughs loud, Cork accent. When he's being serious, he sits on the edge of the ring and lowers his voice. If David didn't come, whatever is meant for him he tells the coterie: “Tell the Hound that…”

  • “We want to know about Vance.”—“Everybody wants to know about Vance. Nobody wants to know about O'Connor.” He laughs. “Get in the ring, Hound. Three rounds. Then we talk.”
  • (After the fight) “What do you know?”—“That in '86 an old friend from the port saw a shipment come in from Lyon. Crates of books, addressed to one of Charles Halloway's companies. My friend opened one out of curiosity. Handwritten journals. On the cover, ‘M.V.’” Pause. “Your sire's journals never burned, lad. A patient Ventrue bought them.” ()
  • “Why didn't you tell anyone?”—“Because by '86 I was nobody. Nobody asks a fallen Sheriff anything.” He shrugs. “And because until tonight I didn't know what he wanted them for.”
  • “Did Halloway do this to you?”—He pulls the letter out from under the ring (@UUID[JournalEntry.4858IAb89fTokFfV]{DOC-08}). “Read it. And then take it where it needs to go.”
  • “Do you know any students of Vance's?”—He thinks. “Back in the seventies I heard the old man had trained a legionnaire in Marseille. A German. Left him half-finished. Never knew what became of him.” (It's @UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{Krell}.)
  • “Anything else?”—“There's something old living in Tacoma that came out of the Larchmont through the drain. I keep an eye on it from a distance. Haven't told Montgomery, because Montgomery never asks me anything.” (Hook for @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.18vJtyOOVZe1Uk41]{GAN-09}.)

Clues

(the journals bought in 1986) · @UUID[JournalEntry.4858IAb89fTokFfV]{DOC-08} · a hint about Krell (“the German” Vance left half-finished)

Exits

@UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.9fTKL8Oeq36BCfU9]{A2-E05 · The Ashes of the Larchmont} (O'Connor mentions the Larchmont; if the coterie goes, it's ten minutes away) · @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center} or @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell} (with P-07, P-08, and P-09, the coterie has the full picture: Halloway has the journals, and someone trained by Vance works for him)

Editor's Note

Doc 11 described O'Connor as having “graying red hair”; the decision was that he looks the age he was at his Embrace (about thirty-one), with red hair and no gray (@UUID[JournalEntry.oQ2AhEeDkwdPRv71]{Liam O'Connor}).

pages.name: A2-E05 · The Ashes of the Larchmont

text.content:
Storyteller Context

Optional scene. Any night of Part 2, usually after @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.wQ2BqzruUybEIhSO]{A2-E04 · The Sheriff That Was}, since the Larchmont is in Tacoma. The coterie can end up here through the Pike USB drive (the Larchmont folder), through @UUID[JournalEntry.oQ2AhEeDkwdPRv71]{O'Connor}, or because @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen} or @UUID[JournalEntry.rg50DlMYSzgbZeBv]{Nadia} insist.

This scene is @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David}'s wound, but the PCs are the ones who live it: they find out what happened and decide what to do about it. It's the second time David arrived too late, and the one Helen doesn't know about. What happened is in @UUID[JournalEntry.Oiln4o98kvxKbOvS]{LUG-11}: a Sabbat pack, seven tenants locked in the cistern, David arrived when the building was already burning, @UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Montgomery} ordered the cistern sealed with the bodies inside. Danny Ruiz, Helen's friend, is still down there.

The question of the scene isn't what happened. It's what to do about it.

David and the Larchmont. David doesn't offer to come. If the coterie asks him, he comes and doesn't speak the whole way. If they don't ask, he doesn't ask where they're going.

Skip this scene if the coterie has no interest in the Larchmont or if the table would rather not touch the subject yet. It remains a hook (@UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.18vJtyOOVZe1Uk41]{GAN-09}).

Twelve years later, the Larchmont is still standing: four stories of blackened brick, windows with no glass, a construction fence with a demolition notice nobody ever acted on. The rain comes in through the roof and runs down the stairwell to the basement, where you can hear water flowing. On the fence, tied on with wire, are seven faded plastic flowers. And an eighth, new, real, still beaded with rain.

Tests

  • Get down to the basement: Dexterity + Athletics (Difficulty 2). The staircase is half collapsed.
  • Find the sealed cistern: Wits + Investigation (Difficulty 3), or no roll if David came: he goes straight to the boiler room and stops in front of it. A slab of new concrete, lighter than the rest of the floor, in the middle of the boiler room.
  • Get David to tell what happened: Charisma + Insight (Difficulty 3). On a success, he tells the whole of @UUID[JournalEntry.Oiln4o98kvxKbOvS]{LUG-11}, including Montgomery's order. On a failure, he only says: “I got there late.” Pressing him with Intimidation works, but David won't help that PC for the rest of Part 2.
  • The new flower: Wits + Awareness (Difficulty 4). Beside the slab there are recent footprints, a night or two old. Bare feet. And a very faint smell of old, rancid Vitae that belongs to no one in the coterie. (The Sabbat survivor, @UUID[Actor.wop4zqE8KwywxhTL]{MEN-08}, visits the site. GAN-09.)

Coterie Options

Escape Leaving without touching anything is a valid option, and it costs nothing. The question stays open for the chronicle.
Manipulate There's no one to negotiate with here. The negotiation is with Helen, afterward, if someone decides to tell her. See Consequences.
Combat There's no combat, unless the Storyteller wants to bring GAN-09 forward: the survivor may be hiding in the drain and flee when he sees the coterie.
Disciplines Auspex 4 (Spirit's Touch) on the slab: seven presences, cold, water, a very long wait. One of them has a recurring thought: “Helen's going to come.” (Use it carefully. It's hard.) Potence to lift the slab: Strength + Athletics (Difficulty 4), or automatic with Potence 2. See Consequences.

Consequences

  • Open the cistern: (broken concrete and the smell of bodies don't go unnoticed in a building the city keeps an eye on). If David is there, he doesn't stop them, but he doesn't help: “The Sheriff sealed that.” When they see what's below, he climbs the stairs and doesn't speak again all night. He doesn't help anyone until the following night. If they bring Danny Ruiz out and hand him over to the Hecata family in Tacoma, the family owes them a major favor.
  • Tell Helen: the relationship between Helen and David changes forever. Who tells her is up to the coterie: they can bring David so he says it himself, or tell her themselves. The Storyteller decides, based on how and who, whether Helen forgives him, pulls away, or decides to write about it. Any option is valid. If a PC tells her before David does, Helen stops trusting him: for the rest of the adventure, any social roll the coterie makes with Helen has its Difficulty raised by 2 if David is present. David doesn't blame anyone out loud.
  • Don't tell her and don't open it: no immediate mechanical cost. But the Larchmont folder is still on USB drive 1 and in the original File. If FIRSTLIGHT reads it, someone else will read it too.
  • Talk to Montgomery: if the coterie asks him about the Larchmont, the Sheriff admits it bluntly. “Seven bloodless bodies were a breach. I sealed the breach. I'd do the same today.” Then, quieter: “I wouldn't do it the same way.”

Exits

@UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.18vJtyOOVZe1Uk41]{GAN-09} (the survivor) · @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.j1wUSqY1dsP0iFfp]{GAN-02} (if Helen finds out)

pages.name: A2-E06 · The One Who Kept One

text.content:
Storyteller Context

New scene. Night 4 or Night 5. @UUID[Actor.9rv5Jdb3y6bZZ1fj]{Lonnie Barras}, the thief who copied the File, is hiding at the Starlite, an Aurora Avenue motel with rooms by the week. Since he found out @UUID[Actor.mto8LnnsUQgFr1DI]{Sal} is dead, he hasn't slept. He has USB drive 3, with the folders from 2023 to 2026, the most recent and the most dangerous for the coterie. And he has a desperate plan: sell it to the only person who has offered him money without asking questions, nrthln_research, at a Denny's at 11:00 p.m. on Night 5.

Three parties are looking for Lonnie at the same time: the coterie (via P-13), @UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{Krell} (who arrives on Night 6), and FIRSTLIGHT (who's expecting him on Night 5). It's a race.

  • If the coterie arrives on Night 4 or before 10:00 p.m. on Night 5: they find Lonnie in his room, terrified.
  • If they arrive between 10:00 and 11:00 p.m. on Night 5: Lonnie is already on his way to the Denny's. They have to intercept him en route or in the parking lot, in front of the FIRSTLIGHT agents.
  • If they arrive later: Lonnie has left with @UUID[JournalEntry.bJA2iRyDgbm2TcuK]{Agent Okafor}. . See Notes.

Aurora Avenue at night is an endless row of motels with neon signs, closed-up auto shops, and gas stations. The Starlite has two floors, an empty pool with a plastic chair at the bottom, and a sign that flickers: VACANCY. Room 214 has its curtains drawn and the light on. Behind the door a TV blares, a quiz show, and beneath it, someone pacing back and forth without stopping.

Tests

  • Find the motel: Sal's note says “Motel?” @UUID[JournalEntry.PBJeE9T9n0BjB6ag]{Ezra} can track Lonnie's phone ( Intelligence + Technology (Difficulty 3)) if they get his number from Sal's records. @UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{Hal} can ask around on the street ( Charisma + Streetwise (Difficulty 3)). @UUID[JournalEntry.dj4gIszHHTN1QRKk]{Thornquist} sells the information for a minor favor.
  • Get in without spooking him: Manipulation + Subterfuge (Difficulty 3), posing as the motel manager or as police. If they force their way in, Lonnie tries to jump out the bathroom window ( Dexterity + Athletics (Difficulty 2) to catch him).
  • Intercept at the Denny's: Wits + Awareness (Difficulty 4) to spot the two FIRSTLIGHT agents (@UUID[Actor.abaWg7NwNQvM0sDc]{MEN-02}) sitting in a van in the parking lot, and Okafor at a table by the window.

Coterie Options

Escape If the coterie intercepts Lonnie in front of FIRSTLIGHT, getting him out without being identified is Dexterity + Drive (Difficulty 4), or Dexterity + Stealth (Difficulty 4) if on foot. The agents record everything with body cameras: any failure, .
Manipulate With Lonnie: he's scared to death. Offering him protection and money is Charisma + Persuasion (Difficulty 2). Telling him what happened to Sal in detail, Charisma + Persuasion (Difficulty 1). Threatening him works ( Intimidation (Difficulty 2)), but then he lies about what he knows. With Okafor: if the coterie crosses paths with her, there's no safe way to manipulate her. See @UUID[JournalEntry.bJA2iRyDgbm2TcuK]{PNJ-18} in chapter 8.
Combat Lonnie doesn't fight. The FIRSTLIGHT agents do, and they carry incendiary ammunition and UV flashlights. A fight in a Denny's parking lot is a first-order Masquerade breach: , and the tactical team (MEN-02) arrives in eight minutes.
Disciplines Dominate on Lonnie is the easiest route: Composure 2. They can make him hand over the USB drive and forget the coterie. But then Lonnie can't testify about who hired him, and P-14 is lost unless they question him first. Obfuscate lets them into the Denny's without Okafor noticing. But the ANOMALY model on the parking-lot camera does register it.

Dialogue Guide: Lonnie Barras

Forty-something, thin, nervous, chain-smokes. Former alarm technician. Talks fast and repeats himself.

  • “Did you steal the drive?”—“I didn't steal anything. I opened doors. It's what I do. They paid me to open doors.”
  • “Who paid you?”—“A big guy, security. Dawson. Guy sniffs things out, I swear, sniffs like a dog. The money came from a company. Cascade something. Cascade Holdings. I've got the receipt.” ()
  • “Why did you make copies?”—“Because nobody pays forty grand for some podcast journalist's hard drive. If they pay that, it's worth more.” He swallows. “I didn't know it was worth this.”
  • “What's on the one you kept?”—“I don't know. I didn't open it. Okay, I opened it a little. Photos. People in photos from ten years ago who look the same as now.” He looks at them. “Same as you.”
  • “Who were you meeting?”—“A guy from the forum. Researcher. Offered me fifty grand and protection. Said he works with the government.” Pause. “Is that a lie?”
  • “What do you want?”—“Out. Far away. Alaska, Mexico, I don't care. Before what happened to Sal happens to me.”

Clues

(the payment from Cascade Holdings) · USB drive 3 (folders 2023–2026) · the name of @UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{Dawson}, Gale's ghoul

Exits

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center}, if the coterie follows Cascade Holdings: it's a Halloway Meridian company, a shareholder in Gale Sentinel. @UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{Celeste} knows because she signed off on it.
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.7brn5AgmWggUl420]{A3-E01 · The Other Son}, if Lonnie is under the coterie's protection: Krell may go after him instead of a Touchstone.

Storyteller Notes

  • If FIRSTLIGHT gets Lonnie and USB drive 3: . Okafor has a witness talking about “people who don't age” and about Cascade Holdings. That, curiously, is also a problem for @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway}: FIRSTLIGHT starts to suspect its own source. If the coterie learns about this later, they can use it in @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}.
  • If Krell gets Lonnie on Night 6: Lonnie dies. USB drive 3 goes to Halloway's vault along with the original.
  • What to do with Lonnie if the coterie protects him: @UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Montgomery} can get him out of the city. @UUID[JournalEntry.WHkwE8CYfaKW5WyO]{Rosa} can hide him in Everett. Thornquist can sell him a new identity. @UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Bear}, if someone asks him, says: “I know guys like this. If you don't get him out of the state, in a week he's selling something again.”
  • USB drive 3 has a special folder: “SAFE.” It contains the fourteen photos of David, the transcript of episode 112, and a note from Helen: “Who is he? What is he? Why does he look out for me?” Who opens it and what they do with it (give it to David, return it to Helen, delete it) is up to the players. If they give it to David, he looks at it without a word and keeps it.

• MEN-01 · Lonnie Barras · MEN-04 · Dawson · MEN-13 · Sal Medeiros · MEN-14 · Corwin (Caitiff)
  • P-13 · Sal's Ledger · P-14 · Payment from Cascade Holdings
  • A2-E06 · The One Who Kept One
  • Minor locations (no map): Sal's warehouse in SoDo, Shamrock gym (Tacoma), Starlite motel (Aurora Avenue)
  • Dates: Night 3 = Sat, Nov 14 (Elysium) · Night 4 = Sun, Nov 15 (warehouse, 2:00 a.m.) · Night 5 = Mon, Nov 16 (Denny's, 11:00 p.m.)

Nights 6 and 7. The plot closes in on the coterie. @UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{Krell} stops hiding and goes after someone they care about. In the @UUID[JournalEntry.zSkwEUUtkNGhfXun]{Gale Sentinel} servers, the hand of @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway} shows itself. The two sons of @UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Vance} come face to face. And the Sheriff, who has been wavering the whole adventure, gets the proof he's been waiting for, even if it's fake.

By the end of Part 3, the coterie should know that Halloway is behind everything. What they don't need to have yet is a way to prove it before the Primogen. That gets decided in Part 4.

What Changes in This Part

  • Krell disobeys. Halloway orders him to eliminate whoever follows the trail. Krell decides otherwise: he wants @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David} face to face, and for that he needs a hostage, not a corpse. It's the first decision of his own he makes in the whole adventure.
  • The original moves. On Night 6, @UUID[JournalEntry.y8Ao3xEHH3W11EJe]{Gale} moves the original drive from the data center to the vault in Halloway Tower (@UUID[JournalEntry.L6Fl1S0tjkWno2we]{Halloway Tower}). If the coterie reaches Gale Sentinel on Night 6 or earlier, the original is still there.
  • A new clue: @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.jqTQDyJH3ogdAuWO]{The Folios on the German}, the folios from Vance's journal that talk about Krell, scanned by @UUID[Actor.eRE6FTNdGO76lzPK]{Mr. Pell} and stored on Gale's servers. Halloway never gave them to Krell. The coterie can find them in @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center} and use them in @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell}.

Storyteller Context

Night 6, Tuesday, November 17, shortly after midnight. If the coterie hasn't stopped @UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{Krell} before now, Krell goes after the most exposed person in the coterie's circle. He doesn't want them dead: he wants them as a bargaining chip to force @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David} to come see him alone.

Choosing the target. The Storyteller picks whoever is least protected at that moment, in this order of preference:

Target When Where
@UUID[Actor.9rv5Jdb3y6bZZ1fj]{Lonnie Barras} If the coterie is protecting him after @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.5Vgl8slqjXlVRbie]{A2-E06 · The One Who Kept One} and has him hidden somewhere other than the hangar Wherever they've hidden him
@UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen Ward} If Helen went back to her apartment or is alone @UUID[JournalEntry.YD0Td8Y9aJyIpGSl]{Helen Ward's Apartment}, or the house where they're putting her up
@UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Tom “Bear” Whitman} If Bear leaves the hangar alone to run an errand A closed gun shop in SoDo where he buys ammunition
A Touchstone of another PC If the previous ones are well protected Maja (hospital), Theo (Capitol Hill bar), Ingrid (boat on Salmon Bay), Lucy Harlan (veterinary clinic)

The scene has two versions. The coterie arrives in time if someone is watching the target, if they have an agreed-upon alarm, or if a PC with Auspex (Premonition) rolls Wits + Awareness (Difficulty 4) that night. The coterie arrives late in any other case. Then they find the scene empty and a message.

If they arrive in time:

The rain slants under the streetlights. Someone stands on the opposite sidewalk, motionless, in a long gray coat too big for him in the shoulders. He isn't hiding. His hands are in his pockets, and he watches you as if he's been waiting for you. When you take a step toward him, he slowly draws out his left hand and holds it in front of his body, open, in a guard. Beside you, David goes still. He knows that guard. Almost.

If they arrive late:

The door is open. Not forced: open, as if whoever left wanted you to come in. Inside there's an overturned chair, a phone on the floor with a cracked screen, and, on the table, a folded sheet of paper weighted down with a bullet casing. The handwriting is cramped, slanting to the right, the hand of someone who writes with his left: “Terminal 86. The silos. Tomorrow, midnight. Only the American. If anyone else comes, I'll know.”

Tests

  • If they arrive in time, recognizing the guard: no roll if David is with them. David has @UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.oGnroV6R68YdMQyD]{LOR-01 · The Doctrine of Controlled Fury} at level 4 and says it quietly, without taking his eyes off him: “It's Vance's.” It's the inverted guard. Whoever uses it is a student of @UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Vance} who never finished the lesson. And David knows exactly how to break it. A PC with @UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.oGnroV6R68YdMQyD]{LOR-01 · The Doctrine of Controlled Fury} at level 4 also recognizes it without rolling.
  • If they arrive late, reading the scene: Wits + Investigation (Difficulty 3). There was a struggle, but a brief one. No blood, or very little. Whoever took the hostage did it carefully. “He doesn't want them dead,” the scene says.
  • Following the trail: Wits + Survival (Difficulty 4), @UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{Hal} at +2 dice. The smell of wet wool leads to an electric car that was waiting at the corner. The wet tires left marks heading south. If the coterie goes after him that same night, they reach Terminal 86 earlier than expected: see @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell}, “If the coterie arrives early.”
  • The note: Intelligence + Academics (Difficulty 2). The handwriting matches the penciled note in the margin of @UUID[JournalEntry.kzeWNRBY6tgLP37S]{Journal of M. Vance, Marseille, 1963, Folio 14 (Typewritten Copy)}, if the coterie has it.

Coterie Options (If They Arrive in Time)

Option What happens
Escape Get the target to safety while someone else distracts Krell: Dexterity + Athletics (Difficulty 3) to reach them, and another identical roll to get out. Krell doesn't give chase: if the hostage slips away from him, he falls back and tries again on Night 7 with another target.
Manipulate Talking to Krell in the street: he doesn't answer. He only talks to David, and only on his own terms. But he listens. If a PC says something about Vance that Krell doesn't know (for example, the cold-water business or a line from @UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.oGnroV6R68YdMQyD]{LOR-01 · The Doctrine of Controlled Fury}) and David confirms it, even with a gesture, Krell hesitates for a turn: that's the moment for another PC to get the hostage to safety.
Combat Krell fights to get away, not to win. If David is in the fight, he doesn't roll: the Storyteller narrates how he presses Krell with the complete guard. Meanwhile, Krell loses 2 dice on melee defense against the PC who attacks alongside David (inverted guard rule). Krell uses Celerity to break away and Soaring Leap to get up onto a roof. If the coterie brings him down to half his Health, he flees across the rooftops toward the water. If they incapacitate him here, scene @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell} changes: see there.
Disciplines Presence (Daunt) on Krell: he has Composure 3 and only one thing that frightens him, which is David's gaze. If whoever uses it has David beside them, Krell takes an involuntary step back: it isn't the PC's gaze that frightens him. Dominate on Krell: it requires eye contact. Krell always looks at David and no one else. Obfuscate: someone approaching unseen can take the hostage without Krell noticing ( Wits + Stealth, Difficulty 4).

Dialogue Guide: August Krell

He speaks very quietly, with a French accent. He only talks to David. He ignores the others as if they were furniture.

  • “Who are you?” — “Someone who came before you and left too soon.”
  • “Let them go.” — “I'll let them go when you come. Alone. Tomorrow.”
  • “Are you working for Halloway?” — A pause. “I work for me. He pays.”
  • “Why didn't you kill them?” — “Because I was ordered to.” He looks at him. “He never finished what he was told to do either. Did you know that? Vance. He never fully obeyed. He taught me that too.”
  • (If someone other than David speaks to him) — He doesn't answer. Doesn't even look. If what they say about Vance is true, he searches David's face to see if it's so.

Clues

None new about @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway}. The scene confirms that Krell is acting on his own and that he wants David.

Exits

@UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell} (the meeting at Terminal 86, the following night, or that same night if the coterie follows him) · @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center} (if the coterie wants to go to the meeting with something in hand, Gale's servers have the folios: @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.jqTQDyJH3ogdAuWO]{The Folios on the German})

Storyteller Notes

  • If the hostage is Bear: Bear fights back. Krell beats him, but Bear breaks two of his ribs and tears a piece off Vance's coat. Bear is left at half Health and wakes up in the silos, furious with himself. If the coterie arrives late, they go looking for something in Bear's room, and the PC who opens the safe finds @UUID[JournalEntry.5mQIPoGa4I0tQtbR]{Note Kept in Bear's Safe}, the note addressed to David. Give it to that player privately. Whether they show it to David, and when, is their call.
  • If the hostage is Helen: Helen sees Krell up close. She doesn't know what he is, but she knows he isn't a man. It counts toward @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.j1wUSqY1dsP0iFfp]{GAN-02 · The Night She Beholds the Beast}.
  • If the hostage is Lonnie: Krell keeps him alive because he thinks David wants him as a witness. That's true. Krell is starting to think like David.

Storyteller Context

Any night in Part 2 or Part 3, but it makes the most sense from Night 5 on, when the coterie is already following Gale's trail (@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.6YVCnLlyxpVum6JX]{Unlogged Gale Sentinel Data Request}, @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.9WkqebVXUF2scLLC]{The Payment from Cascade Holdings}). The coterie breaks into the Gale Sentinel campus in Bellevue (@UUID[JournalEntry.zSkwEUUtkNGhfXun]{Gale Sentinel Campus and Data Center}) to look for the original of the File and the proof that @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway} is behind it.

The campus has three layers of security. The scene is played layer by layer. At each one, the coterie chooses how to get through.

Layer What's there Threat
1 · The perimeter Parking lot, lobby with the mosaic screen, office building ANOMALY cameras at every entrance. Two mortal guards.
2 · The offices Third floor: @UUID[JournalEntry.y8Ao3xEHH3W11EJe]{Preston Gale}'s office. Office server room. Electronic locks. Dawson and two security ghouls (@UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{Halloway's Security Ghouls}) make rounds every 40 minutes.
3 · The data center Windowless building behind the main one. Three rooms: storage, ANOMALY training, private archive. Biometric door (fingerprint and retina) and a security airlock. One ghoul in the control room.

What's inside, by layer:

  • Layer 2 (Gale's office): Gale's email with the order “Recover all copies. Top priority. — C.H.” from November 13. The payment records to Lonnie from Cascade Holdings, if they don't already have them (@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.9WkqebVXUF2scLLC]{The Payment from Cascade Holdings}). Preston Gale's digital signature on the access authorizations for Market Street (@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.Pvm4xZpxzhCtg4rf]{Gale's Signature}).
  • Layer 3, storage: the original drive of the File, only until Night 6. The shipping logs for the ARCHER channel, with the reference SEA-0411 (@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.wRvr7GFOMQsgTJ2z]{SEA-0411 Shipments / DOC-07}). @UUID[JournalEntry.WW7eg88I0uDGj8ks]{FIRSTLIGHT, Internal Memo SEA-0411} in full.
  • Layer 3, ANOMALY training: the “cold subjects” database. Every Kindred in Seattle recorded by the doorbells, with photos, times, and places. It includes the coterie if the 3B camera recorded them in @UUID[JournalEntry.w9xeQJg6psfiMjFU.JournalEntryPage.yyXMKcpDOIhGuZIB]{A0-E01 · The Call from SAFE}. @UUID[JournalEntry.YhmNvLugMfCZezEH]{Gale Sentinel: 2027 Product Roadmap, Confidential}, if they don't have it.
  • Layer 3, private archive: a separate, air-gapped server holding Halloway's personal archive, scanned by @UUID[Actor.eRE6FTNdGO76lzPK]{Mr. Pell}: correspondence, contracts, and @UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Vance}'s complete journals, as images. That's where the folios about “the German” are (@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.jqTQDyJH3ogdAuWO]{The Folios on the German}).

Lobby:

Two a.m. The Gale Sentinel lobby is empty except for a guard looking at his phone behind the front desk. The screen on the wall is still on: a mosaic of thousands of live feeds, porches, hallways, rain. Beneath it, the slogan in white letters: “We see what the city doesn't.” In the top corner of each image is a tiny number. Some of them are red.

Data center:

Past the airlock, the air is dry and cold and smells of hot dust. Rows of black cabinets hum under blue lights. On one wall is a screen with a grid of faces, hundreds of them, each with a label underneath: COLD_SUBJECT, and a number. Some of them you know from Elysium. One of them is your own.

Tests by Layer

  • Layer 1, getting in without being logged by ANOMALY: Intelligence + Technology (Difficulty 4) to disable the module from outside. @UUID[JournalEntry.PBJeE9T9n0BjB6ag]{Ezra} gets +2 dice if he has already discovered that the firmware is his. With @UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.qA75WygzgVjOeJvT]{LOR-03 · The City's Eyes} at level 4, automatic. If no one disables it, every Kindred who enters gets logged: in total.
  • Layer 2, the locks: Dexterity + Larceny (Difficulty 3), or Intelligence + Technology (Difficulty 3). Avoiding @UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{Dawson}'s rounds: Wits + Stealth (Difficulty 3) for the whole group. If anyone fails, see Combat.
  • Layer 2, searching the office: Intelligence + Investigation (Difficulty 3). One success: @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.Pvm4xZpxzhCtg4rf]{Gale's Signature}. Three or more: the “C.H.” email as well.
  • Layer 3, the biometrics: it takes Gale's or Dawson's fingerprint and retina. See Options. Forcing the airlock: Strength + Athletics (Difficulty 5), but it sets off the alarm.
  • Layer 3, the private archive: the server has no network. The files have to be copied by hand with Intelligence + Technology (Difficulty 3). Finding the folios about “the German” among thousands of images: Intelligence + Investigation (Difficulty 4), or automatic if someone searches for the word “allemand.”

Coterie Options

Option What happens
Escape Getting out without leaving a trace, once inside: Wits + Stealth (Difficulty 3) per layer. If the alarm goes off, Dawson takes four minutes to reach the data center, and the Bellevue police take twelve. Running across the campus in front of the cameras: .
Manipulate @UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{Celeste} can walk in the front door as a shareholder. Requesting a night visit “to review the security of the investment” takes no roll, but Pell hears about it within an hour. If she already fell into the trap in @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.uL8F2YNogcToiFc6]{A2-E01 · Elysium Night} and reviewed the Cascade accounts, Gale receives her in person, nervous. With Gale: Manipulation + Persuasion (Difficulty 4) to get him to walk Celeste to the data center and put his hand on the reader. With the mortal guards: a reasonable story and Manipulation + Subterfuge (Difficulty 3).
Combat Direct assault: possible, but loud. Dawson and his two ghouls (@UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{Halloway's Security Ghouls}) fight well, and Dawson can smell Kindred within twenty meters. If the coterie forces its way in, , and Gale warns Halloway, who moves the original that same night if they don't take it. Dawson alive and captured is a witness: Gale's ghoul, he sniffed out Helen's stairwell and took the drive from Lonnie's hands.
Disciplines Dominate on Dawson or Gale to open the biometrics: Gale has Composure 2 and is easy; Dawson has Resolve 3 and a Blood Bond to Halloway that gives him +2 dice to resist. Obfuscate doesn't fool ANOMALY (see @UUID[JournalEntry.YhmNvLugMfCZezEH]{Gale Sentinel: 2027 Product Roadmap, Confidential}), unless the module is disabled. Auspex (Heightened Senses) lets you hear Dawson's rounds before he arrives: +2 dice on the layer 2 Stealth roll.

Dialogue Guide: Preston Gale

Early fifties, salon tan, investor-pitch smile. He talks in slogans. When he's scared, he talks faster. He needs his dose of Vitae every ten days, and he was due three days ago.

  • “What does Gale Sentinel do with the data?” — “We make the city safer. We see what the city doesn't.”
  • “Who is Northline?” — “A security partner. Consulting. Very serious people.” He wipes his forehead. “Why?”
  • “Northline is the Second Inquisition.” — Silence. “No. No, that's not... Mr. Halloway said they were...” He stops. “Who are you people?”
  • “Who gave you the order to steal the archive?” — “I didn't steal anything. I located. It's a service. He asks for something, I find it.” Pause. “I've been finding everything for twenty-six years.”
  • (To Celeste, if she's there) — “Ms. Arden. Your signature is on all of this. You know that, don't you? You authorized it.”

What the Folios on the German Say (P-15)

Hand them out as a handout. They're two folios from Vance's journal, written in Marseille in 1976, in French, with a typewritten translation by Mr. Pell alongside. The text is on the next page, “The Folios on the German,” visible to the players.

Clues

(the SEA-0411 shipments) · (Gale's signature) · (the folios on the German) · the “C.H.” email · the original drive (only until Night 6) · the cold subjects database

If they didn't already have it, Gale's office also yields (the payment records to Lonnie from Cascade Holdings).

Exits

  • @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell}, with P-15 in hand. The conversation with Krell changes completely.
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}, with P-10, P-11, and the C.H. email, the coterie has documentary evidence. What it still lacks is a living witness.
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.aGN9NHO00wmdUzVn]{A3-E04 · The Pack Wavers}, if @UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Montgomery} learns about the break-in before the coterie tells him what they found.

Storyteller Notes

  • Wiping the cold subjects database: Intelligence + Technology (Difficulty 4). If it succeeds, the Thermometer drops 2 (), because FIRSTLIGHT loses half its evidence. But Gale detects it the next day, and Halloway knows the coterie was there.
  • Cutting off Northline's access: Intelligence + Technology (Difficulty 3). The Thermometer stops rising from the cameras for the rest of the adventure. But the analyst @UUID[JournalEntry.D611Mcr17F6HHEUw]{Hale} notices the cutoff and wonders who did it. If Ezra does it with his own code, he leaves a signature Hale may recognize later (chronicle hook).
  • If Celeste goes in alone and sees her signature on everything: this is the moment of her crisis. The player decides what she does with the evidence. Taking it to her sire is a legitimate option, and the most interesting one.
  • If the coterie takes the original: Halloway knows on Night 7. He changes plans: in @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council} he can no longer present the File as evidence against the Prince, so he speeds up the leak to FIRSTLIGHT with what he already has. on Night 7.

Two folios from M. Vance's journal, written in Marseille in 1976, in French, with a typewritten translation by Mr. Pell alongside.

Folio 41 — Marseille, September 1976

I left this morning before he woke. I left him the inverted guard and nothing more. He will hate me. That is only fair.

I am not leaving because he is weak. I am leaving because he is better than the American. Faster, colder, cleaner. And he has nothing on the other side of the sea. The American holds on because he has a daughter he never names. The German has no one. A perfect weapon with nothing to hold it back is not a weapon. It is a catastrophe that has not happened yet.

If I teach him the full guard, no one will be able to stop him. Not even I.

May God forgive me, if there is any left who listens to our kind.

Folio 42

If the American and the German should ever meet, let the American teach him the other guard. I could not. Perhaps he can. He knows what it is to have something to lose.

— M. V.

[At the foot of the translation, in Mr. Pell's hand:] Mr. Halloway: are these folios to be delivered to subject K., as promised? — P.

[Below, in another hand, thin and upright:] No. — C.H.

pages.name: A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell

text.content:
Storyteller Context

Night 7, Wednesday, November 18, midnight, if @UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{Krell} took a hostage in @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.7brn5AgmWggUl420]{A3-E01 · The Other Son}. If he didn't, the summons arrives another way: a note on the hangar door in the same handwriting.

The location is the Terminal 86 grain elevator (@UUID[JournalEntry.lIohEQe1KFTOCQ0U]{The Terminal 86 Grain Elevator}), north of downtown: a row of forty-meter concrete silos by the water, with a conveyor gallery up top linking the silos to the pier. Krell waits in the gallery. The hostage, if there is one, is tied to a chair beside an open loading hatch above the bay, thirty meters over the water.

Krell demands David. The coterie decides whether to bring him, and how. If the coterie found the note, they also decide whether to show it to him.

The coterie... What happens
Brings David alone, as Krell asked, and hides David climbs the outside stairs. The others approach with the Stealth roll (see Tests). While hidden, the PCs earn no steps: either they show themselves, or they give David an open phone line in his pocket and feed him what to say. Every truth David repeats counts as spoken by that PC. He won't repeat the part about @UUID[JournalEntry.VYpDoFtqKkL7FlqL]{Emily}: someone has to say that to Krell's face.
Arrives with David, everyone in plain sight Krell knows, and he pushes the chair to the edge, without letting it fall. He talks just the same, with David. The others are furniture, but he hears them.
Goes without David Krell talks to no one. He asks just once: “Where is the American?” Then he gets up. There are no steps and no offers: the scene is about rescuing the hostage or fighting (Escape or Combat). If David finds out later, let the coterie explain it to him.

Krell said “only the American.” If the whole coterie comes and lets itself be seen, Krell knows ( Krell: Wits + Awareness (7 dice)) and pushes the chair toward the edge, though he doesn't let it fall. He wants to talk, not kill. But if he senses a trap, he goes out through the hatch and takes the hostage with him.

What Krell wants: for @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David} to see him. For him to say out loud that @UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Vance} has two sons. And to know why Vance chose the other one.

What Krell doesn't know: that @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway} was never going to give him the folios, or the Harbor Island domain.

If David doesn't know Krell is his blood brother (the coterie kept the clue from @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.j4TnqYOwVuSCeQ0z]{A2-E02 · “Locate. Evaluate. Execute.”} to themselves), he finds out here, from Krell or from a PC. Who tells him, and whether it's before the climb or up top, in front of Krell, is the coterie's call. If he finds out from Krell, David looks at the coterie and understands that they already knew.

What David does: he's there, he watches, he confirms. He doesn't lead the conversation: the PCs do. Krell talks to him and never once looks at them. Let that be uncomfortable.

The service stairs zigzag up the outside of the silo to a long, narrow gallery of sheet metal and grimy glass. Inside, a stalled conveyor belt runs end to end. It smells of old grain and the sea. At the far end, an open hatch looks out over the bay, letting in the wind and the rain, and in front of it sits a chair with someone tied to it. Seated on the belt, elbows on his knees, gray coat hanging open, a man with a shaved head watches you arrive. He doesn't get up. “Come,” he says to David. “Sit. I've wanted to ask you something for fifty years.”

Tests

  • Getting the rest of the coterie there unseen: Dexterity + Stealth (Difficulty 4) against Krell's Wits + Awareness (7 dice). There are three approaches: the outside stairs (the ones David uses), the inside of the neighboring silo ( Athletics, Difficulty 3, to climb), and the water (coming in by boat under the hatch).
  • Reading Krell during the conversation: Wits + Insight (Difficulty 3). On a success, the Storyteller tells the player whether Krell is about to attack, leave, or weep.
  • The conversation: it isn't a single roll. The Storyteller keeps count of steps toward Krell's turn. Every true thing a PC tells him about Vance, about Emily, or about the guard, with David present, adds 1 step. Krell doesn't believe the coterie: he believes David's face. That's why it counts the same whether David confirms it, breaks down, or gets angry. What changes is what David thinks afterward of whoever said it. A lie adds nothing: David can't hold it up, and Krell sees that. The steps come from what the coterie has discovered and decides to share: @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.xQqepYpthm1bxP8u]{Halloway Knows About the Cold Water}, @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.HYE4rNbNf1sEbYGe]{The Inverted Guard}, @UUID[JournalEntry.kzeWNRBY6tgLP37S]{Journal of M. Vance, Marseille, 1963, Folio 14 (Typewritten Copy)}, the part about @UUID[JournalEntry.VYpDoFtqKkL7FlqL]{Emily}, and the Larchmont. David knows these things, but he doesn't bring them up on his own. At 3 steps, Krell is willing to hear an offer. Showing him @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.jqTQDyJH3ogdAuWO]{The Folios on the German} adds 3 steps at once.

Coterie Options

Option What happens
Escape Freeing the hostage while Krell talks to David: a PC hidden in the neighboring silo can reach the chair with Dexterity + Stealth (Difficulty 4). If they manage it without Krell noticing, the hostage is safe and the conversation goes on. If Krell notices, he gets up and the scene turns to Combat.
Manipulate This scene is a conversation. See the dialogue guide and the “steps.” When Krell reaches 3 steps, the coterie chooses what to offer him. One PC speaks. David is beside them, and Krell looks at him:
1. Witness. “Come with us before the Primogen and say who hired you.” Manipulation + Persuasion (Difficulty 3), +1 die if David backs it out loud. Krell sets a condition: that David promise him no one will destroy him afterward. If the coterie asks him to, David promises. But keeping that promise afterward falls to the coterie. (@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.jXff6tMXQQbmJg0m]{Krell's Testimony})
2. Turn him in. “We're taking you to the Sheriff.” Krell doesn't accept. He has to be subdued.
3. The other guard. “David will teach you what Vance didn't.” The coterie offers it on David's behalf. It only works if the coterie found P-15 and David read folio 42: it's what Vance asked of him, and David honors it. No roll: Krell goes quiet for a very long time. Then he accepts. He becomes a witness and something like a brother.
4. Destroy him. See Combat.
Combat If the conversation breaks down or the coterie attacks, Krell fights for real. David fights alongside the coterie, without rolling: the Storyteller narrates what he does. In the narrow gallery, the inverted guard rule applies against the PC who attacks alongside David: Krell loses 2 dice on melee defense. Krell tries to throw his opponents out through the hatch ( Krell: Strength + Brawl against Dexterity + Athletics; whoever falls takes 4 bashing damage on hitting the water, thirty meters down). If he drops to half his Health, he throws himself into the water and disappears. Destroying him is possible if the coterie immobilizes him: 1 Stain for whoever strikes the final blow, unless it's done in combat. If the players ask David to do it, David does it without a word. The Stain belongs to whoever asked.
Disciplines Dominate: Krell only looks at David. To Dominate him, a PC has to get Krell to look at them. If they manage it, it works, but Krell notices when it ends and considers it an unforgivable betrayal, by the coterie and by David. No later offer is possible. A PC's Presence (Awe) is useless: Krell doesn't want to feel that for anyone else. If the coterie asks David to use his Presence, the Storyteller narrates it without a roll: +1 step, because it's exactly what Krell wants to feel. Auspex 4 (Spirit's Touch) on the coat: Vance wearing it on a cold Marseille morning, his back turned, walking away.

Dialogue Guide: August Krell

Very low, very slow. He talks to David as if the others didn't exist. He doesn't make threats: he says things. When a PC speaks to him, he answers looking at David.

  • “What do you want to ask him?” — “Why you?” A long pause, to David. “I was faster. I wasn't afraid of the cold water. I obeyed him in everything. And he left one morning without saying goodbye, and with you he finished the lesson. Why you?”
  • “He doesn't know.” (a PC, on his behalf) — Krell looks at David. David shakes his head, slowly. “That's the first honest answer anyone's given me in fifty years.” (+1 step.)
  • “Because he had a daughter.” — Silence. “Had?” If a PC tells him about @UUID[JournalEntry.VYpDoFtqKkL7FlqL]{Emily}, Krell searches David's face to see if it's true. He finds it. He lowers his eyes for the first time. (+1 step.) If the one telling it is @UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{Hal}, who was in that apartment in 1996, it's the first time either of them has spoken about that night. David doesn't look at him.
  • “The guard he left you is a lock.” (if the coterie read @UUID[JournalEntry.kzeWNRBY6tgLP37S]{Journal of M. Vance, Marseille, 1963, Folio 14 (Typewritten Copy)} or saw @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.HYE4rNbNf1sEbYGe]{The Inverted Guard}) — Krell looks at David. David raises his right hand and shows him the full guard, without a word. Krell looks at it for a long time. “A lock.” He nods. “And you have the key.” (+1 step.)
  • “Halloway is using you.” — “Everyone uses everyone. He promised me the folios where Vance talks about me. And your domain,” he says to David.
  • “He was never going to give them to you.” (with P-15) — Krell reads the folios. He reads the note at the end twice. He says nothing for a long time. Then: “‘A perfect weapon with nothing to hold it back.’” He laughs, once. “The old man was right.” (+3 steps.)
  • “Where is Vance?” — “I don't know. I looked for him in Cluj in '87. There was nothing. Not even ash.”
  • “What do you want now?” (at 3 steps or more) — To David: “For someone to say out loud that I existed. That I was his son too.” If a PC says it, Krell waits for David to say it. If the coterie asks him to, David says it.
  • (If the coterie offers him the other guard) — He stands. For the first time, he offers David his right hand. “Then you finish what he started, American.”

Clues

(Krell's testimony, if he agrees to be a witness) · confirmation that Krell is Vance's childe

Endings

Ending Consequences
Krell as witness He testifies in @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}. It's the strongest possible evidence against Halloway: +3 dice on the final Council roll. @UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Montgomery} wants to destroy him afterward. David promised no one would, so if the coterie protects Krell, there's tension with the Sheriff. If they don't protect him, David broke his word to his brother, and he doesn't forgive the coterie for it.
Krell learns the other guard Same as above, and in addition Krell becomes Allies 2 for the coterie. David raises @UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.oGnroV6R68YdMQyD]{LOR-01 · The Doctrine of Controlled Fury} to level 5 (Heir of the Fist): from that night on, a PC can buy LOR-01 up to level 3 with David as mentor. To play it: David has something to do for the first time in years, finishing what Vance didn't.
Krell turned over to the Sheriff Montgomery destroys him without a trial. The coterie earns the Sheriff's favor for @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.aGN9NHO00wmdUzVn]{A3-E04 · The Pack Wavers} (+2 dice). But without testimony, the Council is harder. David doesn't stop it, but he's shaken: the coterie handed his brother over to be destroyed without a trial. From that night on he stops trusting the Sheriff, and the coterie a little.
Krell destroyed by the coterie Same as above, without the Sheriff's favor if no one tells him. If the players asked David to strike the blow, the Stain belongs to whoever asked, and David never talks about Vance with them again. @UUID[JournalEntry.AeAhHuCNHL9KWVnT]{Fry}, at the next Elysium, wears mourning.
Krell flees He reappears in @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.tG1m5PTkmBA1pvmc]{A4-E03 · The Last Ferry}, on one side or the other, depending on how the conversation ended. If it reached 3 steps, he shows up to help.

Exits

@UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.aGN9NHO00wmdUzVn]{A3-E04 · The Pack Wavers} (what happened at the silos reaches Montgomery's ears that same night, because Halloway had the meeting photographed from a drone) · @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}

Storyteller Notes

  • This is the most important scene in the adventure for David, and it's the coterie that carries it: what they tell him, what they say for him, what they offer Krell in his name. Give it time. The coterie doesn't need to resolve it quickly.
  • David doesn't resolve the scene. If the players wait for him to speak, let the silence last. David looks at Krell, Krell looks at David, and the rain blows in through the hatch.
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.y8Ao3xEHH3W11EJe]{Gale}'s drone records from outside, two hundred meters away, without sound. What the footage shows is David sitting beside the dockside killer, talking calmly. That's what Halloway shows Montgomery. If the coterie went without David, the drone records the Hound's coterie with the killer, and it serves Halloway just as well.
  • If the hostage is @UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Bear} and gets free, Bear doesn't forgive Krell for the ambush. But if Krell learns the other guard, Bear tells David, grudgingly: “When you train him, do it far from my shop.”

Storyteller Context

Late on Night 7, or early on Night 8. @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway} hands @UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Montgomery} what he's spent a week preparing: the drone footage of @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David} with @UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{Krell} at the silos (or of the coterie with Krell, if they went without David), a photo of @UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Vance}'s coat on Krell's shoulders, a forged letter signed “M.V.” and addressed to David, found “in the hangar” by one of Gale's ghouls (a lie), and the Elysium rumor that the Hound destroyed his sire. Halloway doesn't accuse. He only asks: “Isn't that curious?”

Montgomery summons the coterie to the farm (@UUID[JournalEntry.NNzMhIvsavpG0iTQ]{The Sheriff's Farm and Boat Landing}). This time he invites them inside. That, as @UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{Hal} knows, is a bad sign.

The scene is a trial without judges. Montgomery wants to believe David. But he has evidence on the table and forty-eight years on the job telling him not to believe anyone.

Montgomery questions David. David gives the bare minimum (“I went to get the hostage”) and doesn't explain himself: he never does. The rest has to come from the coterie.

If the coterie has already told Montgomery about Krell and shown him @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.jqTQDyJH3ogdAuWO]{The Folios on the German} or the C.H. email, skip the first half: Montgomery is already convinced, and the scene becomes planning for the climax.

This time, the farmhouse door is open. Inside is a room with a cold fireplace, a long wooden table, and, on the table, a tablet showing a grainy still: the silo gallery seen from outside, two figures sitting on a conveyor belt. Next to the tablet lies an open envelope with a handwritten letter. The dogs lie on the porch with their backs to the house, as if they don't want to look. Montgomery stands by the window. “Sit down,” he says. “This time it really is a visit.”

Tests

The private elevator climbs forty-two floors without a sound. It opens onto an enormous room with a single wall of glass over Elliott Bay: the harbor cranes, the ferry lights, the island where the Hound lives, all of it small, all of it still. In the center stands a long table of dark wood with seven chairs. Halloway stands at its head, hands clasped behind his back. He doesn't smile. On the table, in front of each chair, lies a closed folder with a name on it. When the Prince enters, Halloway inclines his head exactly as far as required. “Your Highness. Thank you for coming. This city has a problem, and I believe you know what it is.”

How the Scene Works

The Council has three stages: the motion (Halloway presents his case), the debate (the coterie and the others respond), and the vote.

1 · The Motion

Halloway speaks for five minutes without interruption. His case:

  • The Second Inquisition has a source inside the court (true: it's him).
  • That source has leaked three havens, all in the Prince's and the Sheriff's circle (true).
  • There's a killer on the docks who fights like the Hound's sire, and the Hound has met with him in secret (half true). He shows the drone footage.
  • The Prince received a warning from Regent Voight and didn't read it for two nights (true).
  • The Inquisition's source has been identified: the deliveries were paid for through Cascade Holdings. And then he opens the folder marked “C. Arden.”

Celeste's sacrifice. Halloway accuses his own childe of being ARCHER, with her signature on the accounts as proof. He does it with rehearsed sorrow: “This pains me more than anyone.” He asks the Primogen to hand her over to the Sheriff. That way he clears himself and shows he's willing to sacrifice his own “for the Masquerade.”

If Celeste is a PC, give the player a moment before you go on. See Notes.

2 · The Debate

The coterie responds. Whoever speaks for it makes the case roll:

Manipulation + Politics (Difficulty 4) or Charisma + Politics (Difficulty 4), +1 die for each piece of evidence on the checklist. Halloway answers with his own pool ( Halloway: Manipulation + Politics (10 dice)). It's a contested test. The margin decides:

Coterie's margin Result
Halloway wins The room believes him. Celeste is handed over. The votes lean toward the regency (see the vote, unchanged).
Tie or 1–2 successes Doubt. Nobody fully believes anybody. The vote decides.
3–4 successes Halloway is exposed. The vote almost certainly turns against him.
5 or more Total exposure. The Prince orders the Sheriff to arrest Halloway on the spot. Halloway flees: see Notes and @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.tG1m5PTkmBA1pvmc]{A4-E03 · The Last Ferry}.

3 · The Vote

Halloway needs 3 votes in favor out of 5. Each Primogen has a default vote and a condition that changes it:

Dialogue Guide: Mr. Pell

Ninety-six, looks sixty. Soft, polite voice, a butler from another era. He has served a single master for more than sixty years.

  • “Give us the briefcase.” — “I'm sorry. It isn't mine.”
  • “Halloway is going to let you die.” — Silence. “Mr. Halloway has fed me since 1958.” A pause. “Though it's true he's been late with it lately.”
  • “What's inside?” — “Twelve years of a woman who watched. Seventy of a man who waited.” He looks at the water. “I typed up Mr. Vance's journals, you know. Three copies. There were sentences that made me weep.”
  • (If he hands over the briefcase) — “Tell the journalist I'm sorry about her apartment. It was very tidy.”

Editor's Note

Doc 13 said Pell has served Halloway since 1950 (“seventy years”); it was settled as 1958, the year of Halloway's Embrace (“more than sixty years”). The age of 96 and the appearance of 60 stand.

What the Players Know and What the Hunters Know

The players know who ARCHER is. The hunters don't. There's only one rule: play what your hunter knows. The Storyteller can ask, “How does Hale know?” and if the answer is “because I read it in Part 3,” it doesn't count.

Sooner or later a player will want their hunter to fail in order to protect their vampire. That's allowed, and it isn't free. Every interlude has an option that leaves the Cell empty-handed: if it's chosen, the Cell's Desperation goes up 1 (@UUID[JournalEntry.dnsWkdXVJ19riBLa.JournalEntryPage.O8yPSIYLlTrKHm8G]{The Puget Cell}). A desperate cell doesn't back off: it goes into the raid with the generator on and no warning. Failing on purpose lowers today's risk and raises Night 8's.

When it ends, the Storyteller notes three things:

Safety

The interludes put the players on the side of whoever is hunting their characters. Go over the table's Lines and Veils (@UUID[JournalEntry.BPqr3MwJXyy5lXZz]{Safety Tools}) before the first one. Northline's white room, with its lamps, is an interrogation room: if the table vetoed it, the room exists, but nobody uses it on screen.

The bare minimum of Hunter: The Reckoning (5th ed.) to play the interludes. If you have the rulebook, the rulebook wins. The pregens' Edges and Perks are written in our own words, built for Seattle: if the rulebook has one that's similar, use the book's.

Creed. What the hunter does best during the Hunt. Each Creed has a Creed field: the type of action in which the hunter can add Desperation dice.

Creed Creed Field In the Cell
Inquisitive Gaining information: documentation, breaking and entering, interrogation Okafor, Hale
Martial Physical conflict, supernatural or not Ransom
Faithful Direct conflict with the supernatural (physical, social, or mental) Navarro
Underground Stealth and subterfuge Pak
Entrepreneurial Building, inventing, enhancing, or repairing Sorensen

Drive and Redemption. Why they hunt. Each Drive says when the hunter is redeemed: when they meet that condition, they come out of Despair (see below). On the wod5e sheet, Drive appears as Motivation.

Desperation. It belongs to the Cell, not to each hunter: a number from 0 to 5. When a hunter rolls something that falls within their Creed field, they can add as many Desperation dice as the Cell has marked. If any of those dice comes up 1, the player chooses:

  • Overreach: the roll stands as rolled, and the Cell's Danger goes up 1. The quarry finds out something.
  • Despair: the roll fails, and the hunter falls into Despair. They can't add Desperation dice again until they're redeemed through their Drive.

If the roll had already failed, there's no choice: Despair. The wod5e roll dialog offers Desperation dice to hunter-type actors and marks the result.

Danger. From 0 to 5, also the Cell's. It measures how much the quarry knows about the hunters. It mirrors the Thermometer: the Thermometer measures what FIRSTLIGHT knows about the coterie; Danger, what the coterie (or the city) knows about FIRSTLIGHT.

Edges and Perks. What the hunter brings to the Hunt that no one else has: access, gear, a gift they don't understand. Each Edge can have Perks that refine it. They're in the Edges tab of the sheet.

They're mortal. Health and Willpower like any mortal in V5. Disciplines work on them, except for Okafor's and Hale's Faith, which subtracts dice. Damage from a Kindred is superficial or aggravated depending on the attack; for the weapons in FIRSTLIGHT's arsenal, see @UUID[Actor.abaWg7NwNQvM0sDc]{FIRSTLIGHT Tactical Team} and the Storyteller Screen.

Tests are written as in the rest of the module, Attribute + Skill and Difficulty. If the test falls within the Creed field, the text says so: (Desperation: Inquisitive).

The tactical team sleeps in a waterfront warehouse, not at Northline.

The hunters (hunter-type actors, with the Cell as their group): Okafor, Hale, @UUID[Actor.5ywnpdrw93wmy235]{Cole Ransom}, and three named operators: @UUID[Actor.cacjzuu13Bv7mJH5]{Teresa “Tess” Navarro}, @UUID[Actor.yyJApTmnANPPdw3O]{Owen Pak}, and @UUID[Actor.2hdWrhkD65ZNl4Xs]{Lena Sorensen}. The other two operators remain the simplified sheet from @UUID[Actor.abaWg7NwNQvM0sDc]{FIRSTLIGHT Tactical Team}.

Desperation and Danger

Proposed. The Cell starts at Desperation 1 (a single cell, a budget that doesn't stretch, and a source nobody trusts) and Danger 0 (the quarry doesn't know it exists). They move like this over the course of the adventure, whether or not the interludes are played:

Desperation When
+1 The quarry beats them in a race: the coterie takes the Pike USB drive before chain of custody (@UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.DtetdHiBnOLQaM6Y]{A1-E02 · Ash on Pier 46}) or snatches Lonnie out from under their noses in @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.5Vgl8slqjXlVRbie]{A2-E06 · The One Who Kept One}
+1 An operator is badly wounded or dies
+1 The coterie cuts Northline's access to ANOMALY or wipes the cold subject database (@UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center})
+1 In an interlude, the players choose the option that leaves the Cell empty-handed
−1 The Cell gets something solid: an identified cold subject, Lonnie and USB drive 3, a confirmed ARCHER target
Danger When
+1 Each Overreach (see Hunter on One Page)
+1 The coterie identifies a member of the Cell: the agents at the Denny's, the van, Hale's face
+1 The coterie, or @UUID[JournalEntry.yaAsxCkCLf8CANL5]{Voight}, reads @UUID[JournalEntry.WW7eg88I0uDGj8ks]{FIRSTLIGHT, Internal Memo SEA-0411}
+2 Someone gets into Northline (@UUID[JournalEntry.KioeAEZP78U0Coz5]{Northline Cyber Advisory}), whether they're discovered or not

Danger in the interludes. At Danger 3 or more, the Difficulty of any hunter test to go unnoticed goes up 1: the quarry already knows what to look for.

Desperation in the raid. When @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.ogKpm1VYgcVGCw1T]{A4-E02 · The Raid} begins:

  • Desperation 3 or more: the sunlight generator is already on when they go in (advantage V4 from @UUID[JournalEntry.dnsWkdXVJ19riBLa.JournalEntryPage.8DXPPUEUUp5bHka5]{INT-00 · Advantages and Cracks for the Raid}, free).
  • Desperation 4 or more: there's no bullhorn. Okafor gives no warning. The first line of the dialogue guide comes after the light (advantage V5, free).
  • Desperation 5: Okafor leaves the car and goes in behind the team, with her Glock and her bad hand in her pocket. Her Faith goes with her.

In Foundry

The Cell is a group actor of type cell, in the FIRSTLIGHT/Puget Cell folder of the characters compendium. The six hunters are its members: their sheets pull Desperation from there. Danger is marked on the Cell's sheet. If From Veil to Vigil is active, its panel finds the Cell too: it's the only cell in the world (see @UUID[JournalEntry.jiea701LDJdMoHoY]{Red Tide · Continuation After FIN-D}).

For 4–5 players using the five new concepts (@UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{Celeste Arden} to @UUID[JournalEntry.gRfqeOIXEHOcLemr]{Dr. Ruth Abernathy}); with four, one goes unused. These are concepts with backstory; the players build the mechanical character sheet with the core rulebook. Sections marked “Secret” are for the Storyteller only.

pages.name: Which Clans I Recommend and Why

text.content:
The coterie has no Brujah: the city already has four, all NPCs (David, who travels with the coterie, Rosa, Krell, and O'Connor), so it's best not to repeat the clan. Each clan below opens a different front of the plot, so everyone gets their moment.

Clan Plot front Why it works
Ventrue Politics and infiltration of Halloway's circle Puts the coterie inside the antagonist's house. Creates the strongest loyalty dilemma in the adventure.
Nosferatu Information, the underground, and the surveillance network Seattle is the city of data, and a hacker Nosferatu is the natural counterweight to Gale Sentinel and FIRSTLIGHT.
Toreador The Prince's court and Helen's circle With a Toreador Prince, this character lives at the center of the coup. They can also be tied to the podcast.
Gangrel The Sheriff's pack, tracking, and combat Connects to Montgomery and to David's past. Gives weight to the scene where the Sheriff hesitates (@UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.aGN9NHO00wmdUzVn]{A3-E04 · The Pack Wavers}).
Tremere (alternative) Forensics, Blood Sorcery, and the crack in the Masquerade With five players, joins the table. With four, can replace any of the above.

Recommendation for 4 players: Ventrue, Nosferatu, Toreador, and Gangrel. The Tremere stays as the spare. For 5: all five.

Every character appears in the Ward File. When the drive is stolen, they're all exposed at once, and Sheriff Montgomery wastes no time telling them: “You're all on the same drive. You get it back together or you go down together.” It's a Commando coterie, with its domain on the Harbor Island docks, around the hangar David lends them as a haven, and each player gets their folder (@UUID[JournalEntry.vtenvgNlXVPd99Rc]{“Your Folder in the File”}).

The full coterie page (concept, alternatives, members and agendas, customs, type, domain, and shared Backgrounds, with what doc 02 says and what doc 08 settles) is at @UUID[JournalEntry.azX1hjbc0PUp2AA2.JournalEntryPage.kiaygGF4KgylB6fb]{The Archived}.

• David and Bear are NPCs. They help: +1 die to the PC who rolls, or an action you narrate without a roll. They don't resolve on their own what belongs to the coterie, and they don't make its decisions; they give opinions, push, react. David's plot (Vance, Emily, Helen, the Larchmont, Krell) is for the PCs to uncover, and they're the ones who decide what to tell him.
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.w9xeQJg6psfiMjFU.JournalEntryPage.yyXMKcpDOIhGuZIB]{A0-E01 · The Call from SAFE}: Helen calls SAFE; David summons the coterie. Nadia, if she's in play, arrives on her own: she knows the apartment.
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.xWx5IoPih8fX83b1]{A1-E03 · The Sheriff Asks}: this is the coterie's formation scene. Montgomery gathers them all at his farm and assigns David to go with them; David lends them the hangar.
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.7brn5AgmWggUl420]{A3-E01 · The Other Son}: Krell goes after the most exposed Touchstone of any character (Helen, Bear, Maja, Theo, Ingrid…).
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell}: Krell demands David. The coterie decides whether to bring him and how. The PCs earn the steps toward Krell's turn with what they tell him; David confirms, breaks, or gets angry.
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.aGN9NHO00wmdUzVn]{A3-E04 · The Pack Wavers}: if Hal is in play, the scene turns against him: Montgomery demands his reports in front of everyone.
  • @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}: if Celeste is in play, Halloway offers her up as a traitor. If Nadia is in play, Whitmore uses her as his voice before the Council.
  • Scaling the tests: Difficulties are the ones in the outline; scale the enemies by adding one minor NPC for each player beyond two.
