Sheet: @UUID[Actor.OE0huDRYvrhnxa9O]{Preston Gale}

Halloway's ghoul, CEO of Gale Sentinel

Early fifties, an investor-pitch smile, talks in slogans. He's been drinking from Halloway for twenty-six years, and for just as long he's been finding whatever he's asked to find.

Standard Dice Pools: Physical 3 · Social 5 · Mental 5

Exceptional Dice Pools: Technology 7, Finance 6, Persuasion 6, Subterfuge 5

Health 6 · Willpower 4 · Discipline: Dominate 1 (Cloud Memory), through Halloway's blood

Weakness: his dose of Vitae has been due for three days. −1 die to everything until he gets it.

Before @UUID[JournalEntry.w9xeQJg6psfiMjFU.JournalEntryPage.yyXMKcpDOIhGuZIB]{A0-E01 · The Call from SAFE}, each PC lives through a brief moment in the small hours of the same night as the break-in. These are one- or two-minute scenes, with no tests, so that every player starts the game with something in hand. Read them separately or together.

Storyteller Notes · Preludes

Celeste (@UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{PJ-02}). At 3:30 a.m., @UUID[Actor.eRE6FTNdGO76lzPK]{Mr. Pell} texts her asking her to authorize “an urgent payment to a security vendor” from one of Halloway Meridian's companies. It's routine. She signs off on it. (It's the payment to the @UUID[Actor.9rv5Jdb3y6bZZ1fj]{MEN-01} crew. If she reviews the transfer later, it's a clue: , early.)

Ezra (@UUID[JournalEntry.PBJeE9T9n0BjB6ag]{PJ-03}). On his monitors underground, at 2:52 a.m., a block of doorbell cameras in Ballard goes dark. All Gale Sentinel, all at once, for eleven minutes. He's never seen an outage that clean. (.)

Nadia (@UUID[JournalEntry.rg50DlMYSzgbZeBv]{PJ-04}). At 3:20 a.m. she gets a voicemail from @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen} on her regular phone. Just four seconds of breathing, then it cuts off. (Helen started to call her and hung up. Nadia can go to the apartment on her own.)

Hal (@UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{PJ-05}). He's watching David's hangar on @UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Montgomery}'s orders, as he does every few weeks. At 3:21 a.m. he sees David and @UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Bear} tear out in the truck. (Hal can follow them or report in.)

Ruth (@UUID[JournalEntry.gRfqeOIXEHOcLemr]{PJ-06}). She's on leave, at home, unable to sleep. At 3:40 a.m. her ex-husband, the retired detective, calls her: “They tell me there's a weird call in Ballard nobody wants to take. You know anything?” (She doesn't know anything yet. But she will.)

Editor's Note · Celeste's Clue

Installment 1 (doc 10) called this clue “P-11, early.” Installment 2 (doc 11) defines P-14 as the payment to Lonnie “made from Cascade Holdings LLC, a Halloway Meridian company (the one Celeste signed in her prelude),” and Part 4 (doc 13) refers to “P-14 and the prelude note.” The newest doc wins: it's @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.9WkqebVXUF2scLLC]{The Payment from Cascade Holdings}. P-11 is still the Gale signature (@UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center}).

Storyteller Context

It's 3:19 a.m. @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David}'s flip phone rings for the first time in four years. The conversation is the one told in @UUID[JournalEntry.CeLqLZCfHQEtHYlk]{CAP-00}. Fifteen minutes later, David and @UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Bear} reach @UUID[JournalEntry.YD0Td8Y9aJyIpGSl]{Helen's apartment}. David doesn't go alone: from the truck, he calls in the coterie. He calls whoever's close at hand and tells them where, not why.

  • Nadia arrives on her own if she followed up on her prelude: she knows the apartment.
  • Hal arrives behind the truck, or because David calls him.
  • Ezra and Ruth already have Ballard on their minds from their preludes. If David calls them, they come.
  • Celeste arrives only if the table agreed on how she knows David (see “Character Tips” in @UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File}). If not, she joins in @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.T8gJWjZpOnL4OisP]{A1-E01 · What They Took} or @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.xWx5IoPih8fX83b1]{A1-E03 · The Sheriff Asks}.

Those who don't arrive tonight meet up in @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.xWx5IoPih8fX83b1]{A1-E03 · The Sheriff Asks}.

The goal of the scene is simple: secure @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen}, figure out what happened, and get out of there before things get worse. What the coterie doesn't know is that the doorbell camera of 3B, across from Helen's door, is still streaming.

Market Street gleams in the rain. The hardware store is closed, its shutter rolled down, and above it, on the third floor, a single window is lit. The street door is open. The stairwell smells of damp, of wet wool, and of something else, metallic and sweet, like coins squeezed in a fist. In the third-floor hallway every door has a doorbell camera, each with its little blue light. Helen's door is closed. From the other side, someone is counting under their breath: “...one hundred forty-one, one hundred forty-two...”

Tests

  • Wits + Awareness (Difficulty 3): the 3B doorbell camera, the only one in the hallway pointed at Helen's door, has a steady blue light and a second, tiny green light, blinking. It's streaming live.
  • Resolve + Awareness (Difficulty 2), or automatic with Auspex 1: the coin smell in the hallway is Vitae, but watered down and with no Beast behind it. It's a ghoul's ().
  • Intelligence + Technology (Difficulty 3): the cameras on her door and the one on 3B are the same Gale Sentinel model. Helen's has a disconnection log from 2:52 to 3:03 ().

Coterie Options

Escape Taking Helen down the fire escape avoids the 3B camera. Dexterity + Stealth (Difficulty 2) so nobody in the building sees them go down. If they leave through the hallway without doing anything about the camera, ANOMALY logs each Kindred as a “cold subject”: .
Manipulate Helen is in shock and only half trusts David, who's the only one she called. One PC talks her into it: Charisma + Persuasion (Difficulty 2) to get her to agree to leave with them tonight; if David backs up the speaker, +1 die. On a failure, she refuses to leave her home until dawn. With 3 or more successes, she volunteers the business about the ghoul who sniffed the stairwell.
Combat There's nobody to fight. But if someone smashes the 3B camera, the last image it sends is a hand moving faster than it should (). Opening it carefully and disconnecting it is Dexterity + Larceny (Difficulty 3), and the Thermometer doesn't rise.
Disciplines Obfuscate (Cloak of Shadows) keeps the camera from recording whoever uses it, but not the others. Auspex 4 (Spirit's Touch) on the doorknob: gloves, a calm pulse, and a thirst for something that isn't food, the mark of a ghoul waiting for their next fix (). Dominate on Helen to calm her down works, but Helen notices the gap in her memory the next day. Helen is David's Touchstone: if he sees it, he steps in (“Not her.”). If they do it anyway, until @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.xWx5IoPih8fX83b1]{A1-E03 · The Sheriff Asks} he does nothing to help whoever dominated her.

Dialogue Guide: Helen Ward

Helen is exhausted and scared, but she's still a journalist. She talks fast, smokes, and asks questions the moment she can. With David she's more direct than with anyone.

  • “Are you okay?” — “I'm in one piece. Okay is something else.”
  • “What did they take?” — “Everything that matters. The drive, the copy in the closet. And somebody wiped the cloud at 3:01. This isn't some random burglar: they didn't even take the TV.”
  • “Who knew the file existed?” — “Nadia, my producer. My source at the M.E.'s office. You, I guess.” She looks at him. “Did you know?”
  • “Did you see their faces?” — “Caps, gloves. One of them stopped in the hallway and sniffed the stairwell. Like a dog. He smelled like wet wool and coins.”
  • (Asked by David, or by a PC who has already seen @UUID[JournalEntry.EQ3lkuiGnEvoSW7x]{DOC-05}) “Why didn't you change the lock?” — She looks at David. She's quiet for a moment. “Because you never told me why. And I don't do things without knowing why.”
  • “Who are they?” (to David, about the PCs who came with him) — “Don't take me for an idiot. I called one number and three people showed up. None of them blinks enough.”

Clues

(the cameras offline from 2:52 to 3:03) · (ghoul Vitae on the doorknob and in the hallway)

Exits

@UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.T8gJWjZpOnL4OisP]{A1-E01 · What They Took} (the scene continues in the apartment) · if the coterie takes Helen away right away, A1-E01 happens at the @UUID[JournalEntry.104UV0anmZHNCTrD]{hangar}, and P-02 is lost if it wasn't detected.

Storyteller Notes

  • If nobody notices the 3B camera, don't say so. Let it be a surprise in @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.wIpc0OR2nQf7WDFO]{A1-E05 · The City's Eyes} or @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center}, when they find their own image on Gale's servers.
  • David, in this scene: he wants Helen out of there, seeing as little as possible. He explains nothing, to her or to the coterie. If a PC asks him who SAFE is, he answers “Me” and nothing more.
  • Bear stays in the truck watching the street. If someone asks him, he saw a gray electric car parked half a block down with someone inside: it's the ghoul lookout (@UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{MEN-04}). If the coterie does nothing, it leaves at 4:10.

Reference (Kindred destroyed in 1996, no actor) · Seattle Anarch · killed @UUID[JournalEntry.VYpDoFtqKkL7FlqL]{Emily Smith} and was destroyed by @UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David}.

This page gathers what docs 00–16 say about Dorsey. The source doc for each fact is in parentheses. The docs give him no clan, sire, or stats.

• ID registry: “REF-03 · Ray Dorsey, the Anarch who killed Emily in 1996 (destroyed by David)” (doc 07).
  • He used teenagers from Rainier Valley as his herd (doc 05, story: “Emily's Night (1996)”).
  • In the fall of 1996 he asked @UUID[JournalEntry.WHkwE8CYfaKW5WyO]{Rosa Iturbe} in Everett to put him up for a week: “he said the Sheriff was after him” (doc 07, Rosa's profile). Rosa gave him a bed at the shipyard (doc 11, @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.aJxUAHXcYpRWrhmG]{A2-E03 · Salt's}).
  • A week later he killed Emily Smith, a social worker, in a half-abandoned apartment in Rainier Valley (doc 05; doc 07; doc 11). The obituary dates the death to October 21, 1996 (doc 15, @UUID[JournalEntry.woF61Oy8f19xxrkA]{Emily Smith's Obituary}; a provisional detail according to doc 16).
  • David arrived minutes too late and destroyed him with a single shot (doc 05; doc 07: “the Hound destroyed him with a single shot”).

• The backup who arrived afterward and cleaned up the scene while David was still on the ground was @UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{Hal Brekke}, a Gangrel two years into his unlife (doc 05; doc 02: “he was the one who cleaned up the scene while David was still on his knees”).
  • To the city, it was a score being settled between gangs. To Montgomery, it was the reason he started keeping an eye on his Hound (doc 05). The obituary says the police are investigating it “as a gang-related confrontation” and that “one of the juveniles was unharmed” (doc 15, AYU-04).
  • That juvenile was @UUID[Actor.rOqsigq4dAfIYQMh]{Marcos Delgado}, fifteen years old, the only kid who survived. Before he passed out, he saw a man with a scar on his face shoot Dorsey and kneel beside the social worker (doc 09, @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.pCLncsxglYsxJtbu]{GAN-01 · The Boy Who Survived}).

• Rosa. She didn't know what Dorsey was going to do. She never forgave herself. Since then she has one rule in Everett: nobody who uses minors as a herd (doc 07). Her agenda in Salt's is “to settle the debt of 1996” (doc 08, @UUID[JournalEntry.azX1hjbc0PUp2AA2.JournalEntryPage.SSDCSJFv8Esl6Ki5]{COT-03 · Salt's}).
  • Rumor 11: “Rosa Iturbe sheltered the Anarch who killed the Hound's daughter.” (True. It was in 1996, a week before Emily's death. Rosa didn't know what he was going to do. She never forgave herself) (doc 05).
  • The confession (@UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.aJxUAHXcYpRWrhmG]{A2-E03 · Salt's}, doc 11): “There's something I have to tell you. Thirty years ago. A guy named Ray Dorsey asked me to put him up for a week. Said the Sheriff was after him. I gave him a bed at the shipyard. A week later he killed a social worker in Rainier Valley. You know which one.” Doc 01 summed it up like this: “Rosa knew the Anarch who killed Emily.”

A chronicle sketch for after @UUID[JournalEntry.oyw1B5aZ7G2vFDuO.JournalEntryPage.on9MlxGjJpFF8yf2]{FIN-D · Red Tide}. It isn't a complete adventure: it's the premise, how to use the Puget Cell (@UUID[JournalEntry.dnsWkdXVJ19riBLa.JournalEntryPage.O8yPSIYLlTrKHm8G]{The Puget Cell}) on either side, six hooks, and the optional crossover with Del Velo a la Vigilia. Everything is Proposed except what's quoted from FIN-D.

The File ended up in the hands of @UUID[JournalEntry.bJA2iRyDgbm2TcuK]{Dana Okafor}. Twelve years of evidence, hunting maps, photos, and names. The Puget Cell requests reinforcements from national headquarters, and within two weeks there are three cells in Seattle. The Thermometer is at 10: Purge. In the first week at least one Camarilla haven falls. PCs who appear in the File lose Mask and Haven until they relocate. The Prince, if still Prince, closes Elysium and the court scatters. @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway}, if he survived, disappears. And @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen} gets a visit from Okafor with a job offer.

That's what FIN-D says. “Red Tide” begins the next morning, when the rain washes Northline's windows and Okafor, for the first time in two years, has more than she can use.

The chronicle's question: when the hunters win, what's left of them? And of the quarry, what's left when it has nowhere left to hide?

The tone shifts. The Ward File was intrigue with a clock. Red Tide is survival, whichever side you play. The rain stays the same.

There are three ways to run Red Tide. Pick one before you start and tell the table.

A · The Coterie Is the Quarry (V5)

The chronicle continues with the vampires. The Puget Cell is the antagonist with a face: the players know it, because they played it in the interludes. The other two cells have no face. They're worse.

  • The Thermometer stops rising and falling: it sits at 10. It's replaced by the Cell's Danger (@UUID[JournalEntry.dnsWkdXVJ19riBLa.JournalEntryPage.O8yPSIYLlTrKHm8G]{The Puget Cell}), read in reverse: now it measures how close the coterie is to striking back. At Danger 5, the Puget Cell has a problem of its own (see @UUID[JournalEntry.jiea701LDJdMoHoY.JournalEntryPage.q1x9tjEwYnEBxpZ0]{MR-02 · Three Cells}).
  • The Cell's Desperation starts at 0. They have everything. It rises every time the coterie tears something away from them.
  • Okafor doesn't want a massacre. The new cells don't share that concern.

B · The Hunters Are the Protagonists (H5)

The table continues with the pregenerated characters (@UUID[JournalEntry.LfywH6qtS3GxDxJx]{The Puget Cell · Pregenerated Characters}) as Hunter: The Reckoning characters. The coterie becomes NPCs: the quarry the players know better than anyone, because they played it for eight nights.

  • It works best if the table played all three interludes: the hunters already have history.
  • The Cell's Desperation and Danger are H5's, unchanged. The Cell starts with Desperation 0 and Danger 2: the whole city knows something is going on.
  • Mind the Veils: hunting your own characters is heavy material. Talk it through in session zero (@UUID[JournalEntry.BPqr3MwJXyy5lXZz]{Safety Tools}).

C · Both Tables in One

Alternating sessions: one with the coterie, one with the Cell. What one side does lands on the other the following session. It's the most demanding option and the best one if the table can sustain it. Use the Cell's Desperation and Danger as the shared clock.

Theme: Loyalty

Cast: Helen Ward (@UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen Ward}), Dana Okafor (@UUID[JournalEntry.bJA2iRyDgbm2TcuK]{Dana Okafor}), Sasha Hale (@UUID[JournalEntry.D611Mcr17F6HHEUw]{Sasha Hale}), David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}).

What happened: this is FIN-D's first hook. Okafor visits Helen and offers her a job with FIRSTLIGHT. It isn't a threat: she needs her. Twelve years of files don't read themselves, and Helen knows which folder goes with which night. Hale has already flagged the ones she doesn't understand.

What could happen:

  • Helen accepts. She works at Northline, at the desk next to Hale's. From there she can protect some names, not all of them. In mode A, she's the coterie's source inside the Cell, for as long as it lasts. In mode B, she's the analyst who lies to the Cell for someone.
  • Helen refuses. Okafor lets her go and parks a van outside her door. The white one. Helen recognizes it.
  • Helen disappears. Someone got there before Okafor: the coterie, Montgomery, or whatever is left of Halloway. FIRSTLIGHT assumes it was “them.” Desperation +1 for the Cell.

Focus: Social.

Theme: Hierarchy

Cast: Dana Okafor, the Puget Cell, two new FIRSTLIGHT cells, and their supervisor from national headquarters (Proposed: Supervisory Agent Marion Kessler, fifty-eight, who has never seen a Kindred and is in a hurry).

What happened: the reinforcements Okafor requested arrive. With them, someone from higher up. The new cells want results in weeks and don't know the city. Kessler strips Okafor of operational command and leaves her the analysis. The Puget Cell ends up caught between the two things Okafor fears most: the quarry and the rush.

What could happen:

  • Okafor falls in line. The new cells hit havens on the list with generators and no questions. People who had nothing to do with it go down: thin-bloods, ghouls, mortals. The Purge turns into noise, and the noise wakes up all of Seattle.
  • Okafor rebels. She keeps part of the File and works it on her own, with Hale and the operators who stay loyal to her. In mode B, the players have to choose: Okafor or the agency.
  • Someone leaks. One of the new cells loses a laptop. In mode A, it's the best gift the coterie will get all chronicle.

Focus: Social and Mental.

Theme: Survival

Cast: the Puget Cell, the owner of whichever haven the Storyteller chooses (FIN-D: if the coterie doesn't move, theirs), Ethan Montgomery (@UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Ethan Montgomery}) and his dogs.

What happened: FIN-D says that in the first week at least one Camarilla haven falls. This hook is that night. If the table plays the hunters, it's their first real raid. If it plays the coterie, it's the first time they run without knowing where to.

What could happen:

  • The raid goes well. FIRSTLIGHT captures a Kindred. They take them to Northline's white room (see @UUID[JournalEntry.jiea701LDJdMoHoY.JournalEntryPage.tsBFltmHvveuqpKp]{MR-06 · The White Room}).
  • The raid goes badly. Operators die. The Puget Cell buries someone with a name (Navarro, Pak, or Sorensen, if nobody's playing them). Desperation +2.
  • The haven is empty. Someone tipped them off. From that night on, Okafor looks at her team differently.

Focus: Physical.

Theme: Truth

Cast: Sasha Hale (@UUID[JournalEntry.D611Mcr17F6HHEUw]{Sasha Hale}), Preston Gale (@UUID[JournalEntry.y8Ao3xEHH3W11EJe]{Preston Gale}), Ezra Lund (@UUID[JournalEntry.PBJeE9T9n0BjB6ag]{Ezra “Static” Lund}) if he was played, the vault in Halloway Tower (@UUID[JournalEntry.L6Fl1S0tjkWno2we]{Halloway Tower}).

What happened: with the whole File in hand, Hale goes back to the question she asked herself in @UUID[JournalEntry.I3XsZ233TNTuehzS.JournalEntryPage.hcNJvEh25hCamG2B]{INT-02 · SEA-0411}: who was ARCHER? She cross-references the shipping records, Okafor's notebook, and, if FIRSTLIGHT had Lonnie, the word “Cascade.” The thread leads to the Eastside and to a security company with cameras all over the city. Halloway is gone. His ghoul isn't. And if the coterie cut off ANOMALY with Ezra's code (@UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center}), Hale now recognizes that style somewhere else: it's the hook doc 14 left behind.

What could happen:

  • Hale reaches Gale. A ghoul without a master, running out of Vitae and scared. He can tell FIRSTLIGHT everything in exchange for protection. Or he can try to kill her.
  • Hale reaches Ezra. The trail of a programmer who doesn't exist in any record. In mode A, Ezra knows they're looking for him a week before they arrive.
  • Hale keeps it to herself. If ARCHER was someone inside the court, FIRSTLIGHT has been someone else's weapon for two years. Hale decides whether that goes in a report. Her Drive, Curiosity, says yes.

Focus: Mental.

pages.name: MR-05 · The Old Buddy, Part Two

text.content:
Theme: Loyalty

Cast: Cole Ransom (@UUID[Actor.5ywnpdrw93wmy235]{Cole Ransom}), Tom “Bear” Whitman (@UUID[JournalEntry.sP1Adp7t6FvaF4zw]{Tom “Bear” Whitman}), David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}).

What happened: this follows @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.NONJmwNuBweLPdPQ]{GAN-04 · The Old Comrade}. After the raid, Ransom knows what they're hunting. And he knows Bear works for one. His oath says nobody gets left behind, and to Ransom, Bear has been left behind: trapped in something that makes him move like he's twenty-five again and that's going to make him pay for it.

What could happen:

  • Ransom tries to get him out. Without telling Okafor. A rescue Bear didn't ask for. In mode B, it's the best session of the chronicle.
  • Ransom turns him in. To the Cell, to save him from himself. Bear in the white room.
  • Bear chooses. He tells Ransom the truth, all of it. What Ransom does with it decides whether he stays in FIRSTLIGHT. If he covered the camera during the raid (@UUID[JournalEntry.I3XsZ233TNTuehzS.JournalEntryPage.mZqnxdlJulTDtmtx]{INT-03 · Artificial Daylight}), he's already out, and this is what he has left.

Focus: Social and Physical.

Theme: Humanity

Cast: the Puget Cell, a captured Kindred (from the raid in @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.ogKpm1VYgcVGCw1T]{A4-E02 · The Raid}, from @UUID[JournalEntry.jiea701LDJdMoHoY.JournalEntryPage.QfTuhZLVuCpIDbxb]{MR-03 · The First Haven}, or three thin-bloods from the docks, as in @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.c5BCc8zELaNV3QV3]{GAN-03 · Marked Blood}), Abel Thornquist (@UUID[JournalEntry.dj4gIszHHTN1QRKk]{Abel Thornquist}).

What happened: Northline has an “interview room” with high-intensity UV lamps (@UUID[JournalEntry.KioeAEZP78U0Coz5]{Northline Cyber Advisory}). Until now nobody had really used it. Now there's someone inside. Okafor wants answers. The new cells want an example.

What could happen:

  • The interrogation. Okafor is a good interrogator, and her Faith shields her from whatever the prisoner tries. The question is what she's willing to do with the lamp. If she crosses the line, her Drive (Atonement) turns against her.
  • The rescue. Thornquist wants his people back. If they're thin-bloods, he offers something in return to whoever gets them out, from either side. Rosa offers Everett.
  • The prisoner talks. What they say changes what the Cell believes it's hunting. In mode B, it's the moment in the chronicle when the hunters stop being sure who the monsters are.

Focus: Mental and Social.

pages.name: Crossover with Del Velo a la Vigilia

text.content:
Optional. The chronicle works without it. If the Del Velo a la Vigilia module (del-velo-a-la-vigilia) is active in the world, the hunters of Red Tide can take one of its Three Paths, that module's hunter powers. You don't need to bring in anything from its plot: just the rules for the Paths.

DVV Path In Seattle Who
Illuminated · The Science of the Threshold (Illuminated Artifacts) Northline is a full-fledged workshop. DVV's Advance calls for study material from a creature, and Northline has it: ANOMALY's cold subject logs, the body camera footage from the raid, whatever is in the white room. The Signature Tracker is ANOMALY built by hand; the Spectral Lens, a pair of modified thermal goggles; the Treated Ammunition, the next step after the incendiary rounds Hale, no contest. Pak, if he gets obsessed with what he saw in gray
Imbued · The Mark of the Heralds Okafor's Faith and Navarro's medal are already something neither of them understands. With DVV, that can be the beginning of the Imbuing Navarro. Okafor, if the table wants
Modified · The Tempered Flesh The new cells bring a lab. National headquarters has programs Okafor knows nothing about Sorensen, for the money. Ransom, to have the knees he had at twenty-five

What changes with the crossover:

  • Hunters can take a Path when its narrative trigger is met in play, as DVV says. The pregens' Edges stay as they are; the Path is added on top.
  • The Desperation the Paths use (activating an Artifact, kindling the Spark, pushing the flesh) is the Puget Cell's. It's a group actor of type cell, the same kind DVV's panel looks for, so the panel finds it without any setup. If there's another cell in the world, the panel uses the first one it finds: leave only one.
  • Northline and the Illuminated Artifacts. If the Storyteller uses this, @UUID[JournalEntry.KioeAEZP78U0Coz5]{Northline Cyber Advisory} becomes the Illuminated's workshop. Breaking in there stops being just the fastest way to raise the Thermometer: it's stealing a hunter's tools.

What changes without the crossover: nothing. The Artifacts, the Faith, and the white room are fiction, with no rules of their own. The hunters use their H5 Edges.

New IDs from this folder and from content/pnjs/cazadores.json. All of it is new content; none of it comes from the docs.

  • Journals: @UUID[JournalEntry.dnsWkdXVJ19riBLa]{Playable FIRSTLIGHT} · Playable FIRSTLIGHT · @UUID[JournalEntry.I3XsZ233TNTuehzS]{From the Other Side · FIRSTLIGHT Interludes} · The Other Side · @UUID[JournalEntry.LfywH6qtS3GxDxJx]{The Puget Cell · Pregenerated Characters} · Pregenerated Characters · @UUID[JournalEntry.jiea701LDJdMoHoY]{Red Tide · Continuation After FIN-D} · Red Tide
  • CEL-01 · The Puget Cell (group actor, type cell, and its page)
  • INT-00 · Advantages and Cracks for the Raid (V1–V6, F1–F6) · INT-01 · The White Van · INT-02 · SEA-0411 · INT-03 · Artificial Daylight
  • CAZ-01 · Teresa “Tess” Navarro · CAZ-02 · Owen Pak · CAZ-03 · Lena Sorensen (named operators from @UUID[Actor.abaWg7NwNQvM0sDc]{FIRSTLIGHT Tactical Team})
  • PRE-01 to PRE-06 · Pregenerated characters: Okafor, Hale, Ransom, Navarro, Pak, Sorensen
  • MR-01 to MR-06 · Red Tide hooks
  • Hunter sheets that replace others (reemplaza: true): @UUID[JournalEntry.bJA2iRyDgbm2TcuK]{Dana Okafor} (Okafor), @UUID[JournalEntry.D611Mcr17F6HHEUw]{Sasha Hale} (Hale), and @UUID[Actor.5ywnpdrw93wmy235]{Cole Ransom} (Ransom). Their mortal and minor NPC sheets remain in fuera.json and menores.json, untouched.

Proposed items the Storyteller has to approve: the Creed, Drive, Edges, and Perks of the six hunters; Navarro, Pak, and Sorensen in their entirety; the conversion of Hale's and the tactical team's pools to Attributes and Skills; the starting Desperation 1 and Danger 0 and their rules; the white van and its schedule; the encrypted drop box and the delivery time (8:12 p.m.); the port warehouse as the briefing room; Supervisory Agent Marion Kessler.

journal.name: Revision to Part 1 · The Chain of Copies

pages.name: Revision to Part 1 · The Chain of Copies

text.content:
Chapter 7 · The Ward File. Installment 2: revision of the chain of copies and Part 2.

This section replaces what installment 1 and Thornquist's profile (@UUID[JournalEntry.dj4gIszHHTN1QRKk]{PNJ-13}) say about the origin of the copies. Where they contradict, this text wins.

@UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway} wanted the whole File, and all to himself. But the crew @UUID[JournalEntry.y8Ao3xEHH3W11EJe]{Gale} hired (@UUID[Actor.9rv5Jdb3y6bZZ1fj]{MEN-01}) wasn't as loyal as the check. One of the thieves, @UUID[Actor.9rv5Jdb3y6bZZ1fj]{Lonnie Barras}, knew that a drive someone pays that much for is worth more in pieces. During the car ride, while his partner was at the wheel, he plugged the drive into a laptop and copied three blocks of folders onto three thumb drives. Then he handed the original drive to @UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{Dawson}, Gale's ghoul head of security (MEN-04), as if nothing had happened.

The next night, Lonnie sold two of the thumb drives to @UUID[Actor.mto8LnnsUQgFr1DI]{Sal Medeiros} (MEN-13), a SoDo fence who buys and sells “strange things” to clients who only come out at night. He kept the third as insurance. Sal, in turn, offered the two drives to @UUID[JournalEntry.dj4gIszHHTN1QRKk]{Thornquist}, who bought them, made a copy of each for his own vault (it's his habit: he duplicates everything he sells), and had @UUID[JournalEntry.BRQMU0Tf8VSNaZ5o]{Jun Takeda} deliver them to two buyers.

On Night 2, Gale found in the drive's logs that someone had opened the folders at 3:40 a.m., in the middle of the ride, and told Halloway. Halloway gave @UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{Krell} a list: recover or destroy every copy, and every Kindred who has touched them. So the hunt begins.

Copy Contents Route Where it is at the start of Part 2
Original The whole File, 2016–2026 Thieves → Dawson → Gale Gale Sentinel data center (@UUID[JournalEntry.zSkwEUUtkNGhfXun]{LUG-07}). Moves to Halloway's vault (@UUID[JournalEntry.L6Fl1S0tjkWno2we]{LUG-06}) on Night 6.
USB 1 Folders 2014–2018 (includes the Larchmont) Lonnie → Sal → Thornquist → Jun → Pike In the coterie's hands if they recovered it in @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.DtetdHiBnOLQaM6Y]{A1-E02 · Ash on Pier 46}; if not, in the police chain of custody and copied by FIRSTLIGHT.
USB 2 Folders 2019–2022 Lonnie → Sal → Thornquist → Jun In Jun's pocket, or in the coterie's hands (@UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.lM1EiE1FoXMkf3Uo]{A1-E04 · Everything Sells Below}).
USB 3 Folders 2023–2026 (the most recent; includes the folders on the most active PCs and episode 112) Lonnie With Lonnie, hiding out in a motel on Aurora Avenue (@UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.5Vgl8slqjXlVRbie]{A2-E06 · The One Who Kept One}).
Thornquist's duplicates Copies of USB 1 and 2 Thornquist In a safe in the Sealed Underground. Krell doesn't know they exist.

Note: Helen started documenting in 2014. I'm correcting the reference to “ten years” accordingly: the archive covers twelve years, though she still says “ten” because it's what she's been repeating for a long time.

• @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.lM1EiE1FoXMkf3Uo]{A1-E04 · Everything Sells Below}, Thornquist's dialogue guide: to “Where did you get them?” he now answers: “From a SoDo fence who buys what nobody else wants to touch. He got it from a mortal who kept something that wasn't his. Knowing the fence's name is worth a minor favor. The mortal's name, I don't know, and that bothers me.” (, partially.)
  • A1-E04, Storyteller Notes: if the coterie doesn't act, the Night 5 auction sells Thornquist's duplicates. Krell doesn't go after them because he doesn't know they exist. all the same, because one of the buyers is @UUID[JournalEntry.D611Mcr17F6HHEUw]{Hale}.
  • Halloway's Clock, updated:
Night Event if nobody intervenes
2 Krell destroys @UUID[Actor.IdLdXpR0cpQaUeFd]{Pike} at Pier 46 (@UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.DtetdHiBnOLQaM6Y]{A1-E02 · Ash on Pier 46}). Gale discovers the drive was copied. ARCHER's first drop.

If he pulls it off: . ARCHER's second drop (). @UUID[JournalEntry.bJA2iRyDgbm2TcuK]{Okafor} contacts Helen.

Editor's Note · MEN-01, MEN-03, MEN-04, and MEN-05

The newest record wins, the one in chapter 8 (doc 14): @UUID[Actor.9rv5Jdb3y6bZZ1fj]{Lonnie Barras} is Lonnie Barras, the thief who kept one (not the whole crew of thieves); @UUID[Actor.L1oU4dlqHg8Yszon]{Montgomery's Bounty Hunters} is Montgomery's Bounty Hunters, with Dutch Lindqvist as a member with his own pools; @UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{Halloway's Security Ghouls} is “Dawson and the Security Ghouls” (Dawson, the boss, with his own pools); @UUID[Actor.k2TLqQkkzzjSLzkp]{Salt's Anarchs} is Salt's Anarchs, with Bas Okonjo and Tavi Mercer as members with their own pools.

Sheet: @UUID[Actor.JtFCjV4kHyARORQl]{Rosa Iturbe}

“Nobody kisses rings here. Here, we weld.”

Clan: Brujah · Sect: Anarchs · Position: baroness of Everett

Rosa Iturbe was born in 1961 in Sestao, beside the shipyards of the Bilbao estuary, and learned to weld from her father at fifteen. When the estuary's shipyards closed in the '80s, she emigrated to the United States with a letter of recommendation from a union and ended up in the Everett shipyards, welding hulls for Navy ships. She was the shipyard's first woman union steward. They called her “Salt” because she said her blood was salty.

In 1991, an Anarch who was hiding in the shipyard Embraced her after a night on strike. Rosa learned fast and organized the Kindred of the north the way she had organized the welders: assemblies, dues, guard shifts. In the fall of 1996, she sheltered a Seattle Anarch for a week who claimed the Sheriff was after him. His name was Ray Dorsey. A week later, Dorsey killed a social worker in Rainier Valley and the Hound destroyed him with a single shot. The social worker was Emily Smith.

Rosa didn't know what Dorsey was going to do. She never forgave herself. Since then she has had one rule in Everett: nobody uses minors as a herd. Since 2023, when the Brujah who left the Camarilla came north, Rosa has been the de facto baroness. Halloway is using her as a scapegoat and she knows it, though she doesn't know it's him.

Clear Everett's name. Rumor says the dockside killer is one of hers. If the Sheriff decides to believe it, there will be a Blood Hunt (@UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.0e8h94hwnGDTnixI]{GAN-06 · Blood Hunt in Everett}). Rosa is looking for the real killer on her own.

The debt to the Hound. She has never told David about 1996. She doesn't know whether telling him would be courage or selfishness. If the coterie makes it to Salt's (@UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.aJxUAHXcYpRWrhmG]{A2-E03 · Salt's}), she confesses it to a PC. That PC decides whether to tell David.

The thin-bloods. She offers them refuge in Everett in exchange for work, without asking them for favors the way Thornquist does. If Jun survives, Rosa can take her in.

Salt's Bar and the old shipyard in Everett (@UUID[JournalEntry.JMwTSsJAcyYdCs3m]{Salt's Bar and the Old Shipyard}; Haven 2 in a ship's hull in dry dock). She feeds on the night-shift welders and longshoremen, with their consent: some know what she is and let her drink in exchange for protection and a union that actually works.

Salt's Anarchs (@UUID[JournalEntry.azX1hjbc0PUp2AA2.JournalEntryPage.SSDCSJFv8Esl6Ki5]{COT-03 · Salt's}; @UUID[Actor.k2TLqQkkzzjSLzkp]{Salt's Anarchs}): some fifteen Kindred.

The union (Allies 3, Herd 2): loyal longshoremen and welders.

Influence 2 at the Port of Everett and the naval base.

David Smith (guilt). She admires him and fears him. She owes him something she can never repay.

Ethan Montgomery (enmity). He has been watching her since 2025. She watches him back.

Liam O'Connor (respect). The old union-man Sheriff. She sends him a bottle of whiskey every Christmas.

Hal Brekke (distrust). The Sheriff's childe. He once spared the life of one of hers, and she doesn't know why.

pages.name: Salt's Bar and the Old Shipyard

text.content: Everett · Anarch domain · Map: yes

The bar sits next to a shuttered shipyard, its rusted cranes cut out against the sky. Inside there are scarred wooden tables, a bar built from a split ship's hull, and photos of old strikes on the walls. The talk stops when you walk in. A woman with short hair and grease-stained hands leans her elbows on the bar and looks at you the way someone sizes up a wound.

Layout: the bar (open to the mortal public until two), the back room (meetings), the shipyard (havens inside three ship hulls in dry dock), and the launching slipway, which overlooks the only road and shows any car coming long before it arrives.

@UUID[JournalEntry.azX1hjbc0PUp2AA2.JournalEntryPage.SSDCSJFv8Esl6Ki5]{COT-03 · Salt's} Backgrounds: Haven 2, Herd 2 (union longshoremen), Allies 2.

pages.name: Mortal Days: The Calligrapher of Montreal

text.content: Solène was born in 1884 in Montreal, the daughter of an Italian typesetter and a seamstress from Quebec. Her handwriting was so beautiful that by fourteen she was already copying parish registers and notarial documents. She spent twenty years writing down other people's lives: births, weddings, wills, deaths. She liked the idea that nothing she wrote would ever be lost.

pages.name: Kindred Nights: The Memory of the Court

text.content:
A Toreador of the Montreal court Embraced her in 1912 to handle his correspondence. She outlived him. In 1955 she arrived in Seattle with a letter of recommendation for Whitmore, who was not yet Prince. When he took the throne in 1962, he named her Keeper of Elysium. Since then she has kept fourteen registers, one for every five years, all written by hand.

She is loyal to Whitmore out of habit and affection, but above all she is loyal to the record. She believes an Elysium without memory is just a party. She knows more about Seattle's political history than anyone, because she has seen all of it and written all of it down. What she doesn't do is interpret. She leaves that to others.

The record as insurance. Without anyone having thought of it that way, her books are another File: the history of every Kindred in Seattle since 1962. If Halloway realizes this, Marchetti will be his next target.

Neutrality. She will keep Elysium open no matter what. If Halloway wins, she will record him as Prince in the same handwriting.

The blank entry. On the night of November 12, the night of the theft, she wrote nothing. She doesn't know why. It worries her.

An apartment above the archive of the Glass Gallery, with floor-to-ceiling shelves (Haven 2). She feeds on artisans: calligraphers, bookbinders, glassblowers. She visits them in their workshops in the small hours, when they work alone, and buys a piece from them before she drinks.

The Gallery staff (Allies 2): five ghouls who serve Elysium.

The registers: fourteen volumes of the city's Kindred history.

Status 3 (Camarilla).

@UUID[JournalEntry.sCVTjJFrnyyVnQDt]{Marcus Whitmore} (affection). She knows him better than anyone. She knows he's weak and loves him anyway.

@UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Charles Halloway} (courtesy). She records every time he requests an audience. She also recorded when he smiled.

@UUID[JournalEntry.rg50DlMYSzgbZeBv]{Nadia Ferro} (protection). She sees her as the clan's new blood and looks after her without saying so.

@UUID[JournalEntry.AeAhHuCNHL9KWVnT]{Wendell Fry} (patience). She writes down everything he asks to have entered in the record, even when she doesn't understand it.

• “Marchetti writes down everything that's said in Elysium.” (True.)
  • “Marchetti was the Prince's lover.” (False. She was his confidant, which to her is more.)
  • “Marchetti's books are in a safe in the Gallery.” (Half true: the last three, yes; the eleven before them are somewhere only she knows.)

To mortals she is the director of the Gallery foundation's archive (Mask 2). She looks about twenty-eight. She is tall, with dark hair gathered in a low bun, and wears old-fashioned dresses in shades of gray and glasses on a chain. She writes with a fountain pen. She rarely smiles, but when she does, she means it. She never raises her voice.

Editor's Note

Doc 06 said “looks about forty”; it was decided that she looks the age she was at her Embrace (1912, born in 1884): about twenty-eight.

Gear Effect
Incendiary ammunition Firearm damage against Kindred is aggravated instead of superficial. Each hit forces a Terror Frenzy test (Difficulty 2).

pages.name: What Does Each Faction Think of the Coterie?

text.content:
Faction Wants Sees the coterie as
Whitmore Nothing to change A useful tool, as long as it doesn't make noise
Montgomery To recover the File and find out whether Vance is alive His emergency pack, which he doesn't fully trust
Halloway The crown An obstacle he can divert or break
Voight For FIRSTLIGHT not to find the Chantry Possible allies against the Inquisition
Thornquist To buy low and sell high Customers
Rosa Iturbe For them to stop blaming Everett The Sheriff's dogs, until they prove otherwise
FIRSTLIGHT The complete index of the File Doesn't know it exists. Yet.

Seattle was built twice. The first city burned in 1889, and the second rose on top of it, one story higher, leaving the old streets buried beneath the new ones. The Kindred who rule it never forgot the lesson: what gets buried doesn't disappear, it just changes owners.

This chapter describes Kindred Seattle as of November 2026: how it got here, who's in charge, what's being said in Elysium, and where things happen.

The Great Fire of 1889 destroyed Seattle's wooden downtown. When the city rebuilt, the streets were raised as much as a story above the original grade, and the ground floors of the buildings became basements, passages, and forgotten galleries. The Nosferatu claimed them before the mud had dried. Ever since, what happens beneath Pioneer Square has been their business.

The city's first Camarilla was small and harbor-bound: a handful of Kindred who lived off the Alaska trade, the gold rush, and the sailors nobody missed. Prince @UUID[JournalEntry.FOgT9FF3NF7ZHdCa]{Adelaide Grange}, a Ventrue from Boston, ruled from 1897 with an accountant's hand. In 1931 she named an Irish Brujah from the docks, Liam O'Connor (@UUID[JournalEntry.oQ2AhEeDkwdPRv71]{Liam O'Connor}), as Sheriff, because nobody knew the port better than he did.

pages.name: The Fair and the Glass Prince (1962–1978)

text.content:
In 1962, Seattle hosted the World's Fair and introduced itself to the country as the city of the future. That same spring, Grange left the city “for health reasons” and was never seen again. Marcus Whitmore (@UUID[JournalEntry.sCVTjJFrnyyVnQDt]{Marcus Whitmore}), a Toreador who had arrived from San Francisco ten years earlier, took the throne with the support of half the Primogen and the silence of the other half. His first act as Prince was to found the Glass Gallery (@UUID[JournalEntry.iyojT7kJHH23BWLd]{The Glass Gallery (Elysium)}) on the Fair grounds and declare it Elysium.

Whitmore understood something Grange never saw: in a city that looks forward, power isn't imposed, it's displayed. His court became famous for its elegance and its tolerance. As long as nobody broke the Masquerade, the Prince didn't care what his subjects did.

In the spring of 1978, during a longshoremen's strike, a Brujah lost control in front of the workers. O'Connor contained him and cleaned up the scene before dawn. Three days later, photos turned up in the newsroom of a local paper. Nobody knows who took them. The press didn't run them, but the Primogen saw them, and Charles Halloway (@UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Charles Halloway}), then a young Ventrue with friends in the media, demanded the Sheriff's head “for the good of the Masquerade.”

Whitmore removed O'Connor and named Ethan Montgomery (@UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Ethan Montgomery}) in his place, a quiet Gangrel who had served the Camarilla on the West Coast since 1903. It was a good choice. Montgomery has spent almost fifty years cleaning up the city without asking for anything. O'Connor left for Tacoma with a letter (@UUID[JournalEntry.4858IAb89fTokFfV]{Letter from Sheriff O'Connor to Prince Whitmore, 1978}) nobody wanted to read.

In 1986, a year after Marcus Vance (@UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Marcus “Ironjaw” Vance}) disappeared in the Carpathians, a broker from Lyon sold the Brujah's journals at a private auction. Vance had asked for his havens to be burned. Someone didn't do it. The buyer was Halloway, who had three typewritten copies made and kept the original in his vault (@UUID[JournalEntry.L6Fl1S0tjkWno2we]{Halloway Tower}). Nobody in Seattle knows, except O'Connor, who heard about it from an old contact at the port and never told anyone because nobody asked.

In the fall of 1996, an Anarch who used teenagers from Rainier Valley as his herd killed Emily Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.VYpDoFtqKkL7FlqL]{Emily Smith}), a social worker, in a half-abandoned apartment. David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}) arrived minutes too late and destroyed the Anarch with a single shot. The backup who arrived afterward, and who cleaned up the scene while David was still on the floor, was a Gangrel two years into his unlife: Hal Brekke (@UUID[JournalEntry.B4nqUk8dojvCw97H]{Halvard “Hal” Brekke}). To the city, it was a score settled between gangs. To Montgomery, it was the reason he started keeping an eye on his Hound.

Note: the 1996 date fits Hal's Embrace in 1994. Emily was 38.

In 2014, an apartment building in Tacoma, the Larchmont (@UUID[JournalEntry.Oiln4o98kvxKbOvS]{The Larchmont Building}), burned in the small hours of a March morning. Seven tenants “could not be located.” One of them was Danny Ruiz (@UUID[JournalEntry.5xUDUgkyHXGD8IPY]{Danny Ruiz}), a college friend of @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen Ward}. The official version blamed a short circuit. The version the Sheriff knows is different, and it's in the location's entry.

When the Gehenna War broke out, the Sabbat emptied out toward the east, and the West Coast lost its age-old enemy. The Brujah and the Gangrel broke with the Camarilla on a global scale. In Seattle, the two most visible cases were exceptions: Montgomery stayed out of personal loyalty to Whitmore, and David kept working for the Sheriff as an independent. The Brujah who did leave headed north to Everett, where Rosa Iturbe (@UUID[JournalEntry.WHkwE8CYfaKW5WyO]{Rosa “Salt” Iturbe}) organized them into something like an Anarch barony.

What's left of the Sabbat in Tacoma is wreckage: Kindred who didn't leave because they had nowhere to go, or because they had something to hide.

The new enemy arrived without fangs. Intelligence agencies discovered the Kindred and created the Second Inquisition. Its American branch, FIRSTLIGHT, opened a small cell on Puget Sound in 2024, the Puget Cell, behind the front of a cybersecurity consultancy in South Lake Union (@UUID[JournalEntry.KioeAEZP78U0Coz5]{Northline Cyber Advisory}). At the same time, Seattle filled up with cameras. In the spring of 2026, Gale Sentinel (@UUID[JournalEntry.zSkwEUUtkNGhfXun]{Gale Sentinel Campus and Data Center}) installed 412,000 smart doorbells across the metro area for free.

Whitmore's Camarilla hasn't taken a single hit from the Inquisition yet. Halloway thinks that's luck. Montgomery thinks it's his doing. Regent Voight (@UUID[JournalEntry.yaAsxCkCLf8CANL5]{Dr. Anneliese Voight}) thinks it's a matter of time, and in November she handed the Prince a sealed envelope he still hasn't opened (@UUID[JournalEntry.lcO0CdwUlZHg2wAX]{Register of the Keeper of Elysium, November Folio}).

Year Event
1889 Great Fire. The Seattle Underground is born.
1897 Adelaide Grange (Ventrue) becomes Prince.
1903 Montgomery joins the Camarilla (San Francisco).
1931 O'Connor becomes Sheriff.
1960 Vance Embraces David in Haiti.
1962 World's Fair. Grange disappears. Whitmore becomes Prince. The Glass Gallery is founded.
The '70s Vance trains and abandons August Krell.
1978 O'Connor falls. Montgomery becomes Sheriff.
1985 Vance disappears in Romania.
1986 Halloway buys Vance's journals.
1994 Montgomery Embraces Hal Brekke.
1996 Death of Emily Smith.
2005 Voight Embraces Ruth Abernathy.
2011 Halloway Embraces Celeste Arden.
2014 The Larchmont fire. Danny Ruiz disappears.
2016 Whitmore Embraces Nadia Ferro.
2019 Thornquist Embraces Ezra Lund.
2023 Rosa Iturbe consolidates the Anarchs in Everett.
2024 FIRSTLIGHT opens the Puget Cell.
2026 Gale Sentinel installs its doorbells. Episode 112 (October 3). The theft (November 12).

journal.name: The City · The Laws of the Seattle Elysium

pages.name: The City · The Laws of the Seattle Elysium

text.content: The Glass Gallery (@UUID[JournalEntry.iyojT7kJHH23BWLd]{The Glass Gallery (Elysium)}) enforces the Traditions of the Camarilla and five customs of its own. Solène Marchetti enforces all five and logs every infraction in her register (@UUID[JournalEntry.lcO0CdwUlZHg2wAX]{Register of the Keeper of Elysium, November Folio}).

• The peace of the glass. No violence and no hostile Disciplines inside the Gallery. Infraction: immediate expulsion, loss of 1 dot of Status, and, if there is damage, a trial before the Prince.
  • The presentation. Every Kindred who arrives in the city presents themself to the Keeper before their third night. Infraction: they are considered a trespasser, and the Sheriff may hunt them.
  • Those who serve. The mortals and ghouls on the Gallery's staff are untouchable, however appetizing they may be. Infraction: a major debt to the Prince.
  • No connected device crosses the threshold. Phones, smartwatches, earbuds: everything is switched off and handed over at the entrance. Voight imposed this custom in 2024. Infraction: confiscation and a note in the register. On the second offense, loss of 1 dot of Status.
  • What is said among the glass. Nothing said in the Gallery is repeated outside without the Keeper's permission. Infraction: Marchetti stops receiving the offender until further notice, which in practice cuts them out of the city's political life.

These rumors circulate through Elysium, the Underground, and the harbor bars. The Storyteller can drop them into any social scene. Each one is marked T (true), F (false), or H (half-true), with an explanation for the Storyteller.

# Rumor T/F/H For the Storyteller
1 “Vance, the Hound's sire, is back in town.” F Halloway spreads it through Krell. Vance is not in Seattle.
2 “The Prince didn't open Voight's envelope because he already knows what it says.” H He opened it two nights later, read it, and did nothing.
3 “Halloway brought O'Connor down in '78.” T It's true, but there's no proof except @UUID[JournalEntry.4858IAb89fTokFfV]{Letter from Sheriff O'Connor to Prince Whitmore, 1978} and O'Connor's memory.
4 “Halloway has the backing of Justicar Panhard.” H He's been writing to her for a year. She doesn't answer, but she doesn't tell him no, either.
5 “Montgomery has a list of Kindred he'll destroy if the Prince falls.” T He has eleven names. The first is Halloway.
6 “The Nosferatu can see through any camera in the city.” H They can see through many. Ezra (@UUID[JournalEntry.PBJeE9T9n0BjB6ag]{Ezra “Static” Lund}) could see through Gale Sentinel's if he checked his own code.
7 “The Second Inquisition has an office in South Lake Union.” T Northline Cyber Advisory, 11th floor (@UUID[JournalEntry.KioeAEZP78U0Coz5]{Northline Cyber Advisory}).
8 “The new doorbell cameras don't record Kindred.” F They do. And the ANOMALY model flags them as “cold subjects” (@UUID[JournalEntry.YhmNvLugMfCZezEH]{Gale Sentinel: 2027 Product Roadmap, Confidential}).
9 “What's left of the Sabbat in Tacoma is three scared childer.” F There's an old, patient one who survived the Larchmont (@UUID[JournalEntry.Oiln4o98kvxKbOvS]{The Larchmont Building}, @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.18vJtyOOVZe1Uk41]{GAN-09 · The Larchmont Survivor}).
10 “The Hound destroyed his own sire to take his position.” F An old rumor that Halloway revives in @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.uL8F2YNogcToiFc6]{A2-E01 · Elysium Night}.
11 “Rosa Iturbe sheltered the Anarch who killed the Hound's daughter.” T It was in 1996, a week before Emily's death. Rosa didn't know what he was going to do. She never forgave herself.
12 “A thin-blood sells secrets in the Underground.” T Jun Takeda (@UUID[JournalEntry.BRQMU0Tf8VSNaZ5o]{Jun Takeda}). She carries copies of the File without knowing what they are.
13 “Club Cinder belongs to the Prince.” T Through a cultural foundation, the same one listed in @UUID[JournalEntry.WW7eg88I0uDGj8ks]{FIRSTLIGHT, Internal Memo SEA-0411}.

journal.name: The Ferry Terminal and the Last Ferry

pages.name: The Ferry Terminal and the Last Ferry

text.content: Colman Dock and Puget Sound · Map: yes (terminal and ferry deck)

The terminal is almost empty. Under the fluorescents there's a handful of sleepy-faced passengers, a security guard staring at his phone, and a broken coffee machine. Outside, the last ferry of the night waits with its lights on and its engines running, like a white building floating on black water. The horn sounds once, long. Five minutes.

Structure: the terminal waiting room, the vehicle ramp, and the ferry: car deck, passenger cabin, bridge, and open stern deck.

The crossing to the far shore takes 35 minutes. Any conflict aboard has mortal witnesses locked in with the characters (Masquerade risk on every conspicuous roll).

Scene: @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.tG1m5PTkmBA1pvmc]{A4-E03 · The Last Ferry}, the climax. @UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Halloway}, @UUID[JournalEntry.y8Ao3xEHH3W11EJe]{Gale}, or a courier tries to get the original of the File out of the city.

It's the “last boat of the night” from @UUID[JournalEntry.FVBnf3yE87K4BOhh]{Wendell Fry: “Song for the Son of the Fist”}.
Seattle Center · Map: yes

The Gallery is a 1962 pavilion of glass and steel, its curved walls reflecting the city at night. Inside, hundreds of pieces of blown glass hang from the ceiling like jellyfish frozen mid-drift: red, amber, black. The light passes through them and paints the floor in colors that shift whenever someone walks by. Strings are playing somewhere. At the entrance, an elegant woman with an open register holds out a velvet tray to you: “Your phones, please.”

Layout: lobby (the Keeper and the device tray), the great hall of the jellyfish, a terrace looking out on the World's Fair tower, the Prince's private salon, and the Keeper's archive in the basement.

Owner: a cultural foundation belonging to the Prince. The mortal staff are all ghouls (@UUID[JournalEntry.ZUud4rgap2FTsiKB]{Law 3}).

Scenes: @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.uL8F2YNogcToiFc6]{A2-E01 · Elysium Night} (Elysium Night). If the Council in @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council} moves here instead of to Halloway Tower, it's a sign the Prince has regained the initiative.

Detail: the glass walls make it impossible to know who's listening from outside. A Wits + Awareness (Difficulty 4) test lets a character notice that someone on the terrace with a telephoto lens could read lips in the private salon.
Elliott Bay · David Smith's Haven · Map: yes

Between shipping containers stacked like giant dominoes stands a corrugated-metal hangar with the faded logo of a logistics company that no longer exists. From outside it looks abandoned. Inside it smells of gun oil, salt, and reheated coffee. The lights are work lights, hanging from cables. In one corner, a coffee maker and an army cot. In another, ammo boxes sorted by caliber. From the back dock you can hear the water slapping against the pilings.

Layout: main bay (armory and work area), a windowless armored room where David sleeps, Bear's room with his safe (@UUID[JournalEntry.5mQIPoGa4I0tQtbR]{Note Kept in Bear's Safe}), a covered dock with a motorboat, and an old cargo tunnel that comes out 200 meters away, next to Terminal 46.

Backgrounds: Haven 3 (David's, which he lends to the coterie), with Sea Access and Armory.

Risk: it appears in @UUID[JournalEntry.WW7eg88I0uDGj8ks]{FIRSTLIGHT, Internal Memo SEA-0411}. If the Thermometer reaches 7, FIRSTLIGHT investigates the company that owns it. If it reaches 9, it can be the target of the raid (@UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.ogKpm1VYgcVGCw1T]{A4-E02 · The Raid}).

Scenes: the coterie's base of operations (@UUID[JournalEntry.azX1hjbc0PUp2AA2.JournalEntryPage.kiaygGF4KgylB6fb]{COT-00 · The Archived}) and the starting point of @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.DtetdHiBnOLQaM6Y]{A1-E02 · Ash on Pier 46}.

Sources: doc 21 (“📍 Safe Heaven Location”), doc 17 (haven and weaponry), and doc 18 (David's sheet). They predate docs 00–16: where they clash, what's above wins.

📍 Safe Heaven Location

  • Area: Port of Seattle, Elliott Bay, docks/industrial hangar zone.
  • Approximate coordinates: 47.615° N, 122.35° W (roughly in the Interbay–West Seattle/Harbor Island sector).
  • Features: Heavy-tonnage hangar, sea and underground access, close to Port of Seattle facilities. (The doc cites as a reference the Northwest Seaport Alliance's port trucker guide: “Seattle Harbor Truckers Guide,” 03/31/2022.)

🧠 Narrative Use

  • This spot is the “hidden haven”: a hangar all but forgotten in the industrial section of the port, equipped with cargo tunnels, sea access, and armor plating.
  • Ideal for tactical prep scenes or vampire ambushes: its harbor location allows for ships, containers, nighttime traffic, and the noise of cranes.
  • Despite being in an active part of the city, its position on an industrial pier offers enough isolation for a clandestine Kindred.

Doc 21 includes a map of the location and doc 17 includes three images (“Safe Heaven,” “Interior,” “Weapons Room”); they weren't exported.

Background on the sheet (docs 17 and 18): Safe Haven (Harbor Hangar) ••••: armored, tunnel access. (Docs 00–16: Haven 3, with Sea Access and Armory.) The Camarilla's file says that “his haven is more an arsenal than a home.”

Loose details from other earlier sources: David receives Bear “sitting in a folding chair in the hangar” (doc 25); Bear spent nights “staring at the hangar ceiling” and keeps a gun in his personal safe (doc 25); Bear “maintains and modifies the weapons in the hangar's armory” (doc 25).

⚔️ Weaponry — Haven Inventory

  1. Revolvers (×6)
    • Model: service revolvers (6 shots).
    • Condition: clean, worn grips, matte finish.
    • One revolver with scarring on the cylinder has a history (an old chase or a duel gone wrong).
  2. Semiautomatic pistols (handgun panel, ×8)
    • Model: compact and service size (9mm / .40).
    • Condition: stored with loaded magazines beside them.
    • Narrative use: weapons of choice for quick missions, urban infiltrations, or for the haven's ghouls. One pistol has red tape on the grip—its owner's personal mark.
  3. Pump-action shotgun (×1, on the upper wall)
    • Model: tactical / hunting shotgun.
    • Condition: oiled, buckshot shells in a nearby box.
    • Narrative use: holding doors and close-quarters combat; its presence intimidates intruders.
  4. AR / M4-style assault rifles (×4 in a vertical rack)
    • Model: tuned assault platforms (approx. 5.56mm).
    • Condition: set up with folding stocks, some with empty rails (ready for accessories).
    • Narrative use: gear for heavy operations or clashes with organized groups; one of them, with white paint stripes, suggests it's assigned to a specific member of the coterie (my ghoul).
  5. Old bolt-action rifle / support rifle (×1, top of the rack)
    • Model: bolt-action rifle with a wooden stock.
    • Condition: well maintained, classic look.
    • Narrative use: a weapon for hunting or improvised sniping; tied to a military past or an old mission.
  6. Machetes and long knives (several, upper right panel)
    • Types: bush machetes, long survival knives (kukri-like).
    • Condition: sharpened, sheaths available.
    • Narrative use: utility tools and silent weapons; perfect for survival scenes or Blood rituals.
  7. Medieval swords and longswords (×2–3, right panel)
    • Models: long blades, greatsword/combat sword type.
    • Condition: well preserved, no rust.
    • Narrative use: relics or ceremonial pieces; they may belong to an old ally or serve as a status symbol in the haven.
  8. Katana (×1, right panel)
    • Condition: polished, with saya.
    • Narrative use: the honor weapon of a ghoul or guardian of the haven; tied to an oath or a debt.
  9. Combat knives / daggers (several, center right panel)
    • Types: tactical knives and double-edged daggers.
    • Narrative use: backup weapons, traps, or for “discreet” delivery of bloody messages.
  10. Bats (wood and metal, ×3, lower right panel)
    • Types: wooden baseball bat, reinforced metal bat, tape-wrapped pipe.
    • Narrative use: blunt weapon for street fights; the metal bat has impact marks (recent use).
  11. Ammo boxes / cases (several, floor and shelves)
    • Contents: labeled boxes (5.56, 9mm, shotgun).
    • Narrative use: logistical resource—a supply line, a possible point of conflict if the stock runs out.
  12. Improvised melee weapon (for example, a sharpened bar, a tool)
    • Condition: adapted tools.
    • Narrative use: an emergency resource; shows the coterie's ingenuity when conventional weapons run short.
  13. Safe/TACSAFE (large safe in the room)
    • Likely contents: high-value pieces, restricted ammunition, documents, or artifacts.
    • Narrative use: the focus of a heist/infiltration scene or the target of a Blood Hunt.

Damage Table — Haven Inventory

# Weapon Type / Range Damage (1–6) V5-friendly suggestion (effect) Narrative notes
1 Revolver (6 shots) Firearm, short/medium 3 moderate lethal (hard-hitting shot; 1 lethal hit) Reliable; +1 to rolls in a tense situation if used by a veteran.
2 Semiauto pistol (9mm) Firearm, short/medium 3 moderate lethal Quick magazines; ideal for urban encounters.
3 Pump-action shotgun Firearm, short (close/0–7m) 4 heavy lethal (increased damage at close range) Devastating in enclosed spaces; loses effectiveness at range.
4 AR / M4 rifle (configurable) Firearm, medium/long 4 heavy lethal (penetrating shots) Versatile; good range, possible damage bonus against cover.
5 Bolt-action rifle Firearm, long / sniper 5 very high lethal (powerful impact) Ideal for taking targets out at a distance; can cause severe incapacitation.
6 Old revolver / service pistol (one-handed) Firearm, short 3 moderate lethal Dependable in a veteran's hands; good backup weapon.
7 Machete (field) Melee 3 cutting lethal Excellent for stealth and cleanup; can open doors/cause deep wounds.
8 Combat knife / dagger Melee 2 light lethal Discreet, for silent attacks; critical on vital points.
9 Medieval swords (greatsword / longsword) Melee 4 blunt/cutting lethal Heavy contact weapon; good stunning effect if it doesn't penetrate.
10 Katana Melee 4 high cutting lethal Sharp blade: deep wounds; good narrative effect (bleeding).
11 Long knives / kukri Melee 3 cutting lethal Versatile in close combat; breaks defenses.
12 Baseball bat (wood) Melee 2 Bashing / light lethal Good weapon for street fights; causes bruises and fractures.
13 Metal bat / wrapped pipe Melee 3 blunt lethal More dangerous than the wooden one; can cause serious wounds.
14 Improvised melee weapons (tool) Melee 1–3 Bashing → light lethal (depending on the object) Variable damage; useful for improvising.
15 Antique collector's revolvers/pistols Firearm, short 2–3 light/moderate lethal Can misfire; dramatic effect if they jam.
16 Ammo boxes (stock) N/A N/A Logistical resource They don't deal damage, but they're a narrative target: if lost, they limit weapon use.
17 Safe / TACSAFE N/A N/A Narrative target Holds special or rare ammunition; a plot point.

Differences from Docs 00–16

  • Haven 4 / Haven 3. David's sheet gives Safe Haven 4; doc 05 gives Haven 3 with Sea Access and Armory.
  • Coordinates. 47.615° N, 122.35° W falls on the north shore of Elliott Bay (the Belltown/Interbay area), not on Harbor Island, which lies farther south (around 47.57° N). Doc 05 places it on Harbor Island, with the tunnel coming out next to Terminal 46.
  • The safe. Doc 17 mentions a “large safe/TACSAFE in the room”; doc 05 puts the safe in Bear's room (@UUID[JournalEntry.5mQIPoGa4I0tQtbR]{Note Kept in Bear's Safe}). They may be the same one.
  • Layout. The earlier sources don't describe the floor plan (armored room, Bear's room, covered dock with motorboat, 200-meter tunnel): that comes from doc 05.
Tacoma · Map: yes

Twelve years later, the Larchmont is still standing, a black box gutted from the inside: four stories of blackened brick, windows with no glass, a construction fence with a demolition notice nobody ever acted on. The rain comes in through the roof and falls down the stairwell to the basement, where you can hear water running. On the fence, someone has left seven plastic flowers tied on with wire.

A pack of three Sabbat Kindred who didn't leave for the Gehenna War used the Larchmont's basement as a farm: they kept seven tenants locked in the old cistern and fed on them for weeks.

One of Montgomery's contacts tipped him off. The Sheriff sent David. David arrived after the pack, warned, had already set the building on fire to erase the trail. The seven tenants were already dead. He destroyed two of the three. The third escaped through the storm drain into the Sound (@UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.18vJtyOOVZe1Uk41]{GAN-09 · The Larchmont Survivor}).

Montgomery ordered the cistern sealed without removing the bodies: seven bloodless corpses were a Masquerade breach. Danny Ruiz (@UUID[JournalEntry.5xUDUgkyHXGD8IPY]{Danny Ruiz}) is still down there.

The photo of David with his back to the fire, in the File, is from that night.

Scene: @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.9fTKL8Oeq36BCfU9]{A2-E05 · The Ashes of the Larchmont} (optional). If the coterie opens the cistern, Thermometer +2 (). If David is there or finds out, he breaks: the Storyteller plays it. What they tell Helen is up to the players. If @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen} ever learns it, the Touchstone relationship changes forever.
Queen Anne · Tremere seat · Map: no

At the top of the hill stands a Victorian house with a green copper dome that was once a private observatory. The dome still opens. What pokes out through the slit isn't a telescope but an antenna. Inside, carved wood paneling shares the walls with server racks and screens showing network traffic graphs.

From here, Voight (@UUID[JournalEntry.yaAsxCkCLf8CANL5]{Dr. Anneliese Voight}) monitors Northline's communications. She knows the Puget Cell exists, but she doesn't know about ARCHER.

Ruth (@UUID[JournalEntry.gRfqeOIXEHOcLemr]{Dr. Ruth Abernathy}) has a lab in the basement.

If the coterie allies with Voight, they can get @UUID[JournalEntry.WW7eg88I0uDGj8ks]{FIRSTLIGHT, Internal Memo SEA-0411} here before @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.EjJ0vfVBCjTTb0QV]{A3-E02 · The Data Center}.

Six FIRSTLIGHT hunters for playing the “From the Other Side” interludes (@UUID[JournalEntry.I3XsZ233TNTuehzS]{From the Other Side · FIRSTLIGHT Interludes}). Each page is meant to be handed to one player: it contains nothing about the vampire plot that their hunter doesn't know. The journal is generated hidden and its pages visible: to hand one out, give the player Observer permission on the journal or show it to them.

Each hunter has a hunter-type actor with the same name in the FIRSTLIGHT/Puget Cell folder of the character compendium, and the Puget Cell (@UUID[JournalEntry.dnsWkdXVJ19riBLa.JournalEntryPage.O8yPSIYLlTrKHm8G]{The Puget Cell}) as a group. The numbers on these pages come from those sheets.

For the Storyteller: anything not in the docs (the Creed, the Drive, the Edges, the lives of Navarro, Pak, and Sorensen, the Touchstones) is Proposed. The breakdown of what comes from the doc and what's ours is in each actor's private notes.

“Every source wants something. Until you know what it wants, it's bait.”

Forty-five, head of FIRSTLIGHT's Puget Cell. You were born in Houston in 1981, the daughter of a Nigerian engineer and a Louisiana schoolteacher. Eleven years in the FBI's violent crimes unit in Chicago, known for closing the cases others had written off.

In 2017 you found the pattern in a string of South Side disappearances that didn't follow any pattern. You also found the basement where they ended. What was inside tore two fingers off your left hand and kept moving after you emptied your magazine into its head. Six months later, a man from Homeland Security visited you in the hospital and told you that you weren't crazy. In 2018 you joined FIRSTLIGHT. In 2024 they sent you to Seattle.

What You Know

  • The orders: confirm whether Seattle has “an organized structure” and, if it does, don't touch it until you can tear it out by the roots. Tight budget. A single cell.
  • ARCHER: an anonymous source who started feeding you things recently. Claims to have access “to the local structure.” It came to you too easily. You use it anyway, because it's all you've got. You don't buy it.
  • Helen Ward: a podcast journalist who did alone, in twelve years, what took FIRSTLIGHT two with a federal budget. You respect her. You think she's in danger.
  • “R. A.”: a signature from the King County medical examiner's office on fifteen impossible reports. You've been preparing a visit for months.
  • ANOMALY: Gale Sentinel's doorbell cameras flag anyone who gives off no heat as a “cold subject.” Northline has been receiving the alerts since September.

In the Cell

  • Sasha Hale: the only person in Seattle you listen to without reservations.
  • Cole Ransom: a good operator. Asks questions that aren't his to ask.
  • The tactical team: six contractors hired as a counterterrorism unit. Most of them have never seen what they hunt. Navarro has.

How to Play

  • You speak low, unhurried. You repeat the other person's last sentence before you answer.
  • Black coffee all day. You never sit with your back to a door. Your left hand is almost always in your pocket.
  • You don't enter combat if you can avoid it. You direct by radio from outside. If you're cornered, you shoot for the head and fall back toward a light source.

Redemption: She's redeemed when the Cell gets someone out alive whom the quarry had already marked, before they become one more name in a folder.

Thwart the Unnatural. It's her Unshakable Faith: Dominate and Presence take −2 dice against her; if they fail, she notices. She can't explain it or understand it. She uses it.

Global Access. Contacts 3 (FBI, Homeland Security, Seattle PD), the liaison with the FBI's Seattle field office, and access to ANOMALY through the Gale Sentinel pilot program.

Desire: To know what ARCHER wants before the next drop.
Touchstone: Her mother, the Louisiana schoolteacher, now retired. She calls her on Sundays and tells her the job is boring.

“Why is it giving us this?”

Thirty-two, former signals intelligence analyst, analyst for the Puget Cell. You've listened to episode 112 of “What the City Forgets” three times. You believe in patterns and you distrust gifts.

You sign your notes “S. H.” At Northline you have a desk with three monitors, a corkboard that's more yours than anyone's, and a “consulting” badge that opens more doors than it should.

What You Know

  • ARCHER: you wrote the analysis of every drop. Provisional reliability B-2. Your question is always the same: what does the source want.
  • Helen Ward: her archive sketches something. If you look at it from far enough back, you can see where someone hunts.
  • ANOMALY: the cold-subject alerts come to your screen in real time. You read them better than anyone.
  • Consulting: with that badge you can request a copy of almost any piece of evidence in the Seattle PD chain of custody, and nobody asks.

In the Cell

  • Dana Okafor: she listens to you. She doesn't always take your advice.
  • The tactical team: people who don't read reports. Pak reads yours.

How to Play

  • Headphones around your neck. Always another screen.
  • You talk in numbered points when you're nervous.
  • You're not an operator: in the field, you stay in the van or the car.

“Nobody gets left behind. Not even here.”

Forty-nine, mustache, wrecked knees. Former SEAL. Now you're a private contractor on the Puget Cell's tactical team. You think you work for Homeland Security, in a special counterterrorism unit. That's what they told you, and the paychecks clear.

You served on the same team as Tom “Bear” Whitman, whose knees were like yours. You haven't heard from him in years.

What You Know

  • The job: surveillance, support, and, if needed, entry. Never alone: always in pairs, with a drone overhead and a light source behind you. If two go down, you pull back and wait for dawn.
  • What you hunt: they told you “subjects.” The weapons are strange for terrorists: incendiary ammunition, ultraviolet flashlights, thermal goggles. You noticed. You asked. They didn't quite answer.
  • The armory: you run it, in the port warehouse where the team sleeps.

In the Cell

  • Dana Okafor: uses you because you're good. Knows you ask questions.
  • The team: your teammates. Absolute loyalty. It's the one thing that's not up for debate.

How to Play

  • You look people in the eyes and at their hands, in that order. You can tell when someone moves differently.
  • You don't say much, and you say it in radio phrases.
  • If a teammate goes down, everything else waits.

“I've already seen it. You haven't. Not yet.”

Thirty-eight, former ATF agent. In 2021, in Tucson, a routine warehouse search: your partner, Ortiz, went in first. What came out of the dark wasn't a person, and it took him. Nobody believed you, except a man from the Department of Homeland Security who was waiting for you when you left the hospital.

You carry Ortiz's Saint Michael medal in your left hand, under the flashlight. You don't know why it works. It works.

What You Know

  • The tactical team: six contractors. Most of them think they know what they hunt and have never seen it. You have, and they know it even if they don't ask.
  • The Cell: Okafor saw something too, in Chicago. The two of you don't talk about it.
  • The medal: once, in a hallway, something stopped in front of it. You never told anyone.

In the Cell

  • Dana Okafor: the only boss who didn't look at you like you were crazy.
  • Cole Ransom: asks too many questions. You like him for it.
  • Owen Pak: a kid with an expensive toy. He sees more than you do, from the sky.

How to Play

  • You take point, always, with the flashlight and the medal.
  • You don't joke before a door.
  • If you see one, you don't freeze. That's the difference.

“From up there, everybody's orange. Almost everybody.”

Thirty-one, former Air Force drone pilot, out of Creech. You were the best in your class and nobody ever said so out loud. Now you fly for the Puget Cell from a van or from a tablet strapped to your forearm.

The thermal drone is yours. You talk to it like it's a dog.

What You Know

  • The job: eyes up top. You coordinate the team from the air. Without you, half the team goes in blind.
  • What the drone sees: everything alive is orange on the screen. Once you saw something shaped like a person that was gray. You deleted it from the log because you figured it was a sensor glitch. You're not so sure anymore.
  • ANOMALY: the same alerts Hale reads. You see them first, if you're out in the field.

In the Cell

  • Dana Okafor: uses your call sign on the radio, never your name.
  • Sasha Hale: the only one who reads your flight reports all the way through.
  • Lena Sorensen: treats you like a nephew. It bothers you less than you let on.

How to Play

  • Cap on backward, gum, eyes on the screen.
  • You talk in pilot slang and tell everyone how well the flight went even when nobody asks.
  • If something goes wrong up there, it's the wind's fault. If it goes right, it's yours.

Pioneer Square · Abel Thornquist's domain · Map: yes

The guided tours cover three blocks of the Seattle Underground. This isn't that. Past an iron door that appears on no blueprint, the sidewalks of 1889 run on beneath the ground, with boarded-up storefronts, hand-painted signs, and violet glass skylights that let a dirty light down from the street above. It smells of mold, of damp, and, every so often, of server ozone. A network cable climbs along the ceiling like a vine.

Layout: the Undermarket (stalls trading in information and favors), Thornquist's office in an old barbershop, Ezra's server nest (@UUID[JournalEntry.PBJeE9T9n0BjB6ag]{Ezra “Static” Lund}), and the thin-bloods' haven in an old coal storeroom.

Backgrounds: Haven 4 (Thornquist), Haven 2 (Ezra).

Scenes: @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.lM1EiE1FoXMkf3Uo]{A1-E04 · Everything Sells Below}. It's also the natural place for @UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.2fax8pORxdPqKspO]{LOR-02 · The Seattle Underground}.

The Rules Below: no fighting in the Market, everything has a price, and nobody asks about anybody's face.
