text.content: Snohomish Valley, 40 minutes north · Ethan Montgomery's haven · Map: yes

The gravel road ends at a dark-timbered farmhouse surrounded by fields flooded with rain. There are dogs, a lot of them, and they don't bark: they watch. Behind the house, through the trees, the river glints. The man waiting for you on the porch doesn't get up from his rocking chair. His eyes are a color that isn't quite human.

Layout: main house, a barn converted into the Wolves' meeting hall, a basement with a tunnel roughly 300 meters long leading to a private boat landing on the Snohomish River, and kennels holding a dozen ghoul dogs.

Backgrounds: Haven 3 and Herd 2 (the bounty hunters, @UUID[Actor.L1oU4dlqHg8Yszon]{Montgomery's Bounty Hunters}, who live in trailers behind the barn).

Scenes: @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.xWx5IoPih8fX83b1]{A1-E03 · The Sheriff Asks} (the coterie forms) and @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.aGN9NHO00wmdUzVn]{A3-E04 · The Pack Wavers} (the pack wavers). It's one of the possible targets in @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.ogKpm1VYgcVGCw1T]{A4-E02 · The Raid}.

Detail: Montgomery receives visitors sitting on the porch, even in the rain. If he invites someone inside, the matter is serious.

North of downtown · Silos and conveyor gallery · Map: yes

Chapter 3 doesn't describe this location. What follows comes from @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell} and the Part 3 ID registry (doc 12); on the domain map (@UUID[JournalEntry.oIF9UlwtOCvcz9Sf]{Map of Seattle with the Domains}) it's point ⑯ “Terminal 86.”

The service stairs zigzag up the outside of the silo to a long, narrow gallery of sheet metal and grimy glass. Inside, a stopped conveyor belt runs end to end. It smells of old grain and the sea. At the far end, a hatch hangs open over the bay, letting in the wind and the rain, and facing it is a chair with someone tied to it. Sitting on the belt, elbows on his knees, gray coat hanging open, a man with a shaved head watches you arrive. He doesn't get up. “Come,” he tells David. “Sit. I've wanted to ask you something for fifty years.”

The Read Aloud is the arrival sidebar from @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell}.

The location is the Terminal 86 grain elevator, north of downtown: a row of forty-meter concrete silos by the water, with a conveyor gallery up top that links the silos to the pier. @UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{Krell} waits in the gallery. The hostage, if there is one, is tied to a chair beside an open loading hatch over the bay, thirty meters above the water.

Access: there are three ways in: the outside stairs (the ones the meeting calls for, in Krell's line of sight), the inside of the neighboring silo (Athletics, Difficulty 3, to climb), and the water (bringing a boat in under the hatch).

The hatch: anyone who falls through it takes 4 blunt damage on hitting the water, thirty meters down.

Scene: @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell} (Night 7, Night 7, Wednesday, November 18, midnight).

It rises with Masquerade breaches, with public violence, with contact between Helen and FIRSTLIGHT, and with the fragments Halloway leaks each night the plot moves forward without a response. It drops when the coterie cleans up traces, recovers copies of the File, or neutralizes the mole.

text.content: Phase 2. Working document for the Storyteller. All cross-references go by ID.

Charles Halloway (@UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Charles Halloway}), the Ventrue Primogen, wants the crown of Seattle. He can't bring down Prince Whitmore (@UUID[JournalEntry.sCVTjJFrnyyVnQDt]{Marcus Whitmore}) while Sheriff Montgomery (@UUID[JournalEntry.1UgmJAqeofD7SSaf]{Ethan Montgomery}) and his Hound, David Smith (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}), keep the city clean. His plan has three pieces:

  • The File. His ghoul Preston Gale (@UUID[JournalEntry.y8Ao3xEHH3W11EJe]{Preston Gale}), owner of a home camera and security company, locates the archive of Helen Ward (@UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen Ward}) through his own customers' data. A team of mortals steals it.
  • The Ghost. In 1986, Halloway bought the journals of Marcus Vance (@UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Marcus “Ironjaw” Vance}), which were never burned. With them he hires August Krell (@UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{August Krell}), a Brujah whom Vance trained and abandoned in the '70s. Krell destroys the Kindred who could expose the theft, imitating Controlled Fury. That gets Halloway two things: David chasing a dead man, and Montgomery starting to distrust him.
  • The Leak. Halloway hands the Second Inquisition (FIRSTLIGHT) selected fragments of the File. They only point at Whitmore's and Montgomery's assets. When the raid comes, he'll convene the Primogen to demand a regent “capable of protecting the Masquerade”: himself.

Vance is not in Seattle. Every sign of him is false. What is real is Krell, the other son, the one who wasn't chosen.

It's a 0-to-10 tracker that measures how much the Second Inquisition knows. It starts at 2. It rises with Masquerade breaches, public violence, contact between Helen and FIRSTLIGHT, and the fragments Halloway leaks each night the plot advances unanswered. It drops when the coterie cleans up traces, recovers copies of the File, or neutralizes the mole.

Threshold What happens in the city
3 FIRSTLIGHT puts Helen under surveillance: vans, drones, and an analyst who listens closely to her podcast.
5 Agent Dana Okafor (@UUID[JournalEntry.bJA2iRyDgbm2TcuK]{Dana Okafor}) contacts Helen and offers her protection in exchange for the archive.
7 They investigate one of David's mortal assets (Bear's contacts or the hangar's cover). Resources or Haven at risk.
9 The raid, @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.ogKpm1VYgcVGCw1T]{A4-E02 · The Raid}, triggers.
10 Purge. At least one Camarilla haven falls and the city enters a Masquerade crisis for the rest of the chronicle.

Tom “Bear” Whitman never wanted to be anybody's soldier again after leaving the Navy.

Then he met David. And it turned out some contracts aren't signed in ink, but in blood.

  • Name: Thomas “Bear” Whitman

  • Apparent age: well into his forties

  • Real age: 48

  • Profession: Ex-SEAL, private security contractor, now David's right-hand man / ghoul

  • Nickname: “Bear”—for his size, the way he charges… and because when he gets angry, you just want him to look somewhere else.

  • Status: Human ghoul, heavily bound to David's Vitae

pages.name: 🎖️ Before the Blood: The Navy's Bear

text.content:
Tom grew up in a working-class neighborhood in Philadelphia, the son of a trucker and a waitress. He was the typical big kid, strong and slow to anger… until someone messed with his people. That's when the “bear” came out.

  • Enlisted in the Navy at 18.

  • Made it through brutal selection and ended up on a SEAL special operations team.

  • Specialty: heavy support, breacher, and long-gun operator.

    • First man through the door.

    • Last out of the blast radius.

In the service he learned the kind of violence that doesn't make it into the movies:

dirty operations, “unofficial” targets, cleanups that never show up in any report.

He got out honorably… but not in one piece.

He carried:

  • Mild but constant post-traumatic stress disorder.

  • A wrecked knee.

  • A list of faces he saw in his dreams.

He retooled as a private security contractor, first for security firms, then for “private clients” who paid under the table.

In the late 2000s, Tom was working security at a loading dock in Seattle, where things happened that didn't add up:

  • containers that “didn't exist” as far as Customs was concerned,

  • night movements with no route plan,

  • quiet guys who never looked at the cameras.

One night, a “live” shipment got out of control:

  • kidnapped people, screams, shadows moving too fast,

  • gunfire that didn't seem to stop a figure inside the container.

Tom did what he always did: he went in first.

He saw:

  • a pale man with his jaw blown loose by a bullet, who kept coming;

  • eyes that shone with an impossible hunger;

  • a guy in a tactical jacket, completely calm in the middle of hell, who grabbed the monster by the back of the neck and slammed it against the metal until he'd broken more than bones.

That guy was David.

Tom fired, shouted, tried to enforce protocol.

It didn't work.

The next clear image he remembers is:

  • the hot, metallic taste in his mouth,

  • a deep voice saying:

    “Either you die here, or you get up knowing too much. Decide.”

It wasn't really a choice.

David offered him his blood. Tom drank.

He woke up hours later with no real wounds, his body like it had just come out of a luxury operating room and a fierce energy in his veins. That night's cameras had “failed.”

So had the reports.

And David, sitting in a folding chair in the hangar, simply told him:

“From today on, you're part of the cleanup.

What you saw doesn't exist.

What's coming doesn't either.

But you'll get to keep fighting for something other than a paycheck.”

The first months were a mix of miracle and damnation.

The good:

  • Knee almost pain-free.

  • Absurd muscle recovery.

  • Physical stamina that made him feel twenty again.

  • Sharper senses, faster reflexes, that rush before going into action.

The bad:

  • David's Vitae became the invisible axis of his life.

  • If he went too long without it:

    • shakes,

    • bad sleep,

    • a shitty mood,

    • a feeling of emptiness, as if the world suddenly drained of color.

At first he rationalized it:

“I've been hooked on adrenaline, on war, on booze back in the day…

Now it's just something else. And at least this is good for something.”

But deep down he knows that without that blood, he'd fall apart.

The relationship between David and Tom isn't a simple “master and servant” thing. It's more complicated:

  • Brother in arms:

    • They share tactical language, silences, that way of entering a room where every angle is calculated.

  • Toxic father / loyal son, dark version:

    • David gives him power, direction, and a cause.

    • But he also keeps him bound through the Vitae.

  • Absolute trust in combat:

    • If David says “cover that door,” Tom covers it even if the world blows up.

    • If Tom says “something about this job doesn't sit right with me,” David listens.

Tom doesn't entirely fool himself:

  • He knows David is a monster.

  • He knows he's becoming one himself, on his own human scale.

  • But he'd rather be a monster in the service of someone with a code than go back to being a loose weapon in anybody's hands.

Tom doesn't have the same code as David, but they overlap:

  • No kids, ever.

  • No clear-cut victims.

  • No killing for sport.

When David has to cross the gray line, Tom sometimes looks the other way… but he feels it.

Sometimes he argues:

“That guy was trash, sure, but he had a family. We could've done something else.”

Sometimes he just keeps quiet… and drinks.

The Vitae dependency shows in everyday details:

  • He always carries a black metal canteen in his backpack. Nobody knows what's inside. He does.

  • When David is gone too long, Tom gets more irritable and risks his neck on dangerous jobs to “kill the jones.”

  • He tried to quit once:

    • three weeks without Vitae,

    • sweats, migraines, flashbacks to old operations,

    • whole nights without sleep, staring at the hangar ceiling.

  • He ended up on his knees on the haven floor, his voice broken:

    “Give it to me or finish me off. But don't leave me halfway.”

David gave it to him.

And with it, a few words Tom never forgot:

“You're not my slave, Bear. But without this, you won't survive what you've already seen.

Decide what kills you: the truth or the withdrawal.”

Tom is:

  • Logistics and fire support for the Hound of the Masquerade:

    • drives the vehicles,

    • maintains and modifies the weapons in the hangar armory,

    • plans entry and exit routes.

  • The coterie's guy, ever since David started lending them the hangar:

    • keeps their weapons ready and the coffee made,

    • treats them like David's unit: with respect, without trust, until they earn it.

  • Human shield:

    • puts himself between David and bullets, explosions, or physical dangers that David could sometimes dodge… but that they'd rather not let hit him.

  • The “human” face:

    • can talk to police, guards, neighbors, and security staff without raising supernatural suspicion.

    • acts as go-between when someone with a clean ID and a pulse is needed.

In combat, he's:

  • the guy who goes in with the rifle,

  • the one who holds the door,

  • the one who drags the wounded out of the crossfire.

And, if need be, the one who finishes off whatever David leaves lying on the floor.

pages.name: 🧨 Wounds and Demons of His Own

text.content:
Tom carries several shadows:

  • War guilt:

    • operations where the target wasn't so clear,

    • orders he followed even knowing they reeked of political bullshit.

  • People he saved who then didn't know what to do with their lives, and came to a bad end.

  • Now he wonders if he's repeating the pattern:

    • he saves people from monsters…

    • but he also helps monsters keep existing.

Over the years, he's developed a quiet conviction:

“If David goes too far over the line, if he becomes one of those monsters with no code…

someone will have to stop him.

And maybe that someone has to be me.”

He doesn't say it out loud.

But sometimes, when he looks at the gun he keeps in his personal safe, he wonders if someday he'll point it at his own master. (Under that gun is the note from @UUID[JournalEntry.5mQIPoGa4I0tQtbR]{Note Kept in Bear's Safe}.)

Personality:

  • Talks little, thinks more.

  • Dry, barracks humor:

    • dark jokes,

    • short sentences,

    • doesn't waste time on speeches.

  • Instinctively protective:

    • of mortals caught in the crossfire,

    • of @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen} if she's in front of him,

    • of David, even when he knows David would survive anyway.

With the coterie:

  • Sometimes he tells them what he can't bring himself to tell David. If something about the job doesn't sit right with him, he says it in front of everyone.

  • If a PC puts David in danger for nothing, Bear doesn't forget it.

Relationship with Helen (if they cross paths):

  • He sees her as a “brave but reckless civilian.”

  • He respects her, but he also wants to yell at her:

    “Drop this, go back to writing about corrupt mayors, this is going to get you killed.”

  • If he ever has to choose between saving Helen and following an order from David, that's guaranteed drama.

1. The Mission That Binds Them Forever

    • An operation where Tom is literally torn apart protecting David and a group of mortals.

    • David “puts him back together” with Vitae.

    • Since then, Tom's dependency has skyrocketed, but so has his loyalty.

  2. The Military Past Comes Back (developed as @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.NONJmwNuBweLPdPQ]{GAN-04 · The Old Comrade}, with Cole Ransom, @UUID[Actor.5ywnpdrw93wmy235]{Cole Ransom})

    • An old SEAL buddy of Tom's shows up in Seattle, now working for someone (Camarilla, Anarchs, hunters… whatever you like).

    • He notices something strange in Tom: impossible reflexes, wounds that heal too fast.

    • He wants answers.

  3. The Possible Break

    • David, for strategic reasons, decides to ration or cut off Tom's Vitae for a while.

    • That creates tension:

      • Tom more vulnerable,

      • more unstable,

      • tempted to look for another source of Blood (another vampire, or even the Sabbat).

NOT GONNA HAPPEN! :D

(The Vitae-rationing hook is excluded: doc 00.)

• Code. Doc 25 says “No kids, ever. No clear-cut victims. No killing for sport.”; doc 07 quotes it as “No kids. No people who didn't do anything. No killing for the hell of it.” It's the same idea in other words.
  • Hooks. Hook 2 is @UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.NONJmwNuBweLPdPQ]{GAN-04 · The Old Comrade}. Hook 3 (rationing the Vitae) is excluded by doc 25 itself and by doc 00. Hook 1 (the mission that binds them) doesn't appear in docs 00–16.
  • Touchstone. David's sheet (doc 18) lists him as a Touchstone; docs 00–16 say he works as an anchor, even though he's a ghoul.
  • Arrival at the hangar. He met David in the late 2000s, at a loading dock in Seattle; docs 00–16 don't date it.

Sheet: @UUID[Actor.XuP20cPC3T1EiCxD]{Wendell Fry}

“You're not crazy, Helen. And the rain has ears.”

Clan: Malkavian · Position: Primogen (by custom) · Sect: Camarilla

For nine years Wendell Fry hosted the overnight show on a Seattle AM station, one to five a.m., the slot nobody wanted. He played jazz, blues, and rare records, and he took calls from insomniacs, truckers, nurses, and drunks. What made the show famous was that Wendell listened. He let people talk for ten, fifteen minutes, and then he said one sentence that stuck with them for the rest of their lives. Listeners said he could guess things. He said he just paid attention.

In 1971, a Malkavian who called the show every night from a phone booth in Fremont waited for him outside the station one night. She told him she had chosen him because his was the only voice in the city that didn't lie, and she Embraced him in the parking lot. His sire disappeared a few weeks later. Wendell kept the show going for two more years, until the station went off the air. Today he has an overnight show again, on a community radio station.

Editor's Note

Doc 06 ended his radio career with the station's closing; it was decided that today he has a late-night show on a community radio station, which is his Mask.

Now he listens to the city another way: police radios, podcasts, voicemails, bar conversations. He believes Seattle speaks in code and that he is the only one who understands it. Sometimes he's right. He holds the Malkavian seat among the Primogen because nobody else wanted it, and he votes based on things nobody understands. For years he has been calling in to Helen's podcast under the name “W.”

The prophecy of the fist. For a month now he has been hearing, in the static of the port radio, that “the fist has two sons.” He doesn't know what it means, but he had it entered in the Elysium log (@UUID[JournalEntry.lcO0CdwUlZHg2wAX]{Register of the Keeper of Elysium, November Folio}) and wrote it on a napkin (@UUID[JournalEntry.FVBnf3yE87K4BOhh]{Wendell Fry: “Song for the Son of the Fist”}).

Protect the prophet. He believes Helen Ward is a sibyl, someone who hears the city's truth without knowing she hears it. If he learns she's in danger, he'll try to help her in his own way, which may not be the best way.

The deciding vote. At the Council (@UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}) his vote can tip the balance. He'll vote for whoever has told him something true out loud.

An abandoned radio studio on the top floor of a building in Fremont, full of old equipment left switched on (Haven 2). He feeds on insomniacs: people who can't sleep and go out walking at three in the morning. He gives them conversation first. Some come back looking for him.

The listeners (Herd 1): a dozen insomniacs who cross paths with him on the same streets and think he's an odd neighbor.

Scanners (Resources 1): police, port, and emergency radios, all on at once.

Fame 1: old listeners of the station still recognize his voice.

@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith} (tenderness). He calls him “the son of the fist” without knowing exactly why.

@UUID[JournalEntry.OmK2qlPVNl758u6h]{August Krell} (pity). He has never seen him, but he hears him in the static: “the one who learned half.”

@UUID[JournalEntry.sCVTjJFrnyyVnQDt]{Marcus Whitmore} (amusement). He considers him an actor who forgot he was in a play.

@UUID[JournalEntry.uDNdrVnGBbAh18Tt]{Charles Halloway} (unease). He says his voice “has no bottom.”

@UUID[JournalEntry.rg50DlMYSzgbZeBv]{Nadia Ferro} (kinship). He knows her work on the podcast. He likes the mix.

• “Fry hears the future on the radio.” (Half true: he hears the present with a clarity that seems like the future.)
  • “Fry is the listener ‘W.’ on Helen Ward's podcast.” (True.)
  • “Fry will always vote with the Prince.” (False.)

To mortals he's the late-night host on a community radio station (Mask 1). He looks about thirty-three. He's thin, with an unkempt beard, thick-framed glasses, corduroy jackets, and a baseball cap from a team that no longer exists. He speaks in a radio voice, deep and slow, that contrasts with his scruffy look. He always has headphones hanging around his neck. Sometimes he puts them on in the middle of a conversation.

Editor's Note

Doc 06 said “looks about fifty-five” and “white beard”; it was decided that he looks the age he was at his Embrace (1971, born in 1938): about thirty-three, with an unkempt beard but no gray. It also said that to mortals he's “an eccentric retiree from Fremont”; it was decided that he's the late-night host on a community radio station.

• Sire: an unnamed Malkavian who called in from Fremont
  • Embraced: 1971 (born in 1938)
  • Ambition: decipher what the city is trying to tell him.
  • Conviction: “Never interrupt someone who is telling the truth.”
  • Touchstone: Helen Ward (@UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen Ward}), though she doesn't know it.
  • Humanity: 7
  • Generation: 10th
  • Blood Potency: 2

Derangement (Malkavian): he can't leave a sentence unfinished. If someone interrupts him, he repeats what he was saying from the beginning.

Attributes: Strength 1, Dexterity 2, Stamina 2 · Charisma 3, Manipulation 2, Composure 3 · Intelligence 3, Wits 4, Resolve 2

Secondary Attributes: Health 5 · Willpower 5

Skills: Academics 2 (Music), Awareness 4 (What Goes Unsaid), Etiquette 1, Performance 4 (Radio), Occult 3 (Prophecy), Insight 5 (Voices), Persuasion 2, Stealth 2, Technology 2 (Analog Radio)

Disciplines:

  • Auspex 3: Heightened Senses (Heightened Senses), Premonition (Premonition), Scry the Soul (Scry the Soul)
  • Dominate 1: Cloud Memory (Cloud Memory)
  • Obfuscate 2: Cloak of Shadows (Cloak of Shadows), Unseen Passage (Unseen Passage)

THE PUGET COURIER · Obituaries · Thursday, October 24, 1996

EMILY ROSE SMITH

February 14, 1958 – October 21, 1996

Emily Smith, a caseworker with the King County Department of Youth Services, died Monday in Rainier Valley while attending to minors in her care. She was 38.

Born in San Diego, she was raised in Seattle by her mother, Anne Smith, who died in 1989. Her father, Marine Sgt. David Smith, died on active duty in 1960, when Emily was two.

She earned her degree in social work from the University of Washington in 1981 and spent fifteen years working with at-risk youth in the south end of the city. Colleagues remember her as “the one who never hung up the phone” and “the one who took the cases nobody else wanted.”

Police are investigating the incident as a confrontation between gangs. One of the minors was unharmed.

She is not survived by any immediate family. A private service will be held Saturday at the cemetery in the cedars. In lieu of flowers, the family asks that donations be made to the Rainier Valley Youth Center.

[Handwritten in blue ballpoint, next to “She is not survived by any immediate family”:] She is.

Medium: Newspaper clipping. Delivery: @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.aJxUAHXcYpRWrhmG]{A2-E03 · Salt's} or Epilogue.

Storyteller: a yellowed clipping from a 1996 local newspaper. David keeps it in the hangar. Rosa has an identical one in the back room at Salt's. If it comes up in @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.aJxUAHXcYpRWrhmG]{A2-E03 · Salt's}, have her be the one who brings it out.

Note: Emily's mother (Anne Smith) and the exact date of death (October 21, 1996) are new details. If they contradict David's character sheet, change them.

Source ARCHER, second delivery

  1. The anonymous source designated ARCHER has delivered a second sample through the agreed channel. Provisional reliability: B-2 (usually reliable; information probably true). The source claims to have access “to the local structure” and to know its hierarchy.

  2. The sample includes three locations of interest:

    a) Rural property in the Snohomish Valley, with a private boat landing.

    b) Industrial hangar on Harbor Island, registered to a dormant logistics company.

    c) Penthouse in a residential building on Capitol Hill, registered to a cultural foundation.

  3. All three match areas flagged in episode 112 of the podcast “What the City Forgets” (WARD, Helen). Recommend increasing passive surveillance on WARD. Direct contact not recommended at this time.

  4. The source claims to be able to deliver, within the next few days, “the complete index” of a private archive documenting ten years of incidents in the area. If so, it would be the cell's biggest find since its creation.

  5. Separately: surveillance continues on statistical anomaly no. 1 (M.E. signature “R. A.,” King County office, 15 reports with an inconsistent pattern).

  6. Open question: why is the source giving us this? Every source wants something. Until we know what ARCHER wants, I propose treating its deliveries as possible bait.

— S. H.

Truth: it's real. Preston Gale is selling technology to Northline without knowing what Northline is. Halloway knows, and considers it an acceptable risk. Celeste Arden (@UUID[JournalEntry.zQMt8VMfKPoL6INq]{Celeste Arden}) is on the distribution list because her shell company is the majority shareholder.

VOICE MEMO 7 — 11/08/2026 — 4:17 AM — 3 min 41 s

[Automatic transcription. Checked by hand by H.W.]

[rain. A lighter that doesn't catch the first time.]

Okay. Seven. Memo seven. For the record, it's four-something and I'm not drunk, I'm tired, which is worse.

Third confirmed case. Kyle Brandt, twenty-three, Crown Hill. His mother found him Tuesday. County report: fentanyl overdose. His mother says he was terrified of needles, that he used to pass out at school when they gave shots. I believe her. Not because she's his mother. I believe her because he doesn't have a single old mark on his arms and because my source at the M.E.'s office told me the same thing again that they told me about the other two.

[long pause]

That they're missing blood. Not all of it. Some. Like someone took just enough.

Three in eighteen months, inside a one-mile radius. All three at night, all three alone, all three in houses with no alarm. And one more thing, and this is the one keeping me up. I requested the cameras. The ones at the 7-Eleven on Kyle's corner, the bus stop, the building across the street. All three “failed” that night. Between one and three. All three.

I don't know if that's a person or a system. I don't know which scares me more, either.

[pause. Exhales smoke.]

To do: cross-check against the Harbor Island folder. To do: don't tell Nadia about this yet, she gets excited and wants to run it in the next episode, and this isn't ready. To do, even though I'm not going to: tell the man on the phone.

No. Not yet. If I tell him, he takes it out of my hands.

End of memo.

Medium: audio transcript. When: @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.T8gJWjZpOnL4OisP]{A1-E01 · What They Took}, if Helen lets the coterie go through her phone, or as reading ahead of session 1.

Foreshadows: the pattern of the Ballard deaths, which is part of the File. The cameras that “didn't record anything” are the first sign of Gale Sentinel (@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.NIaBWn52GOUI61A5]{Professional Mortal Thieves; Looped Cameras}).

Truth: everything she says is true. The three deaths are the work of a minor Kindred who was feeding without control in Crown Hill. It has no connection to Halloway, but it's one of the holes FIRSTLIGHT will find in the archive.

Seattle leaves traces. The twelve fragments in this chapter are some of them: voice memos, messages saved on an old phone, a handwritten log, an email nobody was supposed to read. Each one is written as the object itself and can be printed or uploaded to Foundry as is, to hand out at the table.

Before each document there's a sidebar for the Storyteller: when to hand it out, what it foreshadows, and what's true in it. That sidebar isn't shown to the players.

WHAT WAS IN THE BASEMENT

(from memory, 11/12, 4:20 a.m.—I'm definitely forgetting something)

Structure: twelve years, 2014–2026. One folder per year. Inside, one subfolder per case. 214 cases total, I think. Plus the unnamed folder. Plus the maps.

The heaviest cases (the ones with the most material):

  • 2014 · LARCHMONT. Seven “unaccounted for.” Danny. Forty-one photos of the fire, the fire department report that doesn't add up, the doorman's statement that he later retracted. THE PHOTO.
  • 2015 · GEORGETOWN FOUNDRY. Two night watchmen “missing.” One came back three weeks later remembering nothing.
  • 2016–2018 · HARBOR ISLAND. “Animal” attacks at the port. Bodies with almost no blood. The case where I met him.
  • 2017 · BELLEVUE PARKING GARAGE. A “suicide.” A young woman, very well dressed, crouched next to the body. She's not the one who jumped.
  • 2018 · PIONEER SQUARE. Thermal capture of a figure going into a sewer. The figure has no temperature.
  • 2019–2022 · THE RAINIER DOSES. “Overdose” deaths in a two-mile pattern. Nobody with a history.
  • 2021 · THE IMPOSSIBLE REPORTS. Fifteen county medical examiner's reports with details that don't fit. All with the same signature: R. A.
  • 2023 · THE RUNNING MAN. Cell phone video, Ballard: a guy runs after a car faster than the car.
  • 2024–2026 · CROWN HILL. The three kids. Kyle Brandt. The mother from Lake City.
  • Several years · N. My own producer. She's never in the group photos. Coincidence? [Crossed out. Next to it:] Don't be paranoid, Helen.

The unnamed folder: fourteen photos. 2014–2025. The same man. The same scar. [Underlined twice.]

The maps: one map per year with digital pins. If you overlay them, you see the pattern: zones where nothing ever happens and zones where everything happens. Borders. Like territories.

Recordings: 300-some interviews. The voice memos (7 so far on this case). W.'s messages.

[At the bottom of the last page, smaller, pressing the pen differently:]

If someone has all of this, they can find them all. All of them, whatever they are. And I did this. Me.

Medium: Handwritten notebook. Delivered in: @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.T8gJWjZpOnL4OisP]{A1-E01 · What They Took}.

Storyteller: three notebook pages handwritten by Helen in @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.T8gJWjZpOnL4OisP]{A1-E01 · What They Took}, from memory, with scratch-outs. The PCs' folders have no names: Helen doesn't know them. Each player should recognize their own.

pages.name: Journal of M. Vance, Marseille, 1963, Folio 14 (Typewritten Copy)

text.content:
[rubber stamp, violet ink:] COPY 2 OF 3

Folio 14 — Marseille, March 1963

The American learns fast, but he learns with rage, and rage is a poor teacher. Today I broke his left hand three times. All three times he raised his guard again without my asking. He did not complain. He looked at me the way dogs look at you when they have not yet decided whether to bite.

I explained the doctrine for the fourth time. Locate: no one strikes what he has not seen whole. Assess: how much he weighs, how much he fears, how much of the man is left in him. Execute: one blow, the right one, and nothing more. Everything that comes after the first blow is the Beast asking permission.

Not all of those I train reach the end. To those who do not finish, I teach the inverted guard, the one with the weak hand forward. It will defend against anyone except someone who knows the complete doctrine. It is a gift and it is a lock. That way, if one of them goes astray, the one who did finish will always know how to stop him.

The American will finish. I have known it since Haiti. He has a daughter on the other side of the sea and he does not speak of her, and that is what holds him up. You must have something you do not say to endure this.

Tomorrow, the cold water.

—M. V.

[In the left margin, in pencil, cramped, slanted handwriting:]

This is the one you taught me. You never taught me the other.

Medium: typewritten copy on yellowed paper, with a penciled note in the margin. When: @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell}, in Krell's haven or on his body. If you want to plant it earlier, a photocopy without the note can be found in @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.j4TnqYOwVuSCeQ0z]{A2-E02 · “Locate. Evaluate. Execute.”}.

Foreshadows: the doctrine of Controlled Fury (@UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.oGnroV6R68YdMQyD]{LOR-01 · The Doctrine of Controlled Fury}) and the inverted guard, which gives Krell away (@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.HYE4rNbNf1sEbYGe]{The Inverted Guard}).

Truth: the text is Vance's. Halloway's archivist made the copy in 1986, and the pencil note is Krell's. The line about those who don't finish is Krell's wound.

OFFICE OF THE MEDICAL EXAMINER · KING COUNTY, WASHINGTON

PRELIMINARY EXAMINATION REPORT · INTERNAL USE ONLY

Case No. 26-3307
Date received 11/13/2026, 6:52 AM
Recovery site Terminal 46, Harbor Island, beside container MSKU-4471192
Identity Unidentified (John Doe No. 41-26)
Pathologist Dr. M. Kowalski (covering). Assigned night-shift pathologist: on leave.

Findings. Received: gray particulate material, approximately 4.1 kg, collected from a concrete surface of about 2 m². Contains calcined bone fragments (phalanges, a portion of mandible with three teeth consistent with an adult), unburned remnants of synthetic fabric, and an intact USB drive (released to police as evidence, chain of custody 26-3307-A).

Observations. The degree of calcination is consistent with prolonged exposure to temperatures above 1,000 °C. No ignition source, accelerant residue, or heat marking was found at the scene, either on the concrete or on the adjacent container. The fabric present among the ashes shows no signs of combustion.

These findings are inconsistent with known combustion mechanisms. External review is recommended.

Signed: M. Kowalski, MD

[Yellow sticky note, handwritten:]

Marek: DO NOT send for review until Ruth's back. She handles these. — J.

[Below, in different handwriting:] Already sent it. Sorry. Some guy named Hale, from a consulting firm, asked for it. He had authorization. — M.

journal.name: Letter from Sheriff O'Connor to Prince Whitmore, 1978

pages.name: Letter from Sheriff O'Connor to Prince Whitmore, 1978

text.content:
[Letterhead] OFFICE OF THE SHERIFF · DOMAIN OF SEATTLE · the emblem scraped off with a razor blade

Seattle, April 19, 1978

To His Highness, Prince Marcus Whitmore:

I do not write to ask for clemency. You have already decided, and I have been in this city since before there was a port, so I know a decision made when I see one. I write so that it is on the record.

The business at the strike pier was not what you were told. Yes, there was a fight. Yes, a son of my clan lost his head in front of the longshoremen. I stopped him myself before dawn and cleaned up what needed cleaning. The next day there was nothing anywhere. Three days later there were photographs in a newspaper's newsroom. Photographs I did not see taken, from angles where no one was standing.

Someone commissioned them. Someone with patience and friends at the newspapers, who has spent years saying in Elysium that this city needs “a more modern order.” I do not write his name because you know it, and because written names have a bad habit of ending up in the wrong hands.

I am going south. I will cause you no trouble. But I ask one thing of you, as a last service: do not trust anyone who hands you an easy victory. Easy victories always come due later.

Your servant, until tonight,

Liam O'Connor

Sheriff of Seattle (1931–1978)

[At the foot, in a different ink and a different hand, elegant:]

Received. Filed. Let him go in peace. — M. W.

[Below, in pencil, nearly erased:] C. H. — watch.

Medium: handwritten letter on letterhead paper, worn folds. When: @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.wQ2BqzruUybEIhSO]{A2-E04 · The Sheriff That Was}. O'Connor (@UUID[JournalEntry.oQ2AhEeDkwdPRv71]{Liam O'Connor}) gives it to the coterie if they earn his trust.

Foreshadows: Halloway's patience. He has already brought down a Sheriff once, with the same method: manufacturing a Masquerade breach.

Truth: all of it is true. Whitmore read the letter and filed it anyway, because removing O'Connor suited him. His note at the foot is authentic.

If you're reading this, either I'm dead or I had to do it.

If I'm dead: the truck key is in the coffee can. The guns that aren't his go to the bottom of the canal, don't sell them. Send my sister in Philadelphia the blue envelope and don't tell her anything. Nothing.

If I had to do it, then this is for you, David, even though you won't read it because you won't be around.

I made myself three promises the first time I drank. No kids. No people who didn't do anything. No killing just because. You told me your code was a lot like mine. I believed you. I still believe you. But I'm writing this because one night I stopped being sure, and I promised myself that if you ever crossed it all the way, the one who stopped you was going to be me. Not some other vampire. Not anybody's orders. Me. Because I owe you that.

If I did it, forgive me. If I didn't and you're reading this because I died, then it was never needed, and that's the best thing that happened to me in this strange life.

Cover the door, Hound. I can't anymore.

— T. W.

EXTRAORDINARY SESSION OF THE PRIMOGEN COUNCIL OF THE DOMAIN OF SEATTLE

Convened at the request of the Primogen of Clan Ventrue

Night of November 19, 2026 · 10:30 PM · Halloway Tower, 42nd floor

Attendees summoned:

H.H. Prince Marcus Whitmore · Primogen Charles Halloway (Ventrue) · Primogen and Keeper of Elysium Solène Marchetti (Toreador) · Primogen and Regent Anneliese Voight (Tremere) · Primogen Abel Thornquist (Nosferatu) · Primogen Wendell Fry (Malkavian) · Sheriff Ethan Montgomery, attending as witness

AGENDA

  1. Presentation on the presence in the domain of a Second Inquisition cell and on the existence of a source supplying it with information from within this court.
  2. Presentation on the incidents at Terminal 46 and in SoDo, and on the possible involvement of an agent tied to the Sheriff.
  3. Identification of the Second Inquisition's source. (Documentation attached in a separate folder.)
  4. Motion for an emergency regency.

TEXT OF THE MOTION (item 4)

Whereas the security of the Masquerade in the domain has been gravely and continuously compromised;

Whereas H.H. the Prince was warned of this threat by the Regent of the Chantry on November 5 and no measure whatsoever was taken;

Whereas the security apparatus of the domain, under the charge of the Sheriff and his agents, is under suspicion;

The Primogen REQUEST that H.H. the Prince temporarily delegate his functions to an emergency Regent, chosen from among the Primogen, until the threat has been neutralized, and that the minutes of this session be forwarded to the Justicar of Clan Ventrue for her review and confirmation.

Primogen Charles Halloway is proposed as emergency Regent.

Votes required: simple majority of the Primogen present.

[At the bottom, on the coterie's copy, if anyone looks closely: the paper carries an almost invisible watermark. “Cascade Holdings LLC.”]

REGISTER OF THE ELYSIUM OF SEATTLE

Glass Gallery · Book XIV · Folio 211

Night of October 22. Regular session. Present: H.H. Prince Whitmore, the full Primogen, and the Sheriff. No incidents. Primogen Halloway requests a private audience with H.H. Denied owing to the schedule.

Night of October 29. Sheriff Montgomery withdraws before midnight without taking leave of H.H. No one remarks on it aloud.

Night of November 5. Regent Voight delivers to H.H. an envelope sealed with black wax. H.H. does not open it in the hall. Primogen Halloway again requests a private audience. Denied. This Keeper notes that the Primogen smiled upon receiving the answer.

Night of November 5 (cont.). A guest is relieved of a phone he was carrying, switched on, in his inside pocket. He is reminded of the fourth tradition of this Elysium: no connected device crosses the threshold. He apologizes. The device is returned to him on his way out, switched off.

Night of November 5 (cont.). Mr. Wendell Fry, of Clan Malkavian, asks that the following be entered into the record: “The fist has two sons, and neither of them knows it.” So entered.

Night of November 12. [Entry left blank. Only the date.]

S. M., Keeper

text.content:
Song for the Son of the Fist

There is a father who isn't here

and two sons who wait for him,

one in the water, one in the rain,

both with the same guard of stone.

One finished the lesson.

The other learned half,

and the half, when it rots,

weighs more than the truth.

Don't look for the father on the pier.

The coat isn't his who wears it.

Look for the one who signs with his left,

the one who begs to be seen.

The city has blue eyes

that never blink.

The glass king smiles.

The queen of the rain takes notes.

And the last boat of the night

carries off what no one wanted to read.

If you come late, Hound,

come this time.

— W.

Medium: a poem written in ballpoint pen on a Club Cinder paper napkin, with a wine stain. When: @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.uL8F2YNogcToiFc6]{A2-E01 · Elysium Night}. Fry (@UUID[JournalEntry.AeAhHuCNHL9KWVnT]{Wendell Fry}) leaves it with the PC who listened to him most. It's addressed to the Hound: that PC decides whether to give it to David.

journal.name: “What the City Forgets,” Episode 112: “The Ones Who Don't Age”

pages.name: “What the City Forgets,” Episode 112: “The Ones Who Don't Age”

text.content:
WHAT THE CITY FORGETS

Episode 112—“The Ones Who Don't Age”

Aired 10/03/2026 · Recording script v4 · Producer: N. Ferro

[THEME. 12 s. Duck under voice.]

HELEN There's a photo I'm not going to show you. Not because I don't have it. I do. I've had it for eleven years, and I look at it more than I should. It's a photo of a fire in Tacoma, and in the photo there's a man with his back to the flames. And there's another photo, from last year, down on the docks. And it's the same man.

[N.F. margin note: 2 s pause here. Let it breathe.]

HELEN Not the same kind of man. The same man. Same scar, same way of standing. Eleven years and he hasn't aged a day. You're going to say it's a brother, a son, a lookalike. I said that too. Then I found others.

HELEN A source I can't name, who always writes to me at the same hour, sent me a map last week. On the map were spots where, according to this source, the city “loses its memory.” Buildings where the cameras always fail in the same time window. Bars where nobody remembers seeing certain customers. A stretch of the port where incident reports disappear on their own.

HELEN I don't know what this is. I know what it isn't. It isn't coincidence.

[CUT TO LISTENER CALL. Male voice, older. Identified on screen as “W.”]

LISTENER (W.) Hi, Helen. I've been listening since the beginning. I wanted to tell you you're not crazy. And to be careful, because the ones who don't age don't forget either. And that the rain has ears. That's all. Oh, and I like the new music.

HELEN Thanks, W. It's always you who calls.

[N.F. note: we're keeping the call. It's perfect.]

HELEN Next week: three deaths in Crown Hill the county is calling overdoses. And a mother who says her son was afraid of needles.

[THEME. End.]

Format: podcast script with production notes. When: at session zero, so the players know what Helen puts on the air, or in @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.T8gJWjZpOnL4OisP]{A1-E01 · What They Took}.

Foreshadows: this is the episode that puts FIRSTLIGHT on alert (@UUID[JournalEntry.WW7eg88I0uDGj8ks]{FIRSTLIGHT, Internal Memo SEA-0411}). The “anonymous sources” are Nadia (@UUID[JournalEntry.rg50DlMYSzgbZeBv]{Nadia Ferro}).

Truth: Helen didn't publish David's photos, but she described the pattern. A Northline analyst listened to the episode three times.

UNNAMED FOLDER

Fourteen photos. The first is from 2014: the Larchmont, in flames, and him with his back to the fire, looking into the neighbor's camera. The last is from 2025: Harbor Island, under a streetlight.

Same face. Same scar, from the right cheekbone to the lip. Same coat, or one just like it. Same way of standing: feet apart, weight back, like the ground's about to move.

Eleven years and not one gray hair.

He shows up in four of my cases. Always after. Never during. He arrives when the worst is over and leaves before the police get there. Once I watched him clean up a scene like someone sweeping a kitchen.

He gave me a phone. He said my name before I'd given it to him.

I don't know what he is. I don't know if he's good. I know he looks out for me, and I don't know why.

To do: find out who died in 1960 with his face.

2017 · BELLEVUE PARKING GARAGE

A fifty-year-old man jumps from the fifth level of an office parking garage. He'd lost everything in a takeover bid that went bad that same afternoon. Suicide. Case closed.

But there's a still from the third-level security camera, at 11:47 p.m. A young woman, dark hair, expensive coat, crouched beside him before he jumps. She's touching his face. He doesn't look scared. He looks calm.

Four minutes later, he jumps. She's gone.

I looked for her. She works in finance. In one of the photos from a 2019 gala she looks the same as in 2017. Exactly the same. Same haircut.

I don't think she pushed him. I think she was there for something else. I don't know what.

To do: why would someone seek out people who've just lost everything?

2018 · PIONEER SQUARE

A thermal camera at the light-rail construction site recorded this on March 8 at 3:12 a.m.: a human figure lifts a manhole cover and climbs down. In the thermal image, everything around it has color. The figure doesn't. It's dark blue, like the water of the Sound. Like something that's been dead a while.

The figure showed up on the same camera six more times that year. Always in the small hours. Always the same manhole.

And one more thing, and I don't know if it's related: in the last video, before climbing down, the figure looks toward the camera. And the camera shuts off. Eleven minutes.

Exactly like the ones in my building the night of the break-in.

To do: who shuts off this city's cameras?

SEVERAL YEARS · N.

This is strange to write.

N. has produced my podcast since 2021. She's the best producer I've ever had. She brings me tips and I don't know where she gets them. They always come in at three in the morning.

Going through event photos for something else, I noticed: she isn't in a single group photo. Not one. At the episode 100 party, the whole team is in the picture and she isn't. She was there. I remember she was there. I remember she hugged me.

I asked her once and she said she hates photos. Maybe.

I don't like that I opened this folder. I opened it anyway. It's what I do.

To do: nothing. I don't want a to-do on her.

2023 · THE MAN WHO RUNS

A cell phone video, Ballard, July 14, 2023, 1:40 a.m. A car tears out of a parking lot. A big man, blond, beard, fisherman's jacket, runs after it.

And catches it.

Not in a long chase. In about a hundred yards. The car's doing nearly forty. The man pulls even with it, yanks the driver's door open while it's moving, and the video cuts out because whoever's filming drops the phone.

The next day there's no police report, no accident, nothing. The car turned up down at the harbor, parked and clean.

I have another photo of that man in a fishermen's bar from 1998. Clipped from a local paper. Same.

To do: the Ballard bars. Somebody has to know him.

2021 · THE IMPOSSIBLE REPORTS

Fifteen autopsy reports from the county M.E.'s office between 2008 and 2021. I got them one by one, with favors and patience. They all have something strange: a body with “severe unexplained hypovolemia,” a fire that didn't burn what it should have, an “animal bite” with a pattern no animal leaves.

And they all have the same calm conclusion, the same reasonable explanation. Overdose. Accident. Animal.

And the same signature: R. A., night-shift pathologist.

I don't think she's crazy. I think she's very good at her job. What I don't know is who she works for.

To do: ask her for an interview. No. Not yet.

Format: One sheet per PC. Delivery: Session zero or @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.T8gJWjZpOnL4OisP]{A1-E01 · What They Took}.

Storyteller: one sheet per character. It's what Helen had on each of them, written in her voice, like her working notes. Hand it out in private. If a player creates their own character, write theirs in this same style based on what they decide in session zero.

David's (@UUID[JournalEntry.3zcQLj7aEAxHT0Yr]{David Smith}) isn't handed to any player. It's the folder Helen had on him, the “unnamed folder” with the fourteen photos. The coterie can read it in the “SAFE” folder on USB drive 3 (@UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.5Vgl8slqjXlVRbie]{A2-E06 · The One Who Kept One}). Whether they show it to David, and what they tell him about what Helen wrote, is up to the players.

text.content:
r/SeattleAfterDark · Posted by u/night_crane · 3 hr. ago

Anyone else see this on Harbor Island? Pier 46, last night ~2:30

I work nights on one of the container cranes. From the cab you can see the whole pier. Last night, around two-thirty, I saw two guys next to a container. One was hitting the other. But not like a fight. Like a job. Short punches, always in the same spots, no hurry. The other guy wasn't defending himself very well. Then he grabbed him by the neck and hit him once in the chest and the guy… I don't know how to say it. He came apart. Like ash. I swear I wasn't on anything. I went down to look at four when my shift ended and there was a pile of gray dust and nothing else. No blood. No body.

Took a photo from the cab but it's blurry. Posting it anyway.

Layer 3 of A3-E02: the data center. “A windowless building behind the main one. Three rooms: storage, ANOMALY training, private archive.” “A door with biometrics (fingerprint and retina) and a security mantrap. One ghoul in the control room.”

The infiltration strip. The service road (west) comes from the parking lot (“To the campus parking lot” region, pending: zone map) and the service yard (south) comes from the office building (region → gale-sentinel). The generator and chillers in the yard give cover for approaching the mantrap. Running out across the campus in front of the cameras: Thermometer +1.

The three security levels (the text doesn't detail them; they break down like this):

  1. The mantrap. Outer door with a card reader; inner door locked with a biometric reader (Gale's or Dawson's fingerprint and retina). The two doors don't open at the same time. Forcing it: Strength + Athletics Diff. 5, and the alarm goes off. With Gale in hand (Celeste, Manipulation + Persuasion Diff. 4, or Dominate: Gale has Composure 2; Dawson, Resolve 3 and +2 dice from the Bond) the inner door opens without a roll. The ghoul in the control room watches the mantrap through the armored window.
  2. The rooms (storage and testing): locked card-access doors; they open from the control room console or with the ghoul's card. From the hallway you can see inside through the glass windows: on the left, “rows of black cabinets hum under blue lights”; on the right, the wall of faces.
  3. The private archive, at the end of the hallway: a locked door with its own lock, no network, isolated from everything else.

ANOMALY cameras (at the entrances), anomaly objects with no light: ① above the outer mantrap door; ② inside the mantrap; ③ in the southwest corner, covering the yard and the service road; ④ and ⑤ above the two emergency exits, outside. If the coterie didn't disable the module in layer 1, every Kindred who enters is logged (the Thermometer +1 counts only once for the whole incursion).

What's in each room:

  • Storage (west): four rows of racks. In the fireproof media safe (southwest corner), the original drive of the File, only until Night 6. On the management console, the shipping logs for the ARCHER channel with the reference SEA-0411 (P-10) and the complete DOC-07.
  • Testing room · ANOMALY training (east): “On one wall there's a screen with a grid of faces, hundreds of them, each with a label underneath: COLD_SUBJECT, and a number. Some of them you know from Elysium. One of them is yours.” This is the wall of faces (east wall; off on the map, two “video wall” lights turn it on). At the workstations, the cold subject database (it includes the coterie if the 3B camera recorded them in A0-E01) and DOC-11, if they don't have it. To the north, open to the room, the compute room with the GPU racks.
  • Private archive (north, at the end of the hallway): the air-gapped server with Halloway's personal archive, scanned by Pell. Copying it: Intelligence + Technology Diff. 3. The folios on “the German” (P-15): Intelligence + Investigation Diff. 4, or automatic by searching for “allemand.” This server is the one that may end up in the briefcase in A4-E03.

Alarm. If it goes off (mantrap forced, emergency exit opened), Dawson takes four minutes to arrive from the office building, and Bellevue police take twelve. The emergency exits (west and east) only open from inside and trip the alarm: they're the escape route for an assault.

Assault (Combat): Thermometer +2; Gale warns Halloway, who moves the original that same night if they don't take it. Dawson, alive and captured, is a witness.

Location: @UUID[JournalEntry.jg1zpvYlDFMJRY8Q]{The Sealed Underground (Seattle Underground)}
Scenes: @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.lM1EiE1FoXMkf3Uo]{A1-E04 · Everything Sells Below}

Arrival (A1-E04, Nights 2 to 4). A staircase leads down from a Pioneer Square basement (west) to the iron door that appears on no map. Behind it, the 1889 brick sidewalk runs east beneath the city: boarded-up shopfronts on both sides of the Market's entrance, violet glass skylights in the ceiling (Foundry lights over the sidewalk, nothing painted), and a network cable running along the top of the south wall to Ezra's door. It smells of mold, of damp, and, every so often, of server ozone.

The Undermarket. The big shop in the middle, open to the sidewalk through its cast-iron columns. Stalls of information and favors (fixed, painted) and two stall lanterns. Rules Below: no fighting in the Market, everything has a price, and nobody asks about anybody's face. Fighting here turns Thornquist and a dozen runners against the coterie and shuts off LOR-02.

The barbershop (Thornquist's office). At the far east end of the sidewalk, “there's a carbide lamp burning”: you can see it from a distance through the shopfront window, the only one that still has its glass. Thornquist receives visitors seated in the barber's chair (fixed, bolted to the floor) “as if it were a throne.” The carbide lamp is a lit tile (tile-lampara-carburo) on the counter. In the back corner, the safe with the duplicates of USB drives 1 and 2 (AVE-01-AJUSTE; Krell doesn't know they exist). Tests: Manipulation + Persuasion Diff. 4 (Ezra +2), Wits + Insight Diff. 3.

Ezra's nest (PJ-03, Haven 2). Under the street, across from the barbershop: racks of salvaged servers, the desk with his monitors (“screen” light), and the cot. The network cable from the sidewalk comes in through his door; the cables “come down through nineteenth-century holes” in the ceiling.

The thin-blood shelter. An old coal vault under the street: mattresses, blankets, candles, and the heap of coal nobody ever cleared out. Jun Takeda (PNJ-20) hasn't been back since the Pier 46 business: if they look for her here, she isn't here (she sleeps in a storage unit in SoDo).

LOR-02. The boarded-up shopfronts open onto abandoned shops with no door (the boards are nailed over the wall); if a PC has “Sealed Haven” (•••), the Storyteller can open one with a secret door.

Off the map. The staircase climbs to Pioneer Square (no street map). The sidewalk continues east behind a brick partition wall.

Location: @UUID[JournalEntry.NNzMhIvsavpG0iTQ]{The Sheriff's Farm and Boat Landing}
Scenes: @UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.xWx5IoPih8fX83b1]{A1-E03 · The Sheriff Asks} · @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.aGN9NHO00wmdUzVn]{A3-E04 · The Pack Wavers} · @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.ogKpm1VYgcVGCw1T]{A4-E02 · The Raid}

What it is. Montgomery's haven (Haven 3, Herd 2): main house, a barn converted into the Wolves' meeting hall, kennels with a dozen ghouled dogs, and, behind the barn, the bounty hunters' trailers (MEN-03). The cellar, with the 300 m tunnel to the river boat landing, is the granja-sotano map (the stairwell hall leads down there).

A1-E03 · The Sheriff Asks (on the porch). “The gravel road ends at a dark wooden farmhouse among flooded fields. There are dogs everywhere, motionless, not barking: watching. On the porch, in a rocking chair, sits a heavyset man…” Montgomery doesn't get up from the rocking chair (tile); the sheet with the list is on the porch railing beside him. “When the last of you climbs the steps” (the porch steps, at the center). He doesn't invite them in: what's said on the porch doesn't go into the house (Hal knows this without a roll). The dogs: tokens spread across the yard and the gravel.

A3-E04 · The Pack Hesitates (inside). “This time, the farmhouse door is open. Inside is a room with a cold fireplace, a long wooden table, and, on the table, a tablet, switched on… The dogs lie down on the porch, their backs to the house… Montgomery is standing by the window.” The front door opens straight into the living room: the cold fireplace against the west wall, the long table (tile) with the tablet (tile, “screen” light) and the envelope with the “M.V.” letter, and the front window, which looks out on the porch. Open the front door manually for this scene.

Combat (A3-E04, or if the coterie attacks the Sheriff). The twelve dogs come out of the kennels (behind the house: five wire pens with gates, doors you can see through) and off the porch; the six bounty hunters come out of the three trailers behind the barn (door on the west side of each). Montgomery: Blood Potency 5, Fortitude 4.

A4-E02 · The Raid (if it's the farm). FIRSTLIGHT comes in by the gravel road (south). Escape: the cellar tunnel to the river boat landing (down the stairwell hall stairs; granja-sotano map); the dogs cover the retreat. Animalism on the farm dogs creates chaos among the operators. The trailers and the barn are the other “save the mortals” objectives.

The barn. Sliding door to the west (open), back door to the north toward the trailers, and a small door to the south. Inside, the Wolves' long table with its benches (tiles), the wood stove, and, at the far end, the old stalls converted into storage (low wooden partitions: they block movement, not sight).

The house. Ground floor: living room, kitchen, the Sheriff's office (glass-front gun cabinet), the hall with the stairs down to the cellar, and the mudroom with the back door toward the kennels.

Detail. Montgomery receives visitors sitting on the porch even in the rain. If he invites someone inside, the matter is serious. If anyone attempts Dominate or Presence in A1-E03, he gets up from the rocking chair for the first time: “Do that again and I'll bury you in the back field.”

Scenes: @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.aJxUAHXcYpRWrhmG]{A2-E03 · Salt's}

A2-E03 · Salt's. “The road dies at a shuttered shipyard, rusted cranes cut out against a slate-colored sky. Beside the gate stands a bar with a neon sign missing a letter: SAL S. Inside are scarred wooden tables, a bar counter built from the split hull of a boat, and black-and-white photos of strikes.” The sign is a “neon” light on the façade (it isn't painted: there's no text on the map). Rosa waits with her elbows on the bar and a welder on top of it (tile or token).

The barroom. Open to the mortal public until two. The bar is half the shell of a boat hull, with the bottle shelf behind it; the strike photos hang on the north and south walls. Tables, chairs, and stools are movable (tiles): a dozen Anarchs use them for cover if things break down (Combat: Rosa stops it on the second round, “Not here.”). Tavi Mercer (MEN-05) doesn't take his eyes off them.

The back room. A meeting table (the assembly votes on whether to help the coterie) and a cork board with clippings: that's where Rosa keeps her 1996 clipping (AYU-04: “if it comes up in A2-E03, let her be the one to bring it out”). It's the place for the “private” confession (to a PC, or to David if they let him stay last). The door opens onto the barroom, on the public side; another door leads to the storeroom.

The back. Bas Okonjo hides in the storeroom (kegs, the keg cooler) so Hal won't see him; the back door opens onto the shipyard yard. Hal can talk to him alone there.

The shipyard. The sliding gate closes off the road; the bar sits outside, right up against it. Inside is the head of the slipway: it lines up with the road, and from there you can see any car coming down the only road (the Anarchs' lookout). The slipway continues toward the water, to the north, off the map; the three hulls in dry dock (Salt's havens, Rosa's among them; Ray Dorsey slept there in 1996) are the shipyard exterior (t2i): regions with no destination.

Escape. Nobody holds them back: the bar door opens onto the road.

Location: @UUID[JournalEntry.iyojT7kJHH23BWLd]{The Glass Gallery (Elysium)}
Scenes: @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.uL8F2YNogcToiFc6]{A2-E01 · Elysium Night} · @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}

Elysium night (A2-E01, Night 3). You enter from the plaza, to the south, through the glass doors of the lobby. Solène Marchetti, the Keeper (PNJ-14), waits there at her desk with the register open (DOC-03), and on the threshold that separates the lobby from the great hall stands the velvet tray on its pedestal: “Your phones, please.” The fourth custom of Elysium is literal: “No connected device crosses the threshold” (CIUDAD-LEYES); the threshold is the 2 m gap between the lobby and the hall, and switched-off devices are kept in the cabinet on the lobby's east wall.

The great hall of the jellyfish. “Hundreds of pieces of blown glass hang from the ceiling like frozen jellyfish, red, amber, and black, and the light that passes through them moves across the floor every time someone walks by.” The pieces hang several meters above people's heads: they aren't drawn and don't block movement; their pools of color are the hall's Foundry lights (red and amber, with a slight flicker). On the terrazzo floor there are only two low benches and three pedestals with individual pieces. With every wall made of glass, from almost any point you can see almost everything else: “the glass walls make it impossible to know who's listening from outside” (LUG-03).

The quartet nobody sees. “A string quartet nobody can see is playing”: the musicians play in the west alcove, which opens onto the hall through a gap covered by a frosted-glass screen (it blocks sight, not movement).

Who's where (Read the Room, Wits + Etiquette Diff. 3). Whitmore, “at the back, by the terrace,” beside the north glass doors. Halloway moves through the hall like a host. Voight, alone, on the terrace, checking her watch: “she prefers the terrace because from there she can see who comes in” (from the terrace, through the glass hall, you can see the whole lobby). Thornquist, in the southeast corner of the hall, by the plaza glass, where nobody goes near him. Fry, wherever he likes.

The terrace. Stone paving, railings to the north, west, and east, no lighting of its own: the Fair's tower is visible to the north, off the map. Eavesdrop unseen (Wits + Awareness Diff. 4): on the terrace, Halloway tells a minor Kindred, “The Sheriff is getting old…” The terrace connects to the hall through two glass doors.

The Prince's private salon. Northwest corner: you enter it from the great hall through a wooden door; its north wall is a fixed pane of glass over the terrace, and the west wall another over the plaza. The glass blocks sound but not sight: Whitmore's armchair faces north, toward the terrace and the tower, so from the terrace you can see his lips. This is the LUG-03 detail: with Wits + Awareness Diff. 4, you notice that someone with a telephoto lens, on the terrace, could read lips in the salon. The private audience with the Prince is granted here.

The staff (ghouls, untouchable under the third custom) come out of the pantry in the service block, to the east, carrying the glasses nobody drinks from. The service corridor has a door to the plaza and the stairs to the Keeper's archive, in the basement (map “galeria-archivo”): going down the stairs, the “Down to the archive” region leads to the foot of the basement stairs. Marchetti's apartment (Haven 2) is “above the archive,” on the upper floor of the service block: it has no map.

The curved walls of the 1962 pavilion: the north glass bulges toward the terrace, the plaza panes on either side of the lobby bulge outward, and the private salon has a curved glass bay window to the west. In Foundry each curve is a series of straight glass segments; the two doors to the terrace are two of those segments.

If the Council of A4-E01 moves here (the Prince regained the initiative; Halloway loses 2 dice), it's played in the great hall with a long table brought in by the staff (tile from the tower), or in the private salon if there are only a few of them.

The Keeper's archive, in the basement of the Gallery's service block. You go down by the service stairs (Marchetti's key); the region “Up to the Gallery,” at the top of the flight, takes you back to the service hallway.

The archive. Floor-to-ceiling shelves holding the Elysium ledgers and the foundation's papers, a reading table, and a safe. Marchetti records everything and interprets nothing: her books are “the history of every Kindred in Seattle since 1962” (PNJ-14). Rumor says they're kept in a safe at the Gallery; that's half true: the last three volumes (including XIV, the one from DOC-03) are in this safe; the eleven before them are somewhere only she knows. The archive door is locked: the Keeper has the key. Her apartment (Haven 2) is above, on the upper floor of the service block; it has no map.

The storeroom. Crates of spare glass pieces packed in straw: the jellyfish are blown by Tomás Arriaga (Marchetti's Touchstone), who thinks he works for an eccentric foundation.

No set scene takes place here: it's for anyone who asks to see the register outside the hall, for a heist, or for the chronicle.

Location: @UUID[JournalEntry.Oiln4o98kvxKbOvS]{The Larchmont Building}
Scenes: @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.9fTKL8Oeq36BCfU9]{A2-E05 · The Ashes of the Larchmont}

The basement (A2-E05). You reach it by the half-collapsed stairs (at the bottom, under the stairwell, a heap of wet rubble where the rain falls in) or by dropping down the stairwell. Total darkness: there's no light. Running water can be heard: an open channel in the floor carries the water from the rubble to the mouth of the large drain in the west wall, which empties into the Sound.

The sealed cistern. In the center of the boiler room, a slab of new concrete, lighter than the rest of the floor (Wits + Investigation Diff. 3; no roll if David came along: he goes straight to the slab). Beneath it are the seven tenants, Danny Ruiz (REF-02) among them. If David is there, he doesn't help open it and, afterward, doesn't speak again for the rest of the night. Auspex 4 on the slab: seven presences, cold, water, “Helen will come.”

The new flower. Wits + Awareness Diff. 4: beside the slab, recent bare footprints and a very faint smell of stale Vitae (MEN-08). They aren't drawn and have no tile: they're the reward for the roll, like the repeater at LUG-05.

Inside. Everything is burned: the doors no longer exist (openings), the windows have no glass (openings in the wall). The hallway ends in the collapse from the floors above; 1B and 1C have caved in (mounds of rubble: no way in). Scene with rain weather: the roof is gone, and the rain “comes in through the roof and runs down the stairwell to the basement, where you can hear water running.”

The stairs. In the stairwell, the flight that led down to the basement is half collapsed, and beside it the shaft opens all the way to the basement (solid black: it has no floor). Getting down to the basement: Dexterity + Athletics Diff. 2. The “Climb down” region is at the low end of the flight and leads to the foot of the basement stairs; a failure can mean the fall down the shaft. The shaft region leads to the rubble in the basement (a one-story fall, about 3 m). From the basement, the “Climb up” region brings you back to the landing at the top of the flight.

Arrival (A3-E03, Night 7, midnight). “The service stair zigzags up the outside of the silo to a long, narrow gallery of sheet metal and dirty glass. Inside, a stopped conveyor belt runs end to end.” Krell expects David to come in through the west sheet-metal door; the coterie decides whether to bring him and who goes up with him. At the far end, to the east, is the open loading door over the bay (an open door: the Storyteller can close it), and in front of it, the chair with the hostage (tile tile-silla-madera; Krell pushes it toward the edge if he sees the whole coterie). Krell waits sitting on the belt. The scene has rain and wind weather: it blows in through the loading door.

Heights (one floor per map). The gallery is 40 m above the terminal yard (the height of the silos). The loading door at the end opens over the water, 30 m down (A3-E03). What you see through the windows and through the stair grating is painted exterior: you don't walk there, you reach it through regions.

The three approaches (Dexterity + Stealth Diff. 4 vs. Krell's Wits + Awareness, 7 dice):

  • The outside stair (the one David uses): region “Go down the service stair” on the flight that keeps going down; the arrival is the top landing, in front of the door.
  • The inside of the neighboring silo (Athletics Diff. 3 to climb): comes out through the floor loading hatch marked in the south aisle, about 8 m from the chair. A PC hidden there reaches the chair with Dexterity + Stealth Diff. 4.
  • The water (a boat below the loading door): region in front of the loading door, on the outside.

The loading door. Anyone who falls through it takes 4 bashing damage on hitting the water, thirty meters down. In combat, Krell tries to throw his opponents out through it (Strength + Brawl vs. Dexterity + Athletics); if he drops to half his Health, he jumps himself and disappears. The region outside the loading door is the fall.

Scenes: @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.tG1m5PTkmBA1pvmc]{A4-E03 · The Last Ferry}

A4-E03, 12:55 a.m. “The terminal is almost empty under the fluorescents. A guard looks at his phone; a coffee machine blinks behind an ‘out of service’ sign. Outside, the last ferry of the night waits with every light on, like a four-story white building floating on black water. The horn sounds once, long. On the passenger ramp, an old man in a dark suit with an aluminum briefcase climbs slowly, leaning on the arm of an enormous man who looks back and sniffs the air.”

The waiting room is on the upper floor. Fixed benches in three double rows; a handful of sleepy-looking passengers (tokens). The security guard is at his podium beside the boarding door (west), looking at his phone. The broken coffee machine stands against the north wall (dark on the map; the “screen” light makes it blink). The “out of service” sign isn't painted on.

The passenger ramp. From the boarding door, the elevated walkway, glassed in on both sides, runs west: at its far end it rests on the ferry's stern. When the coterie enters the waiting room, Pell and Dawson are climbing the walkway (place them halfway along): they can be seen through the glass from the room. At the end of the walkway, the “Board the ferry” region leads to the stern deck of the passenger cabin (ferry). Boarding without Dawson seeing them: Dexterity + Stealth Diff. 4 against his Wits + Awareness (6 dice); Obfuscate doesn't fool his nose, but the wind off the Sound does (+1 die for the windward side: the wind comes in from the west, off the water).

The vehicle ramp (below, at dock level, in the southern strip): the vehicle holding lot and the ramp that crosses the water to the car deck. Anyone arriving by car (Dexterity + Drive Diff. 3 to get there before 12:55 a.m.) appears in the holding lot; the region at the end of the ramp leads to the stern of the car deck (ferry-coches). The east stairs go down to the street and the holding lot (twin regions on this same map), and the holding lot exits onto Alaskan Way (no map).

The restrooms (hatched block) aren't played. The horn sounds at 12:50 a.m.: five minutes.

Primogen Council (A4-E01, Night 8, 10:30 p.m.). “The private elevator climbs forty-two floors without a sound. It opens onto an enormous room with a single wall of glass over Elliott Bay”: the car opens directly into the council room, through its east wall. The west wall is all glass (the bay, the cranes, the ferries, the Hound's island: off the map). “In the center there's a long table of dark wood with seven chairs”: the table runs east to west, with the head against the glass wall; Halloway stands at the head, his back to the bay, facing the elevator the Prince comes in by. Six chairs along the sides (Whitmore, Marchetti, Voight, Thornquist, Fry, and the Sheriff). In front of each chair, a closed folder with a name on it (tiles without text; the contents are AYU-08). Celeste (or her stand-in) and Mr. Pell stand behind Halloway, between the head of the table and the glass. The coterie stands. The room's furniture “looks like it has never been used.”

The vestibule. Behind the east double door wait the ghoul security (MEN-04, from the 40th floor) and Montgomery's dogs: “The dogs in the vestibule begin to howl.”

Halloway's office, in the northeast corner, with glass to the north and east. For negotiating with Halloway before the Council, in private.

Leaving (Escape). Either by the private elevator, which needs Halloway's key or Pell's (the car door is locked: the key opens it), or by the emergency stairs off the vestibule: forty-two floors (Stamina + Athletics Diff. 3 to avoid reaching the bottom at Hunger 5); the region at the foot of the flight marks the descent, with no map of the rest of the stairwell.

The private elevator runs from the street to the penthouse and from the penthouse to the vault on level −3, and it's the only access to the vault. In the car, the door half receives arrivals and the back half goes down to the vault (plan “torre-boveda”). The street stop has no map: the Storyteller moves the tokens by hand.

If Halloway flees (total exposure or defeat): “And he heads for the elevator,” goes down to level −3, takes the briefcase out of the vault, and hands it to Pell. If he wins, at 12:30 a.m. Pell leaves with the briefcase by the same elevator.

Combat: attacking Halloway here, in front of the Primogen, hands him the vote. Halloway doesn't fight: Daunt, and into the elevator.

A4-E03, aboard. The last ferry to Bainbridge: a 35-minute crossing, some forty passengers, all mortal, six crew, and security cameras in the cabin (three “CCTV” objects on the map; they aren't ANOMALY). This map is the passenger deck (the boat's second level), cropped to the stern: the cabin continues forward (hatched strip) and isn't played.

Pell “is in the second-floor passenger cabin, by a window, with the briefcase handcuffed to his wrist” (Wits + Investigation Diff. 3 to find him): put him in the marked port booth, by the window, with Dawson and the ghouls nearby. If they voted with the coterie, Fry is in another booth with headphones on (“The last boat of the night. I told you.”). In the cabin, forty witnesses: any visible supernatural act is Thermometer +2. Presence (Daunt) to keep the passengers in the cabin: Charisma + Intimidation Diff. 3. Potence to break the briefcase cuff without taking off Pell's hand: Strength + Larceny Diff. 3.

Aft outer deck. When the ferry casts off, the gangway pulls back: the gate in the rail stays shut and the “Down the ramp” region only works while docked (disable it on departure, at 12:55 a.m.). This is where the negotiation with Halloway happens if he's aboard (“He offers everything: money, domain, the Sheriff's post”). Jumping into the water from the stern: 6 meters; the water is in the high forties and the current is strong: Stamina + Athletics Diff. 3 to reach shore or Salt's launch, which follows the ferry and can board over the stern. Jump with the briefcase and the drive is lost. Throwing the briefcase overboard is the fastest way to destroy it.

Transitions. The starboard and port stairs (by the aft end of the cabin) go down to the car deck (ferry-coches). The bridge stair, in the middle of the cabin, goes up to the upper deck and the bridge (ferry-puente): that's where Halloway runs (“uses Daunt and flees toward the bridge to take control of the ship”).

Galley in the middle of the cabin (fixed counters). The booth benches and tables are bolted to the floor (they're fixed; there's no movable furniture on this map).

The bridge. Halloway “doesn't fight: he uses Daunt and flees toward the bridge to take control of the ship.” He climbs the stair in the middle of the cabin to the upper deck and enters the bridge (wheelhouse) through the aft door; the crew can lock it from inside. Inside are the captain and a deckhand (two of the six crew): Dominate on them, or Halloway forces them (“Stop.” “Let go of that.”). The helm station is in the center, facing the console under the forward windows. The starboard and port bridge wings (open, with rails) each have a control pedestal.

At night the bridge runs dark (only the screens, turned all the way down, to protect night vision): high darkness on purpose. The navigation lights are on the wing rails: green to starboard (north), red to port (south). The two deck lights hang from the wheelhouse's aft bulkhead and light the upper deck; a little of that light gets in through the bridge's aft windows.

Crop: the ferry has two bridges, one at each end; this is the forward one during the crossing (the one steering). Between the cabin stair and the bridge there's more ship that isn't played; the upper deck continues aft (hatched strip). If Halloway falls into the coterie's hands, see Endings (AVE-01-FIN).
